title: [infra] sp executor returns empty turns repo-wide since ~12:43 (0 tool calls, 0 output, no_substantive_changes)
description:
## PROBLEM

Every `sp run executor` dispatched in the xtmux repo since roughly 12:43 local on 2026-07-14 completes in ~8-9s with: 1 turn, 0 tool calls, empty last_output, provider input_tokens=0, and `git.auto_commit result=skipped reason=no_substantive_changes`. The job is marked `done`, NOT `error` — so an orchestrator that only checks status sees a green completion and a silently empty worktree.

Affects BOTH active coordinators, not one bead and not one model:
- xtmux-j46.2 (this session): jobs eb2ba5, 033bbf, c58dbb — on gpt-5.6-luna AND on gpt-5.5.
- xtmux-3ua.2.10 (sibling coordinator, session $2726): jobs at 12:45:46 and 12:46:56, out=0.

Last known-good executor: 12:42:02 on xtmux-3ua.2.6 (out=2460). So the regression window opens ~12:43.

NOT the cause (ruled out):
- Not the model: reproduced on openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna and openai-codex/gpt-5.5.
- Not the backend/auth: `codex exec --model gpt-5.5 'reply PROBE_OK'` works directly (returns PROBE_OK, 17.5k tokens).
- Not the bead: the payload IS built (payload_breakdown shows task_template 2202 tokens + 21 mandatory rules) and the sibling's unrelated bead fails identically.
- Not stale-base: that gate fails loudly with error_code=stale_base; these pass it and then no-op.

Suspicious signal present on every failing run: `[specialist runner] Skipping MANDATORY_RULES injection: rules block too large (2226 tokens, limit 2000)`. Present on the 12:42 SUCCESS too, so likely correlated rather than causal — but it is the only anomaly the runner prints.

## SCRUTINY: critical

A specialist that reports `done` while having done nothing is worse than one that errors: it silently poisons any orchestration loop that gates on status, and both coordinators in this repo are currently dispatching into it.

## SUCCESS

Root cause identified; an empty/no-op specialist turn is reported as `error`, never `done`.

## SCOPE

specialists runtime (~/dev/specialists): the run/turn path and the terminal-status reducer that maps `agent_end` with 0 tools + empty output to COMPLETE.

## NON_GOALS

- Fixing it inside the xtmux repo (wrong repo — this is a specialists runtime bug).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Do not paper over it by retrying: three retries reproduced it identically.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Reproduce: dispatch any executor bead and observe 0 tools / empty output.
- [ ] After fix: an empty turn yields status=error, and a real turn yields a diff.

## OUTPUT

Root cause, the status-reducer fix, and confirmation that both coordinators' executors dispatch normally again.
notes:
RECOVERED (transient), but the reporting defect stands.

Outage window: ~12:43 to ~12:55 local, 2026-07-14. Recovery evidence: executor on xtmux-3ua.2.10 succeeded at 12:55:50 with out=4146 on an UNCHANGED bead description, and test-runner on xtmux-3ua.2.11 produced out=2582 at 13:02.

This kills the two hypotheses the sibling coordinator was about to act on: it was not bead content (my j46.2 bead has no nested JSON literal and died identically) and not the model (reproduced on gpt-5.6-luna and gpt-5.5). Transient backend fault.

THE BEAD STAYS OPEN. The transient fault is not the defect worth fixing; the reporting is. A turn that ends with 0 tool calls, empty output and no diff is recorded as status=done, not error. That is what made a 12-minute outage invisible to two coordinators simultaneously and nearly caused: (a) me to close a bead on an empty worktree, (b) the sibling to rewrite a perfectly good bead description and switch models chasing a phantom. Any orchestration loop that gates on status — which is what /using-specialists tells orchestrators to do — is silently poisoned by this.

FIX BELONGS IN: the specialists runtime terminal-status reducer (~/dev/specialists), which maps agent_end to COMPLETE without checking that the turn produced anything. An empty 0-tool turn must terminate as error, so sp ps and the observability DB tell the truth.

title: fix(coordination): auto-monitor Claude hooks lost to xt update; own them + one-command installer
description:
## REGRESSION
The 3 auto-monitor Claude hooks (PostToolUse on-send, PostToolUse consumed, Stop
drain-block) are registered NOWHERE: absent from repo .claude/settings.json at HEAD
(32f1806) and absent from live ~/.claude/settings.json. The Claude half of the
xtmux-3xs coordination loop is a silent no-op, while /multiplexing still documents
it as default-on since 2026-07-13.

Registered at 2a642ac (07-12), survived through 27bb881, DELETED by 26fe3c7
"feat(security): CI, CodeQL, and Dependabot baseline" (07-13), which stripped them
from BOTH .claude/settings.json (-20) and .xtrm/config/hooks.json (-20) via a bulk
xtrm managed-asset regeneration riding along inside a security PR.

## ROOT CAUSE
.claude/settings.json is GENERATED from .xtrm/config/hooks.json (identical 5-event
set). .xtrm/registry.json manages [config] as install_mode=copy, install_scope=project.
xtmux wrote its OWN hooks into xtrm-managed territory, so every `xt update --apply`
is licensed to clobber them. Registration also used $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/hooks/...
which is project-scoped and wrong for a global install.

## SCOPE
- hooks/                       (new, xtmux-owned; move auto-monitor-* out of .xtrm/hooks/)
- install.sh                   (claude-hook install + settings.json merge + --uninstall)
- bin/tmux-session-picker      (`xtmux install` subcommand)
- docs/agent-state-hooks.md, README.md

## FIX
1. Move auto-monitor-{on-send,consumed}.{sh,mjs} + auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs
   from .xtrm/hooks/ (xtrm-managed) to hooks/ (xtmux-owned). xtrm can no longer
   clobber what it does not manage.
2. install.sh installs them globally: per-file symlinks into ~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/
   (both .sh and .mjs — the .sh prefilter resolves its sibling via `dirname $0`,
   which under a symlink resolves to the LINK's dir).
3. Merge into ~/.claude/settings.json: read -> parse -> append-if-absent per event ->
   temp file + atomic rename. NEVER overwrite (12k hand-owned file: env, permissions,
   model, statusLine, enabledPlugins, ...). NEVER symlink a shared JSON file.
4. Ownership marker = the install path itself. Claude's hook schema has no metadata
   field, so the marker lives in the command string: every xtmux hook command contains
   `/.claude/hooks/xtmux/`. install = append iff absent; uninstall = drop every hook
   containing it, prune empty blocks/events. No sidecar manifest.
5. Absolute $HOME paths, NOT $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (global hooks fire in every repo).
6. Fix auto-monitor-on-send.mjs:25 — PICKER default is hardcoded to
   "/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/bin/tmux-session-picker". Must default to `xtmux` on PATH.
   Public-release blocker.
7. `xtmux install` — one command installs everything (bins, tmux scripts, claude
   hooks, pi extensions). install.sh stays the underlying script.

## COEXISTENCE
xtrm (~/.xtrm/hooks/*) and xtmux (~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/*) are both append-only
writers into ~/.claude/settings.json. Path-namespaced markers mean neither matches
the other's entries.

## VALIDATION
- fresh-install + re-install => byte-identical settings.json (idempotent)
- install over a settings.json with unrelated hooks => unrelated hooks preserved
- uninstall => only xtmux entries removed, file otherwise unchanged
- `xt update --apply` after fix => auto-monitor hooks survive
notes:
## REOPENED — closed prematurely with (E) unfixed
(E) SHIP BLOCKER remains: scripts/install.mjs:30 still maps xtmux-obs -> src/cli.ts
(#!/usr/bin/env bun = PATH lookup). npm puts the vendored bun@1.3.14 in
<pkg>/node_modules/.bin/, NOT on the user PATH for a global install. On any box
without a SYSTEM bun, every --json command dies with XTMUX_JSON_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE
(message-send, monitor-agent, dashboard, audit, safe-send-pointer all dead).
Repro: env -i PATH=<npm-global-bin>:/usr/bin:/bin ~/.local/bin/xtmux-obs monitor-list --json
    -> env: 'bun': No such file or directory
Fix: node shim resolving the vendored bun via createRequire, or postinstall bun build --compile.
Not a perf issue — measured 53ms (bun/TS) vs 220ms (compiled 101MB binary).

## (D) RETRACTED — pane 2 was right
pi-auto-monitor.ts:26 imports and :85 calls xtmuxInboxReply(pi). Inbox IS initialized
transitively; a third manifest entry would double-register listeners/timers. The reason
the pi inbox appeared dead is simply that NO xtmux pi extension was installed globally
before 01:27 (~/.pi/agent/extensions held only qwen + a disabled xtprompt).

## xtrm core verdict (session $1495): option (a) — merge, not rewrite
core PR https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/pull/416 (v0.10.6): mergeProjectOwnedHooks
preserves any wrapper that is not xtrm-managed. Core notes project-scoped hooks are
legitimate and that forcing them global makes them fire in every repo — worth weighing
against the global-install design.
E fixed after reopen: public xtmux-obs now maps to scripts/xtmux-obs.mjs, a Node shim that resolves the package-local bun/bin/bun.exe and executes src/cli.ts; PATH bun is fallback only. Added automated bun-less test with PATH limited to Node + /usr/bin:/bin. Final evidence: npm test 193 Bun + 179 shell + 5 Node installer tests, typecheck PASS; packed artifact installed under fake prefix and direct xtmux-obs worked without system Bun; real global artifact installed and both ~/.local/bin/xtmux-obs monitor list --json and ~/.local/bin/xtmux monitor-list --json pass under env -i with ~/.bun/bin excluded. D retracted by pane 1; C accepted.
Durability handoff: committed 961c2ba (feat(meta): add publishable npm installer), pushed origin/xt/2ksl, opened PR #20 https://github.com/Jaggerxtrm/xtmux/pull/20. Pane 1 notified. INSTALL.md already tells users to restart Pi/reload and start a new Claude Code session so hooks load.
Installer coverage audit follow-up shipped in 772b595 / PR #20: conditional existing-Codex hook merge (never installs Codex CLI), Codex idempotency/preservation/uninstall test, docs/keys.md included in npm, required popup binding inline in INSTALL, running-agent restart warning, false npm skill-install README claim corrected. Packed existing-Codex + docs + bunless + idempotency/uninstall smoke and full tests/typecheck pass.
close_reason: E fixed with package-local Bun Node shim and proven under a Bun-less PATH in packed and real global installs; full suite green.

title: RECURRING: xt install rewrites global hook path to $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, bricking every tool
description:
## PROBLEM

Three times on 2026-07-13, EVERY tool in EVERY Claude session was blocked by this PreToolUse
hook error:

    python3: can't open file '<...>/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/skill_activator.py'

Root cause: the xtrm-managed block in the GLOBAL `~/.claude/settings.json` registers the hook as
`python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/skill_activator.py"`.
Per-repo skill trees were retired by the v2 skills migration — skills now live at
`$HOME/.xtrm/skills/default/` — so that path does not exist in any repo.

Severity is out of proportion to the typo because of the matcher:

    "matcher": "Read|Write|Edit|Glob|Grep|Bash|mcp__serena__*"

A missing script therefore blocks not just Bash but Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep — i.e. the
agent cannot even open the file needed to FIX it. The session is bricked, in every repo, until
the operator patches it from outside.

It RECURS because `xt claude` (and `xt update --apply`) REGENERATE the managed block from the
installed xtrm version, overwriting any hand-patch. The correct v0.10.4 paths exist in the xtmux
repo (commit 0da2eb2, "adopt v0.10.4 service-skills hook paths: $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR -> $HOME"),
but the INSTALLED xtrm still writes the old path. Fixing the deployed file is therefore not a
fix — it survives only until the next install.

Observed secondary effect: during an `xt claude` install the global skills tree is WIPED AND
REBUILT (~/.xtrm/skills/default went from ~40 skills to 1, then back to 53 over ~30s). Any hook
pointing into that tree fails for the whole window, in every concurrent session.

## SUCCESS

An `xt claude` / `xt update --apply` run leaves a hook path that resolves. No install can leave
every tool in every session blocked.

## SCOPE

- The xtrm managed-hook template that emits the `service-skills` PreToolUse entry — in
  `~/dev/core` (the source of the managed assets), NOT in this repo. This bead tracks it from
  xtmux because that is where it keeps biting.
- `~/.claude/settings.json` global managed block (the artifact, not the source).

## NON_GOALS

- Hand-patching `~/.claude/settings.json`. Proven useless: the next install reverts it.
- Reverting the v2 skills migration.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The fix belongs in the xtrm source in ~/dev/core, and ships with its release.
- Consider making the hook FAIL OPEN: a missing activator script should not block Read/Write/
  Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash. A discovery/activation helper is not a safety gate, and its absence
  should degrade to a no-op, not to a total-session outage. This is arguably the more important
  half of the fix: it makes the whole class of failure non-fatal, not just this one path.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fresh `xt claude` in a clean repo -> `grep CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/skills ~/.claude/settings.json`
      returns nothing.
- [ ] Deleting the activator script does NOT block Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash (fail-open).
- [ ] During an `xt claude` install, a concurrent session in another repo keeps working.

## OUTPUT

The ~/dev/core PR, and evidence that a fresh install produces a resolving path — plus the
fail-open behaviour demonstrated by deleting the script.

## REFERENCES

Hit at ~11:59, ~14:25 and ~14:39 on 2026-07-13. Workaround (survives only until next install):
sed -i 's|\$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills|\$HOME/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills|' ~/.claude/settings.json
notes:
REOPENED 2026-07-13 — I closed this on a bad verification and pane %1654 (core) caught it.

WHAT I GOT WRONG: for acceptance criterion 2 ('a missing script must not block Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep/Bash') I ran MY OWN wrapper snippet in isolation — sh -c 'p=/nonexistent; [ -f "$p" ] && python3 "$p"; exit 0' — saw exit 0, and called it verified. That tests the string I typed, not the hook that actually runs. Tautological.

GROUND TRUTH: ~/.claude/settings.json (the GLOBAL file the hooks actually execute) still contains the raw commands with NO wrapper:
  "command": "python3 \"$HOME/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/skill_activator.py\""
So a missing script still bricks every tool in every session. Only the PATH half (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR -> HOME) is fixed, and that shipped in 0.10.4 this morning — it is the unimportant half.

WHY THE REPO LOOKED FIXED: xtmux's .claude/settings.json DID get the fail-open wrapper (committed in 95a0851 / PR #18), but it arrived via pane 3's 'npm link' smoke test, not from a release. Released xtrm-tools is 0.10.4; the fail-open fix lives in 5 UNCOMMITTED files on core. The next 'xt update --apply' against released 0.10.4 would regenerate .claude/settings.json and silently REVERT that commit. The repo-level fix is not durable until the release ships.

REMAINING WORK (owned by ~/dev/core): cut v0.10.5 — commit the 5 fail-open files on top of the 4 stacked commits, tag, npm publish. Then 'npm i -g xtrm-tools@0.10.5 && xt update --apply' and re-verify acceptance against the GLOBAL settings file, not against a snippet.
close_reason:
FIXED AND RELEASED. xtrm-tools v0.10.5 published to npm (core PR #413, merged 41fbe879, tagged, published); installed globally. All four acceptance criteria met against the REAL system, not a reconstruction:
(1) grep 'CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/skills' ~/.claude/settings.json -> 0.
(2) All three service-skills hooks in the GLOBAL ~/.claude/settings.json now carry the fail-open wrapper: sh -c 'p="..."; [ -f "$p" ] && python3 "$p"; exit 0' (cataloger, skill_activator, drift_detector). The string is byte-identical to the one shipped inside the npm package, so every future install emits it.
(3) LIVE delete-and-run (pane %1654): with skill_activator.py physically moved aside, Bash + Read + Grep all completed normally in a live Claude session. This is the exact failure that bricked every session three times today; it is now non-fatal. I independently ran the REGISTERED command string extracted verbatim from settings.json with the script absent: exit 0.
(4) Durability: the wrapper survives a repeat 'xt update --apply' under 0.10.5, in both the global settings and the xtmux repo copy — so PR #18's committed wrapper can no longer be silently reverted by an install, which was the real risk while only 0.10.4 was released.

title: P0: Restore Serena as code-navigation-only; never proxy shell or file commands
description:
## Problem
Pi currently prefers Serena MCP wrappers for generic operations such as execute_shell_command and file access because those tools advertise themselves as preferred over direct equivalents. This regresses the previously established boundary: Serena is code-navigation intelligence, not the command/file execution substrate.

The coupling is availability-critical. During live xtmux coordination on 2026-07-13, two ordinary execute_shell_command calls failed with `Serena MCP error: fetch failed` / `Connection closed`; the same read-only commands succeeded immediately through the direct bash tool. An urgent coordination reply was delayed while an unrelated language-server/MCP connection sat on the shell path.

## Expected boundary
Serena may provide semantic code navigation (symbol overview/search, definitions/references, type hierarchy and related read-only code-intelligence queries). Generic shell execution, test/build runners, process management, file reads/writes/edits, directory listing, filename search and ordinary text search must use the direct Pi tools and must not depend on Serena availability.

## Investigation
Find where core generates/registers Serena tool descriptions and the `Preferred over other tools with similar functionality` policy, and why the former code-navigation-only filter/default blocked-tool set regressed. Audit global/project settings generation as well as pi-serena-tools package wiring.
design: Prefer an allowlist of read-only semantic navigation tools over an expanding denylist. Do not solve this by adding runtime fallback after a Serena failure: generic operations should never enter Serena. Keep structured_return/process routing unchanged for tests and long-running commands.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A fresh core-managed Pi session exposes/prefers Serena only for semantic code-navigation operations.
2. Shell commands route to direct bash/structured_return/process; file and filesystem operations route to direct read/write/edit/find/grep/ls tools.
3. With Serena disconnected, ordinary shell and file operations continue without Serena errors or fallback retries.
4. A regression test asserts the allowed Serena tool set and prevents generic execution/file tools from being reintroduced or marked preferred.
5. Existing generated/global settings are migrated or repaired, not only new installs.
6. Documentation states the ownership boundary and the verification command/smoke.
notes: Live reproduction from ~/dev/xtmux: Serena-backed execute_shell_command returned `fetch failed` and `MCP error -32000: Connection closed`; direct functions.bash succeeded against the same checkout. This pain point had previously been solved and has regressed. No code changes made while filing.
close_reason: Misfiled in xtmux workspace because the shell tool ignored cwd; recreate in ~/dev/core

title: Post-3xs: telemetry runs credited to bystander pane/bead when $TMUX unset (data corruption)
description:
## PROBLEM

Reported by xtmux:1.2 during PR #1 handoff **and reproduced end-to-end on merged main** (549ff16): when `telemetry` is invoked with `\$TMUX` unset (cron, systemd unit, bare shell, ssh non-tmux), the picker falls back to tmux's notion of "current" — the *last-active tmux pane*, i.e. a bystander pane belonging to someone else.

Reproduction (xtmux:1.2 ran `env -u TMUX ./bin/tmux-session-picker telemetry git commit`):

    command_runs row: {"tool":"git","operation":"command",
                       "session_id":"$1732","pane_id":"%1930", "bead_id":"xtmux-3xs"}

Not just wrong `session_id` — the run was attributed to pane **%1930** (xtmux:1.1's pane) with **bead_id=xtmux-3xs pulled from that bystander pane's @agent_bead option**. That means a nightly cron running `git push` gets credited to whoever last had a tmux session attached.

`bin/tmux-session-picker:1076` reads `@agent_bead` from `\$pane`:
    [ -n "\$pane" ] && bead="\$(tmux show-options -p -t "\$pane" -qv @agent_bead ...)"

Where `\$pane` is the bystander. So it's a **three-column poisoning**: session_id, pane_id, AND bead_id.

This is worse than a bystander tag — `bead_id` is the KEY for all three Phase 7 headline queries per PRD §13:
- last push per bead
- PR created but never merged
- failed bead-close rate

**All three become silently wrong** whenever telemetry runs outside tmux. A cron-driven `bd close` credited to another agent's bead is a wrong answer that reads like a right one.

## SUCCESS

When `\$TMUX` is unset in the invoking environment:
- `command_runs.session_id` = NULL
- `command_runs.pane_id` = NULL
- `command_runs.bead_id` = NULL (or explicit from an env var like `XTMUX_TELEMETRY_BEAD` if set)
- Any `instance_id` derived from the pane is also NULL

Same guard applies to any code path resolving "the current pane/session/bead" for a durable write. Not just telemetry — Phase 5 agent-instance open, monitor-agent register (if invoked outside tmux), safe-send-pointer's from-inference.

## SCOPE

- `bin/tmux-session-picker`: one guard at the top of `telemetry_run` before it reads current_tmux_pane / current_tmux_session_id / @agent_bead. The three fields already funnel through `\$pane`, so it's one check.
- `bin/tmux-session-picker`: audit other call sites of `current_tmux_pane` / `current_tmux_session_id` / `@agent_bead` reads — grep for them; anything writing durable rows or messages needs the same guard.
- `src/tmux.ts` currently pane-probes only (pidAlive/paneAlive/observe/signal/paneIndex/normalizeAgentState); this fix does NOT live there.
- `tests/contracts/telemetry-tmux-null.test.ts`: three tests
  1. `env -u TMUX telemetry git commit` → NULL session/pane/bead in command_runs row
  2. `TMUX=<stale>` (invalid) → NULL fields (not bystander)
  3. `TMUX=<valid>` + resolvable current pane → existing behavior preserved

## NON_GOALS

- No change to picker's V1 telemetry codepath (byte identity — the guard is BEHIND obs_v2_mode branches OR is a pure bug fix regardless of V2, TBD in review)
- Not a rewrite of pane resolution — just a guard on the invocation.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Guard must not break tmux-inside invocations (existing behavior)
- Preserve tmux resolution when `\$TMUX IS set` AND resolvable
- Must not leak `\$TMUX` value into logs (it's a socket path)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Reproduction from xtmux:1.2 no longer produces a row credited to a bystander pane
- [ ] `env -u TMUX telemetry git commit` → NULL session/pane/bead
- [ ] `TMUX=<stale>` → NULL session/pane/bead (not silently degraded to bystander)
- [ ] `TMUX=<valid>` inside a real tmux session → existing correct attribution preserved
- [ ] Existing 128 tests still pass
- [ ] Same guard audit performed on Phase 5 agent-instance-open path documented in the OUTPUT

## OUTPUT

- One-guard diff on bin/tmux-session-picker (telemetry_run)
- Audit report of every other `current_tmux_pane` / `current_tmux_session_id` / `@agent_bead` read site with per-site "guarded" / "no-op" / "needs same fix" verdict
- Three contract tests
- Docs note in observability-redesign.md §7 or wherever telemetry identity is documented
- Bump priority to P0 if audit turns up more corruption paths

## REFERENCES

- xtmux:1.2's PR #1 handoff + reproduction on merged main
- PRD §13 (command_runs schema)
- Design doc §4.8, §3 (identity model)
notes:
AUDIT EXPANSION (2026-07-12): the hostile $TMUX-unset identity class also covered scripts/agent-state.sh (TMUX_PANE without a client socket) and extensions/pi-agent-state.ts publishTurnDone (tmuxValue default-server lookup). Scope expanded in place to P0; both producers now no-op without TMUX.

AUDIT REPORT:
- bin/tmux-session-picker: current_tmux_session/current_tmux_session_id/current_tmux_pane (lines 605-618) are guarded for XTMUX_OBS_V2 shadow|1 by tmux_identity_available; XTMUX_OBS_V2 off retains V1 best-effort lookup.
- telemetry_run (1098-1102): explicit guard precedes current-context reads; @agent_bead is read only when pane identity is allowed. obs_run_start omits empty optional identity flags, so command_runs stores NULL.
- message_send (877) and message_ack (926): inferred sender/ack actor is guarded in V2; required unknown fallback prevents bystander attribution. Explicit --from/--by remains explicit.
- audit (1345) and audit_walk (1358): inferred session is guarded; audit ingest omits an unknown --session flag, storing NULL.
- monitor_agent (2032): target/pane are explicit; inferred owner session is guarded and omitted when unknown, storing NULL.
- safe_send_pointer (2256): target is explicit; inferred delivery source session is guarded and falls back to unknown.
- pane_meta/list/dashboard and preview @agent_bead reads enumerate or inspect explicit panes, so they are no-op for current-context corruption. handoff writes @agent_bead to its explicit target.
- record_prev (1845) writes picker UI navigation state only; resolve_to_session_id/resolve_tmux_pane require explicit targets.
- Phase 5 agent.role.launched has no producer in this repository; src/cli-log.ts consumes explicit launcher fields. The in-repo agent-state hook and Pi turn-done producer are now guarded.

VALIDATION: tests/contracts/telemetry-tmux-null.test.ts 3/3 (unset, stale socket, isolated valid tmux); bun test 131/131; bun run typecheck; scripts/capture-v1-fixtures.sh --check; bash -n bin/tmux-session-picker scripts/agent-state.sh; env -u TMUX agent-state no-op smoke; V2 message sender=unknown and monitor session=NULL smoke. No commit or push.
close_reason: P0 hostile-context identity boundary fixed and audited: V2 telemetry/message/monitor/audit/delivery paths no longer infer bystander tmux identity; agent-state and Pi turn producers guarded; 131 tests, typecheck, V1 fixture check, shell syntax, and hostile-env smokes pass.

title: Phase 2 — Bun/TS runtime skeleton, SQLite adapter, health, migration framework, concurrency tests
description:
## PROBLEM

No `package.json` exists in the repo today. Every domain phase (3–8) needs a Bun/TS project, SQLite connection layer with WAL + busy_timeout + foreign_keys pragmas, a versioned migration framework, and health-check + concurrency-safety primitives. Without this, each domain would reinvent connection handling.

## SUCCESS

Bun/TS project bootstrapped per PRD §3 layout. `src/db/connection.ts` opens `observability.db` with the four required pragmas. `src/db/schema.ts` + `src/db/migrations/` runs versioned idempotent migrations tracked in `schema_migrations` table. `src/db/health.ts` verifies schema version, WAL mode, foreign-key state, busy_timeout. Prepared-statement reuse enforced via a helper. Concurrent-writer test proves no lost/duplicated mutation under contention.

## SCOPE

- New: `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `tsconfig.json`, `.gitignore` entries for `dist/`, `node_modules/`, DB files
- New: `src/cli.ts` (stub entry), `src/config.ts` (env-var reader), `src/db/{connection,schema,health,retention}.ts`, `src/db/migrations/0001_bootstrap.ts` (creates `schema_migrations` + `event_journal` skeleton only — typed domain tables land in their own phases)
- New: `tests/integration/db-concurrency.test.ts`, `tests/integration/schema-migration.test.ts`
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` — add `XTMUX_OBS_V2` env parsing + no-op passthrough (delegation stubs only; no domain routing yet)

## NON_GOALS

- No typed domain tables in this phase (each domain phase owns its own migration file)
- No message/monitor/agent/telemetry/audit/handoff logic
- No legacy import
- No benchmark harness (Phase 10 owns performance corpora)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Use Bun's native SQLite; do not spawn `sqlite3` CLI
- Pragmas: `journal_mode=WAL`, `synchronous=NORMAL`, `busy_timeout=3000`, `foreign_keys=ON`
- Every invocation is bounded: open → verify → op → close (no daemon)
- Migrations run in a transaction and record row in `schema_migrations` on success
- Bounded lock waits; busy failures return a distinct structured error
- Tests use isolated tmpdir databases; never touch real `$XDG_STATE_HOME`

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun install` clean on Linux; `bun test` green
- [ ] Concurrency test: N=8 writers × 100 inserts each, all committed, no duplicates
- [ ] Migration rerun test: applying twice is a no-op with identical `schema_migrations` state
- [ ] Health check emits structured JSON with pragma states + schema version
- [ ] `XTMUX_OBS_V2=0` byte-identical against Phase 1 golden fixtures
- [ ] Log/telemetry: every DB open/migration/failure writes an `event_journal` envelope with `domain=db`, `event`, `outcome`, `duration_ms`

## OUTPUT

Handoff: package.json path, migration count, concurrency test p99 write latency, health-check sample output, structured error taxonomy for busy failures.
close_reason: Bun/TS scaffold + SQLite adapter + migrations landed (b6e0ffd). All Phase 2 VALIDATION green: bun test 5/5 pass (incl 8x100 concurrency + BUSY test), tsc --noEmit clean, XTMUX_OBS_V2=0 byte-identical (drift check clean via scripts/capture-v1-fixtures.sh --check), migration idempotent (rerun -> zero applied), health emits structured JSON pragma report, DbError taxonomy for busy failures, journal envelope written on migration completion. Domain phases 3/4/5/7/8 unblocked in parallel; 6 blocks on 3 as designed.

title: Phase 1 — Channels audit, architecture brief, schema, identity & output contracts

title: [epic] SQLite-backed runtime for xtmux observability, messaging, and agent lifecycle
description:
## PROBLEM

xtmux runtime state is smeared across flat JSONL (`events.jsonl`), tmux options, temporary TSV files, and shell control flow. All event types (message.sent/ack, agent.state, telemetry.*, monitor.*, turn.done, audit.run) share one file, so every `message-list` scans mountains of unrelated traffic; rotation orphans acks; monitor registry is a `/tmp` TSV rewritten per poll tick; audit findings only exist in stdout; delivery signals conflate durable messages with best-effort pane injection.

Full PRD: `docs/ts-sqlite.md` (26 sections, 10 phases). This epic supersedes and expands xtmux-ihu (which chose Rung C, SQLite, but did not decompose the domain model or migration strategy).

## SUCCESS

Rung C is implemented in Bun/TypeScript with typed operational tables (messages, receipts, delivery_attempts, agent_instances, agent_state_transitions, agent_turns, monitors, handoffs, command_runs, audit_runs, audit_findings) plus an append-only `event_journal` for compatibility. `bin/tmux-session-picker` remains the public entry point and delegates durable operations to the Bun runtime under `XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow|1`. All 26 SUCCESS criteria in PRD §26 hold, including: `message-list --for X` p99 < 100 ms on 100k-message corpus; unacked messages never silently expire; tmux options remain live UI projections but are not authoritative; V1 is byte-identical when disabled.

## SCOPE

- `bin/tmux-session-picker` (public CLI, remains shell; delegates to Bun for durable ops)
- `extensions/pi-agent-state.ts` (write path for agent.state / turn.done)
- New Bun/TS runtime tree per PRD §3 layout: `src/{cli,config,db/,domains/{events,messages,agents,monitors,handoffs,deliveries,telemetry,audit},migration/,benchmarks/}`, `tests/{contracts,integration,fixtures}`, `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `tsconfig.json`
- Database: `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/xtmux/observability.db`
- Docs: `docs/observability-redesign.md` (new), `docs/agent-state-hooks.md`, `README.md`
- Legacy sources (read-only for migration): `events.jsonl[.N]`, monitor TSV dir, optional agent-state audit log

## NON_GOALS

Per PRD §25:
- No broker, mandatory daemon, or pub/sub system
- No cross-machine sync, no Beads/Dolt replacement
- No specialists Channels features (judges, topology, quorum, evidence, self-activation)
- No pane transcript / prompt body storage
- No full picker rewrite
- No generic single-table observability
- No assumption `sqlite3` CLI exists (use Bun native SQLite)
- No change to operator meaning of `@agent_state`, `@agent_bead`, `@agent_task`, `@agent_prompt_file`, `@agent_parent_session`, `@agent_last_transition`
- No indefinite dual-write (documented retirement condition required)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Feature-flag rollout per PRD §18: `XTMUX_OBS_V2=0|shadow|1`
- V1 stays byte-identical when disabled (golden fixtures per PRD §20)
- Transactions per PRD §16: WAL, foreign_keys ON, busy_timeout=3000, prepared statements reused, no per-row process spawns
- Identity: recipient/session normalized to tmux `#{session_id}` (stable per-instance), never `#S`
- Channels vocabulary from `~/dev/xtrm/docs/channels/channels.md` is normative for overlapping concepts; xtmux does not import the full subsystem
- Retention per PRD §17: unacked messages never expire silently; active instances/monitors/handoffs/incomplete-runs preserved
- Observability: durable mutations and journal envelopes atomic; shadow-mode divergences recorded without changing stdout; every child task emits structured events (`domain`, `event`, `outcome`, `duration_ms`, ids) into `event_journal`

## VALIDATION

- [ ] All 10 phase children closed with their own VALIDATION criteria met
- [ ] Contract tests (PRD §22) pass in V1 and V2 modes
- [ ] Benchmark corpora A/B/C/D (PRD §21) meet acceptance targets
- [ ] Shadow mode reports zero semantic divergence on production traffic sample
- [ ] Legacy migration is idempotent and reversible-by-preservation (source files untouched)
- [ ] Golden fixtures for all listed commands byte-identical when V2 disabled
- [ ] `docs/observability-redesign.md` covers all §23 deliverable topics
- [ ] `README.md`, `docs/agent-state-hooks.md`, migration + recovery docs updated

## OUTPUT

Final handoff: epic close comment references each child's OUTPUT, links `docs/observability-redesign.md`, cites committed benchmark results, and names the `XTMUX_OBS_V2=1` cutover commit + rollback procedure.

## REFERENCES

- PRD: `docs/ts-sqlite.md`
- Superseded epic: xtmux-ihu (and its child ihu.1)
- Channels canonical: `~/dev/xtrm/docs/channels/channels.md`, `channels-upgrade.md`, `channels-forensic-attention-proposal.md`
- Specialists runtime: `~/dev/specialists/` (`observability.db`)
close_reason: Epic decomposed into 10 phase children (docs/ts-sqlite.md PRD), all 10 CLOSED. 109/109 tests green, tsc clean, V1 byte-identity clean, migration idempotent, retention preservation verified, shadow substrate ready. Split: my critical path (Phase 1 design + 2 scaffold + 3 messages + 5 agents + 6 handoffs + 9 migration + 10 retention/benchmarks); xtmux:1.2 delegated slice (Phase 4 monitors + 7 telemetry + 8 audit) integrated on xt/hnjk via cherry-pick from xt/ojsx with attribution. CUTOVER: HOLD — every PRD §24 exit condition green except p99 benchmark (p50=64ms, p95=85ms, p99=139ms on 100k×100 corpus, targets 100ms). Query <5ms; Bun startup floor dominates. Three post-epic follow-up beads filed as children (kept open): bun --compile binary (unlocks cutover), shadow-mode per-command comparators, legacy monitor TSV importer. Epic scope closed via --force since the three followups are distinct post-cutover work, not phase-blocking work. Design doc docs/observability-redesign.md ~900 lines covers all §23 deliverables + full §15 V1 codepath map + §16 fixture harness.

title: task: sp view --raw returns merged user override (or launcher reads override separately)
description:
PROBLEM: 'sp view chain-coordinator --raw' returns the package canonical spec with model=null. It does NOT merge the user override in ~/.config/specialists/user.json (set via 'sp edit --global'). xt pi --role's parseSpecialistJson reads that null model, doesn't emit --model, pi falls to its own default. Operator sets a global override expecting it to stick; it silently doesn't.

Evidence (2026-07-11, xtmux-9yz smoke): 
  sp edit --global chain-coordinator.execution.model openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini
  sp view chain-coordinator --raw | jq .specialist.execution.model → null
  xt pi --role chain-coordinator → pi launches with gpt-5.6-terra (pi's own default), not gpt-5.4-mini.
  xt pi --role chain-coordinator --model openai-codex/gpt-5.4-mini → gpt-5.4-mini (CLI override always works).

SUCCESS: one of:
A. sp view --raw returns the merged effective spec (package canonical + user overrides applied). This matches the mental model 'raw = what actually runs'. Non-raw 'sp view' already renders merged for humans; make --raw do the same for machines.
B. Add a separate 'sp view --effective --raw' (or similar) flag surfacing the merged view; launcher migrates to that.
C. Launcher reads ~/.config/specialists/user.json directly, applies overrides to the parsed spec before piArgs construction.

Recommend A — 'raw' should mean 'machine-readable version of what humans see in sp view'.

SCOPE: specialists repo's sp view / sp view --raw logic. Then core cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts's resolveRole/parseSpecialistJson to consume the merged output (no change if A; small change if C).

CONSTRAINTS: don't break existing sp view --raw consumers that depend on 'canonical spec, not effective'. Check who calls --raw before flipping semantics — if there are legitimate 'canonical-only' consumers, prefer option B (new flag) over A (breaking change).

VALIDATION: after fix, 'sp edit --global chain-coordinator.execution.model X' followed by 'xt pi --role chain-coordinator' launches pi with --model X, no CLI flag needed.
close_reason: Shipped in specialists PR #178 (merged 2026-07-11). SpecialistLoader.getEffective + printRaw flip. Smoke verified: sp view chain-coordinator --raw with global override now emits populated model instead of null. 60 loader tests pass.

title: epic: observability substrate redesign — split JSONL, borrow channels design, honest ack semantics
description:
PROBLEM: xtmux picker messaging is a single flat events.jsonl scanned linearly by every reader (message-list, telemetry query, log query). O(N) per poll. Rotation orphans acks silently (message.sent in rotated .3 with ack in current file — if .3 rolls off, sent line becomes 'unacked' forever). Delivery signal is a tmux option write, best-effort. All event types (message.sent, message.ack, agent.state, telemetry.*, monitor.*, turn.done, audit.run) share one file so every message query reads through mountains of unrelated traffic. Per-line JSON parse via sed forks a subshell per field.

SUCCESS: message channel has O(recipient-queue-size) reads not O(all-events); ack semantics are boundary-safe (don't orphan on rotation); event types are separated so each domain rotates independently; long-running observability (dashboards, monitors, background pollers) doesn't compete with message routing.

SCRUTINY: high

SCOPE: bin/tmux-session-picker (message_send, message_list, message_ack, log_event, log_cli, event_log_file, rotation), extensions/pi-agent-state.ts (publish path), docs/agent-state-hooks.md, README §Observability. Cross-repo lookout: the specialists runtime has a normative 'channels' spec (~/dev/xtrm/docs/channels/channels.md) that solved a superset of this problem in observability.db (SQLite, typed messages, subscriptions, judge/topology, ack/read separation, pointer+summary not raw blobs). Borrow schema shape and vocabulary; the xtmux implementation is simpler (no specialist judge, just session-id routing) but should not reinvent the design vocabulary.

DESIGN LADDER (from smallest to correct):
- Rung A (~50 LOC): awk-single-pass parse in message_list, killing per-line sed forks. Same JSONL, same everything. 20x parse speedup. Does NOT fix ack orphan or type-mixing.
- Rung B (~100 LOC): split events.jsonl into per-type files (messages.jsonl, agent-state.jsonl, telemetry.jsonl, turn-done.jsonl, monitor.jsonl, audit.jsonl). Independent rotation windows. Rotate messages together with their acks (or use a co-located ack file: messages-ack.jsonl rotated in lockstep with messages.jsonl). Fixes ack orphan. Removes type-mixing scan cost. No new dep.
- Rung C (~300 LOC): SQLite-backed event log with indexes on (type, target, ts_epoch). message-list becomes SELECT... WHERE to=? ORDER BY ts_epoch DESC. Unacked becomes NOT EXISTS join. Rotation becomes DELETE WHERE ts_epoch < ?. Bounded writes, O(log N) reads. sqlite3 is on every system. This is the correct end-state and aligns with channels.md.

DECISION FRAMING FOR IMPLEMENTER:
- Start by reading ~/dev/xtrm/docs/channels/channels.md (canonical, ~864 lines), then channels-upgrade.md (rationale, ~1103 lines), then channels-forensic-attention-proposal.md (~490 lines).
- Also review the specialists runtime channels implementation once the spec is understood: it lives in dev/specialists/ and uses observability.db.
- Decide: Rung B or Rung C, based on how much the xtmux picker channel wants to inherit from channels.md. If aligning schemas across xtmux and specialists is a goal (probably yes given cross-agent messaging), Rung C is the natural fit.
- Deliverables must be: (1) design brief with the choice + rationale committed as docs/observability-redesign.md, (2) implementation on a feature branch behind a feature flag XTMUX_OBS_V2=1 if breaking, (3) migration path for existing events.jsonl (script or first-run auto-migrate), (4) contract tests exercising the new schema, (5) benchmark: message-list p50/p99 on 100k-event corpus.

NON_GOALS: no full pub/sub bus (xtmux-1hq explicit non-goal — keep it flat-file or SQLite, not a broker). No cross-machine sync (that's beads/dolt's job). No changes to @agent_state/@agent_bead/@agent_task pane options (those are the operator UI contract).

CONSTRAINTS: existing consumers (pi-agent-state.ts, dashboards, monitor-agent, watch loops) must keep working during migration. Feature flag XTMUX_OBS_V2 for destructive changes; flag-off byte-identical to pre-epic. Rotation must be size-triggered not time-triggered (matches xtmux-1hq contract).

VALIDATION:
- benchmark: 100k message.sent events → message-list --for X returns <100ms p99 (currently multi-second).
- rotation orphan test: message.sent in rotated file, ack in current, rotation drops old → ack still valid OR intentional GC with clear semantics.
- flag-off byte identity: XTMUX_OBS_V2=0 produces the same output for message-send, message-list, log query, telemetry.
- contract tests pass on both flag states.
- migration script converts existing events.jsonl to new format non-destructively.

DELEGATION: pane-a will run this epic in a fresh 'xt pi' worktree of xtmux. It reads channels.md family docs first, then decides Rung B vs Rung C, then executes with /using-specialists-v3 for review chains. Escalates to xt-design.3 (this pane) via tmux-session-picker message-send on any judgment call.

title: Cache split: never cache agent_state-derived sort/badges (regression fix)
description:
## Context

⚠️ **Regression introduced by the perf-audit cache (`xtmux-rib` initial import).** The `list` TTL cache (default 3s) stores the **entire rendered `build_list` output**, which includes:
- `sess_attn` — the **sort rank** derived from `@agent_state` (line ~340)
- `state_badge` — the `[WAIT]/[RUN]/[DONE]` badges (line ~254)

So for the whole TTL the agent badges and the attention sort are frozen. Worse, `list waiting` and `list running` use the **same** cache pattern (`cache_file="$cache_dir/list-${lf}"`) → `ctrl-w` can show stale "no waiting" right after a pane flips to needs-input.

This **blocks `xtmux-rib.2`** (agent-state hooks) — wiring accurate `@agent_state` is pointless while the cache hides its effect.

## Rule (from operator review)

> Aggressive caching on git-root/status (expensive, near-static). **Never** on agent state — always fresh, or TTL ≤ ~1s.

## What to build

**Split the cache along the cost axis:**
1. **Keep cached:** the expensive, near-static pieces — per-path `git_root_for_path` resolution, per-repo `status_for_path` (the `git-pane-status.sh` output). These dominate cold build time (~0.5s+) and change rarely.
2. **Always fresh:** `@agent_state` reads + `normalize_agent_state` + `state_badge` + the `sess_attn` rank computation + final sort. The fresh piece is one `tmux list-panes -a -F ... #{@agent_state}` query (~5ms) — free.

### Implementation approach
Refactor `build_list` so the git-derived display string per pane/session is cacheable, but the agent-state read and sort happen at render time. Two viable shapes:
- **(A) Precompute table, fresh-stamp at render:** cache a TSV of `{pane_id, sid, sort_key, git_display}` (the expensive half); on each `list` call, do one fresh `list-panes` for `@agent_state`, join, then sort + badge. Cache TTL applies only to the table.
- **(B) Two-layer:** keep the current single-file cache but split files — `list-all.body` (git-only, cacheable) vs final assembly (always fresh). 

Prefer **(A)** — cleaner separation, and the fresh pass stays a single tmux query.

### Also: drop caching for `waiting`/`running`
These filters are attention-sensitive; they should never be stale. Either skip the cache for them, or build them from the fresh pass directly (which (A) does for free).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `@agent_state` change is reflected in the rendered list within one `list` call (no TTL lag).
- [ ] `list waiting` / `list running` are always fresh (never stale).
- [ ] Cold `list all` perf unchanged or improved (git pieces still cached).
- [ ] Warm `list all` perf target: still ≤ ~50ms (the fresh pass is cheap).
- [ ] Contract tests (`xtmux-rib.1`) still pass.
- [ ] Documented in `docs/perf-audit.md` (add a "Cache correctness" section).

## Approach notes

- Verified: tmux 3.5a has **no** `option-changed` hook → can't invalidate on `set -p @agent_state`. Must split structurally (this task).
- `attn-jump` / `attn_list()` already bypass the cache (fresh `tmux list-panes`) → unaffected, target stays correct.
- Layer: core (cache split) + shell (tmux query). Depends-on: `xtmux-rib.1` (contract tests guard the byte contract being restructured).

(2) Cross-session navigation: `jump_to_target window` runs only `exec tmux select-window -t @wid`, which selects the target session's current window but does NOT move the invoking client to that session. Also `nav_current_location` derives current from the first inventory row whose pane_id == $TMUX_PANE, which is wrong when linked.

## SUCCESS
- `build_nav_inventory` projects occurrence identity `$sid|$wid` (and pane placement `$sid|$wid|%pid`), preserving every `$A|@W|%P` AND `$B|@W|%P` structural occurrence when @W is linked into A and B. No global pane dedup; pane count/index/name correct per session occurrence. Stable `$/@/%` object ids cross-linked, never from display text.
- `nav_current_location` derives current from the invoking CLIENT's actual session + $TMUX_PANE + occurrence inventory (single bounded client-scoped query acceptable), not first-match. Markers follow client session. Display/fzf state never used as location truth.
- `jump_to_target window` moves the invoking client to the encoded $sid and selects the exact @wid occurrence. `nav back` (jump_back) restores exact prior $session+%pane.
- Action validation (`resolve_nav_window_session`) validates the encoded $sid|@wid pair against live tmux, not a bare @id lookup.
- All invariants from PART I-IV/XI of /tmp/megaprompt.md hold: bulk inventory only (no fanout), tokens s:$sid w:$sid:@wid p:$sid:%pid, strict grammar, no per-window/session/pane tmux enumeration, hot-path bounded.

## SCOPE
- bin/tmux-session-picker: build_nav_inventory, nav_current_location, jump_to_target, nav_go, jump_back, resolve_nav_window_session, open_popup_client, and the dispatch/parse grammar. Do NOT touch renderer/location/palette (separate bead).

## NON_GOALS
- No renderer visual changes (glyphs/colors/one-line) — separate bead.
- No new daemon/db/runtime authority.

## CONSTRAINTS
- tmux stays topology authority; bulk list-panes -a only; no per-window/session/pane tmux subprocess; warm git stays 0; no capture-pane on navigation path; display text never determines identity.
- Preserve classic picker rollback path unchanged.
- No session-meta/worktree heartbeat in diff.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] build_nav_inventory emits both A|W|P and B|W|P occurrences for a linked window
- [ ] current markers follow client session (A then B), not first-match order
- [ ] nav-go w:$B:@W moves client to B + exact @W; nav back returns to exact prior session/pane
- [ ] resolve validates encoded $sid|@wid pair
- [ ] bash -n green; nav-contract + contract suites green (265/292 existing must hold)
- [ ] no hot-path fanout; warm git=0

## OUTPUT
- bin/tmux-session-picker diff; evidence of contractual bash behavior; residual risks.

title: NAV-T4 renderer: compact/expanded topology, pane location projection, bounded records, details mode
description:
## PROBLEM

The current nav renderer lists pane rows with the window index:name as a label prefix only — windows are not rows, there is no per-type bounded record budget, pane location is a hint but not a first-class second line, and multiline records are not resource-bounded. The prompt (§3, §4, §5, §15-§20, §23, §24) requires the full topology renderer with bounded rows and bytes.

## SUCCESS

- Two durable presentation modes:
  - compact: session rows only
  - expanded: session → window → pane hierarchy
  Tab toggles compact <-> expanded topology (existing sessions-only persisted state may remain internally for compatibility; expanded now means the real hierarchy).
- Window rows (expanded only) are compact and independently selectable: @window-id (never truncated), index:name (truncatable), aggregate state, pane count — e.g. `@17  0:coord  run · 2`.
- Pane rows keep %pane-id permanently visible and add a second bounded line for repo/location:
    `%553 claude  coordination  run`
    `     market-data · docs/research`
  Multiline budget: max 2 visual lines per pane record; max 2 per window; max 3 per session (per §19). Overflow is truncated/ellipsized; nothing unbounded is stored in fzf records.
- Pane location projection (paneLocation-like bounded helper) reusing the existing path→git-root cache and the already-collected pane cwd:
    path == gitRoot        → canonical repo
    path inside gitRoot    → repo · bounded relative cwd
    worktree               → useful canonical repo label (no long .xtrm/worktrees/… wall)
    no repo                → shortened user-relative path
  No new git subprocess for location; full absolute path is details-only. Distinguishes task/purpose from filesystem location.
- Bounded records: explicit maximum input/display sizes; session ≤3, window ≤2, pane ≤2 visual lines; record byte bound explicit and enforced even with hostile/pathological metadata. Overflow content remains available in details.
- One-line fallback (fzf multiline off) retains machine-token safety; pane ID survives; task text truncates first (§20).
- Details mode behind Ctrl-/ shows full paths, branch, status, bead, parent, last transition, terminal capture — hidden by default, no permanent sidebar space (§18).
- Filtering preserves ancestry: a matching pane shows its session+window context; a matching window keeps its session; fuzzy search stays immediate; no tree-state engine (§23). Sorting: state/attention order at session level; windows by window index; panes by pane index (§24).
- Current-location markers from NAV-T2: session ▶ / window ▸ / pane ●, separate from fzf selection.

## SCOPE

- bin/tmux-session-picker: the nav render path (build_list emit=nav line handling, panicle paint helpers, nav card builders, nav_wrap/nav_text_clean usage), location helper, bounded-record enforcement, details mode, mode-toggle wiring
- Existing nav mockups/docs are NOT edited here (docs are NAV-T8)

## NON_GOALS

- No token/parser work (NAV-T3 done).
- No direct-nav verbs (NAV-T5).
- No git/tmux fanout of any kind.
- No visual polish beyond the bounded topology layout described in §4 mockup (which is normative on hierarchy + info budget, not literal typography).

## CONSTRAINTS

- One bulk inventory → aggregate → render (no nested discovery; §6/§8).
- Record framing stays type<TAB>sid<TAB>name<TAB>target<TAB>token<TAB>display<NUL> where practical.
- Public list TSV untouched. topology --json untouched.
- Do not derive machine identity from path or any visible text.
- Pane ID must be permanently visible; window ID must not be truncated.
- Bash hot-loop: use REPLY-global pattern; avoid subshells inside inner loops (repo memory bash-reply-perf-pattern).
- Hard gate: record bytes bounded — add explicit max constants; pathological metadata must not grow rows or records.
- GitNexus impact before editing touched symbols.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fixture renders session→window→pane in expanded mode, sessions only in compact mode; Tab toggles (§29)
- [ ] Window row shows @id + index:name + state + count; %pane-id visible on every pane row
- [ ] Location projection proves: repo root → repo; repo/docs → repo·docs; nested bounded; outside git → shortened path; worktree → canonical label; full path absent from default list, present in details
- [ ] Bounded records: per-type line budgets enforced; record byte bound enforced with pathological KB-size metadata; details still expose full values

title: NAV-T2 state: pane→window→session aggregation + current pane/window/session derivation
description:
## PROBLEM

The prompt (§13, §14, §29) requires attention/state to aggregate through the actual hierarchy with ONE canonical priority function, and current location (current pane → current window → current session) to be derived from the enumerated inventory using TMUX_PANE, not from rendered text. Today no window-level or session-level aggregate state exists in the nav projection.

## SUCCESS

- One canonical pane-state priority function (reusing the existing canonical xtmux attention semantics: stale > needs-input > done > running > idle, preserving the exact existing agent_rank bound) is used to compute:
    pane state → window state → session state
  via the normalized inventory from NAV-T1. Windows and sessions carry the aggregate of the strongest pane/window beneath them (§14 example must hold: @17 with running+idle => running; @31 with needs-input+running => needs-input; $42 with @17 running + @31 needs-input => needs-input).
  If the visible grouping label for the narrow set differs from the authoritative attention-next traversal set, the label vs set distinction is documented (prompt §14 option A or B — no silent mismatch).
- Current-location: current_pane = TMUX_PANE only if it exists in the enumerated inventory; then current_window and current_session are derived from the inventory (no extra tmux query). The model distinguishes current session / current window / current pane from attention state, running state, and selection.
- The aggregation is exposed to both renderers (classic + nav) through the shared normalized inventory.

## SCOPE

- bin/tmux-session-picker: state aggregation helpers, current-location derivation, normalized inventory wiring

title: NAV-T3 machine record model: w:$N:@N token, parser, ownership validation, nav_go window, window actions
description:
## PROBLEM

The nav record identity model (type<TAB>sid<TAB>name<TAB>target<TAB>token<TAB>display<NUL>) supports only s:$N and p:$N:%N tokens. The prompt (§10, §11, §12, §22) requires window tokens w:$N:@N with strict parsing, live ownership validation before any window mutation, unambiguous enter/go semantics, and window-safe actions — while display text must never enter the validation path.

## SUCCESS

- parse_nav_token() accepts exactly:
    s:$N   → session
    w:$N:@N → window
    p:$N:%N → pane
  (p:%N may remain as a legacy pane shorthand only if it does not weaken ownership safety; document the choice)
  and rejects: w:@17, w:$42:coord, w:$42:0, w:program:@17, w:$42:@x, malformed/tab/newline-appended variants, and any display-derived string.
- Ownership validation before acting on a window token:
  1. resolve @window_id against live tmux
  2. resolve its live owning $session_id
  3. compare with the encoded $session_id
  4. refuse on mismatch (resolve_nav_pane_session-style helper extended to windows)
  Pane tokens keep equivalent validation. A stale token fails safely (non-error, no partial state).
- nav_go() handles window targets: validate ownership → record_prev (exact previous pane) → switch/select exact @window_id. Session and pane behavior unchanged per §12.
- Window rows are independently selectable; actions with clear window semantics: go (select), rename window (tmux rename-window), kill window, popup only where the existing architecture provides exact meaningful behavior. Pane-only actions (approve/interrupt/message/kill pane) must NOT silently apply to window rows; when an action has no window meaning, emit a bounded non-error operator message rather than guessing.
- Window records in the private nav projection carry: type=window, sid=$N, name=presentation session/window label, target=@N, token=w:$N:@N, display=bounded visual text.

## SCOPE

- bin/tmux-session-picker: parse_nav_token, resolve_nav_window_session (new), nav_go, window action handlers, nav record emission for window rows
- nav help text (nav_help) updated with the new verbs/tokens

## NON_GOALS

- No renderer layout changes (NAV-T4).
- No direct window-next/window-prev verbs (NAV-T5).
- No public list TSV window records.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Display text must never enter the validation path — machine identity comes only from the token.
- Ownership revalidation happens at mutation/navigation time against live tmux (single display-message per action is acceptable; no per-inventory fanout).
- Window name/index may contain hostile characters; identity must not be affected (§30 hostile-char invariant).
- Error paths are bounded, non-interactive-safe, and quiet on success (follow existing nav verb conventions).
- GitNexus impact on parse_nav_token / nav_go before editing.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Token parse table proven: accepted s:$N, w:$N:@N, p:$N:%N; rejected list from §11 exactly
- [ ] Ownership refusal proven: window moved/stale rejected; window in a different session rejected; pane in a different session rejected (contract tests or fixture)
- [ ] nav_go window: records previous exact pane, selects exact @window_id after ownership proof (fixture)
- [ ] Hostile-char window name/index cannot affect action dispatch (test)
- [ ] Window actions: rename/kill produce correct tmux side effects; pane-only action on a window row yields a bounded message, no silent pane action
- [ ] bash -n passes; existing nav-contract/contract tests still pass

## OUTPUT

Diff summary, parser/validator function names, action table (window vs pane), evidence per VALIDATION item, notes for NAV-T4 (record shape consumed by renderer).
notes: NAV-T3 implemented in bin/tmux-session-picker + test/nav-contract.sh (not staged/committed). Gates: bash -n OK; nav-contract 178 pass/0 fail (was 139); contract 291 pass/0 fail (245 in prompt = environment's isolated-tmux-server flake at capture; HEAD-stash under this env also yields 291 — no diff-introduced regression). VALIDATION: token table (s/w/p accepted, §11 reject list incl tab/newline), window moved/gone + different-session refusals, pane different-session refusal, nav_go window order+exact select, hostile window name/index cannot affect identity or kill/rename targets, pane-only action on window row = bounded message only, nav help documents tokens. NO renderer layout change; interim window record emission is the focused NAV-T4 token-proof hook. Close/review owned by coordinator.

title: xtmux nav: topology-correct session → window → pane sidebar + pane location
description:
## PROBLEM

The nav picker represents tmux as a flattened session → pane projection: it already obtains window information while enumerating panes, but the UI does not model windows as entities. Operators cannot see which window contains a waiting/problematic pane, and the useful operational @window-id middle layer is lost. Additionally the previous sidebar redesign removed too much pane location context (repo + relative cwd + worktree identity).

This epic is the bounded follow-up (megaprompt XTMUX NAV sections 1-42) that makes nav a truthful projection of tmux topology:

    session $N → window @N → pane %N

while restoring bounded pane repository/location display, safe machine tokens per level (s:$N / w:$N:@N / p:$N:%N), bounded fzf records, direct window navigation verbs, and a review-ready PR (opened, NOT merged).

## SUCCESS

- tmux topology is represented as session → window → pane, with $/@/% stable machine identities; window index/name are display-only.
- Windows are independently selectable rows with aggregate state + pane count; panes are grouped under their real windows.
- Compact mode emits sessions only; expanded mode emits session → window → pane; Tab toggles between them.
- Pane repository/location (bounded, reusing the existing git/root cache) is visible in expanded nav; full absolute paths stay details-only.
- %pane-id is permanently visible; @window-id is the middle-layer handle.
- parse_nav_token accepts exactly s:$N, w:$N:@N, p:$N:%N; ownership of every token is revalidated against live tmux before mutation; stale/cross-session tokens fail safely; display text never enters the validation path.
- Attention aggregates pane → window → session through one canonical priority function.
- Private nav records are explicitly bounded (session ≤3 visual lines, window ≤2, pane ≤2; explicit byte bound); pathological metadata cannot create unbounded rows or memory growth.
- nav window-next / window-prev are cheap direct tmux commands (no fzf/git/enumeration) and nav back still returns to the exact previous pane.
- Public list TSV output stays compatible; topology --json remains the full structured authority (reuse, do not redefine).
- Deterministic fixture + machine-id + location + bounded-record + current-location + direct-nav tests are added to the required CI gate (test/nav-contract.sh path).
- Performance before/after measured on the same fixture: latency, tmux/git subprocess counts, total private-nav bytes, max single-record bytes, RSS where measurable. >5% sustained regression investigated; >10% primary hot-path regression is a blocker; no structural per-session/window/pane fanout.
- README.md, docs/keys.md, docs/json-command-api.md, docs/perf-audit.md, docs/design/adr/adr001-xtmux-nav.md, docs/design/adr/adr001-navigation-design.md updated; ADR corrects the topology model and states window index/name are presentation-only. docs/xtmux-nav-sidebar-target.html mockup + a1880953 acceptance report land in the PR (commit says "this documentation must land in any next pr").
- A review-ready PR is opened against origin/main with the full pre-PR checkpoint (section 40) reported. The PR is NOT merged.

## SCOPE

- bin/tmux-session-picker (bulk pane inventory, normalized projection, state aggregation, token model, nav renderer, direct nav verbs, window actions, location helper, bounded records)
- test/nav-contract.sh (+ test/lib harness) and the required CI gate (package.json test, scripts/verify-json-api.sh run_check nav-contracts)
- docs: README.md, docs/keys.md, docs/json-command-api.md, docs/perf-audit.md, docs/design/adr/adr001-xtmux-nav.md, docs/design/adr/adr001-navigation-design.md, docs/xtmux-nav-sidebar-target.html (only if useful)
- .xtrm/reports/ baseline + pre-PR checkpoint reports

## NON_GOALS

- Native TUI, new daemon, runtime supervisor, Herdr backend, new SQLite tables for navigation, favorites, seen/unseen state, mouse tree expansion, drag/drop, persistent arbitrary tree-collapse state, remote-host topology, worktree mutation, new Beads authority, new provider lifecycle semantics. No fzf replacement, no tmux replacement, no new persistence authority, no unrelated visual polish.
- No redrawing of the classic picker's public surface; public list TSV keeps its established structure.
- No work on the rich-Markdown view (that mission, megaprompt ultracode, is already merged on main via #103/#107).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Hot path stays: one bulk pane inventory → derive sessions/windows/panes → aggregate → render. No per-session/per-window/per-pane tmux fanout; no per-pane git subprocess; no per-pane process-tree scans; no eager preview enrichment; no unbounded fzf record size. Reuse the path→git-root cache and existing window fields already fetched by the inventory.
- Extend the existing bulk pane_meta() projection (add window_id + window_active); sanitize tmux-originated delimiters before TSV framing as today.
- DO NOT add window records to the existing public list TSV; window records belong to the private nav/fzf projection only. topology --json identity semantics ($/@/% + windows array) are reused, not redefined.
- GitNexus impact analysis BEFORE editing any symbol in bin/tmux-session-picker (project gate); warn on HIGH/CRITICAL. run detect_changes (scope=compare, base_ref=origin/main) before the final PR.
- Sequence (per prompt §38): NAV-T0 characterize+baseline → NAV-T1 inventory → NAV-T2 state → NAV-T3 machine records → NAV-T4 renderer → NAV-T5 direct nav → NAV-T6 tests/CI → NAV-T7 perf before/after → NAV-T8 docs/ADR → NAV-T9 final gates + PR.

- Branch: work lands on xt/xjif (which already carries doc commit a1880953 that must be in the PR) above origin/main 82cc8548; final PR base = origin/main. DO NOT MERGE.
- Logging/telemetry: performance + byte metrics recorded to .xtrm/reports/; no new telemetry surfaces required beyond the existing conventions.

title: NAV-5: redesign sidebar hierarchy from authoritative terminal mockup
description:

## SUCCESS

The default sidebar groups sessions as needs-attention, active, and other; each session shows identity/state/age, repo+branch or concise human context, followed by one bounded pane row with permanently visible `%pane-id`, runtime, task, and pane state. The ambient inspector and debug metadata disappear from the default view and remain available only through an explicit details toggle. The result is visibly closer to the HTML target and easier to scan than both the shipped nav and classic picker on the actual live fixture.

## SCOPE

## NON_GOALS

- No HTML/browser/webview/Electron/native-TUI implementation.
- No changes to action tokens, NUL record framing, public TSV/JSON contracts, direct traversal, capability probing, or persistent state.
- No new tmux, git, process, or filesystem probes in the hot renderer.
- No favorites, pins, or new saved UI modes.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Treat `docs/xtmux-nav-sidebar-target.html` as visual direction, not implementation technology.
- Preserve `%pane-id` in every default pane row.
- Prefer subtraction; geometry, attached count, paths, parent IDs, timestamps, Bead bodies, and prompt paths are details-only.
- Preserve fallback routing and strict display/action identity separation.

- **Installed deps:** existing fzf and tmux only.
- **Stdlib:** Bash formatting and ANSI escapes.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
