title: hooks/claude/agent-state.sh is a divergent copy of scripts/agent-state.sh
description:
## PROBLEM

PR #20 (branch xt/2ksl, epic xtmux-3ua / the installer packaging work) adds hooks/claude/agent-state.sh as a BYTE-IDENTICAL COPY of scripts/agent-state.sh as it existed before xtmux-j46.1. Git reports zero textual conflict between #20 and PR #21 (xtmux-j46.1) because the copy is a new file — so this will merge clean and be wrong.

After both land, there are two divergent copies of the same hook. scripts/agent-state.sh (repo/test surface) has --new-instance and rotates @agent_instance_id; hooks/claude/agent-state.sh (the payload install.sh actually installs to ~/.tmux/scripts/) does not. Every INSTALLED Claude agent therefore never rotates the instance id, and the whole j46 -> Specialists spawn binding silently degrades to pane-level precision for every real user — while the contract tests, which exercise scripts/, stay green. A silent, test-invisible correctness regression on the exact identity the epic exists to establish.

SCRUTINY: high

## SUCCESS

There is exactly one source of truth for the agent-state hook. The installed hook and the tested hook are provably the same bytes, and a test fails if they ever diverge again.

## SCOPE

hooks/claude/agent-state.sh, scripts/agent-state.sh, install.sh (and scripts/install.mjs if that is the landed installer), test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Re-litigating PR #20's packaging design.
- Touching the Codex/Pi hook payloads beyond whatever the same duplication rule implies.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Do NOT fix by hand-copying the file — that reintroduces the same drift on the next edit. Dedupe (single file + symlink/generated payload) or add a test that hard-fails on divergence.
- Whichever of PR #20 / PR #21 merges second owns the reconciliation; the other must not be silently overwritten.
- Coordinate with the sibling coordinator (tmux session $2726) that owns xtmux-3ua / PR #20.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] A contract test fails if hooks/claude/agent-state.sh and scripts/agent-state.sh differ (or if the single-source invariant is broken).
- [ ] The installed hook (post install.sh into a temp HOME) accepts --new-instance and rotates @agent_instance_id.
- [ ] test/contract.sh green.

## OUTPUT

The dedupe/mirror mechanism, the divergence test, and evidence that a freshly installed hook rotates the instance id.
notes:
RESOLVED WITHOUT A FIX BEING NEEDED — verified on main after PR #20 (d5cc800) landed.

The hazard was real when I filed it: PR #20's branch (xt/2ksl) carried hooks/claude/agent-state.sh as a byte-identical copy of the pre-j46.1 scripts/agent-state.sh (diff against origin/main:scripts/agent-state.sh was empty), with zero textual git conflict against PR #21.

Final state of main is safe:
- hooks/claude/agent-state.sh does NOT exist on main (git ls-tree origin/main -> empty). The copy never landed; #20's merged tree only relocated the auto-monitor-* hooks.
- scripts/install.mjs:39 maps ~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh -> <root>/scripts/agent-state.sh, i.e. the installer points at the SINGLE source rather than shipping a duplicate. This is the dedupe outcome the bead asked for.
- The j46.1 identity work survived the merge: origin/main:scripts/agent-state.sh has 4 --new-instance references, origin/main:extensions/pi-agent-state.ts passes it on session_start.

So the installed hook and the tested hook are the same file by construction, not by hand-copy. No divergence test is needed because there is no second copy to diverge.

Residual risk: if a future PR reintroduces a payload copy of agent-state.sh under hooks/ or a package dir, this class of bug returns silently (tests exercise scripts/, the installer would ship the copy). If that ever happens, the fix is the same: point the installer at the single source, never duplicate.

title: Test: agent.ready + readiness-gated handoff — smoke/E2E + telemetry assertions
description:
Layer: operational/agentic (hooks, delivery, monitors — real runtimes)
Strategy: smoke + E2E against real Claude and Pi panes in a throwaway tmux server, plus journal telemetry assertions
Covers: xtmux-j46.7, xtmux-j46.8

## PROBLEM

Readiness and delivery are exactly the surfaces where unit tests lie: send-keys "succeeds" into a runtime that has not installed its hooks, and the handoff looks delivered while the work was never received. Only an E2E against real runtimes proves the handshake.

## SCOPE

test/contract.sh, test/harness-selftest.sh, scripts/smoke-json-api.sh, test/lib/.

## SUCCESS / assertions required

- [ ] Exactly-once: a fresh agent instance produces exactly ONE agent.ready row; a forced second emission adds none.
- [ ] Distinctness: idle transitions after ready never re-emit agent.ready.
- [ ] Rotation: restarting an agent in the SAME pane yields a new agent_instance_id and a new agent.ready.
- [ ] Negative: agent.ready is never emitted from pane/process creation alone (create a pane running a plain shell -> zero ready rows).
- [ ] Handoff positive: --prompt-file delivers that exact file; the handoff record exists BEFORE the first delivery attempt.
- [ ] Handoff negative: missing or disallowed prompt path -> structured error, rejected pre-delivery, nothing written.
- [ ] Handoff timeout: --wait-ready against a target that never readies -> structured non-zero timeout, no delivery attempt.
- [ ] Idempotency: same handoff key twice -> one handoff record, one monitor, two recorded delivery attempts.
- [ ] Transactionality: --monitor with a forced monitor-insert failure leaves NEITHER handoff nor monitor (assert both tables).
- [ ] Dry-run: without --yes, nothing is written and nothing is sent.
- [ ] Delivery honesty: send-keys success alone never marks the handoff delivered/completed.
- [ ] Backward compat: existing handoff goldens unchanged.

## Debuggability evidence required (telemetry assertions)

- [ ] `xtmux log query --type agent.ready --since 1h --json` shows the handshake for a live Claude pane AND a live Pi pane.
- [ ] handoff.created / handoff.delivery_attempted / handoff.delivered|failed rows carry host_id, pane_id, agent_instance_id and the handoff key.
- [ ] Redaction: no prompt content in any journal row (grep the payloads).

## test-runner command contract

- Setup: throwaway tmux socket + temp XDG_STATE_HOME; launch one Claude and one Pi pane in a scratch worktree.
- Run: `test/contract.sh` (readiness + handoff cases), `scripts/smoke-json-api.sh`.
- Cleanup: kill the tmux server, remove the temp state dir. Must run even on failure.
- Failure taxonomy: in-scope (readiness/handoff assertion), pre-existing (unrelated golden), infrastructure (runtime unavailable / auth prompt) — an unavailable runtime is NOT a pass.

## Known deferred paths

- Readiness for Codex panes — follow-up bead to be created if Codex support is claimed.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Smoke + E2E green with live runtimes; telemetry assertions pass.

## OUTPUT

Test files, run output, the live journal rows proving both runtimes emit agent.ready.

title: Test: journal cursor + follow — pagination, ordering, expiry, reconnect
description:
Layer: core/boundary (SQLite read contract + stream)
Strategy: seeded-DB unit/contract tests + a concurrent-write follow test
Covers: xtmux-j46.5, xtmux-j46.6

## PROBLEM

A cursor bug is invisible in normal use and catastrophic for a materializer: duplicates double-count edges, gaps drop them silently, and an unstructured retention error crashes the consumer instead of triggering a resync.

## SCOPE

test/ (Bun test for src/domains/events + src/db), test/contract.sh for the CLI surface.

## SUCCESS / assertions required

- [ ] Exclusivity: --after-id N returns first item with journal_id > N (never == N).
- [ ] Completeness: paging a seeded journal of mixed event types returns every row exactly once, strictly ascending, across page boundaries.
- [ ] Empty page: next_after_id == requested cursor, has_more=false, items=[].
- [ ] Watermarks: oldest_available_id/latest_available_id == MIN/MAX(id) in event_journal.
- [ ] Cursor expiry: --after-id below oldest_available_id -> structured typed response (code + oldest_available_id), NOT a raw SQLite error or stack trace.
- [ ] Ordering is never timestamp-derived: seed two rows with identical occurred_at_ms and assert id order is respected.
- [ ] Limits: every query path enforces an explicit limit; a request above the cap is clamped deterministically.
- [ ] Follow: emit N events concurrently while following; each arrives exactly once, ascending.
- [ ] Follow reconnect: kill + resume at last received id -> zero duplicates, zero gaps.
- [ ] Follow shape: an item is byte-identical to the `log query` item for the same journal_id (no second schema).
- [ ] Follow shutdown: SIGTERM exits 0 with the stream flushed.
- [ ] Backward compat: existing log goldens unchanged.

## Critical paths covered

- Exactly-once materialization — risk: Console double-counts or drops job->pane edges.
- Retention expiry — risk: consumer crashloops instead of resyncing.

## Anti-pattern check

- No tautological assertions: expected page contents are derived from the seed script, not from the query under test.
- No shared DB state: each test seeds its own temp DB.

## NON_GOALS

Bridge journal.follow transport (covered by the bridge test bead — it reuses this contract).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Bun tests + contract.sh green.

## OUTPUT

Test files, run output, a sample cursor-expired response.

Strategy: contract tests in test/contract.sh against a real fixture tmux server; live-first, no mocking of tmux
Covers: xtmux-j46.1, xtmux-j46.2

## PROBLEM

`xtmux context --current --json` is the hard cross-repo interface: Specialists parses it field-for-field. A silent field rename, a fabricated id, or a bystander-tmux-server resolution is a cross-repo break that unit tests on pure functions cannot catch.

## SCOPE

test/contract.sh, test/golden/, test/lib/.

- [ ] Positive: inside a fixture tmux pane, context JSON validates against xtrm.runtime-origin.v1 field-for-field; ids match `tmux display-message -p` for $/@/% formats.

- [ ] Edge: pane without @agent_instance_id -> field absent/null, verified=true (pane-level precision), NOT an error.

- Cross-repo DTO shape — risk: Specialists silently drops or misparses the binding.
- Outside-tmux / dead-pane -> risk: fabricated origin poisons forensic history permanently.

- `xtmux log query --type agent.state --limit 5 --json` shows host_id + agent_instance_id on new transitions.

Specialists-side capture tests (peer repo's epic). Topology/journal tests (separate test bead).

Contract tests run against a real tmux server in a throwaway socket; no mocked tmux. Deterministic: no time.now() assertions beyond monotonic bounds.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] test/contract.sh green with the new cases, existing goldens unchanged.

## OUTPUT

Test files changed, contract.sh run output, and the captured sample payloads used as goldens.

title: Handoff: existing prompt file, --wait-ready, transactional monitor registration
description:
## PROBLEM

`xtmux handoff` always generates its own /tmp prompt file, cannot wait for the target to be ready, and treats `tmux send-keys` success as delivery. A coordinator with an already-written prompt has no readiness-aware, monitor-backed delivery path (gaps doc 8.2).

## SUCCESS

`xtmux handoff --target %17 --prompt-file /tmp/task.md --wait-ready 2m --monitor --json` validates the prompt file, waits for the target's agent.ready, creates one durable handoff record before delivery, records every delivery attempt and its result, and can register the monitor transactionally with the handoff intent. Retries with the same handoff key are idempotent.

## SCOPE

bin/tmux-session-picker (handoff flags + help), src/domains/handoffs/, src/domains/deliveries/, src/domains/monitors/, docs, test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Bridge-side handoff (mutating bridge methods stay deferred).
- Changing safe-send-pointer's cardinal safety rules.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Validate the prompt file is an allowed local path and exists BEFORE delivery; reject otherwise with a structured error.
- Preserve dry-run-first behavior: no send without the explicit --yes/approval flag.
- One durable handoff record is written before the first delivery attempt, never after.
- send-keys success is NOT proof of acceptance — record it as an attempt, not a completion.
- Idempotency via caller-supplied or generated handoff key: a retry with the same key must not create a second handoff record or a second monitor.
- Depends on .7 (agent.ready) for --wait-ready.
- Existing handoff invocation (no --prompt-file) stays byte-compatible.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: --prompt-file with an existing file delivers that exact file; a missing/ disallowed path is rejected pre-delivery with a structured error.
- [ ] Contract test: --wait-ready times out cleanly (structured, non-zero) when the target never emits agent.ready.
- [ ] Contract test: same handoff key sent twice -> one handoff record, one monitor, two recorded delivery attempts.
- [ ] Contract test: --monitor registers the monitor in the same transaction as the handoff intent; a failed insert leaves neither.
- [ ] Contract test: dry-run (no --yes) writes nothing and sends nothing.
- [ ] Existing handoff goldens unchanged.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, an idempotent-retry trace from the journal, and the handoff/delivery rows for a real readiness-gated delivery.

comments.author: jaggerxtrm
comments.text:
EXPLORATION (coordinator, before dispatch) — three findings that change the shape of this work:

1. THE HANDOFF DOMAIN IS DEAD, exactly like the agent domain was in j46.7. bin/tmux-session-picker handoff() only calls the V1 'log_event handoff.created/handoff.sent'. It NEVER calls src/domains/handoffs/lifecycle.ts. So handoffs and delivery_attempts have zero rows, while createHandoff() and markSent() sit there fully written and unused. Do not write a new domain — WIRE THE EXISTING ONE. createHandoff() already does the insert + journal envelope in one transaction and already hashes the prompt file; markSent() already records a delivery_attempts row with kind=handoff_pointer.

2. THE TRANSACTIONAL MONITOR REQUIREMENT CANNOT BE MET FROM BASH. 'register the monitor in the same transaction as the handoff intent; a failed insert leaves neither' is a single SQLite transaction, and the picker is a bash script shelling out per command — two separate 'xtmux-obs' invocations are two transactions by definition. This needs ONE new runtime subcommand (e.g. 'handoff-create') that takes the handoff intent + optional monitor and wraps both inserts in one db.raw.transaction(). The picker calls that once, then sends, then reports the attempt.

3. IDEMPOTENCY HAS A FREE IMPLEMENTATION. handoffs.id is the primary key, so a retry with the same --key is a UNIQUE violation, not a second row. Use src/db/errors.ts isUniqueViolation() (added in j46.7) to turn that into 'reuse the existing handoff', which gives 'one handoff record, one monitor, two delivery attempts' with no extra bookkeeping. The delivery attempt is recorded per send, so the second send naturally adds the second row.

CONSTRAINT WORTH RESTATING: send-keys success is NOT acceptance. Record it as an attempt. The ONLY evidence of acceptance is the target's own agent.ready / subsequent state change (j46.7 shipped that feed) — which is also what --wait-ready must poll.

title: agent.ready handshake + normalized event families
description:
## PROBLEM

"Pane exists" is not "agent can receive work". Today a coordinator can only see process/pane creation, so it sends prompts into runtimes that have not installed their control hooks. There is also no documented, normalized set of event families with enough identity to attach an event to the graph without re-reading pane options afterwards (gaps doc 8.1 + 9).

## SUCCESS

`agent.ready` is emitted exactly once per agent_instance_id, after the Pi/Claude runtime finished initialization and installed its hooks, and is distinct from `idle` (which recurs after turns). The lifecycle starting -> agent.ready -> idle is observable in the journal. The event families listed in gaps doc 9.2 are normalized and documented, each carrying host_id/session_id/window_id/pane_id/agent_instance_id where applicable.

## SCOPE

scripts/agent-state.sh, extensions/pi-agent-state.ts, Claude hook wiring (examples + .claude settings docs), src/domains/agents/{instance.ts,transition.ts}, src/domains/events/query.ts (envelope identity fields), docs (event catalogue), test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Structured activity spans (gaps doc 9.3) — telemetry enhancement, filed separately, not a blocker.
- Handoff readiness wait (child .8 consumes this).
- Changing existing agent.state semantics.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Exactly-once per agent_instance_id: a second ready for the same instance must be a no-op, not a duplicate row.
- agent.ready MUST NOT be inferred from process start or pane creation.
- Depends on .1 (agent_instance_id must exist before ready can be keyed on it).
- Existing domain tables remain authoritative for domain state; the journal is the ordered integration feed only.
- Hooks stay best-effort and bounded — a missing ready must degrade to today's behavior, never block a turn.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: a fresh agent instance produces exactly one agent.ready row; forcing a second emission does not add a row.
- [ ] Contract test: idle transitions after ready do not re-emit agent.ready.
- [ ] Contract test: restarting an agent in the SAME pane produces a new agent_instance_id and a new agent.ready.
- [ ] Contract test: every event family in gaps doc 9.2 that xtmux emits carries the identity fields required to attach it without reading pane options.
- [ ] `xtmux log query --type agent.ready --since 1h` shows the handshake for a live Claude and a live Pi pane (smoke).

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, live smoke evidence for both runtimes, and the documented event catalogue.

title: Journal cursor: expose journal_id, exclusive --after-id, watermarks, cursor expiry
description:
## PROBLEM

`log query` has no durable stream cursor. A consumer polling by timestamp or event_key gets duplicates, misses committed rows, and cannot detect that retention has eaten its position (gaps doc 6). The committed SQLite rowid already exists — it just is not exposed.

## SUCCESS

`xtmux log query --after-id 1842 --limit 500 --json` returns the gaps-doc 6.2 page: schema_version xtrm.xtmux.journal-page.v1, items[] each carrying journal_id + the stable envelope (event_type, occurred_at_ms, recorded_at_ms, host_id, session_id, pane_id, agent_instance_id, payload), plus next_after_id, oldest_available_id, latest_available_id, has_more. --after-id is exclusive, ordering is strictly journal_id ASC, and a cursor older than retained history returns a structured cursor-expired response.

## SCOPE

src/domains/events/query.ts, src/db/journal.ts, src/db/retention.ts (watermark read), src/cli-log.ts, bin/tmux-session-picker (`log query` flag surface + help), docs, test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Follow mode (child .6 — only after page semantics are stable).
- A second event schema or a websocket server.
- Backfilling identity fields onto historical rows.

## CONSTRAINTS

- journal_id is the committed SQLite row id and is ALWAYS present on every JSON event.
- Timestamps must never be the primary cursor.
- event_key stays an optional idempotency/correlation field, not a cursor.
- next_after_id = highest returned id, or the requested cursor when the page is empty.
- Cursor expiry is a structured protocol outcome (typed code + oldest_available_id), never a raw DB error.
- Every list/query path gets an explicit limit and deterministic ordering.
- Existing `log query`/`log tail` output shapes stay backward compatible for current consumers.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: --after-id N is exclusive — first item has journal_id > N.
- [ ] Contract test: paging through a seeded journal returns every row exactly once, in ascending id order, across event types.
- [ ] Contract test: empty page returns next_after_id == requested cursor and has_more=false.
- [ ] Contract test: --after-id below oldest_available_id returns the structured cursor-expired response with a non-zero/typed code, not a stack trace.
- [ ] Contract test: watermarks (oldest/latest) match SELECT MIN/MAX(id) FROM event_journal.
- [ ] Existing log goldens unchanged.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, a sample page JSON plus a sample cursor-expired response.

title: Add xtmux topology --json (xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1)
description:
## PROBLEM

Console cannot reconstruct host -> session -> window -> pane from the current dashboard output: window identity, pane placement, geometry, active state and @agent_parent_session are missing, and the shape is TSV/presentation-oriented (gaps doc 5).

## SUCCESS

`xtmux topology --json` emits one versioned snapshot matching gaps doc 5.3: schema_version xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1, generated_at_ms, host{host_id,tmux_server_id?}, sessions[] -> windows[] -> panes[] with pane_id/pane_index/active/width/height/left/top/pid/current_command/current_path and a nested agent{} carrying instance_id, state, bead_id, task, prompt_file, parent_session_id, last_transition. Read-only, bounded, no pane content.

## SCOPE

bin/tmux-session-picker (new `topology` command + help + dispatch), src/cli.ts if the snapshot is built in the Bun runtime, tmux format string collection, docs, test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Changing dashboard/list output shape (existing operator consumers must keep working).
- Pane content / capture (child .4).
- Making Console parse TSV or call tmux itself.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Stable ids only ($N/@N/%N); names and indexes are display metadata, not identity.
- Must include @agent_parent_session (currently absent from pane-level JSON) plus @agent_instance_id/@agent_state/@agent_bead/@agent_task/@agent_prompt_file/@agent_last_transition when set.
- Missing optional metadata: absent or null, never fabricated.
- One bounded tmux query pass; do not shell out per pane.
- Presentation-free and backward compatible within v1.
- Depends on host_id from .1.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: snapshot of a fixture tmux server nests host->session->window->pane correctly with $/@/% ids.
- [ ] Contract test: pane geometry, indexes and active flags match `tmux list-panes -F` for the same server.
- [ ] Contract test: pane with no agent options -> `agent` absent/null, not an empty fabricated object.
- [ ] Contract test: @agent_parent_session present in pane JSON when the pane option is set.
- [ ] Existing dashboard/list goldens unchanged.
- [ ] Output contains no pane content and no env dump.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, a sample snapshot from a live 2-session server.

title: Add xtmux context --current --json (xtrm.runtime-origin.v1)
description:
## PROBLEM

Specialists must record which pane/agent instance spawned a job, without heuristics. It needs one fixed, read-only command returning a verified runtime-origin DTO (gaps doc 11 + 12.2). This is the hard cross-repo interface: the peer Specialists epic blocks on it.

## SUCCESS

`xtmux context --current --json` prints exactly the `xtrm.runtime-origin.v1` object from gaps doc 12.2: schema_version, kind, host_id, tmux_session_id/window_id/pane_id, agent_instance_id, bead_id, parent_session_id, captured_at_ms, capture_source='xtmux-context', verified. It resolves the invoking pane via -t "$TMUX_PANE", requires both TMUX and TMUX_PANE, exits non-zero with a structured error outside tmux or when the pane cannot be verified, and never lazily creates an agent instance.

## SCOPE

bin/tmux-session-picker (command dispatch + help), src/cli.ts, new src/domains/identity/runtime-context.ts, docs (command reference), test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Writing any state. The command is strictly read-only.
- tmux_server_id (emit only if trivially derivable; optional in v1).
- Any Specialists-side capture/propagation code.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Field names and schema_version are normative — Specialists validates them. Do not rename or reshape.
- Resolve with `-t "$TMUX_PANE"`; use tmux formats #{session_id}/#{window_id}/#{pane_id}. NEVER #S or window/pane indexes.
- Must never select a bystander tmux server: no TMUX env -> structured error, no fallback to a default socket.
- verified=true only when the pane was resolved against the live tmux socket at capture time.
- Absent optional fields serialize as absent/null, never fabricated.
- No human decoration in --json mode; no secrets or env dump.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: inside a real tmux pane, output validates against the 12.2 schema field-for-field, with $/@/% shaped ids.
- [ ] Contract test: outside tmux (TMUX unset) -> non-zero exit + structured JSON error, nothing on stdout.
- [ ] Contract test: TMUX set but TMUX_PANE dead/stale -> non-zero, no fabricated ids.
- [ ] Contract test: pane with no @agent_instance_id -> field absent/null, verified still true (pane-level precision).
- [ ] Contract test: command performs no writes (no new agent instance row, no pane option set).
- [ ] Output contains no environment variables, prompts, or command text.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, a real sample JSON payload, and an explicit "cross-repo interface is live on main" note for the Specialists epic.
notes:
MERGED to main as 009901a (PR #25). Contract tests 196 pass / 0 fail; tsc clean.

Files: src/domains/identity/runtime-context.ts (new), src/cli.ts (context case, opens no DB), bin/tmux-session-picker (context dispatch + json allowlist + V2-gate exemption + help), docs/json-command-api.md (both surfaces registered), test/contract.sh (+8).

Live payload from a real pane:
{"schema_version":"xtrm.runtime-origin.v1","kind":"xtmux.agent_instance","host_id":"09d02b30-...","tmux_session_id":"$1732","tmux_window_id":"@1733","tmux_pane_id":"%2423","captured_at_ms":...,"capture_source":"xtmux-context","verified":true}

THREE DESIGN CALLS worth remembering:
1. Both TMUX and TMUX_PANE required. TMUX_PANE alone lets tmux resolve -t %17 against a default server; a bystander server's %17 is a DIFFERENT pane, and binding a job to it is a fabricated verified:true lie Specialists persists forever.
2. Absent optional fields omitted, never "". Missing agent_instance_id = pane-level precision (honest); "" would look like a real binding.
3. context is EXEMPT from the --json V2-mode gate. XTMUX_OBS_V2 selects the observability STORE; context reads no store, only tmux + the host-id file. Left gated, an operator's XTMUX_OBS_V2=0 opt-out would silently break the job->pane binding with no visible error. This was caught by the contract tests, which export XTMUX_OBS_V2=0.

DEPLOY GAP (filed as xtmux-hbm): the command is on main but NOT in the installed binary. ~/.local/bin/xtmux symlinks into npm @jaggerxtrm/xtmux@0.1.0, which predates it. Installed Specialists gets XTMUX_JSON_UNSUPPORTED -> no binding. A release must be cut before real consumers see the contract.

title: Persist host_id and rotate @agent_instance_id per agent occupation
description:
## PROBLEM

Nothing in xtmux identifies "one agent occupation of a pane". A reused pane inherits the previous occupant's links, and no stable, non-sensitive host identifier namespaces tmux ids across machines. Both are prerequisites for the runtime-origin DTO Specialists needs (gaps doc 12.1, 12.3).

## SUCCESS

A UUID host_id is generated once and persisted in the xtmux state dir, reused across restarts, and available to every command. `scripts/agent-state.sh <state> --new-instance` writes a fresh UUID into the pane option `@agent_instance_id` before emitting the state event; ordinary transitions preserve it. Pi calls the new-instance path on session_start; Claude on SessionStart. Missing UUID tooling never fails an agent turn.

## SCOPE

scripts/agent-state.sh, extensions/pi-agent-state.ts, Claude hook wiring (.claude settings/examples in examples/ + docs), new src/domains/identity/ (host id read/write), src/db or state-dir helper for persistence, docs/agent-state-hooks.md.

## NON_GOALS

- The `xtmux context --current --json` command itself (child .2).
- tmux_server_id (optional, deferred; host_id + agent_instance_id is the required matching key).
- Emitting agent.ready (child .7).

## CONSTRAINTS

- host_id must be a generated UUID persisted under the normal xtmux state dir; NEVER derived from /etc/machine-id or any other machine fingerprint.
- `--new-instance` only on session start, never on every idle transition.
- UUID source order: /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid -> uuidgen -> Bun helper; a tested fallback must exist. Absence of all three degrades gracefully (no instance id) and must not fail the hook.
- `off` leaves the last instance id in place for post-mortem; the next --new-instance overwrites.
- Hooks stay best-effort and latency-bounded; existing agent-state.sh CLI stays backward compatible (no required new args).
- Emit the identity on the existing event envelope (agent_instance_id column/field), not a new event stream.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] test/contract.sh: host_id persists identically across two separate command invocations.
- [ ] Contract test: `agent-state.sh idle --new-instance` sets a new @agent_instance_id; a following `agent-state.sh working` preserves it.
- [ ] Contract test: two consecutive --new-instance calls in the same pane yield different ids.
- [ ] Contract test: with all UUID sources stubbed unavailable, agent-state.sh still exits 0.
- [ ] Existing agent-state hook goldens unchanged.
- [ ] `xtmux log query --type agent.state --limit 5` shows agent_instance_id populated on new transitions.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, a sample event row showing host_id + agent_instance_id, and the state-dir path where host_id lives.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED. Files: scripts/agent-state.sh (arg loop now accepts --new-instance; gen_uuid with /proc -> uuidgen -> composite fallback; host_id() persists a UUID at ${XDG_STATE_HOME}/xtmux/host-id via noclobber-atomic create; agent.state event now carries host_id + agent_instance_id), src/domains/identity/host-id.ts (same file, same semantics, wx-atomic — the CLI and the hooks must never disagree about host identity; j46.2 reuses this), extensions/pi-agent-state.ts (setState(state, newInstance); session_start passes --new-instance and bypasses the debounce), examples/claude/settings.agent-state.json (SessionStart -> 'idle --new-instance'), test/contract.sh (+9 identity assertions on an isolated tmux socket + throwaway XDG_STATE_HOME).

EVIDENCE: bash test/contract.sh -> 188 pass, 0 fail. New: uuid-shaped instance id on --new-instance; host_id uuid-shaped, stable across invocations, asserted NOT equal to /etc/machine-id; ordinary transitions preserve the id; off preserves it (post-mortem attribution); a reused pane gets a fresh id; the event carries host_id + agent_instance_id; no env leak in the event.

RESIDUAL RISK: the third gen_uuid rung (composite from date/RANDOM/pid) is not exercised by the suite — /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid always wins on Linux and stubbing it would only test a copy of the formula (tautological). Left to xtmux-j46.12 to cover on a non-Linux runner if we ever have one.

title: xtmux runtime contracts for Console + Specialists integration
description:
## PROBLEM

docs/xtmux-gaps.md specifies the contracts a graphical Console/Electron viewer and the Specialists repo need from xtmux. The SQLite V2 store already holds the data (messages, receipts, agent instances, turns, monitors, handoffs, telemetry, audit), but there is no stable read contract on top of it: no complete topology snapshot, no durable journal cursor, no stable agent-instance identity, no readiness signal, and no bounded remote transport. Specialists cannot record "job J was spawned by runtime origin R" without a verified origin DTO from xtmux.

## SUCCESS

xtmux exposes: a persistent host_id; `xtmux topology --json` (host -> session -> window -> pane with stable ids and full agent metadata); `xtmux pane capture --json`; a per-agent-occupation `@agent_instance_id`; `xtmux context --current --json` emitting `xtrm.runtime-origin.v1`; `log query --after-id` cursor pagination with watermarks and cursor-expiry; an `agent.ready` handshake distinct from idle; existing-prompt-file handoff with readiness wait + monitor; and a read-only `xtmux bridge --stdio` NDJSON protocol. Specialists (separate repo, separate epic) consumes `xtmux context --current --json` unchanged.

## SCOPE

bin/tmux-session-picker (CLI dispatch, dashboard, handoff, log), src/cli.ts, src/domains/{events,agents,handoffs,monitors}, src/db/{journal.ts,migrations}, new src/domains/identity/, scripts/agent-state.sh, extensions/pi-agent-state.ts, .claude hook examples, docs/, test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Any change inside xtrm-dev/specialists (owned by the peer session's epic).
- Console/Electron implementation.
- Storing Specialists job/chain/evidence state in the xtmux DB as authoritative data.
- A new daemon, a second event schema, or a second database.
- Mutating bridge methods (pane.input, message.send, ...) — deferred behind a separate review.
- Reopening JSONL-era problems already solved by SQLite V2.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Contract is docs/xtmux-gaps.md sections 5-12, 17, 18. Field names and schema_version strings are normative — Specialists parses them.
- Identity is tmux stable ids only ($N, @N, %N). Names and indexes are display metadata.
- host_id is a generated UUID persisted in xtmux state; never derive it from /etc/machine-id.
- JSON output is presentation-free, backward compatible within v1, missing optional fields serialize absent/null, never fabricated.
- No secrets, prompts, terminal content, or env dumps in any JSON contract.
- MERGE SEQUENCING: other worktrees are active in this repo. Children merge in order .1 -> .2 -> .3/.4 -> .5 -> .6 -> .7 -> .8 -> .9; rebase on main before each PR. The peer Specialists epic hard-blocks on .2 being merged and released.
- Events use the existing event_journal envelope; no parallel event family.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] test/contract.sh green for every new JSON contract (topology, context, journal page, pane capture, bridge handshake).
- [ ] `xtmux context --current --json` validated against xtrm.runtime-origin.v1 field-by-field.
- [ ] Journal cursor: exclusive --after-id, strict id ordering, no duplicates, structured cursor-expiry.
- [ ] agent.ready emitted exactly once per agent_instance_id; not re-emitted on idle.
- [ ] Bridge rejects every mutation in read-only mode and survives malformed frames.
- [ ] Existing agent-state hooks and existing JSON consumers remain backward compatible.
- [ ] xtmux log query --type <new event types> shows the new event families with correct identity fields.

## OUTPUT

Merged PRs A-D, contract-test evidence per child, and a cross-repo handoff note confirming `xtmux context --current --json` is live on main for the Specialists epic to consume.

## REFERENCES

- docs/xtmux-gaps.md (this worktree)
- Peer epic: xtrm-dev/specialists (PR E/F — runtime-origin capture + descendant lineage)

All children closed. xtmux runtime contracts for Console + Specialists shipped to main (green) across PRs #25-#41: identity/host-id, context/runtime-origin (xtrm.runtime-origin.v1), topology --json, pane capture, journal cursor + follow, agent.ready + durable agent domain, readiness-aware handoff, read-only ssh bridge (security-reviewed twice, 5 findings fixed), activity spans, plus full contract/unit test coverage (every new assertion mutation-verified to fail) and docs (help, json-command-api.md, bridge.md, agent-state-hooks.md, CHANGELOG). .18 resolved via source-linked install mode (operator decision); fresh-npm publish deferred to standalone backlog bead xtmux-ro1. .23 skill callouts applied to installed ~/.xtrm copies; canonical core edit + release tracked in core bead xtrm-dhvqz. title: explorer: audit current marker directories, migrations, and Pi/Claude coordination flows
description:
PROBLEM: The xtmux-3ua ADR needs an evidence-backed snapshot of what SQLite already owns and what the three marker directories (xtmux-reply-obligations, xtmux-outbound-expectations, xtmux-auto-monitor) actually encode today, before we can design the SSOT state machines. Without this map the ADR would guess at legacy semantics and produce an incompatible migration.

SUCCESS: One concise findings report cites: (a) exact schema shape of messages/message_receipts/monitors after migrations 0002/0003/0009, including which columns are unused/underused for reply and outbound-wake semantics; (b) every write, read, delete, and TTL rule on each of the three marker directories, cited to file:line in extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts, extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts, and the auto-monitor hooks under hooks/claude/ (both .sh and .mjs where present); (c) the current Claude Stop-hook obligation-drain flow (auto-monitor-on-send / auto-monitor-consumed / auto-monitor-drain-stop) plus its env-toggle XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_*; (d) the current safe-send-pointer / message-send handshake for reply obligations; (e) the current outbound wait/expectation flow (xtmux wait-agent, monitor-agent, pi outbound-expectations); (f) at least one worked example of each edge case named in bead xtmux-3ua.1 CONSTRAINTS (send→ack→reply, reply→late ack, duplicate ack, duplicate reply, invalid correlation, cross-recipient, cancellation/retention, monitor arm/terminal/wake/replay, safe-send injection).

SCRUTINY: high

SCOPE:
- Migrations under src/db/migrations/ (specifically 0002_*, 0003_*, 0009_* plus any 0011+ that touches messages/receipts/monitors).
- src/db/ schema helpers, src/domains/messages/*, src/domains/monitors/*.
- src/cli.ts / src/cli-*.ts message-send, message-list, unread-count, wait-agent, monitor-agent handlers.
- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts and extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts.
- extensions/coordination-json.ts.

- .claude/settings.json xtmux-auto-monitor hook triples.

NON_GOALS:
- No design of the target state machine (that is xtmux-3ua.1.2's job).
- No production code edits, migrations, or hook edits.
- No changes to specialists/beads workflows.
- No broader tmux/transport redesign.

CONSTRAINTS:
- READ_ONLY. Cite every claim to file:line.
- If a marker directory is created by more than one code path, name each one.
- For every column that IS present but underused for reply-obligation or outbound-wake semantics, say so explicitly — the ADR must know what capacity already exists in the schema.
- Note anything discovered that would make one of the ADR's declared transitions impossible without a schema change (this is the highest-value output).
- Do not stop at file listing; produce a semantic summary per marker directory: who creates, who reads, who deletes, when TTL prunes, what a duplicate write means today, what a stale marker means today.

VALIDATION:
- Every entity name (table, column, hook, env var, marker file) traces back to a cited file:line.

- The report lists at least one open question the ADR needs to close.

OUTPUT: A structured findings report with sections: (1) current SQLite reply/monitor schema surface, (2) marker directory: xtmux-reply-obligations, (3) marker directory: xtmux-outbound-expectations, (4) marker directory: xtmux-auto-monitor, (5) end-to-end walkthroughs of the six edge cases, (6) open questions and gaps that the design pass must resolve, (7) recommended next-step for the overthinker design bead.

title: Review: coordination trust boundary, migration safety, and release evidence
description:
## PROBLEM

This refactor changes a CRITICAL message-send path and introduces authorization-sensitive correlation between messages plus durable cross-process wake state. Green functional tests alone may miss a sender/recipient spoof, cross-pane discharge, retention data loss, migration replay, or docs/skills contract that teaches an unsafe bypass.

## SUCCESS

An adversarial final gate independently reviews the merged diff and E2E evidence for trust-boundary correctness, migration/retention safety, concurrency/idempotency, redaction, backward compatibility, generated/package drift, and operator-contract accuracy. Any P0/P1 finding is fixed and revalidated before epic closure.

## SCOPE

Review all implementation children `xtmux-3ua.2`–`.10`, test evidence from `.5` and `.11`, GitNexus affected flows, SQLite migrations/queries, CLI validation, Pi/Claude adapters, installer/build artifact, docs, and canonical skill updates. Use reviewer, security-auditor, code-sanity, and obligations-scanner gates as appropriate.

## NON_GOALS

- No unrelated architecture redesign or style cleanup.
- No acceptance based only on author assertions or typecheck output.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Treat message summaries, marker files during import, CLI identity flags, and tmux pane/session input as untrusted.
- Verify authorization at the DB/domain boundary, not only shell parsing.
- Require evidence for concurrent/idempotent behavior and crash replay.
- Inspect structured journal fields and fixtures for secret/private payload leakage.
- GitNexus compare/detect-changes and direct-caller review are mandatory because `sendMessage` impact is CRITICAL.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Completion is verified by the validation checklist below.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Reviewer maps every epic acceptance criterion to code/test/docs/skills evidence.
- [ ] Security review covers spoofed reply correlation, cross-pane/session access, malicious legacy files/symlinks, SQL parameters, and payload/log redaction.
- [ ] Code-sanity review finds no remaining dual state, dead marker code, speculative abstraction, or generated drift.
- [ ] Obligations review confirms ack/reply/wake semantics and no untracked P1 follow-up.
- [ ] GitNexus affected processes and all seven direct `sendMessage` callers are reconciled.
- [ ] Final verdict is PASS or PASS_WITH_NOTES with no unresolved P0/P1 finding; any fix reruns `.11` critical smoke.

## OUTPUT

Fixed-vocabulary final verdict, ranked findings with file/line and confidence, gate outputs, criterion-to-evidence matrix, fix/retest links, residual risks, and explicit release recommendation.
notes:

Independent cross-cut checks (evidence not derivable from any single-PR gate):

1. TRUST BOUNDARY. Per recall xtmux-3ua-cli-ownership: CLI operations derive requester identity from live TMUX+TMUX_PANE (not caller flags, not message metadata). safe-send-pointer fulfils reply obligation only after successful pane injection. Per epic CONSTRAINTS: acknowledgement is receipt-only; --in-reply-to REQUIRED for fulfilment (no free-text/target/bead heuristic). Postmerge worktree source (HEAD 8e406d4) grep for marker names returns ONE source file: src/migration/legacy-markers.ts (importer), plus bin/cli.js.map (sourcemap). No writers. Retention + orphan reporting land via migrations 0010/0011 per CHANGELOG lines 66-67. Backup pre-install-3ua10-20260716T100928Z retained.

3. CONCURRENCY/IDEMPOTENCY. Per .2.6/.2.10 executor + .2.9 security gates: sendMessage uses SQLite tx.immediate; SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED normalized to DbError(XTMUX_DB_BUSY); XTMUX_ALREADY_FULFILLED preserved on lock re-read; XTMUX_MESSAGE_KEY_CONFLICT contract stable. XTMUX_OBS_V2 parser accepts 0|shadow|1; shadow mode never mutates authoritative state (src/db/shadow.ts). No fallback path reintroduces marker readers/writers.

VERDICT: PASS. title: Replace Claude auto-monitor marker hooks with DB-backed gates
description:
## PROBLEM

Claude hooks use `xtmux-auto-monitor` files to remember sends that still need a native Monitor arm. TTL/reboot can lose that gate, manual deletion bypasses it, and it is disconnected from durable monitor/requester state.

## SUCCESS

Claude PostToolUse/Stop hooks query the same SQLite outbound-wait state as Pi, record/link native Monitor arms using the accepted CLI contract, and consume terminal/reply state without filesystem markers. Stop blocking remains loop-safe, fast on no-op paths, and produces exact actionable commands.

## NON_GOALS

- No Claude CLI installation/model selection changes (`xtmux-e88` owns launcher model behavior).
- No Pi extension, DB migration, docs, or skill edits.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve shell prefilter startup performance and Stop-hook loop guard.
- Broad Bash matching must not add a Bun/Node cold start on irrelevant commands.
- DB/CLI failure must produce a bounded, actionable diagnostic without permanently trapping Stop.
- `safe-send-pointer` and `message-send` follow the ADR's explicit expectation/correlation semantics.
- Structured journal evidence is authoritative; hooks must not write replacement state files.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [ ] Terminal/reply completion clears/consumes the correct requester state once.

title: Test: SQLite coordination and CLI contracts — migration + integration
description:
## PROBLEM

## SUCCESS

Migration, domain, raw CLI, and shell picker integration tests falsifiably prove the accepted reply and wake state machines, error contracts, concurrency, retention, restart, pane isolation, and structured journal evidence. This is the Phase 2 gate before runtime adapters switch away from files.

## SCOPE

Covers `xtmux-3ua.1` through `.4`. Extend focused tests under `tests/contracts/`, DB fixture/migration tests, differential raw/picker fixtures, and JSON smoke scripts. Use isolated real SQLite DBs and subprocess commands; mock only tmux identity where unavoidable.

- No assertion-free snapshots or tests that only restate production queries.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Every test owns a clean temp DB/runtime; deterministic IDs/times where needed.
- Include positive, negative, and concurrency paths. Validate structured events by querying the real journal.
- Test output/payload redaction; never persist secrets in fixtures.
- Test-runner contract: run focused Bun tests first, then `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, and `bash scripts/smoke-json-api.sh` with isolated env; classify product vs pre-existing/infrastructure failures.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Completion is verified by the validation checklist below.

## VALIDATION

title: ADR: define SQLite reply and outbound-wake state machines
description:
## PROBLEM

The current file markers conflate four different facts: receipt acknowledgement, reply owed, monitor must be armed, and terminal wake already delivered. Implementing a migration before fixing these semantics would simply move ambiguity into SQLite, especially for `safe-send-pointer`, duplicate replies, retention, and restart recovery.

## SUCCESS

A short accepted design defines authoritative entities, transitions, identities, CLI operations, error rules, retention, structured journal events, and one-time legacy import. It explicitly covers `message-send`, `safe-send-pointer`, Pi auto-monitor, Claude Stop-hook gating, and operator reply workflows so implementation children do not invent incompatible contracts.

## SCOPE

`docs/observability-redesign.md` decision section plus schema/API sketches for messages, reply correlation, outbound wait/monitor requester ownership, wake consumption, legacy marker reconciliation, retention, and JSON errors. Inspect migrations 0002/0003/0009 and current Pi/Claude marker flows.

## NON_GOALS

- No production code, migration, generated binary, or runtime hook edits.
- No broad transport or tmux addressing redesign.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Prefer the smallest relational model that represents all states without heuristic target/bead matching.
- Ack is receipt-only; fulfilment requires explicit correlation to the inbound key.
- Specify how `safe-send-pointer` participates: either a correlated durable envelope or a separate explicit fulfilment operation; silent heuristic clearing is forbidden.
- Define requester session/pane, monitor link, terminal wake delivery/consumption, crash replay, and retention.
- Define journal event names/fields and redaction: message/monitor/session/pane IDs and outcome are allowed; secrets and full payload text are not.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Transition tables cover send→ack→reply, reply→late ack, duplicates, invalid/cross-recipient correlation, cancellation/retention, monitor arm/terminal/wake/replay, and safe-send injection.
- [ ] Every legacy runtime marker maps to an import, safe discard, or explicitly documented non-goal.
- [ ] SQL/CLI sketches can support pane-scoped queries without extension file reads.
- [ ] Implementation, test, docs, and skill children acknowledge the decision.

## OUTPUT

Accepted ADR/state-machine notes with schema fields, indexes/constraints, command examples, JSON shapes/errors, telemetry contract, compatibility decision, and implementation mapping to children of `xtmux-3ua`.

## RATIONALE

The architecture already treats SQLite as authoritative for messages and monitors; defining one relational state machine before implementation prevents another dual projection and makes reply/wake recovery testable.

## ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED

- Keep runtime markers and patch late ack: rejected because files remain a second source of truth.
- Infer replies from target/bead/text: rejected because correlation is ambiguous and unsafe across panes.
- Put all state directly on message/monitor rows without a decision: rejected until safe-send, retention, and wake-consumption transitions are specified.

title: refactor(coordination): make SQLite the SSOT for reply obligations and monitor wakes
description:
## PROBLEM

xtmux currently splits coordination truth across SQLite and three runtime-marker directories: Pi reply obligations (`xtmux-reply-obligations`), Pi requester-to-monitor wake mappings (`xtmux-outbound-expectations`), and Claude monitor-arming gates (`xtmux-auto-monitor`). Messages, receipts, monitors, and event history already live in SQLite, but the marker state can disagree with them, disappears at TTL/reboot, and leaks into the public `obligations list` implementation. Smoke `xtmux-efp.2` demonstrated the disagreement: a delivered reply followed by a late ack recreated a stale file-backed obligation.

## SUCCESS

SQLite is the sole authoritative store for reply obligations, explicit reply correlation, outbound wait/monitor ownership, and wake consumption. Pi and Claude integrations query/mutate those contracts through stable CLI JSON; no coordination marker directories are created. Existing installations upgrade safely, user help and architecture docs describe the same semantics, operator skills teach the correlated-reply workflow, generated/package artifacts are rebuilt, and a fresh packed Claude↔Pi session smoke passes across restart boundaries.

## SCOPE

- Database migrations, retention, message and monitor domains under `src/db/` and `src/domains/`.
- Raw `xtmux-obs` and shell `xtmux` command parsing, JSON contracts, errors, and help in `src/cli*.ts` and `bin/tmux-session-picker`.
- Pi integrations in `extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts`, `extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts`, and coordination parsing.
- Claude hooks in `hooks/claude/auto-monitor-*` and installer deployment/upgrade behavior.
- Tests under `tests/contracts/`, `test/`, smoke scripts, packed installation, and fresh interactive session verification.
- User/reference docs, changelog, and canonical operator skills that teach messaging/ack/reply/monitor behavior.

## NON_GOALS

- No free-text or target/bead heuristic for deciding that one message fulfills another.
- No replacement of SQLite, tmux addressing, Beads ownership, or the message transport.
- No automatic prose generation or trust elevation from inbound message bodies.
- No unrelated tmux temporary payload files (for example handoff pointer content) migration.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Explicit user-visible correlation must identify the inbound message being answered; acknowledgement remains receipt-only.
- Preserve pane-scoped routing, idempotent message keys, existing message/receipt/monitor history, and safe concurrent SQLite access.
- Define safe retention and legacy-marker import/cleanup before implementation; upgrades must not silently resurrect or duplicate obligations.
- `message-send`, `safe-send-pointer`, Pi auto-monitor, and Claude Stop-hook workflows must share one documented state machine.
- Emit structured journal evidence for reply linking/fulfilment, monitor request/arming/terminal wake consumption, legacy import/cleanup, and validation failures. Include correlation/message/monitor/session/pane IDs and outcome; never log secrets or full unredacted payloads.
- Source help, generated binary/help, npm package contents, docs, and deployed canonical skill copies must not drift.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Pending and fulfilled obligations are derived only from SQLite and survive Pi/Claude reload plus process restart.
- [ ] Ack-before-reply, reply-before-late-ack, duplicate ack, duplicate reply, invalid correlation, and cross-pane isolation behave deterministically.
- [ ] Outbound waits record requester identity, monitor linkage, terminal state, and one-time wake consumption without runtime files.
- [ ] No `xtmux-reply-obligations`, `xtmux-outbound-expectations`, or `xtmux-auto-monitor` directory is created in a clean isolated runtime.
- [ ] Legacy valid markers are reconciled once; corrupt/stale/foreign files are handled safely with structured evidence.
- [ ] Raw and picker `--help`, JSON API docs, README/architecture/install/release docs, changelog, and operator skills agree on exact commands and semantics.
- [ ] Unit, migration, contract, shell, operational smoke, packed-install, and fresh Claude↔Pi E2E gates pass; test artifacts include journal queries proving the critical path.

## OUTPUT

A consolidated handoff listing schema/API decisions, all changed runtime/help/docs/skill surfaces, migration compatibility evidence, exact test and fresh-session smoke results, structured journal samples/queries, package artifact verification, and any residual compatibility risks.

## REFERENCES

- Root-cause smoke: `xtmux-efp`, especially `xtmux-efp.2`.
- Original narrow reproduction messages: inbound `msg-1783987714-1326589`, reply `msg-1783987744-1336791`.
- Existing architecture: migrations 0002/0003/0009, `extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts`, `extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts`, and `hooks/claude/auto-monitor-*`.

Reframed from the narrow late-ack marker bug after architecture review: the root cause is extension-owned runtime files acting as authoritative coordination state beside SQLite. Fix the model and correlation once rather than patching operation order.

Companion gates are .5 (migration/domain/raw+picker integration with journal assertions) and .11 (packed fresh Claude↔Pi E2E with restart/cleanup); .12 is adversarial reviewer/security/code-sanity release gate.    The first launcher attempt for this pane FAILED: the explorer role's default

   could not start. The relaunch with an explicit `--model opus` succeeded and is
   the session recorded above. Fresh-Claude hook install is therefore proven only
   via the explicit-model launch path; the explorer role default model needs a
   Claude-valid value (or a runtime-aware default) before `xt claude --role explorer`
   works unattended. Also noted: @agent_parent_session on %3204 is $1732 (the
   launching orchestrator session), not the paired Pi $2700 — did not affect the
   loop, which used explicit --to targeting.

No edits, commits, pushes, config changes, new issues, or closures were made.
