title: smoke gate is flaky: contract.sh rename + bead-derive tests are environment-sensitive on CI
description:
## PROBLEM

The required 'smoke' check (scripts/verify-json-api.sh -> test/contract.sh) failed on PR #9 and PASSED on a plain re-run of the identical commit. A required gate that flaps will randomly block merges.

Observed on the red run (job 86826864765):
- 3 'rename:' tests FAILED ('can't find window: xtmux-renamed-session', expected newwin / actual oldwin) — live-tmux races on the runner. These printed FAIL but were NOT counted in the tally (they run in a subshell, so nok()'s fail/failed increments are lost to the parent).
- The counted failures were 'bead derive: from path convention' and 'bead derive: avoids loose numeric slug' — for which NO FAIL line appears anywhere in the log. The tally and the printed failures disagree, so the harness is misreporting which test failed.

## ROOT CAUSE (partial, confirmed by reading the source)

refine_derived_bead_id (bin/tmux-session-picker:479) branches on 'command -v bd':
- bd present  -> validates the candidate against the beads DB via 'bd show', returns '' when absent
- bd absent   -> returns the candidate verbatim

So bead-derive outcomes depend on whether bd is installed. contract.sh guards SOME bead tests behind 'command -v bd' (lines 132, 139) but leaves lines 144-145 unguarded. Not reproducible locally in either configuration (with bd: 143 pass / 0 fail; without bd, no tmux server: 99 pass / 1 fail, the 1 being an unrelated tmux-layout test), which points at a third CI-only difference (HOME / beads DB / runner tmux).

## SUCCESS

- nok() inside subshells propagates to the tally, so the FAILED list names the tests that actually failed.
- rename tests are robust to (or skipped without) a live tmux server.
- bead-derive tests are guarded on bd presence like their neighbours, or made bd-independent.
- smoke passes deterministically on re-runs of the same commit.

## CONTEXT

Found while landing xtmux-d0a.14 (PR #9). Not caused by that PR: the failing tests run before its added section and touch none of its files. Re-run of the same commit went green and all 4 checks now pass.
notes:
PR #13 (xt/04vp-harness). All 4 checks green. FIXED — and it was worse than filed.

REPRODUCED BOTH DEFECTS AT ONCE (injected one subshell failure, OLD harness):
  printed FAIL: xtmux-monitor, INJECTED, rename x3  (5)
  tally:        1 fail
  FAILED list:  xtmux-monitor                       (1)
Four of five printed failures never reached the count; the list blamed one test and omitted the rest. Lost counts AND misattribution, demonstrated in one run.

ROOT CAUSE: pass/fail/failed were shell VARIABLES, so any result produced in a ( ... ) subshell died with it. The rename tests run in a subshell (they scope a tmux() override) => they could never fail the suite however loudly they failed.

FIX: test/lib/harness.sh — every result appended to ONE record file; tally, FAILED list and exit status all derived from that file. Subshell appends survive; printed/counted/blamed are the same records, so they cannot disagree by construction.

META-TEST (test/harness-selftest.sh, 5 assertions): fails a test INSIDE a subshell and asserts the suite exits non-zero, counts it, names exactly what printed FAIL; plus the inverse (an all-passing suite still exits 0, so the harness cannot just always fail). Wired into verify-json-api.sh BEFORE shell-contracts and into 'make test': a green contract run means nothing unless the harness under it can go red.

WHAT THE COUNTER WAS HIDING — TWO REAL BUGS:
1. 'rename' and 'rename-apply' NEVER EXISTED. The dispatcher and the Alt-R fzf binding call rename_target/rename_apply, defined in NO commit in history — both exited 127 'command not found'. The inline rename the README advertises has never worked, and its 3 contract tests failed on EVERY run (local and CI) while the suite exited 0. Implemented both to the contract the tests already specified.
2. xtmux-monitor built a 2-pane 'monitor'. tmux 3.5a performs a split into a clientless session but exits 1 ('no current client'); under set -e that killed the script after the FIRST split, silently. Older tmux exits 0 — which is why CI never saw it and every dev machine did. Splits now ignore that bogus status; the layout is VERIFIED by pane count.

So the 'flake' was never a flake: rename had been failing permanently and the counter hid it. The one thing I could NOT reproduce is the exact 'bead derive' naming on the red CI run — which is exactly the misattribution this PR makes impossible: the tally can no longer name a test that did not fail.

GATES: harness-selftest 5/0 / build / bun test 177/0 / typecheck clean / contract.sh 132 pass 0 fail (rename x3 + xtmux-monitor now genuinely pass) / verify-json-api PASS.
NEEDS_CHANGES addressed in 16e1921. PR #13 all 4 checks green, Codex thread replied + RESOLVED (required_conversation_resolution satisfied).

CODEX FINDING WAS MINE AND REAL — and worse than a truncation bug. In 'run-shell '$self rename-apply $type $handle "%1"'' the quotes around %1 never survive: the outer shell eats them, tmux gets a BARE %1, substitutes the typed text, and hands it to /bin/sh. 'new sprint board' stored 'new', and a name with ; or $( ) was EXECUTED. Verified end-to-end: the test renaming to 'evil; touch $WORK/pwned' ACTUALLY CREATED THE FILE against the old line. (Codex's read on kill-confirm is right: same %1 pattern is harmless there — y/N answer, word-splitting can't hurt.)

FIX IS NOT BETTER QUOTING. Single-quoting %1 for sh only moves the hole — an apostrophe in the name reopens it. The typed name now never reaches a shell: rename_prompt_command builds a NATIVE tmux command (rename-session/rename-window) with %1 quoted at the TMUX parse level. tmux does no command substitution => metacharacters are inert text; a typed apostrophe makes tmux fail to PARSE (renames nothing, executes nothing) — safe failure, not executed one.

TESTS WITH TEETH (3 new): split the template out of rename_target so it is testable without an attached client, then reproduce tmux's real pipeline — substitute %1, then let TMUX'S OWN PARSER run it via source-file. (a) spaces survive whole, (b) 'evil; touch pwned' creates no file, (c) metacharacters stored literally. All three FAIL against the old line, pass now. My own harness fix is what makes them enforceable: they live in the rename subshell, which until this PR could not fail the suite.

TRAP recorded: the test first substituted with ${tpl//%1/$name}; bash 5.2 expands & in a replacement to the MATCHED TEXT, so a name containing && came back as %1%1 and the test failed for a reason unrelated to the code. Now splices literally.

GATES: harness-selftest 5/0 / build / bun test 177/0 / typecheck clean / contract.sh 135 pass 0 fail / verify-json-api PASS.
close_reason: PR #13 merged (e19886b). Two fixes: (1) harness counters moved from shell vars to a file so subshell failures cannot be swallowed, with test/harness-selftest.sh proving it (5/0, incl. 'FAILED list == tests that printed FAIL — no phantoms, no omissions'); (2) the failure the lying gate was HIDING: tmux split-window into a clientless session exits 1 while creating the pane, killing xtmux-monitor.sh mid-layout under set -e — green on CI (older tmux), red on every dev machine. Now an outcome check on pane count. Verified independently from inside tmux: verify-json-api.sh PASS on the branch where main is RED; sabotaged layout correctly exits 1 with 'expected 3 panes, got 1'.

title: install.sh never links ~/.local/bin/xtmux-obs — fresh installs silently lose the V2 backend
description:
## PROBLEM

install.sh links tmux-session-picker, xtmux (d0a.14), xtmux-monitor, git-pane-status.sh and agent-state.sh — but NOT xtmux-obs.

The picker derives root as ${self%/bin/*} without resolving symlinks. Invoked via ~/.local/bin/<entry>, root = ~/.local, so it looks for the compiled V2 backend at ~/.local/bin/xtmux-obs. On this machine that symlink exists only because someone created it by hand (mtime 13 Jul 02:13); nothing in the repo creates it.

On a FRESH install.sh run the file is absent, so obs_available() falls through to `bun run $root/src/cli.ts` = ~/.local/src/cli.ts, which does not exist. The V2 observability backend is then silently unavailable — every --json command returns XTMUX_JSON_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE, with no error at install time.

Found while validating d0a.14. The alias itself is unaffected (root resolution is byte-identical to tmux-session-picker); this is a pre-existing bug on the symlink-install path.

## SUCCESS

A fresh clone + ./install.sh yields a working V2 backend, or fails loudly at install time.

## CONSTRAINTS

bin/xtmux-obs is a gitignored ~100MB compiled artifact produced by `bun run build`. install.sh must not assume it exists — guard the link (e.g. link when present, otherwise warn 'run bun run build first').
close_reason: Already fixed by PR #9 (xtmux-d0a.14): install.sh now builds bin/xtmux-obs if absent (or fails loudly with the exact command) and links it to ~/.local/bin/xtmux-obs, with a contract test that runs the REAL install.sh under a fresh HOME and asserts it reaches a non-stub V2 backend. Filed by the worker mid-flight; the fix landed in the same PR.

title: safe-send-pointer: Claude-pane detection fails when pane_current_command is 'node' — first Enter silently swallowed
description:
## PROBLEM

`safe-send-pointer` applies its auto-double-Enter safety default only when the target pane's
`pane_current_command` is `claude` or matches `claude-*`. Claude Code panes launched via
`xt claude` report `pane_current_command=node` — the Node binary, not a `claude`-named process.

Detection therefore misses, `double_enter=0`, and Claude Code's paste-detection heuristic eats
the single Enter. The pointer text lands in the input box and is NEVER SUBMITTED. The pane sits
at `needs-input` looking idle, and the orchestrator believes the instruction was delivered.

Reproduced twice on 2026-07-13 against pane %2635 (Claude Code, `xt claude` worktree
xt/04vp, footer confirms "Claude Code"):

    sent target=%2635 pane=%2635 state=needs-input double_enter=0
    → pane still needs-input 6s later; manual `tmux send-keys -t %2635 Enter` required

This is a SILENT delivery failure in the multiplexing safety wrapper — the exact failure mode
the wrapper exists to prevent. An orchestrator that trusts the `sent` line will wait forever on
a worker that never received its task.

## SUCCESS

`safe-send-pointer` reliably identifies Claude Code panes regardless of how the process presents
in `pane_current_command`, and either applies double-Enter or reports honestly that it could not
determine the harness. No silent non-delivery.

## SCOPE

- `bin/tmux-session-picker`, `safe_send_pointer` — the `pane_current_command` probe and the
  `double_enter` decision.

## NON_GOALS

- Changing the pointer-payload safety checks (multiline, shell-substitution, working-target
  refusal). Those work; only harness detection is broken.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Do NOT simply always-double-Enter: pi and Codex panes submit on the first Enter, so a second
  would inject a stray newline into the next prompt.
- Detection must survive `xt claude`-launched panes (command reads `node`). Candidate signals,
  in preference order: the `@agent_*` pane options xtmux already sets; the pane title (%2635
  reports "Claude Code"); the process COMMAND line (`node .../claude`), not just the basename.
- If the harness genuinely cannot be determined, say so in the output rather than defaulting to
  `double_enter=0` and reporting `sent`. Reporting success on a non-delivery is the bug.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Against a live `xt claude` pane (command=`node`), `safe-send-pointer` sets double_enter=1
      and the pointer is actually submitted — pane transitions out of `needs-input` with no
      manual Enter. Regression test must FAIL against today's basename-only probe.
- [ ] Against a pi pane, double_enter stays 0 and no stray newline is injected.
- [ ] `bash test/contract.sh` and `bash scripts/verify-json-api.sh` pass.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, the detection signal chosen and why, and the regression test demonstrating a
`node`-presenting Claude pane now receives its pointer.
close_reason: Fixed: pane_is_claude_code now falls back to a bounded process-subtree walk (pgrep -P + ps -o comm=, depth 3) when pane_current_command is inconclusive. 'xt claude' panes run a node wrapper so they reported 'node' and missed detection. Verified live end-to-end: safe-send-pointer to a real xt-claude pane now reports double_enter=1 (was 0), the pane received the pointer and replied, with ZERO manual Enter — the workaround I needed all session. Contract test reproduces the real shape (copy of sh named node spawning a copy of sleep named claude, asserts pane_current_command=node first so the test cannot be vacuous) and fails against the old detector. Non-claude panes stay negative: 'xt pi' panes correctly get double_enter=false.

title: Defect: retarget existing Pi extensions off command-regex onto --json
description:
## PROBLEM

The three existing Pi extensions infer coordination side effects by REGEX-MATCHING Bash command
text and results — stated in the PROBLEM sections of both xtmux-d0a.7 and .8 ("extensions detect
sends/acks by regex", "infer side effects by parsing Bash command text/results").

That coupling is fragile TODAY, independently of any native tool work. A quoting change, an
extra flag, or a reworded command silently stops a wake-up or an obligation record — and it
fails silently, which is the worst failure mode for a coordination bus.

The `--json` API (xtmux-d0a.1-.6) is merged and gives these extensions a stable, typed surface
to read instead of scraping command strings. The design consult (Claude pane) named this
explicitly: "if a bug exists, fix the bug. Retarget the existing pi extensions at --json. That
is a defect ticket, not an API epic."

## SUCCESS

`pi-agent-state.ts`, `pi-auto-monitor.ts` and `pi-inbox-reply.ts` determine sends, acks, monitor
arming and obligations from `--json` output (stable field names, exit codes) rather than from
regexes over command text. Behaviour is unchanged; the coupling is no longer string-shaped.
This lands and delivers value even if the native tool pilot (xtmux-d0a.8) is never built.

## SCOPE

- `extensions/pi-agent-state.ts`
- `extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts`
- `extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts`
- `.xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs` — the Claude-side counterpart; check whether it shares
  the same regex coupling and fix it in the same pass if so. The root-cause fix belongs wherever
  all callers route through, not only in the path the ticket names.

## NON_GOALS

- Building native Pi tools. This bead is deliberately the CHEAP alternative to that epic, and
  its whole point is that it is independent of it.
- Adding a second event bridge. Both consult panes rejected that: the existing CLI events remain
  authoritative.
- Changing any observable behaviour. This is a coupling fix, not a feature.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve exit-code semantics, including 75 and 124 (per the Pi consult's drift-control list).
- Extensions must call the CLI (`pi.exec`) and read its `--json`; they must NOT reach into
  SQLite or domain code directly.
- The existing tmux `has-session` precheck and SKIP_TARGETS bypass behaviour (xtmux-3xs.23/.29/
  .30, covered by contract tests) must be preserved exactly.
- Fail loudly on malformed JSON or an incompatible CLI version. Silent degradation is the bug
  being fixed; reintroducing it in a new form is a regression.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bash test/contract.sh` passes, INCLUDING the auto-monitor .23/.29/.30 contracts, which
      only run where `bd` is on PATH (they are skipped on CI — run them locally, on purpose).
- [ ] `bash scripts/smoke-json-api.sh` passes (CI `smoke` gate green).
- [ ] A regression test proves the failure mode: a send whose command TEXT is reworded (extra
      flag / different quoting) still triggers the wake / obligation record. Under the old regex
      coupling this test must fail; that is the proof the defect was real.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` clean — note this only means anything after xtmux-d0a.13 puts
      `extensions/**` inside tsconfig. Today it passes vacuously.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, the regression test that fails before and passes after, contract + smoke output,
and a statement of which regexes were removed and what replaced them.
notes:
Implemented regex-decoupling with red/green proof. RED: reworded send command + stable JSON output failed under old command regex (pi-auto-monitor test ENOENT/no monitor call). GREEN: side effects now discriminate message-send/message-ack/safe-send-pointer JSON fields; monitor-list/monitor-agent use --json; Pi extension subprocesses use pi.exec; Claude hook reads tool_response JSON. Removed extractTarget/commandAction and all message/monitor/send-keys regexes from affected extension/hook. pi-agent-state audited: it had no command regex and already calls CLI directly, so unchanged. Preserved SKIP_TARGETS and tmux has-session precheck. Malformed/incompatible JSON throws loudly. Gates PASS: bun run build; bun test; bun run typecheck; local bash test/contract.sh including .23/.29/.30; bash scripts/verify-json-api.sh. GitNexus post-change risk HIGH because 8 inbox refresh/obligation flows are touched; all are covered by focused/full/contracts/live smoke.
PR #12 opened at commit 0acd560; branch xt/nap1 recreated after merged PR #8 branch deletion. Do not merge/close pending review. All mandated local gates pass.
PR #12 CI PASS at 0acd560: test 20s, smoke 27s, analyze 1m11s, CodeQL 2s. No review threads currently present. PR remains open/unmerged; bead remains open for orchestrator verification.
MERGED: PR #12 -> 6f20973. Coordination effects now derive from --json RESULTS (messageKey/recipientId), not from regexes over Bash command text. Root-caused across ALL callers, not just the ticketed path: pi-auto-monitor.ts + pi-inbox-reply.ts + the Claude-side .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs, sharing extensions/coordination-json.ts. Regression test has teeth: it sends a command whose literal text is 'reworded send' — matching no regex — and asserts the wake/pending still fires. That test fails against the old coupling. No SQLite access introduced; CLI --json remains the sole source.
close_reason: Merged PR #12 (6f20973). Regex coupling removed on both pi and Claude sides; regression test proves it.

title: Structured 'xtmux help' surface, including --json output field docs
description:
## PROBLEM

xtmux has no usable discovery surface. `help` / `--help` emit ONE unbroken ~1,500-character
usage line covering ~40 subcommands. Compare the sibling tools an agent already primes with:
`bd --help` 148 lines, `sp --help` 154, `xt --help` 53 — all grouped and scannable. A separate
`mux-help` exists (36 lines) but documents the delegation PROTOCOL, not the command reference.

This is not cosmetic. In the design consult, Pi listed five retries it hit while using the CLI;
TWO are pure discoverability failures that a real help surface would have prevented:

1. Called `message-list --json` without the required `--for` -> exit 2, retry. (`--for` IS in
   the usage blob — unreadable, so it was missed.)
2. Guessed JSON output fields (`id`, `text`) instead of the real ones (`messageKey`, `summary`)
   -> silent nulls, retry. **The output field names are documented NOWHERE** — not in the usage
   blob, not in `mux-help`. The orchestrator hit this same bug an hour later.

Undocumented --json output shapes are the sharper half of the bug: a wrong input arg fails
loudly (exit 2); a wrong output field returns `null` silently.

## SUCCESS

An agent that runs `xtmux help` at session start can call any command correctly on the first
attempt — required args are visible, and `--json` output field names are documented. The two
discoverability retry classes above become unreachable. Works for EVERY harness (Claude, pi,
codex, shell) with no per-harness dialect.

## SCOPE

- `bin/tmux-session-picker`: the `usage` string and the `help`/`--help` routing; `mux-help`
  (kept, protocol-only, cross-referenced).
- `docs/json-command-api.md` — already documents the `--json` API; the help surface must not
  fork from it. Prefer generating or cross-referencing over duplicating.
- `~/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md` — add the session-start `xtmux help` step,
  mirroring how the skill already primes `bd`. NOTE: that file is an xtrm-MANAGED asset; its
  source of truth is `~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md`. Edit at the
  source or `xt update --apply` will overwrite it.

## NON_GOALS

- Renaming any subcommand (see xtmux-d0a.14 NON_GOALS).
- Native Pi tools. This bead deliberately lands BEFORE any tool work.
- Rewriting the 647-line multiplexing skill. Only the session-start priming step is added here.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Group by domain (messages / monitors / sessions / dashboard / observability / hygiene), the
  same grouping the tool pilot would use — so the help doubles as the tool-surface spec.
- Document `--json` OUTPUT fields per command, not just input flags. This is the undocumented
  half and the reason the bead exists. `messageKey` / `summary` are the known trap.
- Mark required args unambiguously (`message-list --for <target>` is required, not optional).
- Use the canonical `xtmux` prefix in all examples (depends on xtmux-d0a.14).
- Single source of truth: help output and `docs/json-command-api.md` must not be able to drift.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xtmux help` is grouped, scannable, and in the 50-160 line band of `bd`/`sp`/`xt`.
- [ ] For every command with `--json`, the output field names appear in help or in a doc it
      points at. Assert specifically that `messageKey` and `summary` are discoverable.
- [ ] Every required argument is marked required. Assert `message-list --for` explicitly.
- [ ] `mux-help` still works and is cross-referenced from `help`.
- [ ] `bash scripts/smoke-json-api.sh` and `bash test/contract.sh` pass.
- [ ] A contract test asserts help stays in sync with the actual command list — help that rots
      is worse than no help.

## OUTPUT

The new help output, the drift-guard test, the diff to the multiplexing skill (at its ~/dev/core
source), and confirmation that the two Pi retry classes are now answerable from `xtmux help`
alone.
notes:
PR #11 (branch xt/04vp-help, based on main after #9 merged). All 4 checks green. No Codex thread yet.

HELP: 112 lines (bd/sp/xt band 53-154), grouped messages/monitors/delegation/sessions+dashboard/observability/hygiene — the grouping a tool surface would use, so help doubles as the tool spec. Required args marked REQUIRED. Per-command --json OUTPUT field names. Message block names the trap outright: body is 'summary', id is 'messageKey', there is NO 'text' and NO 'id' field. Also warns on '$1732' quoting (unquoted => empty => acts under WRONG identity). mux-help untouched, cross-referenced both ways. Unknown command now points at 'xtmux help' instead of dumping the blob. help/--help/-h registered in the picker dispatcher matrix (the existing bun test caught them immediately — good mechanism already in place).

DRIFT GUARD (14 new contract tests) — nothing trusts the help text:
- command list checked BOTH ways vs the real dispatch table (no undocumented command; no phantom command). The help FORMAT is the contract: a command is the first word of a 2-space-indented line.
- documented --json fields checked against LIVE output, not against a doc (a doc rots in lockstep with help).
- fields checked INSIDE the owning command's block: grepping whole-help let messageKey survive elsewhere and mask its removal from the message block — a FALSE PASS I hit and closed. Same class as the .14 stub bug: an assertion that cannot see the thing it is asserting.
- help vs docs/json-command-api.md stable Message fields, so the two cannot fork.
Verified by INJECTING both drifts: undocumented dispatch command fails; stale field name fails.

GATES: build / bun test 177 pass 0 fail / typecheck clean / contract.sh 163 pass 0 fail / verify-json-api.sh PASS.
(bun test failed 2 initially: one was my stale node_modules — 'bun install' fixed it, pi binary was absent; the other was the new help arm tripping the existing matrix test, fixed by registering it in the doc.)

SKILL STEP NOT APPLIED — ROUTED: source of truth is ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md, a separate repo, currently DIRTY with another session's changes, outside my worktree. Exact patch written to /tmp/xtmux-d0a15-multiplexing-skill.patch for the orchestrator to route (adds a 'Session start — prime the command surface' section: 'xtmux help' alongside 'bd prime', naming both retry classes).

FOUND NOT FIXED: xtmux-d0a.21 — monitor-list crashes with raw SQLiteError (no such table: monitors) on a fresh obs DB while unread-count works. Violates the documented --json error contract. Same family as the .14 finding: paths that only worked because an existing machine had state a fresh install lacks.
MERGED: PR #11 -> ad304ee. The 1,500-char usage blob is gone; help is 112 grouped lines (bd=148/sp=154/xt=53 band). Documents --json OUTPUT fields per command, and closes THREE of pi's five consult retries, not two: (#1) 'message-list --for is REQUIRED. Without it: exit 2'; (#3) explicit TRAP block — 'the message body is summary and its id is messageKey. There is no text field and no id field — reading those yields null'; (#5) 'Quote pane/session ids in shells: $1732 unquoted expands to nothing, which silently sends or reads under the WRONG identity'. Drift guard: contract test asserts help documents EVERY dispatch command, so an undocumented new command fails CI.
close_reason: Merged PR #11 (ad304ee). Real help surface; closes 3 of pi's 5 retries harness-neutrally; drift-guarded.

title: Expose canonical 'xtmux' command prefix via alias
description:
## PROBLEM

The agent-facing binary is named `tmux-session-picker` — a legacy name that predates the
project being called xtmux. Every skill, hook and doc reads `tmux-session-picker message-send`,
which is verbose and does not match the product. `xtmux` is free as a command name. A full
rename is not viable: 1,888 occurrences across 224 files in this repo, 85 in the global skills,
and ~1,400 across 153 files in OTHER repos under ~/dev — plus live tmux panes and hooks that
invoke the old name at runtime.

## SUCCESS

`xtmux <subcommand>` works identically to `tmux-session-picker <subcommand>` from any harness.
The old name keeps working indefinitely — no call site anywhere is broken. New docs, help output,
and skills can standardise on `xtmux` and migrate the old name by attrition.

## SCOPE

- Install path: an `xtmux` entry alongside the existing `~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker`
  symlink (which points at `bin/tmux-session-picker`).
- `bin/tmux-session-picker` `install-hooks` subcommand, if it is what creates the symlink.
- Self-referential output: `$self` (bin/tmux-session-picker:14) is used to re-invoke the script
  (monitor-run, tmux `run-shell`, fzf `--bind` transforms, and the command line printed by
  `safe-send-pointer`). Invoked as `xtmux`, those printed/re-invoked commands become `xtmux …`.

## NON_GOALS

- Renaming subcommands. `message-send` -> `send-message` etc. is explicitly OUT: it fixes none
  of the five retry classes observed in the Pi consult and costs ~3,300 call sites.
- Renaming or removing `tmux-session-picker`. It stays, forever, as the compatibility name.
- Touching the `xtmux-obs` binary name.

## CONSTRAINTS

- `root` is derived as `${self%/bin/*}` (bin/tmux-session-picker:727,737) — it does NOT resolve
  symlinks. The alias MUST therefore live in the same directory as the existing symlink
  (`~/.local/bin/`), where `~/.local/bin/xtmux-obs` already sits, so `root` resolution is
  byte-identical to today. An alias placed anywhere else silently breaks the V2 obs backend
  (it would fall back to `bun run $root/src/cli.ts` against a nonexistent path).
- Zero breaking changes. Any change that makes `tmux-session-picker …` stop working is a defect.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xtmux help` and `tmux-session-picker help` produce identical output.
- [ ] `xtmux log query --type query.completed --json` returns valid JSON — proves the V2 obs
      backend resolved through the alias (this is the `${self%/bin/*}` trap).
- [ ] `xtmux dashboard expanded --json` returns valid JSON.
- [ ] `bash scripts/smoke-json-api.sh` still passes (CI `smoke` gate stays green).
- [ ] `bash test/contract.sh` still passes.
- [ ] A monitor armed via `xtmux monitor-agent` self-re-invokes correctly (exercises `$self`).

## OUTPUT

Changed files, how the alias is installed (and whether `install-hooks` now creates it), and the
JSON output of the two validation commands above proving `root` still resolves.
notes:
PR #9 (branch xt/04vp). Alias = 2nd symlink to bin/tmux-session-picker, added to install.sh. ZERO changes to the picker script needed: $self is already absolute at every re-invocation site (monitor-run:2366, safe-send-pointer:2522, fzf binds:3300-3318, run-shell:2930/2949) and help hardcodes no name.

TRAP CLEARED: root=${self%/bin/*}, BASH_SOURCE does not resolve symlinks => root derives from the DIRECTORY THE ALIAS SITS IN, not its target. In ~/.local/bin it finds $root/bin/xtmux-obs. 3 new contract tests pin it, incl. a negative test proving a MISPLACED alias loses the backend (XTMUX_JSON_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE).

VALIDATION (live): xtmux log query --type query.completed --json => valid JSON (root resolved). xtmux dashboard expanded --json => valid JSON. Monitor armed via xtmux re-invokes as 'bash /home/dawid/.local/bin/xtmux monitor-run' => $self correct.

DEVIATION from VALIDATION line 1: help is identical EXCEPT the usage: line, which echoes $self (argv[0]) — i.e. the name you invoked. Making it byte-identical requires hardcoding a literal name, which would make 'tmux-session-picker help' print 'usage: xtmux' (behaviour change for every existing caller, violates zero-breaking-changes) or freeze the old name. Declined both; test asserts identity modulo argv[0]. .15 owns the help surface and can set a stable literal there if it wants one.

GATES: build (rebuilt, not stale) / bun test 176 pass / typecheck clean / contract.sh 143 pass 0 fail / verify-json-api.sh PASS.

FOLLOW-UP FILED (xtmux-d0a.18): install.sh never links ~/.local/bin/xtmux-obs — fresh installs silently lose the V2 backend. Pre-existing, independent of this alias.
CI: all 4 required checks GREEN on PR #9 (test, analyze, smoke, CodeQL).

smoke went red on the first run and PASSED on a plain re-run of the identical commit => runner flake, not this PR. Investigated rather than waved through: the red run's printed failures were 3 live-tmux 'rename:' races, while the counted failures were 2 'bead derive' tests that printed no FAIL line at all — the tally and the printed failures disagree, because nok() inside a subshell loses its increments. Also confirmed refine_derived_bead_id (picker:479) branches on 'command -v bd', so bead-derive results depend on bd presence, and contract.sh guards lines 132/139 on bd but NOT 144/145. Not reproducible locally in either config (bd present: 143/0; bd absent + no tmux server: 99/1, unrelated tmux-layout test). Filed as xtmux-d0a.19 (P1) — a required gate that flaps will randomly block merges.

Bead left OPEN and PR left UNMERGED per contract; orchestrator merges + closes on evidence.
NEEDS_CHANGES addressed in c3abd3f (pushed to xt/04vp). All 4 checks green again.

CODEX FINDING (install.sh) — real, and WORSE than filed: install.sh never linked bin/xtmux-obs for EITHER entrypoint. tmux-session-picker was equally broken on a fresh clone; it only ever worked because the symlink was hand-created. Fixed here (not deferred to d0a.18) because .14 makes xtmux canonical and puts weight on that path: install.sh now links bin/xtmux-obs, builds it via 'bun run build' when missing, and exits with the exact command when it cannot — no more silently-broken install.

THE TEST HOLE MATTERED MORE. My contract test stubbed xtmux-obs into the fake home => it proved root RESOLUTION but was structurally blind to the artifact being MISSING. A test that stubs the thing under test cannot see it absent. Added a section that runs the REAL install.sh into a throwaway HOME and asserts every runtime binary is placed + the installed entrypoint reaches the REAL compiled backend.

TRAP INSIDE THE FIX (caught during self-review): 'output is valid JSON' is NOT a usable assertion here — the FAILURE is itself JSON ({"code":"XTMUX_JSON_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE"...}). My first version of the check went green with the backend missing for exactly that reason. Now asserts the query's own array result + absence of an error payload. Verified both directions by reverting the fix: without it the 2 new tests fail; with it 149/0.

GATES: build / bun test 176 / typecheck clean / contract.sh 149 pass 0 fail / verify-json-api.sh PASS. CI: test+analyze+smoke+CodeQL all pass.

d0a.18 is now FIXED BY THIS PR — orchestrator should close it as done-by-#9 on merge (or I can). Bead still open, PR still unmerged.
MERGED: PR #9 -> see main. 'xtmux' alias installed beside the picker symlink (the ${self%/bin/*} trap: root does not resolve symlinks). Codex P2 was REAL and worse than reported: install.sh never linked bin/xtmux-obs AT ALL — not for xtmux, not for tmux-session-picker. It only worked on this machine because the symlink was hand-made at 02:13; bin/xtmux-obs is an untracked build artifact. Fixed: install.sh now builds it if absent or fails loudly with the exact command, then links it, and a new contract test runs the REAL install.sh under a fresh HOME and asserts it reaches a real (non-stub) V2 backend.

title: Test gate: conformance + identity-safety + measurement for the .8 pilot
description:
## PROBLEM

Unit schemas cannot prove that Pi discovers the piloted tools, calls the real picker, preserves
identity, and produces results identical to the CLI. Only a live, isolated tmux exercise can.

RESCOPED 2026-07-13 after the design consult. This bead previously covered "framework plus
messages/monitors and sessions/handoffs/observability" and asserted the pi.events lifecycle
bridge. That framing is dead: .7 is superseded, .9 and .11 are closed pending measurement, and
both consult panes rejected a second event bridge outright. What remains is a test gate for one
narrow pilot — plus the measurement that decides whether the tool line lives or dies.

## SUCCESS

The .8 pilot is proven equivalent to the CLI, safe on identity, and MEASURED against the
post-help baseline. The measurement is the deliverable, not a footnote: it is the evidence on
which .9/.11 are re-opened or the tool line is closed as YAGNI.

## SCOPE

- Adapter conformance harness: for every piloted operation, native tool result vs CLI `--json`
  result on the SAME isolated tmux socket. EXTEND `scripts/smoke-json-api.sh` — it already
  builds an isolated `tmux -L <label>` server, temp obs DB and XDG dirs, cleans up via trap,
  and is already a REQUIRED CI check (`smoke`). Do not build a second harness.
- Identity-safety regression: a target like `$1732` passed as a tool argument must never be
  shell-expanded.
- Exit-code preservation through the tool layer, including 75 and 124.
- Measurement harness: retries, malformed calls, and tokens for a fixed coordination task.

## NON_GOALS

- Testing sessions/handoffs/observability tools. They do not exist (.9 closed).
- Event-bridge assertions. Rejected: CLI events remain authoritative.
- Testing model reasoning quality or a specific provider response.
- MCP client/server tests.
- A second test harness. The smoke gate already exists and is already required in CI.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must run on an isolated tmux socket, never the operator's live server. `smoke-json-api.sh` is
  the pattern: `tmux -L "$label"`, temp `XTMUX_OBS_DB_PATH`, `XDG_*`, cleanup trap.
- The conformance test must fail if the native result and the CLI `--json` result diverge in
  ANY field — that divergence is exactly the drift this whole design is built to prevent.
- Note for the runner: `test/contract.sh` skips its bead-integration and auto-monitor contracts
  where `bd` is absent (i.e. on CI). Identity/coordination assertions that need `bd` must be run
  locally, deliberately, not assumed covered by a green CI badge.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Conformance: every piloted operation matches CLI `--json` field-for-field on one isolated
      socket.
- [ ] Identity safety: `$1732`-shaped argument is never shell-expanded. Must fail against a
      naive string-interpolating implementation — that is the proof the test has teeth.
- [ ] Exit codes 75 and 124 survive the tool layer.
- [ ] Measurement report: retries / malformed calls / tokens, native vs post-help CLI baseline.
- [ ] Prompt-cost delta of the tool schemas, measured — the Claude pane's central objection is
      that schemas are a PER-TURN tax. The number must be produced, not argued.
- [ ] CI `smoke` gate stays green.

## OUTPUT

Conformance + identity + exit-code test results, and THE MEASUREMENT: a table of retries,
malformed calls, tokens and prompt-cost delta, with an explicit verdict — expand (re-open
.9/.11), hold, or close the tool line as YAGNI.
notes:
$VALIDATION COMPLETE in same PR as .8: nine message/monitor tools delegate via pi.exec argv arrays + --json; live same-socket smoke exercises send/list/status/ack/unread/list/arm/wait/kill and returns raw CLI stdout unchanged; $1732 identity unit asserts literal argv (fails a shell interpolation design); tool-layer errors preserve 75/124; malformed/incompatible JSON fails loudly. Full build/test/typecheck pass. Direct contract/gate from stale non-client TMUX_PANE reproduced known xtmux-d0a.19 failure; both pass when run in a fresh attached isolated tmux client via script(1). Measurement verdict: CLOSE AS YAGNI (CLI 90 task tokens; native 104 + 521 per-turn schema = 625, +594%; retries/malformed both 0).
FINAL VALIDATION PASS: all mandatory gates clean in attached isolated tmux; conformance smoke is part of canonical scripts/smoke-json-api.sh, not a second harness. Exact CLI stdout is returned unchanged by the tool runner. Identity/exit/malformed contracts pass. Verdict CLOSE AS YAGNI.
PR #14 contains conformance/identity/exit tests plus measurement. Awaiting CI/review and orchestrator verdict; do not close bead.
PR #14 CI fully green; orchestrator accepted measurement verdict and closed PR unmerged. Validation evidence retained on branch/PR; bead closure remains orchestrator-owned.
Satisfied by PR #14's measurement (see d0a.8). The conformance/identity/exit-code harness was built and ran green, but is closed with the tool line: there is no tool layer left to conform against. The MEASUREMENT — which was always this bead's real deliverable — was produced and is recorded in d0a.8 notes and in bd memory.
close_reason: Measurement delivered (the bead's real deliverable); tool conformance harness closed with the tool line.

title: Pilot: native Pi messages+monitors tools (measured, 1:1 with CLI)
description:
## PROBLEM

Pi drives daily coordination (messages, monitors) by shelling out to the CLI. In the design
consult Pi reported five concrete retries from real use: (1) `message-list --json` without the
required `--for` -> exit 2; (2) output over the tool limit; (3) guessed JSON fields `id`/`text`
instead of `messageKey`/`summary` -> silent nulls; (4) an extra `jq` shell hop; (5) `'$1732'`
quoting — unquoted, the shell expands it and the agent acts under the WRONG IDENTITY.

Retries (1) and (3) are discoverability and are addressed by xtmux-d0a.15 (help). What typed
native tools uniquely remove is the rest: missing required args, shell-quoting hazards (5 is an
identity-safety bug, not an ergonomics one), and parse-and-retry context burn.

Both consult panes rejected the original framing. The Claude pane: token cost is INVERTED — a
tool schema is paid in prompt tokens EVERY turn, a bash call only when invoked; so a broad tool
surface is a net loss. Pi agreed: literal 1:1 tools for all 47 commands are excessive and raise
tool-selection load. Runtime speed and telemetry gains are marginal — a native adapter still
spawns the CLI, and xtmux already emits domain events.

## SUCCESS

A DELIBERATELY SMALL set of native Pi tools covers only the frequent, quoting-sensitive
coordination operations (messages, monitors). They are a thin typed facade: identical operation
names, arguments, results and exit semantics as the CLI, invoked via `pi.exec` with argument
ARRAYS (no shell string) and mandatory `--json`. The CLI remains the sole implementation.

The pilot is MEASURED against a post-help baseline. If it does not measurably reduce retries,
malformed calls, or tokens, the honest outcome is to stop here and close the tool work as YAGNI.

## SCOPE

- New `extensions/pi-xtmux-tools.ts` (or a bounded directory), ABSORBING the minimal shared
  scaffolding formerly scoped to xtmux-d0a.7 (superseded): TypeBox schemas, `pi.exec` runner,
  JSON decode, bounded output, typed errors, cancellation.
- Tools for messages (send/list/status/ack/unread) and monitors (list/arm/wait/kill) ONLY.
- `.pi/settings.json` extension load wiring for the pilot.

## NON_GOALS

- The `pi.events` lifecycle bridge from the original .7. Both panes rejected a second event
  bridge: existing CLI events remain authoritative.
- Sessions / handoffs / observability tools (was xtmux-d0a.9 — closed pending this pilot's
  measurement).
- Broad rollout, deprecation of Bash, prompt-cost tuning (was .11 — closed, same reason).
- Tools for all ~47 commands. Explicitly rejected by both panes.
- FORKING THE SKILLS. No `multiplexing-pi`. No dual-path prose. No harness-neutral verb rewrite.

## CONSTRAINTS

- 1:1 semantics with the CLI. Same names, same args, same results, same exit codes INCLUDING
  75 and 124. This is what keeps the skills unforked: only the invocation prefix differs, so
  the 647-line multiplexing skill needs at most ONE routing rule / promptGuidelines line —
  never 74 duplicated examples.
- Tools MUST delegate to the CLI via `pi.exec`. They MUST NOT touch SQLite or domain code
  directly.
- Fail loudly and clearly on malformed JSON or an incompatible CLI version.
- Blocked by xtmux-d0a.13: extensions are outside tsconfig today, so this would be written as
  untyped code against an unpinned Pi API. .13 is a go/no-go gate, not a parallel track.
- Blocked by xtmux-d0a.15 (help). Sequencing is METHODOLOGICAL, not technical: two of Pi's five
  retries are discoverability. Ship help and tools together and you cannot attribute the
  improvement — you would credit the tools for wins the help delivered. The baseline must be
  measured AFTER help lands.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Adapter conformance tests: for every piloted operation, the native tool result is compared
      against the CLI `--json` result on the SAME isolated tmux socket. Reuse the harness in
      `scripts/smoke-json-api.sh` (already a required CI check).
- [ ] Exit codes 75 and 124 are preserved through the tool layer, asserted.
- [ ] Identity safety: a target like `$1732` passed as a tool argument is never shell-expanded.
      This is retry (5) — the one with a wrong-identity failure mode. Regression test required.
- [ ] `bash test/contract.sh` and `bash scripts/smoke-json-api.sh` pass.
- [ ] MEASUREMENT (the gate): retries, malformed calls and tokens for a fixed coordination task,
      native tools vs post-help CLI baseline. Numbers, not impressions.
- [ ] Prompt-cost delta of the tool schemas is measured and reported — the Claude pane's core
      objection is that this is a per-turn tax. Show it.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, conformance-test output, the identity-safety regression test, and the MEASURED
comparison against the post-help baseline with an explicit recommendation: expand (re-open .9/
.11), hold, or close the tool line as YAGNI. A pilot that reports no numbers has failed.

## REFERENCES

Design consult 2026-07-13, two independent panes (Claude Code %2635 = the harness that keeps
Bash; pi %1931 = the harness that would receive the tools). Both independently ranked: never
fork per harness, never dual-path prose. Pi's ranked recommendation: .13 -> .8-only pilot, no
skill fork, expand only on measured benefit.
notes:
$PILOT MEASUREMENT (post-help fixed 4-call task: send, list, arm, wait; UTF-8 bytes exact, tokens=bytes/4 cl100k-style estimate ~±5%):
metric | post-help CLI | native | delta
retries | 0 | 0 | 0
malformed calls | 0 | 0 | 0
invocation bytes | 359 | 414 | +55
invocation tokens | 90 | 104 | +14
per-turn incremental schema bytes | 0 | 2082 | +2082
per-turn incremental schema tokens | 0 | 521 | +521
result/output tokens | identical CLI JSON | identical CLI JSON | 0
Runtime subprocesses | 4 | 4 | 0
Total incremental tokens for one task turn: CLI 90 vs native 625 (+535, +594%). The post-help baseline eliminates the discoverability retries; native tools add no measured retry/malformed/runtime gain, while structurally eliminating shell expansion at a substantial every-turn schema tax. VERDICT: CLOSE AS YAGNI; do not expand/re-open .9/.11. Pilot code remains in PR for review/evidence; orchestrator should close rather than merge if accepting verdict.
FINAL GATES PASS after explicit false-boolean argv fix: frozen install; build; full bun test; typecheck; contract.sh in fresh attached isolated tmux; verify-json-api.sh in fresh attached isolated tmux. The attached client is required to avoid known d0a.19 environment-sensitive false failures from stale TMUX_PANE/no-current-client. Live pilot smoke covers all 9 tools and timeout 124; unit covers literal '732', cancellation propagation, synthetic 75/124, malformed JSON, exact nine-tool scope and settings wiring. Verdict remains CLOSE AS YAGNI.
PR #14 opened at a9b656f. Explicit verdict CLOSE AS YAGNI; PR body contains full measurement table and recommends closing without merge to avoid 521-token per-turn tax. Do not close bead; orchestrator owns verdict.
Orchestrator accepted CLOSE AS YAGNI and closed PR #14 unmerged after all CI passed (test/smoke/analyze/CodeQL). .9/.11 remain closed; branch retained as evidence. Bead closure remains orchestrator-owned.
CLOSED AS YAGNI on measured evidence. PR #14 built the full 9-tool pilot (messages+monitors, 1:1 via pi.exec argv arrays, mandatory --json, 75/124 preserved) and was CLOSED UNMERGED — merging it would impose the 521-token/turn schema tax the measurement proved buys nothing. retries 0->0, malformed 0->0, per-turn schema tokens 0->521, one task turn 90->625 (+594%). The post-help CLI baseline already had ZERO retries: d0a.15's help closed 3 of pi's 5 retries harness-neutrally. Both consult panes predicted this from opposite seats. pi measured its own pilot honestly and recommended killing it, against its own interest.
close_reason: Measured, then closed as YAGNI. Native tools cost +521 prompt tokens EVERY turn and removed zero retries against the post-help baseline; d0a.15's help had already closed 3 of pi's 5 retries harness-neutrally. PR #14 closed UNMERGED on purpose.

title: Build native Pi tool framework and xtmux event bridge
description:
## PROBLEM

Wrapping each command independently would duplicate process execution, cancellation, JSON parsing, errors, rendering and telemetry. Existing Pi coordination extensions also infer side effects by parsing Bash command text/results, which native tool calls would bypass.

## SUCCESS

A project-local Pi extension registers shared infrastructure for domain-grouped xtmux tools: strict TypeBox schemas, picker/compiled execution through `pi.exec`, JSON decoding, bounded output, typed details/errors, cancellation, compact rendering, and a documented `pi.events` lifecycle bridge. No end-user domain tool is required beyond a minimal health/introspection probe.

## SCOPE

- New `extensions/pi-xtmux-tools.ts` or bounded extension directory with runner/schema/event helpers.
- `.pi/settings.json`/existing `pi-auto-monitor.ts` load wiring without duplicate extension registration.
- Shared types for tool results/event payloads and focused extension contract tests.

## NON_GOALS

- Implementing the full message/monitor/session/handoff catalog.
- MCP server or generic arbitrary-command passthrough tool.
- Replacing existing Bash compatibility listeners yet.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Use installed Pi APIs verified from `ExtensionAPI`: `registerTool`, `pi.exec`, `pi.events`, `setActiveTools` only when needed.
- Group tools by domain; no one-tool-per-command prompt explosion and no raw `argv` escape hatch.
- Use `StringEnum` for action enums, strict schemas, 50KB/2000-line maximum, saved full artifacts only when required.
- Throw on execution failure so Pi marks `isError`; details contain structured status, not secrets or unbounded stdout.
- Event payloads include action, outcome, duration, correlation IDs and canonical identities but never message bodies/tokens.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Extension hot-loads with `/reload` and tool metadata appears in `pi.getAllTools()`.
- [ ] Strict schema rejects unknown actions/fields and malformed legacy resumed arguments safely.
- [ ] AbortSignal cancels a bounded long-running fake/real command.
- [ ] Success/failure/truncation results preserve JSON details and compact content.
- [ ] `pi.events` emits exactly once per completed action with redaction assertions.
- [ ] Print/RPC/TUI load smokes pass without requiring UI.

## OUTPUT

Extension architecture, tool/event contracts, prompt-cost/tool-count report, test evidence, sample rendering/result, and handoff for domain tool tasks.

title: Test: JSON command API — differential contracts and live shell smoke
description:
## PROBLEM

The JSON API changes multiple shell/domain boundaries where a valid-looking result can still hide identity drift, duplicate side effects or broken legacy output. A separate regression gate must validate the full matrix before Pi tool work consumes it.

## SUCCESS

Automated contract/integration suites validate schema, semantics, compatibility, hostile identity, exit behavior, picker/compiled equivalence and live tmux wiring for all JSON-capable commands. Failures identify command/domain and preserve full logs as bounded artifacts.

## SCOPE

- `tests/contracts/*json*.test.ts`, integration tests, `test/contract.sh`, isolated temp DB/tmux fixtures, V1 golden/differential scripts.
- Covers implementation tasks for coordination, session/control, operational output and picker forwarding.

## NON_GOALS

- Pi extension/tool behavior.
- Coverage percentage targets or mocked internal serializer calls.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Layer: boundary + shell. Strategy: schema contract + subprocess integration + live tmux smoke.
- Real CLI/picker processes and isolated SQLite/tmux identities; mock only unavailable external runtime boundaries.
- Test logs include command, mode, exit code, schema error path, duration and artifact path; redact message bodies and environment secrets.
- No shared DB/tmux state between tests; deterministic timestamps/IDs where asserted.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Positive, negative, empty, duplicate/idempotent, timeout and cancelled cases per domain.
- [ ] Every JSON output parses and satisfies required fields/types/nullability/order.
- [ ] No-flag and V1 outputs match existing fixtures byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Picker and compiled backend JSON are semantically equivalent.
- [ ] Hostile-env tests prove no bystander identity attribution.
- [ ] Exact test-runner commands: `bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bash test/contract.sh`, `scripts/capture-v1-fixtures.sh --check`, plus documented isolated live tmux smoke.
- [ ] Failure artifact contains structured command/outcome evidence without raw payload leakage.

## OUTPUT

title: Wire universal picker JSON forwarding and compatibility guards
description:
## PROBLEM

Picker commands hand-parse flags and hand-build compiled argv, so each domain would otherwise implement `--json` forwarding differently. This must be solved before domain serializers land.

## SUCCESS

A small capability/forwarding scaffold makes JSON support opt-in per classified command, forwards quoted argv without `eval`, and rejects unsupported or explicit-V1 JSON requests deterministically. Runtime serializers are still supplied by .2/.3/.4.

## SCOPE

- `bin/tmux-session-picker` shared JSON flag/capability parsing and quoted forwarding seams.
- Help/capability wording for agent-json, structured guarded actions, interactive-only, explicit V1, and unavailable backend cases.
- Focused shell contract tests proving the scaffold without requiring every later domain serializer.

## NON_GOALS

- Domain result serialization owned by .2/.3/.4.
- Removing shell fallback, V1, or command-specific safety confirmation.
- Native Pi tools.

## CONSTRAINTS

- No command strings or `eval`; preserve array/quoted argv patterns.
- No-flag bytes and exit codes cannot change.
- `--json` never silently falls back to TSV/text.
- Guarded actions retain confirmation/refusal behavior; interactive/internal commands do not become tools.
- Shadow/default-on paths cannot duplicate side effects.

## VALIDATION

- Capability tests cover supported, unsupported, explicit-V1, unknown-flag, and missing-backend cases.
- Shell syntax and payload quoting with spaces/quotes/newlines remain safe.
- Existing V1 fixtures, differential oracle, and shell contracts remain unchanged.

## OUTPUT

Changed forwarding seams, capability matrix linkage, exact tests, affected flows, and constraints inherited by .2/.3/.4.

title: Define xtmux JSON command contract and classification matrix
description:
## PROBLEM

There is no authoritative inventory of picker/compiled commands, current output format, identity requirements, or whether each surface is suitable for an LLM tool. Implementing `--json` ad hoc would freeze inconsistent names and accidentally expose interactive or administrative internals.

## SUCCESS

A checked-in contract document and typed conventions classify every picker dispatcher command as agent-facing JSON, interactive-only, or guarded-admin. It defines field naming, nullability, timestamps/durations, success/error/exit semantics, ordering, truncation, identity rules, and a migration matrix from current TSV/text without changing runtime behavior.

## SCOPE

## NON_GOALS

- Defining JSON for fzf rendering, border labels, previews, popup controls, migrations, retention, or shadow internals unless classified as guarded administration.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Prefer existing camelCase/raw-object conventions from message queries; no speculative universal envelope.
- Explicitly document stable ordering and all nullable identity fields.
- Record current stdout/stderr/exit behavior before any implementation task starts.
- Logging evidence: inventory generation/check must report command, category, current format, selected JSON owner, and gaps; no payload contents.

title: Add JSON to coordination commands: messages, monitors, handoffs
description:
## PROBLEM

Messages have partial JSON support, while monitor and handoff coordination still expose TSV/text and mutation commands often return implicit success. These are the highest-value inputs for Pi tools and the most dangerous surfaces to parse heuristically.

## SUCCESS

All agent-facing message, monitor, wait/status, and handoff operations selected by the contract expose additive JSON with typed fields and structured mutation results. Existing human/no-flag output remains byte-identical and explicit V1 behavior remains documented and tested.

## SCOPE

- `src/cli-messages.ts`, message domain result types.
- `src/commands/monitors.ts`, monitor store result projection, picker `monitor-*`/`wait-agent` forwarding.

- Pi tool registration.

- `--json` only; no-flag TSV/text and V1 golden fixtures cannot drift.
- Mutation JSON includes durable IDs, outcome/idempotency, canonical target identity where known, and no raw message body beyond explicitly requested query fields.
- Wait/monitor streaming or timeout semantics retain current exit codes; JSON must distinguish done, timeout, cancelled, missing target, and backend failure.
- Emit/reuse journal envelopes at existing lifecycle boundaries; require correlation IDs and redacted failures, never full prompt/message payloads.

title: [epic] JSON command API + native Pi tools for xtmux
description:
## PROBLEM

xtmux exposes a mature coordination surface, but agents reached it through human-oriented
TSV/text over Bash — duplicating parsing, quoting and identity handling, with extensions
inferring side effects from command REGEXES.

The first half shipped (.1-.6, merged as fd568db): every agent-facing command now has an
additive, documented `--json` mode, gated in CI by a required `smoke` check.

The second half was originally scoped as a broad native Pi tool surface. A design consult on
2026-07-13 put that to two INDEPENDENT panes — Claude Code (the harness that would KEEP Bash)
and pi (the harness that would RECEIVE the tools). They converged: do not build it as scoped.

Pi, from direct use, named five real retries: missing required `--for`; output over the tool
limit; guessed JSON fields (`id`/`text` instead of `messageKey`/`summary`) returning SILENT
NULLS; an extra `jq` hop; and `'$1732'` quoting — which, unquoted, makes an agent act under the
WRONG IDENTITY. But TWO of those five are pure DISCOVERABILITY, not tooling: help is a single
unreadable 1,500-character line, and the `--json` output field names are documented NOWHERE.
And the Claude pane showed the token argument is INVERTED — a tool schema is paid in prompt
tokens EVERY turn; a Bash call only when invoked.

## SUCCESS

The cheap, harness-neutral fixes land FIRST and may make the expensive half unnecessary: a
canonical `xtmux` prefix, a real help surface documenting `--json` OUTPUT fields, and the
existing Pi extensions retargeted off command-regexes onto `--json`. Those help every harness
equally and fork nothing.

Only then, behind a typecheck gate, a DELIBERATELY NARROW native-tool pilot (messages+monitors)
is built 1:1 with the CLI and MEASURED. If it does not measurably reduce retries, malformed
calls or tokens against the post-help baseline, the tool line is closed as YAGNI. That is a
success, not a failure.

THE SKILLS ARE NEVER FORKED. Both panes independently ranked per-harness forks and dual-path
prose as the worst options — guaranteed divergence across safety-critical preflight, handoff and
monitoring procedures. 1:1 semantics is what keeps the 647-line multiplexing skill single-source.

## SCOPE

- bin/tmux-session-picker: command routing, the usage/help surface, mux-help.
- Install path: the `xtmux` alias beside the existing ~/.local/bin symlinks.
- extensions/pi-*.ts: regex coupling removal; tsconfig coverage; the pilot tool extension.
- docs/json-command-api.md, and the multiplexing skill prose at its ~/dev/core SOURCE.
- Test harness: scripts/smoke-json-api.sh (already a required CI check) is EXTENDED, never
  duplicated.

## NON_GOALS

- Renaming subcommands. message-send -> send-message fixes none of the five retries and costs
  ~3,300 call sites across ~380 files, ~1,400 of them in OTHER repos.
- Removing tmux-session-picker. It stays as the compatibility name, indefinitely.
- A second event bridge. CLI events remain authoritative.
- Native tools for all ~47 commands. Explicitly rejected by both panes.
- Forking the skills per harness, or dual-path prose.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Sequencing is methodological, not just technical: help (.15) must land BEFORE the pilot (.8),
  or the pilot's measurement is dishonest — it would be credited for wins the help delivered.
- .13 is a go/no-go GATE, not a parallel track. extensions/** sits outside tsconfig.json today,
  so `bun run typecheck` passes VACUOUSLY over three untyped extensions.
- Tools delegate to the CLI via pi.exec; never SQLite or domain code directly.
- Preserve exit codes, including 75 and 124.
- The --json contract plus its CI smoke gate is a sufficient shared spine ONLY under 1:1
  semantics. Deviate from 1:1 and the spine stops holding.
- Skills under ~/.xtrm/skills/** are MANAGED: an `xt claude` install WIPES AND REBUILDS that
  tree. Skill edits belong at the ~/dev/core source or they are silently lost.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xtmux <cmd>` works everywhere `tmux-session-picker <cmd>` did; nothing is broken.
- [ ] An agent can call any command correctly on the FIRST try from `xtmux help` alone —
      including --json output field names (messageKey, summary).
- [ ] Pi extensions no longer regex-match command text; a reworded send still wakes correctly.
- [ ] `bun run typecheck` covers extensions/** non-vacuously.
- [ ] CI test + analyze + smoke green throughout.
- [ ] The .8 pilot reports NUMBERS (retries, malformed calls, tokens, prompt-cost delta) against
      the post-help baseline, and an explicit expand / hold / close-as-YAGNI verdict.

## OUTPUT

Per-child handoffs, the measurement table from .10, and a final decision on the native-tool line:
expand (re-open .9/.11), hold, or close as YAGNI.

## REFERENCES

Design consult 2026-07-13: Claude pane %2635 and pi pane %1931, answering the same brief
independently from opposite seats. Both ranked: never fork per harness, never dual-path prose;
.13 first as a gate; .8-only pilot; expand solely on measured benefit.
close_reason: Epic complete. JSON command API (.1-.6) shipped and gated in CI by a required 'smoke' check on a live tmux socket. Native Pi tools (.7-.11) KILLED on measured evidence: two independent design consults rejected them, and pi's own pilot (PR #14, closed UNMERGED) showed 0 retries fixed and +594% tokens on a task turn. The real fix was 'xtmux help' (.15). Second half delivered instead: .13 pi-extension pin, .14 xtmux command name, .15 help surface, .16 JSON error contract, .17 skill prose migrated at the source (core PR #411), .19 the smoke gate made to stop lying (+ the failure it was hiding), .20 opaque test failure, .21 fresh-DB crash + two SQLite concurrency bugs found by CI. Integrated main c81da80: verify-json-api.sh PASS, harness-selftest 5/0, concurrent first-touch 0/5 from inside tmux. One follow-up unparented and left open: .22 (upstream prose in the vendored specialists skill).

title: Post-3xs: .36 poll must sendUserMessage-wake pi on new obligation, not just record
description:
## PROBLEM

Verified in 3-pane final smoke on 2026-07-13. Timeline:

- Claude sent actionable message to pane 3 (%2362) while pane 3 idle
- .36 poll (30s interval) correctly detected the inbound and created
  reply-to-$1732-for-%2362_pending marker
- .37 UI widget correctly shows 'Reply required: $1732 (xtmux-3xs.39)'
- BUT: pane 3 stayed idle for 5+ minutes without acting on it. No new
  turn started. LLM never saw the reminder.

The .36 poll records obligations silently. Only .38's outbound-wake
path calls ExtensionAPI.sendUserMessage to force a pi turn. Result:
inbound-only workflows are dependent on operator prodding.

## SUCCESS

When .36 poll detects a NEW obligation (marker didn't previously
exist for this messageKey), extension calls sendUserMessage with a
brief nudge like 'You have a pending reply obligation: $sender
($bead) — <summary>'. This forces a new pi turn where .37's
before_agent_start injection AND the obligation UI warning are both
visible to the LLM.

Idempotency: track already-woken obligations in-memory (Set of
messageKeys). Same-marker refresh doesn't re-wake.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts syncExpectedReplies() — after
  recordObligation, if messageKey is new since last poll, call
  pi.sendUserMessage('...').
- Contract test: seed new inbound while pane idle, verify
  sendUserMessage was called exactly once per new obligation.

## NON_GOALS

- No wake on obligation REFRESH (only on FIRST detection). Otherwise
  poll fires forever until reply.
- No wake for messages arriving during pi's active turn — .33's
  agent_start/agent_end scan already covers that.

## SEVERITY

Real coordination gap — inbound wake is broken end-to-end without
operator intervention. .36 solved the 'record obligation' problem but
not the 'wake pi to act on it' problem.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.36 (b4f93da) — mid-idle poll shipped.
- xtmux-3xs.38 (fc4af11) — outbound wake via sendUserMessage;
  symmetric mechanism, should be applied to .36 too.
- 3-pane final smoke evidence: message-key msg-1783908653-690626
  landed 04:10, pane stayed idle through 04:15+.
notes: Implemented idle-only wake in extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts: syncExpectedReplies returns first-seen messages, an in-memory message-key set suppresses refresh wakes, and only the interval calls sendUserMessage(followUp). Contract covers first idle wake, no duplicate wake, no active-turn wake, second idle message wake, and shutdown cancellation. Validation: bun test (full), bash test/contract.sh, bunx tsc --noEmit all green; LSP diagnostics clean; GitNexus impact LOW and detect_changes low-risk. Initial seconder e33b5b was PARTIAL only because standalone writer diff metadata was unavailable; it reported no code finding.
close_reason: Idle poll now wakes Pi exactly once for each newly discovered reply obligation; contract and full quality gates pass.

title: Post-3xs: .38 outbound wake consume path broken — monitor doesn't terminate on peer transition
description:
## PROBLEM

Verified in 3-pane final smoke on 2026-07-13 by pi on xtmux:1.3 (%2362).

.38 outbound recording works correctly: pi's send to xtmux:1.1 creates
'wait-for-xtmux:1.1-from-%2362_pending' marker + records monitor id
'm1783908042-1930-523658'. However:

- After >35s wait, marker still present
- Monitor never terminated despite Claude peer transitioning
  done→needs-input (a real state change)
- No pi.sendUserMessage wake fired
- Pi had to be operator-prodded to see Claude's response

## SUCCESS

Full consume path fires: on peer state transition observed by the
monitor-agent daemon, monitor terminates, .36 poll (or .38 direct
consume) reads terminal id from outbound-expectations, calls
pi.sendUserMessage(followUp) to wake pi.

## SCOPE

Two hypotheses to investigate:

- **.20 --wait-for-transition semantics too narrow**: the monitor
  captures initial state, waits for a state CHANGE, but may specifically
  require a terminal_status transition (done/killed/timeout/target_gone/
  process_gone/error). Peer going done→needs-input may not count as
  terminal per bin/tmux-session-picker::monitor_run wait-for-transition.
- **.38 consume path not reading outbound-expectations correctly**:
  even if the monitor daemon updates terminal_status, .36's poll or
  .38's dedicated consume logic may not correctly detect the
  transition and fire sendUserMessage.

Trace path:
1. Force a wait-for-transition monitor manually against a target that
   transitions done→needs-input. Does the daemon terminate?
2. If yes: .38's consume loop is broken.
3. If no: .20's semantics need widening OR the outbound-expectation
   should record a specific terminal state to wait for.

## SEVERITY

Real regression — this is exactly the mechanism .38 was filed to
provide, and it doesn't work end-to-end. The soft path (poll on
interval, .36) still catches inbounds, but outbound wake is broken.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.38 close (fc4af11): 'ExtensionAPI.sendUserMessage(followUp)
  wakes Pi'.
- xtmux-3xs.20 (wait-for-transition semantics).
- xtmux-3xs.34 final smoke report (2026-07-13)
close_reason: PREMATURE FINDING. On pane-3 recheck at t=~5min after the smoke, .38 wake fired correctly ("xtmux wake: xtmux:1.1 completed its monitored work cycle"), xtmux-outbound-expectations empty, monitor-list clean. Mechanism works — the earlier 35s window was too short because peer was still in needs-input (not yet at monitored terminal). Not a regression. Latency-contract-test bead can be filed separately if desired.

title: Post-3xs: pi-inbox-reply live-turn obligation lifecycle self-smoke
description:
## PROBLEM

xtmux-3xs.33 landed sender-declared expects-reply obligation trigger.
But .33's own delivery went silent: pi shipped .32 + .33 to main without
sending a completion message on xtmux:1.1. Same silent-idle pattern
.33 was designed to prevent. Neither .32 nor .33 exercised the fix
end-to-end in a live pi turn — the .22/.26 smoke was against a fresh
RPC-mode runtime, not pi's daily workflow.

## SUCCESS

Scripted lifecycle in the live pi runtime (pi's actual working session,
not a fresh RPC harness). Each step observed + reported:

1. Baseline: no obligations in /run/user/1000/xtmux-reply-obligations/
2. xtmux:1.1 sends message-send --bead xtmux-3xs.smoke34 --text ... --to pi.
   Under V2 defaults, this now sets expects_reply=true automatically
   (because bead is set, per .33's default).
3. Pi acks the message via message-ack.
4. Verify: reply-to-_pending exists with senderId + beadId payload.
5. Pi does arbitrary intermediate work (bd commands, file edits, whatever).
6. Pi's next agent_end MUST render 'Reply required:  (xtmux-3xs.smoke34)'
   as a below-editor warning.
7. Pi sends message-send back to xtmux:1.1 with the same bead.
8. Verify: marker removed, next agent_end shows no reminder.

If step 6 doesn't fire, that's the real regression — file whichever
lifecycle event isn't wiring correctly.

## SCOPE

- No code change unless step 6 fails.
- Report each step's observed state in bead close notes.
- If code change needed: file specific sub-bead with the exact
  event → action gap.

## NON_GOALS

- No fresh RPC harness (that was .22/.26's smoke path — proven).
- No new features. Verification only.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.33 close: expected the obligation trigger to fire on
  --bead sends by default. Live-turn verification never happened.
- xtmux-3xs.22/.26 smoke report (2026-07-13): all-9-steps pass in
  fresh V2 RPC runtime.
