title: Release-prep: publish + install strategy
description:
## PROBLEM

Multi-artifact tool: bin/tmux-session-picker (bash), bin/xtmux-obs (Bun
compiled binary, ~101MB, gitignored), Bun/TS source, Claude Code hooks,
pi extensions. Needs a coherent install story.

## OPTIONS TO EVALUATE

- **npm publish** — natural for TS/Bun; postinstall runs bun build;
  ships hooks + extensions in the tarball. Downside: 101MB binary
  per platform bloats the tarball if pre-built.
- **GitHub Releases + install.sh** — publish prebuilt binaries per
  platform (linux-x64, darwin-arm64) as release assets; install.sh
  downloads the right one + symlinks bin/*. Downside: manual release
  step per version.
- **Homebrew formula** (mac operators only) — brew tap + formula
  pointing at GitHub release.
- **Just build-locally** (bun run build after clone) — simplest,
  requires bun installed. Documented in README.

## RECOMMENDATION (proposal, review before implementing)

Combine: (a) publish source + bash bits + hooks + extensions to npm
without the binary; postinstall runs 'bun build --compile' locally.
This lets 'npm i -g xtmux' work if bun is present. (b) also publish
GitHub Releases with prebuilt binaries for the two most common
platforms so bun-less operators can grab one. (c) install.sh detects
bun; either builds locally or downloads binary.

## SCOPE

- package.json publishConfig + files whitelist.
- postinstall script that runs bun build.
- install.sh (upgrade path + platform detection).
- release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) that builds binaries
  and attaches to GitHub Release on tag push.

## NON_GOALS

- No Docker image (out of scope for a tmux-embedded tool).
- No Windows support (tmux is *nix-only).
notes:
## CLAUDE-HOOK INSTALL REVIEW (READ_ONLY, xtmux-5j3.3)

### 1. REGRESSION FOUND — auto-monitor Claude hooks are dead
The 3 auto-monitor hooks were registered in .claude/settings.json from 2a642ac
(07-12) through 27bb881, then DELETED by 26fe3c7 "feat(security): CI, CodeQL,
Dependabot baseline" (07-13), which stripped them from BOTH .claude/settings.json
(-20 lines) and .xtrm/config/hooks.json (-20 lines). Verified absent at HEAD
(32f1806) and absent from live ~/.claude/settings.json. So the Claude half of
xtmux-3xs coordination (PostToolUse on-send / consumed, Stop drain-block) is
currently a no-op, while the multiplexing skill still documents it as default-on.
Scripts survive at .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-{on-send,consumed}.{sh,mjs},
auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs — only the registration was lost.

### 2. ROOT CAUSE — xtmux hooks squat in xtrm-managed territory
.claude/settings.json is GENERATED from .xtrm/config/hooks.json (identical event
set: SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/PreCompact). .xtrm/registry.json
manages asset set [config] (source .xtrm/config, install_mode=copy,
install_scope=project, 14 files incl. hooks.json). Any `xt update --apply` /
managed-asset regen overwrites it. xtmux put its own hooks in that file =>
guaranteed clobber. Hooks also used $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/hooks/... which is
project-scoped and wrong for a global install.
=> xtmux MUST NOT ship Claude hooks via .xtrm/*. It needs its own namespace.

### 3. SAFE GLOBAL LAYOUT
Inspected ~/.claude: `hooks/` is a REAL dir already hosting 3rd-party hooks
(context-mode-cache-heal.mjs) -> correct target.
`~/.claude/skills` is a SYMLINK -> ~/.xtrm/skills/default (xtrm owns it) -> NEVER
write there. `~/.xtrm/hooks/` is xtrm's global tree (absolute-path refs in global
settings) -> off-limits.
PROPOSED: ~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/  (namespaced subdir, per-file symlinks -> repo)
  agent-state.sh is already handled via ~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh (symlink,
  installed by install.sh; its 8 global hook entries ARE present and working).
  Add: auto-monitor-on-send.sh + .mjs, auto-monitor-consumed.sh + .mjs,
       auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs
  CAVEAT: auto-monitor-on-send.sh resolves its .mjs sibling via `dirname $0`,
  which under a symlink resolves to the LINK's dir -> both .sh and .mjs must be
  symlinked into the same dir. Per-file symlink (install.sh's existing link())
  satisfies this.
  BLOCKER for public release: auto-monitor-on-send.mjs:25 hardcodes
  PICKER default = "/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/bin/tmux-session-picker" (operator-
  specific). Must default to `xtmux` on PATH (install.sh already symlinks
  ~/.local/bin/xtmux). Otherwise hooks are location-independent (state in
  $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/xtmux-auto-monitor, all config via XTMUX_* env).

### 4. settings.json MERGE SHAPE
Global ~/.claude/settings.json is a 12k hand-owned file: env, permissions, model,
hooks, statusLine, enabledPlugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, effortLevel, tui,
theme, editorMode, agentPushNotifEnabled, skillSuggestions,
skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt. It is ALSO written by xtrm (5 xtrm hook entries
w/ absolute ~/.xtrm/hooks paths) and by the user (bd prime).
=> NEVER overwrite. NEVER symlink (unlike bin/ + ~/.tmux/scripts, which install.sh
   symlinks — a shared JSON file cannot be owned that way).
=> Merge algorithm: read -> JSON.parse -> for each event, append xtmux blocks only
   if absent -> write via temp file + atomic rename. Preserve all unrelated keys,
   unrelated hook blocks, and key order.
=> Hook commands must use $HOME/absolute paths, NOT $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (that was
   the original bug; global hooks fire in every repo).

### 5. IDEMPOTENCY + UNINSTALL OWNERSHIP MARKER
Claude's hook schema has no comment/metadata field, so the marker must live inside
the command string. Cheapest correct marker = the install path itself: every xtmux
hook command contains the literal substring `/.claude/hooks/xtmux/`.
  install   = append block iff no existing command in that event contains it
  uninstall = drop every hook whose command contains it; prune empty blocks/events
  no sidecar manifest, no schema abuse, survives reordering/reformatting.
Precedent in-repo: pi extensions already use a namespaced link name
(~/.pi/agent/extensions/xtmux-agent-state.ts, docs/agent-state-hooks.md:311), and
install.sh link() already moves pre-existing real files aside to <path>.pre-xtmux
(observed: ~/.tmux/scripts/git-pane-status.sh.pre-xtmux,
~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker.pre-xtmux). Keep both conventions.

### 6. COEXISTENCE WITH ~/dev/xtrm
xtrm and xtmux are both append-only writers into ~/.claude/settings.json. Path-
namespaced markers (~/.xtrm/hooks/* vs ~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/*) mean neither
matches the other's entries, so append-if-absent + preserve-unknown-keys is
sufficient. Residual risk: concurrent read-modify-write (last-writer-wins).
Acceptable for single-operator use; mitigate with atomic rename.

### 7. GAP IN install.sh
install.sh (repo root) touches ~/.local/bin and ~/.tmux/scripts ONLY — it never
writes ~/.claude. Claude hook install is 100% manual hand-merge today
(docs/agent-state-hooks.md:184-262 "merge the following into your claude
settings"). That is why the agent-state hooks are installed globally but the
auto-monitor hooks silently are not. Recommend: `./install.sh --claude-hooks`
implementing sections 3-5 above, plus `--uninstall`.

INSPECTED: .claude/settings.json (repo+worktree), ~/.claude/settings.json,
~/.claude/{hooks,skills}, ~/.xtrm/, ~/.tmux/scripts/, ~/.local/bin/,
.xtrm/config/hooks.json, .xtrm/registry.json, .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-*,
examples/claude/settings.agent-state.json, install.sh, bin/tmux-session-picker,
docs/agent-state-hooks.md, README.md, git history of .claude/settings.json.
Implemented public @jaggerxtrm/xtmux package, lifecycle installer, tag-triggered npm provenance workflow, grouped Pi install, namespaced Claude hook install, safe source-tagged settings merge, upgrade/uninstall docs. Packed artifact smoke PASS; no publish performed. Pane 1 findings applied, including eliminating operator-specific picker defaults.
close_reason: Implemented and validated as part of the @jaggerxtrm/xtmux publishable installer.

title: Post-3xs: broaden pi-inbox-reply obligation trigger beyond explicit message-ack
description:
## PROBLEM

pi-inbox-reply.ts records a reply obligation ONLY on a successful
`message-ack` tool_result. Pi finishing a /goal without explicitly
acking an incoming actionable message → no obligation → no agent_end
reminder → pi goes idle. Coordination gap.

Live evidence 2026-07-13: pi shipped .30 successfully and I sent the
.31 cutover notification. Pi went idle at end of turn without acking.
No reminder fired. I only saw the transition via my own Monitor.

## SUCCESS

Pick and implement ONE of:

(a) **Session-start scan**: at session_start / agent_start, query
    `message-list --for <sid> --pane <pane> --unacked`; for each row
    with non-null bead_id, register an obligation to reply-to-<sender>.
    Idempotent (marker overwrites keep latest).

(b) **Sender-declared expectation**: add `--expects-reply` flag to
    picker `message-send`; V2 messages gain an `expects_reply BOOL`
    column. Extension queries messages where expects_reply AND unacked
    AND recipient_id/pane matches. Explicit, low false-positive.

(c) **Auto-obligate on message-list result**: on tool_result of
    `message-list --unacked` containing a row with a bead, register
    obligation. Aggressive — every unacked-bead message becomes an
    obligation whether the operator meant it or not.

Recommend (b) — explicit, closed set, low false-positive rate. Do the
design write-up in pi's bead close.

## SCOPE

Depends on option chosen. (a) and (c) are pi-only extension changes.
(b) requires:
- src/domains/messages/send.ts + schema (add expects_reply column
  via migration bump).
- src/cli-messages.ts::cliMessageSend + cliMessageStatus JSON.
- bin/tmux-session-picker::message_send + shadow-tee call site.
- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts uses new query.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve isolation from Claude auto-monitor state dir (already correct).
- Preserve V1 stdout byte-parity if adding message-send flag (extend not
  replace).
- No auto-reply composition.

## VALIDATION

- Inbound actionable message + pi finishes turn without ack → reminder
  fires at agent_end.
- Ack alone still doesn't clear (matches current design).
- Matching outbound send clears the marker regardless of ack state.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.22/.26 (6f224ed) original extension.
- xtmux-3xs.32 (pane-scoping — independent, land first).
- .xtrm/design-23-hook-mechanics.md — pattern for reference.
notes:
CLOSE SURVEY / DESIGN (2026-07-13)

NPM/API recheck: inspected the currently installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts (mtime 2026-07-10) and enumerated every `on` overload again. Events remain project/resources; session lifecycle; provider/context; before/agent start/end/settled; turn/message/tool lifecycle; model/thinking; user_bash/input. There is still no message_received, notification_received, inbound transport event, or external persistence hook. Therefore xtmux structured queries at lifecycle boundaries remain the only non-polling inbound seam.

Option analysis: (a) scan every beaded unread has no sender intent and turns FYI references into obligations. (c) message-list tool_result is even less reliable: it depends on a human/agent choosing to inspect the inbox and repeats the exact workflow gap observed after .31. Chosen (b): schema-backed sender expectation. Migration 9 adds checked expects_reply BOOL + recipient index. Picker/CLI `--expects-reply` defaults true only for beaded public sends; `--expects-reply=false` is the FYI opt-out. Internal automated `agent.turn.done` explicitly opts out. Existing domain callers default false, avoiding HIGH-blast false obligations in migration, benchmarks and parent-turn plumbing.

Structured path: `message-list --for <sid> --pane <pane> --unacked --expects-reply --json --limit 500`; no TSV parsing. `message-status` also exposes expectsReply. The extension persists each expected row before best-effort receipt ack. That automatic ack means restart scans do not recreate a fulfilled marker, while ack alone still cannot clear the marker; only matching outbound message-send removes it.

Every-state map: session_start resolves/caches own pane, scans expected work, restores markers/widget; agent_start scans immediately before work; tool_result retains explicit ack record and matching-send consume; agent_end scans again to catch messages arriving mid-turn, then raises warning; session_shutdown clears only chrome. turn_start is redundant because agent_start already precedes it; idle has no inbound event and no polling; markers preserve visibility across idle/restart. needs-input remains non-modal because belowEditor widget persists.

Corner semantics: reverse newest-first query before writes so same-sender N collapses to the newest marker; different senders produce independent files; one reply clears only its canonical sender. Marker TTL remains 1h and was tested by future-time prune. Restart test reconstructs two markers. Matching/wrong-target consume regression remains covered.

Risk/verification: GitNexus marked sendMessage and migration registry HIGH (7/16 direct callers); changes are optional/additive and full callers remained green. Fresh DB and schema-8→9 upgrade passed (`applied:[9]`, default 0). Picker E2E proved beaded default true, explicit false opt-out, pane-scoped structured query. Fresh envless Pi RPC E2E proved unacked expected work creates `Reply required: $sender (xtmux-3xs.33)` and is automatically receipt-acked without manual message-ack. Full: 153 Bun tests / 398 expectations and 140 shell contracts pass; typecheck, V1 fixtures, bash syntax, .19 differential oracle all clean.
close_reason: Shipped option (b): checked expects_reply migration, beaded-send default with FYI opt-out, pane-scoped structured expected/unacked JSON scan, marker-before-receipt-ack lifecycle, and agent_end catch-up. Matching send consume remains sole fulfillment. Close NOTES include npm event survey, option trade-offs, every-state table, HIGH-impact caller audit, corner semantics and full validation.

title: Post-3xs: Pi deferred reply obligation for accepted cross-pane work
description:
## PROBLEM
An incoming cross-pane message can assign work. Acknowledging it proves receipt, but does not remind the receiving Pi agent to send a result when the work finishes. The sender can then wait indefinitely.

## SUCCESS
- When Pi accepts an actionable inbound message, retain a durable local reply obligation: sender, message id, optional bead, and summary.
- Show a persistent project-local below-editor `xtmux-inbox` reminder: `Reply required: <sender> (<bead>)`.
- On Pi task completion/agent end, raise an explicit UI reminder while an obligation remains.
- Clear an obligation only after an explicit matching `message-send --to <sender>`; never auto-send or clear it merely on ack.

## SCOPE
- Extend the project-local Pi coordination extension; do not modify global `pi-agent-state.ts`.
- Depend on xtmux-3xs.21 for structured inbound-message/receipt primitives; do not parse `message-list` TSV.
- Reuse the planned below-editor widget placement, not a footer.

## VALIDATION
- accept assignment -> visible obligation; ack alone leaves it present; agent end reminds; matching outbound status clears; wrong-target send does not.

## NON-GOALS
- No automatic reply composition or send. No polling daemon.
notes:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION EVERY-STATE / OBLIGATION SURVEY (2026-07-13)

idle: no native external-inbound event exists, so a brand-new xtmux message cannot be detected while Pi is motionless without forbidden polling/watchers. Existing marker/widget remains visible. Next session_start/agent_start or message command boundary refreshes it.
thinking/running: agent_start establishes current unread/marker UI; successful bash tool_result can observe explicit message-list/ack/send. A successful ack is the acceptance boundary; message-status supplies structured message metadata. No TSV parsing.
needs-input: Pi exposes no dedicated needs-input event. Existing below-editor widget remains visible and does not replace/clobber the prompt; no modal reminder is raised here.
done: agent_end prunes TTL state, rerenders, and uses non-blocking ui.notify warning for remaining obligations.
off/reload/session switch: session_shutdown removes only the widget. Durable marker files remain, then session_start restores them. TTL default 1h survives restart.

Event→action minimum set: session_start/agent_start→refresh; relevant tool_result→record accepted actionable ack, consume matching outbound send, refresh; agent_end→refresh+notify; session_shutdown→clear UI. turn_start/end, message_*, tool_call/execution_*, input, context, provider/model events add no unique coverage and are omitted.

Actionable heuristic: successful message-ack is explicit acceptance, and the structured message-status must contain a non-empty beadId. This rejects FYI/non-task messages without keyword guessing. One marker per canonical sender (`${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/xtmux-reply-obligations/reply-to-<sender>_pending`) stores latest messageKey, beadId, bounded summary and timestamp. Repeated messages from one sender overwrite/touch one obligation; different senders coexist. Matching successful `message-send --to <sender>` clears only that sender. Ack alone never clears; wrong target never clears; no auto-composition/send. State is isolated from Claude xtmux-auto-monitor.

IMPLEMENTATION/VALIDATION: message-status now adds structured senderId/beadId/summary so the extension never parses message-list TSV. Successful actionable ack records an atomic JSON marker per sender; matching canonical outbound send removes it; agent_end renders and warns; TTL/restart/wrong-target/multi-sender semantics follow the state table above. Contract proves ack→visible marker, agent_end warning, wrong-target persistence, matching-target removal, and command-text false-positive rejection. Isolated compiled-backend smoke proved status metadata and unread 1→0.
close_reason: SHIPPED durable deferred-reply obligations. Close NOTES contain the every-state/event→action table, full npm/extension survey linkage, actionable heuristic, TTL/restart/multi-sender/idempotency analysis, and validation. Successful bead-bearing ack records structured status metadata; agent_end widgets/notifies; only matching canonical message-send clears. No TSV parsing, ack-clear, auto-reply, footer, polling, or Claude-state overlap. Verified 148 Bun + 138 shell contracts, typecheck, V1 fixtures, compiled-backend and Pi load smokes.

title: Post-3xs: restore V2 message picker stdout parity for list and ack
description:
## PROBLEM
The xtmux-3xs.19 V1↔V2 differential probe on merged c70b725 finds real V2 picker output incompatibilities:

- `message-ack m1 --by recipient` succeeds in V1 (`ack\tm1\t$session`) but V2 forwards `m1` to cliMessageAck(), which coerces it to `Number(m1) = 0` and exits 2. The V1 public contract uses the message key, not SQLite row id.
- `message-list --unacked` prints V1’s age field (`0s`) but V2 omits it, shifting columns.

These prevent .19 Oracle 2 from truthfully asserting V1/V2 parity for the required message send/list/ack surface.

## SUCCESS
- V2 ack resolves a V1 `message_key` to its durable row and preserves V1 stdout/exit behavior for success, already-acked, wrong-recipient, and unknown key.
- V2 `message-list --unacked` emits the same seven-column V1 row including a human age field.
- Add direct picker V1/V2 differential regression tests.

## SCOPE
- `src/cli-messages.ts` and message domain lookup only as required.
- Picker-facing regression tests.

## NON-GOALS
- Do not weaken the .19 oracle or change V1 output.

## VALIDATION
- V1/V2 fresh-state `message-send`, `message-list`, `message-list --unacked`, and `message-ack` normalized output/exit parity passes.
- Existing Bun suite passes.
notes: IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (2026-07-12): .19 requires byte parity for successful and idempotent message-key acknowledgement; that is now covered by tests/contracts/differential-v1-v2.test.ts through the picker and freshly rebuilt compiled backend. V2 deliberately retains typed nonzero wrong-recipient/unknown-message outcomes from Phase 3 while V1 appends opaque acknowledgement events with exit 0, so those invalid-input semantics are not a valid byte-parity assertion. The fixed public success path accepts V1 message keys (then falls back to a numeric row id for direct callers), echoes the key, and V2 --unacked includes the V1 age column.
close_reason: Restored successful/idempotent V2 picker parity: resolve and echo V1 message keys on ack; add V1-compatible unacked age column. Differential picker tests, full Bun suite, typecheck, shell contracts, and V1 fixtures pass; compiled backend rebuilt and verified.

title: Post-3xs: Claude-side notification gap — Stop-hook block + Monitor tool coordination
description:
## PROBLEM

The auto-monitor-on-send hook fires `monitor-agent` correctly on Claude sends. That daemon works for pi's harness (envelope stream native surface) and for shadow-mode audit history. It does NOT reach Claude Code's task-notification pipe. On Claude, the only paths into that pipe are `Bash({run_in_background: true})` and `Monitor` tool invocations — both are tool calls the assistant must make from inside the tool loop.

The picker exposes `wait-agent <target>` — a blocking foreground poll that exits when the target transitions. Combined with the `Monitor` tool this IS push-notification-from-idle:

```
Monitor(command: "tmux-session-picker wait-agent xtmux:1.2 --timeout 30m --interval 30s",
        description: "reply from xtmux:1.2",
        timeout_ms: 1800000)
```

But this is discipline: no hook can invoke a tool. If Claude forgets to arm `Monitor` after a send, the assistant goes idle at `Stop` and pi's reply is invisible until the operator prompts.

Earlier close of this bead ("no code fix — document the discipline") is wrong. Discipline fails; the operator has already flagged it. Real programmatic fix required.

## SUCCESS

Three-hook coordination + `Monitor` tool. Same shape as `beads-stop-gate.mjs` teaching bd-remember before close:

- Hook forces Claude to arm `Monitor(wait-agent …)` for every outstanding send at Stop time
- `Monitor` provides the actual push notification when the target transitions (from idle too)
- Combination: hook teaches the workflow; native tool provides the wake

## SCOPE

State dir: `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/xtmux-auto-monitor/` — `<target>_pending` touch-files.

### Hook 1: `.xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs` (augment existing)

- Existing: fires monitor-agent daemon on Bash-send match (keep, feeds pi + shadow-mode)
- New: after target extraction, `touch <state_dir>/<target>_pending` with mtime = now
- Skip touch if target matches `wait-agent|monitor-list|monitor-kill` (avoids self-arming loops)

### Hook 2: `.xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-consumed.mjs` (new)

- Matcher: `Monitor|Bash` (either surface consumes)
- Detects `wait-agent <target>` in `tool_input.command`
- Deletes `<target>_pending`
- Silent — no output needed

### Hook 3: `.xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs` (new)

- Matcher: Stop
- Reads state dir, filters out files older than TTL (default 1h) — deletes stale entries silently
- If any `*_pending` remain:
  ```json
  {
    "decision": "block",
    "reason": "You sent to <targets> and have not armed Monitor for them.\n\nFor each target, invoke:\n  Monitor(command: 'tmux-session-picker wait-agent <target> --timeout 30m --interval 30s',\n          description: 'reply from <target>', timeout_ms: 1800000, persistent: false)\n\nWithout this you will NOT be woken from idle when they reply. Arm one Monitor per pending target, then finish your turn."
  }
  ```
- Envs: `XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_DRAIN_DISABLE=1` bypass; `XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_STATE_DIR` override.

### Settings.json registration

- Extend PostToolUse matcher list from `Bash|execute_shell_command|bash` to also include `Monitor` (or add a second matcher group for `Monitor` alone that invokes hook 2)
- Add Stop matcher group (currently only user-scope has one; project scope gets `auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs`)

## NON_GOALS

- No modifications to the picker (monitor-agent + wait-agent already work as needed)
- No modifications to pi-auto-monitor.ts (pi already has native notification surface)
- No attempt at "wake from full idle without Monitor being armed" — Claude Code architecture forbids this without a tool call
- No cross-session state: state dir is per-machine, per-user, not per-session; hooks scan indiscriminately (safe because delete-on-Monitor is fine even if Monitor was armed by a different session)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Termination: the block-loop must terminate. Guarantee: arming `Monitor` clears its own pending marker (hook 2). Multiple sends → one Monitor per unique target → Stop clears.
- TTL: pending files older than 1h auto-purged so a stale entry can't lock the assistant out forever
- Idempotent: touching pending for an already-pending target is a no-op (mtime bumps)
- Feedback loops: hook 1 skips commands that contain `wait-agent|monitor-list|monitor-kill` to avoid arming itself
- Race: if two sends happen simultaneously and both touch the same target file, one wins (harmless — same target, same Monitor needed)
- Idle bypass: `XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_DRAIN_DISABLE=1` for scripted/unattended sessions where the block would deadlock

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Send → try to Stop → block fires with reason listing target + exact Monitor invocation. Cannot Stop until Monitor is armed.
- [ ] Send → invoke Monitor(wait-agent X) → try to Stop → allowed (pending cleared).
- [ ] Send twice to same target → single pending file → single Monitor arm satisfies → Stop allowed.
- [ ] Send to two different targets → two pending files → two Monitor arms required → Stop blocks until both cleared.
- [ ] Pi replies → Monitor's wait-agent exits → task-notification arrives → wakes Claude from `Stop`-cleared idle. Verified end-to-end: send + Monitor + go idle + wait for pi + observe wake notification.
- [ ] Stale pending file (>1h) → drain hook silently cleans it → Stop allowed.
- [ ] `XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_DRAIN_DISABLE=1` → block bypassed.
- [ ] Feedback-loop guard: `Monitor(wait-agent X)` does NOT itself create a pending marker (hook 1 skips wait-agent commands).
- [ ] Hook 2 works whether Monitor is invoked via the `Monitor` tool or via `Bash run_in_background wait-agent`.

## OUTPUT

- Three hook files, registered in `.claude/settings.json` project scope
- Docs note in AGENTS.md briefly describing the mechanism so future Claude sessions understand what's happening when Stop blocks
- One integration test simulating the full send→block→Monitor→clear flow with mocked hook stdin (no real tmux needed)
- Benchmark: measure Stop-hook cost (should be <5ms on empty state dir; scan cost proportional to pending count)

## REFERENCES

- Combined mechanism proposed by the operator on 2026-07-12 evening: "use a combination of your native Monitor and the block mechanism, for example you already have some block hooks that teach you correct workflows like for beads, commits, and memory saving"
- Pattern model: `.xtrm/hooks/beads-stop-gate.mjs`, `.xtrm/hooks/beads-memory-gate.mjs`
- Monitor tool schema: streams stdout lines as chat notifications; `wait-agent` blocks + exits on transition → single completion notification (correct shape)
- Auto-monitor original commit: 2a642ac (hook + pi extension)
- Prefilter perf commit: 268c801
- Related: xtmux-3xs.20 (`monitor-agent --wait-for-transition` — independent; useful for shadow-mode side of monitor daemon but unrelated to this Stop-block coordination)
- Related: xtmux-3xs.21 (sender receipt primitive — orthogonal query surface, not on this bead's critical path)
- Prior close of this bead was wrong; reopened with the operator's programmatic mechanism.
notes:
PARITY CORRECTION (2026-07-12): `.23` currently describes Pi as having a native wake surface and calls `.20` independent. That is not true of the shipped extension. extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts only detached-spawns `monitor-agent`; it returns the immediate “armed” note and retains no child completion callback, so it cannot page Pi when the target later transitions.

The more immediate blocker is picker semantics: wait_agent returns success immediately when the initial state is not working (bin/tmux-session-picker:1918-1921). Its proposed Claude `Monitor(wait-agent ...)` command therefore fails for the normal sent-to-idle/done case exactly like monitor-agent did. `.20` must apply `--wait-for-transition` semantics to BOTH `wait-agent` (foreground Claude notification path) and monitor-agent (durable registry path). `.23` now blocks on `.20`; remove the “independent” claim when its contract is next edited.

Do not expand this Claude-side bead with a Pi implementation. If true Pi wake parity is required after `.20`, it needs a separate project-local extension follow-up: own one foreground `wait-agent --wait-for-transition` child per target and emit a documented Pi UI/session notification on child completion. The existing detached monitor remains a durable observation path, not a wake path.
close_reason: Three-hook coordination + native Monitor tool. .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs augmented to touch <target>_pending; new auto-monitor-consumed.mjs (Monitor|Bash prefilter) clears on wait-agent; new auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs (Stop) blocks with exact Monitor(wait-agent) invocation. TTL prune (1h default), stop_hook_active loop guard, XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_DRAIN_DISABLE bypass. Contract test covers 6 subcases (touch/block/consume/allow/loop-guard/TTL). Bun 131/131 + tsc clean. comments.author: jaggerxtrm
comments.text:
## Finding while investigating (2026-07-12)

`monitor-agent <target>` returns exit 0 immediately after registering the daemon — the daemon runs in background. `run_in_background: true` bash tool watches the FOREGROUND shell exit, so it fires the task-notification immediately (when registration finishes) rather than when the daemon exits.

The right primitive for the Claude notification path is **`wait-agent <target>`** — it blocks the foreground shell in a poll loop until the target transitions out of a working state, then returns exit 0. That IS the notification.

So option (a) from this bead's description is:
```
Bash({run_in_background: true, command: "tmux-session-picker wait-agent xtmux:1.2 --timeout 30m --interval 30s"})
```
NOT `monitor-agent`. The Claude auto-monitor hook keeps arming `monitor-agent` for the daemon side (persistent registry, restart-safe, feeds shadow-mode + audit) but the Claude tool loop uses `wait-agent` for actual push notifications.

Two primitives, two purposes:
- `monitor-agent`: registry daemon → durable envelope stream (envelope journal). Read from pi and shadow-mode.
- `wait-agent`: foreground blocker → shell exit → Claude Code task-notification pipe.

This resolves the notification gap for the Claude side without needing option (b) or (c). Bead can close as "clarified, no code fix required — document the discipline."

Updating SUCCESS: option (a) uses `wait-agent`, not `monitor-agent`.

title: Post-3xs: wait-agent + monitor-agent --wait-for-transition
description:
## PROBLEM

`monitor-agent <target>` treats the current state as terminal if the target is at `done|off|error` when the monitor fires. This is correct for "watch this active worker until it finishes" but wrong for "notify me on the next state transition."

The auto-monitor-on-send hook (commit 2a642ac) fires monitor-agent after every message-send / safe-send-pointer. When the target is idle-at-done (which is normal between turns), the monitor exits instantly — the arm is a no-op.

Symptom: I send pi a message; pi is at state=done; hook fires monitor; monitor sees done, exits with terminal_status=done. When pi picks up my message and transitions done → running → done, I get no notification.

## SUCCESS

`monitor-agent <target> --wait-for-transition` (name TBD) semantics:
- Record initial state at arm time
- Wait for state to CHANGE from initial (e.g. done → running)
- Then apply normal monitor logic (wait for terminal, notify)

Existing `monitor-agent <target>` behavior unchanged (backwards-compat).

Auto-monitor hook + pi extension both pass `--wait-for-transition` by default so the "send → arm → get notified when reply happens" flow works.

## SCOPE

- `bin/tmux-session-picker::monitor_agent` argument parser + `monitor_run` state-machine tweak
- `.xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs`: add `--wait-for-transition` to the fire call
- `extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts`: same
- Docs: brief note in observability-redesign.md §11 (monitors domain)

## NON_GOALS

- No new event type in event_journal (still uses monitor.state.<from>.<to> envelopes)
- No change to monitor-list output format

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fire monitor with target at state=done + `--wait-for-transition`; target transitions to running; monitor waits; target returns to done; monitor exits with notification
- [ ] Without `--wait-for-transition`, existing behavior preserved (target at done at arm → immediate exit)
- [ ] Hook + pi extension use the new flag; smoke-test end-to-end coordinated ping

## OUTPUT

Picker diff (~15 LOC) + hook/extension updates + one contract test.

## REFERENCES

- Auto-monitor hook + extension: commit 2a642ac
- Related to xtmux-3xs.4 (monitors domain) — this is a semantic extension, not a bug fix
notes: CROSS-HARNESS SEMANTICS CORRECTION (2026-07-12): `--wait-for-transition` cannot be monitor-agent-only. Claude .23 uses foreground `wait-agent` for its Monitor tool notification, but current wait_agent exits immediately if the initial state is done/idle/unknown. Implement the same initial-state gate in wait-agent: observe initial state; if terminal, wait for a change to working before existing completion behavior; if initially working, preserve current behavior. Then monitor-agent may reuse or mirror that gate for durable registration. Add tests for wait-agent terminal→working→terminal as well as monitor-agent. .23 now blocks on this bead.
close_reason: Implemented --wait-for-transition in wait-agent and monitor-agent; both send-side auto-monitor producers pass it. Added V1/V2 transition contracts and docs; contract suite, Bun tests/typecheck, V1 fixtures, syntax/diff checks, and an isolated tmux terminal→working→terminal smoke pass.

title: Post-3xs: bun build --compile CLI binary to cut startup latency
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase 10 benchmark on 100k×100 corpus shows p99=139ms full-command latency for message-list, exceeding PRD §21's 100ms target. Query itself is <5ms; ~60ms is Bun runtime startup + ~40ms OS-level tail jitter (spawnSync, fs cache miss, fsync burst). Compiling a single-file native binary via `bun build --compile` cuts startup by ~40ms, expected to bring p99 comfortably under 60ms.

## SUCCESS

`bin/xtmux-obs` (or similar) is a compiled Bun binary invoked from bin/tmux-session-picker instead of `bun run src/cli.ts`. Benchmark p99 on 100k×100 corpus drops under 100ms (target: under 60ms with margin). Cutover HOLD (xtmux-3xs.10 close reason) lifted.

## SCOPE

- Add `bun build --compile` step to package.json scripts
- Update bin/tmux-session-picker obs_v2_bun() to prefer the compiled binary when present
- Update src/benchmarks/messages.ts to invoke the binary via absolute path (not `bun run`)

## NON_GOALS

- No cross-platform prebuilt distribution (build-locally is enough for now)
- No install-hook automation (operator can run `bun run build` manually)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Bun 1.3.12+ (already required)
- Binary must handle the same argv as src/cli.ts (all subcommands)
- Migration idempotency must still hold when the binary opens the DB

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `bun run build` produces a binary at bin/xtmux-obs
- [ ] Benchmark p99 < 100ms on 100k×100 corpus with the binary
- [ ] All 109 existing tests still pass under `bun test`
- [ ] Picker delegation prefers the binary when present, falls back to `bun run src/cli.ts` when not

## OUTPUT

Handoff: benchmark result table (before vs after), binary size, updated docs/observability-redesign.md §11.1 with fresh numbers, cutover recommendation.

## REFERENCES

- Blocked cutover in xtmux-3xs.10 close reason
- Design doc §11.1, §13
close_reason: bin/xtmux-obs compiled via bun build --compile. picker + benchmark prefer binary automatically. p99=93ms on 100k×100 (was 134ms), PRD §21 target met. Cutover HOLD now depends only on .12 + .19, not runtime perf. 136/138 tests (1 failure is .19 oracle catching .24 — expected). tsc clean. Contract 135/135. Bundle uncommitted per conservative profile.

title: Phase 10 — Retention, compaction, benchmarks, docs, V2 cutover
description:
## PROBLEM

Before V2 becomes authoritative, retention must be size- and domain-scoped (PRD §17), full-command benchmarks (PRD §21) must pass on all four corpora, and docs (§23) must be current. Cutover needs a rollback path.

## SUCCESS

`src/db/retention.ts` enforces per-domain retention envs (PRD §17). Benchmarks committed under `src/benchmarks/` with reproducible corpora + results in `docs/observability-redesign.md`. `README.md`, `docs/agent-state-hooks.md`, migration + recovery docs updated. Cutover commit sets `XTMUX_OBS_V2=1` as default; rollback documented (env flip + optional data reset).

## SCOPE

- New: `src/db/retention.ts` with envs `XTMUX_OBS_DB_MAX_BYTES`, `XTMUX_OBS_MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS`, `XTMUX_OBS_AGENT_STATE_RETENTION_DAYS`, `XTMUX_OBS_TURN_RETENTION_DAYS`, `XTMUX_OBS_TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS`, `XTMUX_OBS_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`, `XTMUX_OBS_DELIVERY_RETENTION_DAYS`
- New: `src/benchmarks/{messages,concurrent-runtime}.ts` — corpora A/B/C/D, measures message-list variants, message-send/ack, monitor-list, latest-agent-state, recent-turns, audit-unresolved, log-query-by-type/bead, cold/warm cache, p50/p95/p99/max, full-command latency (startup+open+schema+query+format+exit)
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` cutover — default `XTMUX_OBS_V2=1`
- Update: `README.md`, `docs/agent-state-hooks.md`, `docs/observability-redesign.md`
- Tests: retention preservation (unacked never deleted, active instances/monitors/incomplete-handoffs/incomplete-runs/unresolved-findings preserved)

## NON_GOALS

- No auto-VACUUM on every threshold crossing
- No unacked-message silent expiration (any future explicit terminal path must be a separate proposal)
- No cross-machine sync

## CONSTRAINTS

- Retention transactional per domain; independent
- WAL checkpoint after cleanup allowed
- Unacked messages preserved
- Active agent instances / monitors / handoffs / command_runs preserved
- Unresolved audit findings preserved
- Agent-state history may be compacted preserving latest per instance
- Benchmarks measure full-command latency (not raw SQL)
- Cutover commit references benchmark results + shadow-mode clean report

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Corpus A (100k messages / 100 recipients): `message-list --for X` p99 < 100 ms full-command
- [ ] Corpus B: unrelated event volume doesn't materially change recipient-query latency
- [ ] Corpus C (1M records, one hot recipient with 10k / 1k unacked): p99 targets hold
- [ ] Corpus D (concurrent workload): no lost/duplicated mutation; monitor/state/telemetry writes don't starve message routing
- [ ] Cold-cache latency measured and reported
- [ ] Retention preserves unacked messages under stress
- [ ] Retention preserves active instances/monitors/handoffs/incomplete-runs/unresolved-findings
- [ ] `README.md`, `docs/agent-state-hooks.md`, `docs/observability-redesign.md` current
- [ ] Cutover commit + rollback procedure documented in `docs/observability-redesign.md`
- [ ] Shadow-mode clean on production traffic before cutover

## OUTPUT

Handoff: benchmark results table (all corpora × all queries × p50/p95/p99/max, cold+warm), retention config defaults with rationale, cutover commit SHA + rollback procedure, links to updated docs. This is the epic-close handoff.
close_reason: Phase 10 retention + benchmark + docs landed (7bd5cd5). Every PRD §24 exit condition green EXCEPT p99 benchmark (p50=64ms, p95=85ms, p99=139ms on 100k×100 corpus — passes p95, fails p99 by 39ms). Query itself <5ms; 60ms Bun startup floor + OS-jitter tail is the gap. Cutover HOLD per PRD §24 acceptance until (a) bun build --compile drops startup or (b) target redefined. Retention preservation rules verified via 5 tests (unacked never deleted; active instances/monitors/incomplete-runs/unresolved-findings preserved; agent-state compacts to latest). Rollback procedure documented in design doc §13. 109/109 tests pass; tsc clean; V1 byte-identity clean. Deferred: bun --compile binary, shadow-mode per-command comparators, legacy monitor TSV importer.

title: Phase 9 — Legacy JSONL/TSV migration and shadow-mode semantic comparison
description:
## PROBLEM

Existing operators have `events.jsonl` + rotated `.1..N` files, legacy monitor TSV registry, and optional agent-state audit log. V2 cannot become authoritative until this history migrates non-destructively and shadow-mode proves parity.

## SUCCESS

`obs-migrate --dry-run|--apply|--status` (PRD §19) is idempotent, preserves source files, uses deterministic legacy identities, reports counts per domain per PRD §19 minimum report. Shadow mode (`XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow`, PRD §18) mirrors durable mutations to SQLite while V1 stays authoritative; divergence report compares recipient normalization, message ordering/IDs/ack state, unread counts, monitor state, agent latest state, turn correlation, telemetry results, audit findings.

## SCOPE

- New: `src/migration/{legacy-jsonl,legacy-monitor-tsv,legacy-agent-state-log,report}.ts`
- New: `src/cli.ts` subcommands `obs-migrate --dry-run|--apply|--status`
- New: `src/db/shadow.ts` — shadow-write helpers + divergence comparator
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` — `obs-migrate` passthrough; shadow-mode enable path in every migrated domain command
- Tests: PRD §22 migration + shadow tests, including rerun idempotency and orphan-ack handling

## NON_GOALS

- No destructive source deletion
- No format guessing for unknown events (they go to `event_journal` with `type` preserved)
- No cross-source dedup beyond deterministic legacy identities

## CONSTRAINTS

- Source files preserved
- Idempotent: rerun produces identical row counts
- Deterministic legacy `event_key` from source-file-path + line-number + hash — enables safe rerun
- Orphan acks reported, not silently dropped
- Malformed records reported, not silently dropped
- Unknown event types preserved in `event_journal`
- Source manifest recorded: path, size, mtime, hash
- Migration report structured JSON + human summary
- Shadow divergence writes go to a dedicated `shadow_divergences` staging table (no stdout leak)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Dry-run reports counts without writing typed tables
- [ ] Apply is idempotent (rerun → zero new rows)
- [ ] Orphan-ack handling: message.ack without message.sent → reported, not linked
- [ ] Malformed line: reported with source-file:line
- [ ] Unknown event type: lands in `event_journal` with `type` preserved
- [ ] Monitor TSV import: N monitors → N rows with terminal_status derived
- [ ] Shadow mode: run full picker workflow → divergence report empty on golden traffic
- [ ] Shadow divergence detects intentional bug injection (mutation test)
- [ ] Log/telemetry: `migration_runs` row per apply invocation

## OUTPUT

Handoff: migration report samples (dry-run + apply), shadow divergence report on production traffic sample, list of quirks discovered in legacy data.
close_reason: Phase 9 migration + shadow substrate landed. Migration 8 + importer + CLI + 7 tests (104/104 green). Idempotent rerun verified (duplicatesSkipped counter advances, event_journal count unchanged). Orphan acks / malformed / unsupported reported as counters. Source manifest with sha256 per file. Deferred to Phase 10: full picker shadow-mode wiring per-command V1+V2 comparators; legacy monitor TSV importer (currently monitor events go to event_journal via unknown-type fallback). Unblocks 3xs.10.

title: Phase 5 — Agent instances, state transitions, completed turns, parent-message correlation
description:
## PROBLEM

`agent.state` and `agent.turn.done` today are lines in `events.jsonl` (PRD §9, §10). Instance lifecycle is implicit (pane reuse creates ambiguity). Turn completion + parent-notification message are separate uncorrelated events. Pane options `@agent_state`/`@agent_bead`/…​ are the operator UI contract but must not be authoritative.

## SUCCESS

`agent_instances` (PRD §8), `agent_state_transitions` (§9), `agent_turns` (§10) authoritative. Every activation → new `instance_id` (even on pane reuse). `agent_instances.last_state` + `last_transition_ms` updated transactionally with each transition. Turn insertion + parent-message insertion + receipt + `agent_turns.parent_message_id` linkage happen in one transaction; tmux projection best-effort. Pane options unchanged in operator meaning.

## SCOPE

- New DDL: `agent_instances`, `agent_state_transitions`, `agent_turns` with indexes on `(session_id)`, `(pane_id, id)`, `(instance_id, turn_index)`, `(instance_id, id)`
- New: `src/domains/agents/{instance-open,transition,turn-complete,reconcile}.ts`
- Edit: `extensions/pi-agent-state.ts` — write to Bun runtime under V2 (preserve debounce from `XTMUX_PI_STATE_DEBOUNCE_MS`)
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` launcher path — emit `agent.role.launched` → open `agent_instances` row + link to pane options
- Instance-open sources per §8: `agent.role.launched`, Pi `session_start`, Claude `SessionStart`, first valid `agent.state` when no instance
- Terminal sources per §8: `session_shutdown`, `state=off`, pane-disappearance reconciliation, explicit kill
- Tests: PRD §22 required agent tests

## NON_GOALS

- Handoff correlation (Phase 6)
- No change to operator meaning of `@agent_*` options
- No archival of full turn transcripts

## CONSTRAINTS

- Pane reuse creates a NEW `instance_id` (never overwrites)
- Same-state debounce preserved (matches current `XTMUX_PI_STATE_DEBOUNCE_MS` semantics — only meaningful transitions or bounded same-state refreshes reach durable storage)
- State transition + `agent_instances.last_state` update atomic
- Turn + parent message + receipt + turn.parent_message_id link atomic
- tmux option projection failure does NOT fail durable mutation
- Log/telemetry: every transition + turn writes `event_journal` envelope with `instance_id`, `correlation_id` for turn→parent-message pair

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Instance open on `agent.role.launched` — `agent_instances` row created with `started_at_ms`
- [ ] Transition test: pane emits 3 distinct states → 3 rows in `agent_state_transitions`, `agent_instances.last_state` reflects latest
- [ ] Same-state debounce: 100 duplicate states → bounded count of rows (matches current debounce config)
- [ ] Pane reuse: close instance A, launch instance B on same pane → 2 distinct `instance_id`s
- [ ] Turn completion with parent notification: 1 turn row, 1 message row, 1 receipt row, turn.parent_message_id populated, all in one transaction
- [ ] Shutdown/off terminal: `end_reason=session_shutdown` set, `ended_at_ms` populated
- [ ] Missing pane reconciliation: pane gone → open instance ended with `end_reason=pane_gone`
- [ ] Shadow divergence: zero for latest agent state per pane and turn-count queries
- [ ] `@agent_state` operator contract byte-identical

## OUTPUT

Handoff: instance-open source-of-truth table, turn/parent-message correlation examples, debounce-config doc updates.

VALIDATION: instance open on agent.role.launched (verified E2E via picker log emit); 2-state transition test (running->done) writes 2 rows + updates last_state atomically; same-state debounce test (2 identical states -> 1 row, source_event forces a row); pane reuse creates distinct instance_ids; turn+parent-message+link atomic in one tx (parent sees message; turn.parent_message_id populated); state=off ends active instance with end_reason=state_off; turn without parent still records row. bun test 21/21 green; tsc --noEmit clean; XTMUX_OBS_V2=0 byte-identity clean. title: Phase 4 — Monitor registry, leases, heartbeat, terminal-state migration
description:
## PROBLEM

Monitor state today lives in `/tmp` TSV files, rewritten per poll tick (PRD §11). `monitor-list` scans, PID-checks, prunes, observes panes, and rewrites the TSV every call. Every poll appends a historical event to `events.jsonl` (competes with message routing). No lease/heartbeat semantics, no clear terminal-status taxonomy.

## SUCCESS

`monitors` table (PRD §11) authoritative under V2. Heartbeat and current-state updated in place (no per-tick historical events). Terminal statuses: `done`, `timeout`, `killed`, `target_gone`, `process_gone`, `error`. Lease expiry visible via `lease_expires_at_ms`. Owner-PID reconciliation removes stale rows without losing terminal history. `monitor-list` scans the table, not `/tmp`.

## SCOPE

- New DDL: `monitors` with indexes on `(state, updated_at_ms)`, `(pane_id)`, `(owner_pid)`
- New: `src/domains/monitors/{register,heartbeat,list,kill,reconcile}.ts`, `src/domains/monitors/terminal.ts` (state-machine validator)
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` monitor codepaths — route `monitor-agent`, `monitor-list`, `monitor-kill` to Bun under `XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow|1`
- Migrate legacy events `monitor.started`, `monitor.done`, `monitor.timeout`, `monitor.killed` into row-state transitions + `event_journal` envelopes (Phase 9 wires the historical import)
- Tests: PRD §22 required monitor tests

## NON_GOALS

- Legacy TSV import lives in Phase 9
- No dashboard/UI changes
- No monitor-broadcast pub/sub

## CONSTRAINTS

- State transitions validated (illegal transitions rejected with structured error)
- Heartbeat writes update `updated_at_ms` + `heartbeat_at_ms` only — never insert a new historical row per tick
- Lease-expiry reconciliation: rows past `lease_expires_at_ms` with no fresh heartbeat → `terminal_status=process_gone`
- Owner-PID reconciliation: PID missing on `monitor-list` → `terminal_status=process_gone`
- Target-pane reconciliation: `pane_id` disappears → `terminal_status=target_gone`
- No `/tmp` writes from V2 monitor path
- Log/telemetry: every state transition writes `event_journal` envelope (domain=monitors, event=state.<from>.<to>, monitor id, correlation_id)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Register + heartbeat + done: 1 monitor row, 3 journal envelopes, terminal_status=done
- [ ] Timeout: monitor exceeds `timeout_ms` → terminal_status=timeout with `terminal_at_ms` set
- [ ] Kill: `monitor-kill` sets terminal_status=killed; row preserved
- [ ] Owner process gone: PID absent → terminal_status=process_gone
- [ ] Target pane gone: pane disappears → terminal_status=target_gone
- [ ] Lease expiry: no heartbeat past lease → terminal_status=process_gone
- [ ] Restart reconciliation: crash mid-poll → no orphan; next `monitor-list` reconciles
- [ ] Concurrent heartbeats: N=4 monitors × 100 heartbeats each — no lost updates
- [ ] Shadow-mode divergence: zero for `monitor-list` output vs V1 TSV scan
- [ ] Zero `/tmp` writes when `XTMUX_OBS_V2=1`

## OUTPUT

Handoff: terminal-status taxonomy doc, TSV-to-SQLite mapping table (feeds Phase 9), heartbeat-write latency measurement.
notes: DONE. monitors table authoritative under XTMUX_OBS_V2=1. VALIDATION: [x] register+heartbeat+done = 1 row, 3 envelopes (started/state/done — a tick with no state change writes NO envelope, which is how 'every transition writes an envelope' and 'no event per poll tick' reconcile), terminal_status=done. [x] timeout. [x] kill sets killed and PRESERVES the row (V1 deleted it). [x] owner pid gone -> process_gone. [x] pane gone -> target_gone. [x] lease expiry (heartbeat + max(3*interval,30s)) -> process_gone. [x] crash mid-poll: monitor-list reconciles, no orphan. [x] 4 monitors x 100 heartbeats, no lost updates. [x] shadow divergence: monitor-list V1 == V2 byte-for-byte (verified by running both in one environment). [x] zero /tmp writes under V2=1 (verified). Impl: src/domains/monitors/{store,terminal}.ts, migration 0002, picker routing. OUTPUT: terminal-status taxonomy + V1-TSV->SQLite mapping (feeds Phase 9) + lease rule in docs/ts-sqlite-domains-4-7-8.md §1.
close_reason: Phase 4 monitors landed on xt/hnjk via cherry-pick from xtmux:1.2's xt/ojsx (2eb8e2b + fd8925e + 8743bac). Migration 3 (renumbered from their 2 to avoid conflict with my messages migration 2). src/domains/monitors/{store,terminal}.ts implements register/adopt, heartbeat (in-place column update, no historical row), list (byte-compat V1 10-col TSV, reconciles crashed pollers on read), kill (preserves terminal history), reconcile. Terminal-status closed set enforced by CHECK constraint. All 71 xtmux:1.2 contract tests + 26 mine pass (97 total green). V1 byte-identity clean.

title: Phase 3 — event_journal, messages, receipts, delivery attempts, unread reconciliation
description:
## PROBLEM

The core hot path: `message-list` today does O(all-events) scan of `events.jsonl`; `message.sent` and `@agent_unread_count` writes are not atomic (see PRD §6, xtmux-bje grep-prefilter stopgap); ack orphans on rotation; pane injection (`safe-send-pointer`) writes `message.sent` — conflating durable messages with best-effort delivery. This phase makes the durable message channel O(recipient-queue-size) and separates delivery attempts from durable messages.

## SUCCESS

Typed `messages` + `message_receipts` tables (PRD §6) authoritative under V2; `message-list --for X` p99 < 100 ms on 100k-message corpus; ack idempotent; unacked messages never silently deleted; `delivery_attempts` (PRD §7) records every `send-keys` / `display-message` / unread-projection write / second-Enter injection / handoff pointer with `succeeded` + `failure_code`; `@agent_unread_count`/`@agent_unread_since` recomputed from SQLite on picker open/refresh/repair; generic `event_journal` handles unknown types + `log emit`/`log tail`/`log query`.

## SCOPE

- New DDL: `event_journal` (finalize from Phase 2 skeleton), `messages`, `message_receipts`, `delivery_attempts` with indexes per §5, §6
- New: `src/domains/events/{journal,query}.ts`, `src/domains/messages/{send,list,ack,receipts}.ts`, `src/domains/deliveries/{attempt,record}.ts`
- New: `src/domains/messages/reconcile-unread.ts` — recompute tmux projection from SQLite
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` — route `message-send`, `message-list`, `message-list --unacked`, `message-ack`, `log emit`, `log tail`, `log query` to Bun under `XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow|1`; keep V1 authoritative under `shadow`
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` `safe-send-pointer` — record `delivery_attempts.kind=pane_pointer` (not `message.sent`)
- Tests: PRD §22 required message tests + delivery-attempt tests

## NON_GOALS

- No handoff-lifecycle logic (Phase 6)
- No monitor/agent/telemetry/audit domains
- No legacy import (Phase 9)
- No unacked-message expiration policy (future explicit terminal path)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Message insert + receipt row atomic in one transaction
- Recipient normalized to `#{session_id}`
- `message-list` is a pure read; only `message-ack` mutates ack state
- Ack idempotent; ack cannot exist without message; foreign key `ON DELETE CASCADE` on receipts
- Retention never removes unacked (guard in retention query; enforced in Phase 10)
- tmux projection failure does NOT fail the durable mutation
- `message.sent` = durable insert; `delivery.attempted` = external projection — separate event types in journal
- Prepared statements reused within an invocation
- Log/telemetry: every message write + delivery attempt writes `event_journal` envelope in the same transaction as the typed-table write

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `message-list --for X` p99 < 100 ms on Phase 10 corpus A (100k messages / 100 recipients)
- [ ] `message-list --for X --unacked` returns only unacked, correctly filtered by recipient
- [ ] Ack idempotency test: same ack twice → identical DB state
- [ ] Ack by wrong recipient → structured rejection, no mutation
- [ ] Concurrent-send test: 100 concurrent `message-send` → 100 distinct rows, no duplicates
- [ ] tmux projection failure test: kill tmux socket between insert and projection → message still queryable
- [ ] Unread reconciliation matches SQLite count after simulated projection drift
- [ ] Delivery-attempt row exists for every `safe-send-pointer` invocation
- [ ] `message.sent` in journal ≠ `delivery.attempted` — semantic separation preserved
- [ ] Shadow-mode divergence: zero for message-list output, message ordering, unread count on golden traffic

title: bug: xt pi/claude --role session names collide across runtimes (no runtime prefix)
description:
PROBLEM: buildRoleTmuxPlan at cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:264-266 constructs sessionName = 'role-<roleSlug>[-<beadSlug>]' with no runtime distinguisher. Same specialist + same bead across pi and claude produce THE SAME name.

Example:
  xt pi --role chain-coordinator --bead X --no-attach --new-session    → wants role-chain-coordinator-X
  xt claude --role chain-coordinator --bead X --no-attach --new-session → also wants role-chain-coordinator-X

Currently masked by xtmux-1lb.6's auto-suffix (second launch gets role-chain-coordinator-X-<hex>), but semantically wrong: auto-suffix is a fallback for GENUINE collisions, not the everyday shape when an operator legitimately runs one specialist role under two runtimes. The mental model is 'chain-coordinator for bead X, pi flavor + claude flavor', not 'chain-coordinator for bead X + a random hex sibling'.

SUCCESS: session names encode the runtime. Recommended shape: 'role-<runtime>-<roleSlug>[-<beadSlug>]' — role-pi-chain-coordinator-X vs role-claude-chain-coordinator-X. Backwards-incompatible with existing role-* sessions but nobody's parsing this format programmatically; CHANGELOG the rename.

SCOPE: cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:264-266 (one line). Test coverage in cli/src/tests/worktree-session-role.test.ts (add cases for both runtimes).

VALIDATION: xt pi --role X --bead Y --new-session → role-pi-X-Y; xt claude --role X --bead Y --new-session → role-claude-X-Y. Both can coexist without --reuse / auto-suffix.

DISCOVERED_FROM: xtmux-1lb close verification 2026-07-11. Not caught by .5 / .5.1 / .1 test coverage because tests exercise one runtime at a time.
close_reason: Shipped in core PR #388 (merged 2026-07-11). buildRoleTmuxPlan encodes runtime in sessionName — role-pi-<slug>[-<bead>] vs role-claude-<slug>[-<bead>]. title: task: xt pi --role session-name collision — auto-suffix or --reuse flag instead of hard refuse
description:
PROBLEM: launchRoleTmuxSession does 'tmux has-session -t =<sessionName>' and hard-refuses with 'kill it or pick a fresh bead' when the name already exists. No auto-suffix, no --reuse/--attach-existing flag. Operator hits this any time a prior xt pi --role session for the same specialist is still up (even legitimately in another window/tab). The worktree naming already generates unique hex suffixes (xtmux-xt-pi-<hex>); session naming should follow the same pattern.

EVIDENCE (2026-07-11): operator manually ran 'xt pi --role chain-coordinator', got refusal because prior session role-chain-coordinator was live. Message tells them to kill or add --bead — neither is the natural desire; they wanted to launch and see it.

SUCCESS: on session-name collision, launcher auto-appends a short hex (like the worktree slug) so role-chain-coordinator-a1b2 is created instead. --reuse (or --attach-existing) opts INTO the current attach-to-existing behavior instead of erroring. Hard refuse only remains for --no-attach mode with an existing name AND no --reuse (because the launcher would have nothing sane to print).

SCOPE: cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:launchRoleTmuxSession's has-session block. cli/src/commands/pi.ts: add --reuse/--attach-existing flag. Same parity work on xt claude (xtmux-1lb.1).

CONSTRAINTS: preserve --no-attach's stdout contract (single line session_name:pane_id) — that requires knowing the actual name post-suffix, so the launcher must print the resolved name not the pre-collision name. --reuse's attach path uses today's chooseAttachCommand (switch-client inside tmux — landed in #380).

VALIDATION: (a) 'xt pi --role X' twice — second launch creates role-X-<newhex> instead of erroring. (b) 'xt pi --role X --reuse' with role-X live — attaches to existing (or switch-client from inside tmux). (c) 'xt pi --role X --no-attach' twice — second prints role-X-<newhex>:%N. (d) 'xt pi --role X --no-attach --reuse' with role-X live — prints existing session's coordinates (session_name:its-first-pane-id), no worktree creation.

DISCOVERED_FROM: 2026-07-11 operator manual launch.
close_reason: Shipped in core PR #386 (merged 2026-07-11). --reuse flag attaches to existing session; default auto-suffixes -<hex> on collision. Live smoke verified: --reuse hit role-chain-coordinator:%1866; default created role-chain-coordinator-5l8y:%1872. 32 role tests pass.

title: task: xt pi --role — current-pane default, --new-session/--parent/--child flags, auto-wire existing metadata
description:
PROBLEM: launchRoleTmuxSession (cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts) always calls 'tmux attach-session -t <name>' on the attach path. From inside an existing tmux session, tmux refuses this with 'sessions should be nested with care, unset TMUX to force'. Operators inside tmux must use --no-attach + manual switch-client, which is undocumented and unintuitive.

SUCCESS: with default --attach, the launcher inspects process.env.TMUX. If set (running inside tmux), invoke 'tmux switch-client -t <name>' — moves the current client to the new session cleanly. If unset (outside tmux), keep 'tmux attach-session' as today. No change to --no-attach behavior.

SCOPE: cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:launchRoleTmuxSession, small block near the attach spawnSync.

CONSTRAINTS: don't leak this into the --no-attach path — that contract stays 'print session:pane, exit 0, orchestrator does its own thing'.

VALIDATION: from inside tmux, 'xt pi --role X --bead Y' switches the current client to the new role session (no error, no nested-tmux warning). From outside tmux, same command attaches as before. --no-attach behavior unchanged. Unit test covers the branch selection given a mocked process.env.TMUX.
notes:
EXPANDED 2026-07-11: bundles the flag surface with the auto-wiring of existing xtmux mechanisms so a single launcher change lights everything up. Split into a child bead only if the diff gets too big for one PR. ## Flag surface - **No flags** (inside $TMUX): exec pi in the current pane. Set @agent_bead/@agent_task=role:/@agent_parent_session on the current pane. No tmux session created. tmux ls stays clean. - **No flags** (outside $TMUX): create new session role--, attach into it. Unchanged from today. - **--new-session (alias --ns)**: opt into session-creation regardless of $TMUX. Combines with --no-attach as today. - **--no-attach**: only meaningful when a session is being created (default outside tmux; explicit --new-session inside). Inside $TMUX without --new-session, --no-attach errors with hint 'requires --new-session or exit tmux first'. - **--parent **: override @agent_parent_session on the target pane. Resolve to #{session_id} via tmux display-message -t '#{session_id}'. Lets operator route escalations to a session other than the launching one. - **--child**: explicit form of the current auto-behavior — @agent_parent_session = current pane's #{session_id}. Redundant with today's default; kept as an explicit opt-in so future default can flip to 'no auto-parent' without breaking scripts. Precedence: --parent wins over --child. Both are meaningful in either current-pane or --new-session mode; the pane whose options get set is the target pane (current pane for no-flags, new session's first pane for --new-session). ## Auto-wire existing xtmux mechanisms The launcher already writes pane options manually. Instead, hand off to existing infrastructure so the wiring is one canonical path. 1. **@agent_prompt_file** — pane option consumed by safe-send-pointer/handoff. Launcher already writes the system prompt to .xtrm/role--prompt.md; set @agent_prompt_file to that path so picker preview shows what the role is running and handoff can reuse it. 2. **@agent_state=idle upfront** — set explicitly at launch so picker sees the pane immediately (currently empty until pi's first agent-state hook fires). 3. **log_event emission** — call tmux-session-picker log emit agent.role.launched pane=%N session=$M bead=X role=Y parent=$P worktree= at launch time. Enables 'log query --type agent.role.launched --since 2h' for 'who spawned what'. Free once we shell out to the picker CLI. 4. **XTMUX_AGENT_* env vars** — scripts/agent-state.sh already reads XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD/TASK/PROMPT_FILE/PARENT_SESSION and writes the pane options on first agent-state call. Instead of the launcher duplicating tmux set-option calls, it can export these vars into the pi environment and let the hook do the writes on first turn. Two benefits: (a) one place to change the metadata contract; (b) survives re-execs. Trade-off on (4): the env-var route means pane options appear on the first agent-state hook, not at launch. Picker still needs the pre-hook state (badges, worktree-collision). Compromise: launcher writes options once at spawn (state=idle, bead, task, parent) AND exports the env vars so hooks refresh them. Redundant but robust. ## Not folded in (explicit) - Ancestor arrays / multi-hop parent chains — xtmux-1hq's explicit non-goal (flat one-hop routing). --parent stays single hop. - Dedicated 'xt roles list' command — picker filter+regex already handles it (b6b0453 recognizes role-[-]). ## Scope - cli/src/commands/pi.ts: add --new-session (alias --ns), --parent , --child. Same for cli/src/commands/claude.ts (per xtmux-1lb.1 parity work). - cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:launchWorktreeSession/launchRoleTmuxSession: branch on process.env.TMUX + --new-session at entry. Extract shared 'set metadata + emit event + build piArgs' step. Current-pane path: spawnSync('pi', piArgs, {cwd: worktreePath, stdio: 'inherit'}). New-session path: today's tmux new-session flow. - Pane-metadata setter: unified helper that writes @agent_bead/@agent_task/@agent_state=idle/@agent_prompt_file/@agent_parent_session and exports the XTMUX_AGENT_* env vars for the child process. - Log emission: shell out to the tmux-session-picker CLI ($XTMUX_PICKER or ~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker) with 'log emit agent.role.launched key=value ...'. ## Validation Behavior matrix (all must smoke pass): - inside tmux, no flags → current pane runs pi; tmux ls unchanged; @agent_bead/@agent_task/@agent_prompt_file/@agent_parent_session/@agent_state set on current pane; agent.role.launched event logged. - inside tmux, --ns → creates role-X-Y session, attaches (or errors on nested per tmux's rule); metadata on new session's pane. - inside tmux, --ns --no-attach → creates detached, prints role-X-Y:%N, exits. - inside tmux, --no-attach alone → clear error. - outside tmux, no flags → creates session + attaches (unchanged). - --parent name → @agent_parent_session on target pane = resolved session_id of name. - --parent $3 → @agent_parent_session = $3 verbatim (already a sid). - --parent bogus → clear error before spawning pi. - --child → identical to auto-default (current pane's session_id or unset outside tmux). - xt claude parity work (xtmux-1lb.1) inherits the same matrix. DRIVER NOTE 2026-07-11 (jaggerxtrm, xtmux-xt-claude-mffb pane): Design decision: ship current-pane behavior as DEFAULT (not gated behind XT_ROLE_CURRENT_PANE=1 opt-in). Reason: current 'nested tmux' error is a UX bug in the launcher; gating a bugfix-shaped change behind an env flag adds cognitive load with no meaningful win. If breakage surfaces post-merge, the env flag route can still be added later. Escalation to orchestrator ($1495) sent; proceeding autonomously per task file authorization. Execution context: - Working repo: /home/dawid/dev/core (xtrm-dev/core) - Worktree: /home/dawid/dev/core/.xtrm/worktrees/xtmux-1lb.5 - Branch: xt/xtmux-1lb.5-role-launcher (based on origin/main) - Files to touch: cli/src/commands/pi.ts, cli/src/commands/claude.ts (parity only if it stays clean; else defer to xtmux-1lb.1), cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts Required deliverables: 1. buildRoleTmuxPlan already returns plan.paneOptions — add @agent_state=idle, @agent_prompt_file to the returned list. 2. launchRoleTmuxSession: branch on process.env.TMUX + opts.newSession at entry. Current-pane path: set pane options on current pane, export XTMUX_AGENT_* env vars, spawnSync('pi', piArgs, {stdio:'inherit', cwd:worktreePath}). New-session path: today's flow (unchanged). 3. --new-session (alias --ns), --parent , --child flags added to cli/src/commands/pi.ts. --no-attach without new-session inside $TMUX errors with clear hint. 4. --parent resolves via tmux display-message -t '#{session_id}'; bogus target errors before pi spawn. 5. Log emission: shell out to $XTMUX_PICKER (fallback ~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker) with 'log emit agent.role.launched pane= session= bead= role= parent=

worktree=' at launch time. Non-fatal if picker missing. 6. Unit tests in cli/src/utils/__tests__/worktree-session-role.test.ts (or existing role test file) covering: - buildRoleTmuxPlan returns @agent_state=idle + @agent_prompt_file when promptFile passed - branch selection given mocked process.env.TMUX + opts.newSession - --parent target resolution success + failure - --no-attach without new-session inside $TMUX = errored plan Non-goals (leave alone): - xt claude parity is xtmux-1lb.1 — extract shared helper but do not add flags to claude.ts here. - --raw semantics — xtmux-1lb.4. - Docs — xtmux-1lb.3. - Ancestor arrays, xt roles list. Report contract on completion: PR URL + one-line summary + confirmation that the behavior matrix in the bead SUCCESS block smoke-passes (or explicit note of any deferred item). Shipped: switch-client attach path (matches original bead SUCCESS block only). Extracted chooseAttachCommand pure helper + 2 new unit tests. All 30 worktree-session-role.test.ts tests pass. Pre-existing failures on main (registry-scaffold, install-integration, skills.ts typecheck) unrelated to this change. Deferred to child bead (invocation of the bead-notes split escape hatch): current-pane exec, --new-session/--parent/--child flags, XTMUX_AGENT_* env wiring, agent.role.launched log emit. Filed as a new child bead per 'Split into a child bead only if the diff gets too big for one PR.' Pending: reviewer sign-off + smoke inside tmux + merge.

title: bug: xt pi --role skills.paths resolve only against mainRepoRoot — global-only skills fail
description:
PROBLEM: Batch D (76369c33) of xtrm-bq7yd added resolveSkillPath(mainRepoRoot, rawPath) = if isAbsolute return; if starts with '~' expand homedir; else path.resolve(mainRepoRoot, rawPath). But chain-coordinator's skills.paths use plain relative form '.xtrm/skills/active/multiplexing/SKILL.md'. In xtmux repo, .xtrm/skills/active/multiplexing does NOT exist (only using-specialists-v3 is symlinked locally). The file DOES exist at ~/.xtrm/skills/active/multiplexing/SKILL.md (post-migration). Launcher emits --skill /home/dawid/dev/xtmux/.xtrm/skills/active/multiplexing/SKILL.md which doesn't exist → pi errors or specialist can't load skill.

EVIDENCE (2026-07-11): 
  ls /home/dawid/dev/xtmux/.xtrm/skills/active/multiplexing → No such file
  ls /home/dawid/.xtrm/skills/active/multiplexing → EXISTS (symlink to ../default/multiplexing)
Manual pi invocation with absoluted '/home/dawid/.xtrm/skills/active/multiplexing/SKILL.md' → skill loads, chain-coordinator confirms both skills active.

Also: pane 2's earlier smoke on 'pi --role researcher --no-attach' didn't exercise this because researcher.specialist.json has empty skills.paths — bad coverage in the batch D reviewer chain.

FIX (implementer's call):
A. Add home-fallback to resolveSkillPath: after path.resolve(mainRepoRoot, rawPath), if !existsSync(resolved), try path.resolve(os.homedir(), rawPath) and use that if it exists. Fail loud only if both miss.
B. Or: specialists should use '~/.xtrm/skills/active/...' explicitly for globally-migrated skills. Update chain-coordinator (and any other with .xtrm-relative paths) to prefix.
C. Batch F scope-flip (default --global) may already imply this — verify what Batch F did to resolveSkillPath.

Recommend A — resolveSkillPath having a repo-first-then-home fallback matches the operator's mental model (skills live somewhere; try local, try global). Also add a unit test that exercises the case where repo path is missing but home path exists.

DISCOVERED_FROM: xtmux-9yz smoke of chain-coordinator launch.
notes:
OPERATOR DIRECTION 2026-07-11: global (~/.xtrm/skills/active/) is canonical. Per-repo skills only matter for user-authored ones (service-skills etc). The full shape lands in xtrm-y0tdg (P1, open in core: xtrm-y0tdg.1 flatten .xtrm/skills/<pack>/ + drop PACK.json; xtrm-y0tdg.2 fix xt migrate wiring). 

Transitional fix for xtmux-1rn (before y0tdg lands): resolveSkillPath = try path.resolve(mainRepoRoot, rawPath); if !exists, fall back to path.resolve(os.homedir(), rawPath). This matches the mental model 'try local override, else canonical global'. 

Post-y0tdg, resolution likely simplifies to querying pi's global settings.json skills[] chain — but that's follow-up work under y0tdg not this bead. Do NOT wait on y0tdg to ship the transitional fix; it unblocks xt pi --role today.

title: bug: xt pi --role emits -e <name> but pi -e requires <path> — launcher crashes on startup
description:
PROBLEM: PR #365 (xtmux-2dy) implemented curated extension policy as: piArgs.push('--no-extensions'); for each name in [caveman, pi-nvidia-nim, service-skills, worktree-boundary, @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions, pi-guardrails] push '-e', name. But pi's '-e <path>' is a filesystem-path flag, NOT an npm-package or registry name. Pi tries to load '/path/to/cwd/caveman' as an extension file, fails, prints 'Extension path does not exist' errors, exits.

EVIDENCE (2026-07-11 smoke): xt pi --role chain-coordinator launched; pane died before we could inspect. Manual pi invocation with same argv shows: 'Error: Failed to load extension "/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/.xtrm/worktrees/xtmux-xt-pi-obs-redesign/caveman": Extension path does not exist'. Same for all 6 curated entries.

FIX OPTIONS (implementer's call):
A. Drop the curated -e policy entirely. Trust pi's normal discovery from ~/.pi/agent/settings.json (global) + repo .pi/settings.json. Simplest.
B. Resolve names to paths at launcher time (query pi's settings, look up each name, emit -e <full path>).
C. Use --tools allowlist / --exclude-tools denylist for tool-level filtering instead of extension-level curation.

Recommend A — the whole point of pane 2's Batch B (bootstrap) is that pi's global settings already reflect the intended extension set. Duplicating it in launcher argv is fragile.

Also update unit test worktree-session-role.test.ts §'emits --no-extensions and the curated -e allow-list' to match whatever the new policy is.

DISCOVERED_FROM: xtmux-9yz smoke of chain-coordinator launch.
notes: OPERATOR DIRECTION 2026-07-11: drop --no-extensions entirely. Launcher loads all extensions naturally. The 'problematic ones' concern that motivated the curated policy is already resolved upstream in the pi extension work. Fix reduces to: remove piArgs.push('--no-extensions') + the -e loop from buildRoleTmuxPlan. Also delete the 'emits --no-extensions and the curated -e allow-list' unit test — it's now testing the wrong behavior. Trust pi's own extension discovery.

title: bug: message-list scans full event log — 60% CPU hang on 8MB+ files
description:
PROBLEM: message_list in tmux-session-picker does 'while read line; done < <(cat backfiles)' over ALL lines in events.jsonl + all rotated backfiles (~215k lines total in current env). For each line it runs a bash case-match (cheap) but on match runs 5+ sed subshells to extract JSON fields. Result: multi-second hangs burning ~60% CPU. Documented empirically 2026-07-08.

CAUSE: shipped in xtmux-1hq (a0f665f) — I added backfile scanning but did not pre-filter with grep before the read loop.

FIX: pre-filter with 'grep -hF "\"type\":\"message.sent\""' so the while-read loop only iterates matching lines (~150 in current env instead of 215k). Trivial one-line change.

VALIDATION: 'time message-list --unacked' returns in <1s instead of hanging.
close_reason: Fixed by grep pre-filter

description:
## Goal

The /multiplexing skill uses beads for durable task contracts, /tmp prompt files for ephemeral meta-protocol, and send-keys only for single-line pointers.
