title: perf: eliminate subshell overhead via REPLY pattern (warm 500ms → 122ms)
description:
## Context

After xtmux-rib.17 fixed the cache correctness, warm `list` was still ~500ms-1.3s. Profiling (not guessing) found the culprit: `$(paint ...)` and ~12 other hot functions called via command substitution, each costing ~2.4ms per subshell fork. With ~85 paint calls + ~50 other hot-fn subshells per build, that was ~330ms+ of pure fork overhead I introduced.

Proof of concept: render with 2 `$(paint)` = 4.96ms; same with REPLY pattern = 0.04ms (125× faster).

## What was built

Converted 13 hot functions to the bash `REPLY` convention (no subshell):
paint, normalize_agent_state, agent_rank, state_badge, short_path, short_rel_path,
relative_hint, git_root_for_path, status_for_path, status_meta_from_root_status,
render_list_status, pane_location_hint, render_pane_line. Updated all call sites
in build_list, attn_list, preview_session_row, preview_pane_row from `var="$(fn ...)"`
to `fn ...; var="$REPLY"`. Also replaced `$(basename "$x")` with `${x##*/}` and
`$(printf -v)` for the session_col padding.

## Results (measured)

| Path | Before REPLY | After REPLY |
|---|---|---|
| `list` cold | ~843 ms | **484 ms** |
| `list` warm | ~500-1300 ms | **122 ms** (4-10× faster) |
| `ctrl-r` (no cache) | ~845 ms | ~882 ms (git-bound) |
| git calls (warm) | 0 | 0 |
| tmux calls (warm) | 2 | 2 |

Verified: output byte-identical to baseline (list) and to baseline modulo transient
spinner/timer glyphs (preview); agent_state changes still immediate (no staleness
regression from xtmux-rib.17).

## Notes

- The "stale cache" version delivered ~20ms warm but at the cost of correctness
  (frozen agent state). This REPLY refactor keeps correctness AND gets warm to
  ~122ms — perceived as instant (<200ms threshold).
- If 122ms ever feels slow, a structure-cache (rendered rows without badges, agent
  state stamped at render) could target ~30ms warm — but that's a separate task
  and likely unnecessary.

title: tmux binds: attn-jump M-1..5 + jump-back (path-corrected)
description:
## Context

The operator's review draft proposed `bind -n M-1..5` to jump to the Nth waiting pane. Two issues to fix before shipping:
1. **Wrong path** in the draft: `~/.tmux/scripts/tmux-picker.sh` does not exist. Actual picker is `~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker`.
2. **`bind -n M-<digit>` collides** with `Alt+digit` in many TUIs (browser tab switching, shell history, irc clients). Need a conscious decision: root-level (no prefix) vs prefix-gated.

## What to build

- Ship a `tmux.conf` snippet (documented in README + `docs/keys.md`) wiring attn-jump and jump-back:
  ```tmux
  bind -n M-1   run-shell '~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker attn-jump 1'
  bind -n M-2   run-shell '~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker attn-jump 2'
  bind -n M-3   run-shell '~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker attn-jump 3'
  bind -n M-4   run-shell '~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker attn-jump 4'
  bind -n M-5   run-shell '~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker attn-jump 5'
  bind -n M-grave run-shell '~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker jump-back'
  ```
- Decide and document the collision policy (see AC).
- `attn-jump` and `jump-back` already exist in the picker (verified) and bypass the list cache, so targets are always fresh.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Binds use the correct path `~/.local/bin/tmux-session-picker`.
- [ ] `M-1..5` jumps to the Nth waiting pane; `jump-back` returns to the previous pane.
- [ ] Collision policy decided: either (a) root-level `bind -n` with a documented warning about Alt-digit conflicts, or (b) prefix-gated (e.g. `bind 1..5` under prefix) to avoid conflicts. Document the choice.
- [ ] No conflict with existing `bind s/g/G` picker opens or tmux-resurrect keys.
- [ ] README `tmux keys` table updated with the jump binds.

## Approach notes

- `attn_jump()` (picker, ~line 374) calls `attn_list()` which queries `tmux list-panes` directly — fresh, cache-immune.
- For prefix-gated alternative: `bind 1 run-shell '... attn-jump 1'` (note: `bind 1` may already be window-select in some configs — verify against `~/.tmux.conf`).
- Layer: shell (tmux config). Soft-depends on `xtmux-rib.2` (only useful once agents actually write `@agent_state`).
close_reason: Completed: documented root-level M-1..5 attention jumps and jump-back binds with correct tmux-session-picker path, collision policy, and conflict notes.

title: Specialist (sp-*) awareness: detect, enrich preview, feed attention, flag stale/orphan
description:
## Context

Specialist runs open `sp-<role>-<jobhash>` sessions (cmd `bun`). Today they're indistinguishable from any other pane. Verified signals: session-name prefix + alive PID; per-job record at `~/dev/specialists/.specialists/jobs/<hash>/`; `sp ps` reports running/waiting/orphans. Currently `sp ps` shows `orphans=1` with "no active jobs" while two `sp-*` panes are still open — exactly the dead-pane case to surface.

## What to build

- **Detection**: name matches `^sp-<role>-<hash>$` AND `pane_pid` alive. No capture-pane guessing.
- **State mapping**: resolve `<hash>` → job record → `{state, bead_id, role, last_event_time}`; map job state into the existing `running|needs-input|done|idle` taxonomy so specialists feed attention ranking + the `waiting` filter + `attn-jump` as peers of pi/claude.
- **Stale/orphan**: if pane is alive but job record is `done`/missing (or `sp ps` would count it orphan) → badge `[STALE]`/`[ORPHAN]`, rank for cleanup.
- **Preview enrichment**: for `sp-*` sessions/panes, add a header line `job=<hash> bead=<id> role=<name> state=<…>` + a `bd show <id>` line.
- Badge glyph distinct from agents (e.g. `[SP]` prefix on the role).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `sp-*` panes get a specialist badge + role label in the list.
- [ ] A waiting specialist appears in the `waiting` filter and via `attn-jump`.
- [ ] Finished-but-pane-open specialist shows `[STALE]`/`[ORPHAN]`.
- [ ] Specialist preview shows job/bead/role/state + `bd show <id>` line.
- [ ] Detection is name+pid based; no per-tick capture-pane cost.

## Approach notes

- Resolve hash→record lazily and cache per `list`/`preview` pass (same TTL-cache pattern as `list`).
- Tolerate missing job dir (older/ephemeral runs) → fall back to name-derived role + `[UNKNOWN]`.
- Don't hardcode `~/dev/specialists` — derive specialists root from `sp` config / `SPECIALISTS_HOME` if available, else default.
- Layer: integration (reads specialists state dir). Depends-on: t0 (mutates preview/list output).

title: @agent_state hooks: pi/claude/codex write tmux pane option on state transitions
description:
## Context

Today `@agent_state` is empty on all panes, so the picker's entire attention system (badges, attn-jump, WAIT/RUN/DONE sorting) leans on slow capture-pane regex (`TMUX_PICKER_AGENT=1`). This is the keystone: once state is written by the agents themselves, badges become accurate and free, and the perf cache covers the warm path.

⚠️ **BLOCKER:** task `xtmux-rib.17` (cache split) must land first — otherwise the list cache freezes the agent-derived sort/badges for the whole TTL, hiding this work's effect.

## What to build

### Universal contract (shared across agents)
- `~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh <running|needs-input|done|idle|off>` — thin wrapper calling `tmux set -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" @agent_state <state>`.
- Every agent invokes this script at its lifecycle transitions. The picker only cares about the five state strings.

### Claude Code (settings.json hooks — VERIFIED against anthropics/claude-code docs + the operator's live plugin set)
All nine event names are valid: `PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, Notification`.
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh running"}]}],
    "Notification":     [{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh needs-input"}]}],
    "Stop":             [{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh done"}]}],
    "SubagentStop":     [{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh done"}]}],
    "SessionEnd":       [{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh off"}]}]
  }
}
```
- `$TMUX_PANE` is inherited from the pane env, so hooks see it.
- `Notification` = "user notified" (broader than just permission-wait, but in practice it's the WAIT signal — acceptable).
- The operator's `~/.claude/settings.json` already uses `SessionStart`/`PreCompact` in this exact `{matcher, hooks:[{type,command}]}` shape.

### pi (pi-coding-agent) — DIFFERENT ARCHITECTURE, not settings.json
⚠️ Verified in pi's npm docs (`extensions.md`, v0.80.1): **pi has NO settings.json-style hooks.** Zero occurrences of `PreToolUse/PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit/SubagentStop/SessionEnd` in the package. pi uses **TypeScript extensions** subscribing via `pi.on(event, handler)`.

Correct mapping (pi → `@agent_state`):
| pi event | state |
|---|---|
| `before_agent_start` / `agent_start` | `running` |
| `tool_execution_start` / `message_update` | `running` (stay) |
| `agent_end` | `done` |
| `session_start` (reason startup/new/resume) | `idle` |
| `session_shutdown` (reason quit) | `off` |

The extension invokes the shared script via `pi.exec("~/.tmux/scripts/agent-state.sh", ["running"])` (API documented at `extensions.md:1545`).

⚠️ **Known gap — `needs-input` for pi:** there is **no documented pi event** for "awaits permission/input". Permission flow happens in the TUI and isn't exposed as an extension event. Sub-investigation needed: check for an undocumented event, or infer via `ctx.isIdle()` polling, or accept pi can only do running/done/idle/off (not WAIT badge). File as a sub-task if investigation is non-trivial.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agent-state.sh` shipped and `tmux set -p` works from within an agent pane.
- [ ] At least **Claude Code** writes `@agent_state` end-to-end; verify `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id}=[{@agent_state}]'` shows non-empty for the Claude pane.
- [ ] pi extension (separate file under `extensions/`) writes running/done/idle/off via `pi.exec`.
- [ ] Picker WAIT/RUN/DONE badges reflect real Claude transitions without `TMUX_PICKER_AGENT=1`.
- [ ] `attn-jump` and the `waiting` filter surface a Claude pane within ~1s of `Notification`.
- [ ] `docs/agent-state-hooks.md` is copy-pasteable for Claude Code; pi extension install steps documented.
- [ ] Investigate pi `needs-input` gap; document outcome (unsupported / workaround / accepted limitation).

## Approach notes

- States normalized by `normalize_agent_state()` in `bin/tmux-session-picker` — emit the canonical words directly to skip inference.
- Use `set -p` (pane option). Verified: tmux 3.5a has NO `option-changed` hook, so cache invalidation can't be hook-driven → that's why `xtmux-rib.17` splits the cache instead.
- Layer: integration (tmux + Claude Code settings + pi extension).
- Sources: context7 `/anthropics/claude-code` (Claude hook events/semantics); pi npm docs `docs/extensions.md` v0.80.1 (event taxonomy, `pi.exec`).

title: Act-on-preview: send-keys to approve/interrupt/message panes from the list
description:
## Context

Wringling N concurrent agents means attach→respond→detach per pane. The picker already shows who's waiting; let the operator act without attaching.

## What to build

fzf binds (pane rows only; {4} = pane id target) over `tmux send-keys -t <pane>`:
- `ctrl-y` → `send-keys -t {4} y Enter` (approve / yes-to-all waiting agent).
- `alt-i` → `send-keys -t {4} C-c` (interrupt), then `reload`.
- `ctrl-o` → `tmux command-prompt -p 'send:' 'run-shell "tmux send-keys -t {4} %%"'` (ad-hoc line).
- Show a `tmux display-message` toast on action.
- Guard: these binds are no-ops on `session` rows (only pane rows carry a target).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ctrl-y`/`alt-i`/`ctrl-o` act on the highlighted pane and do nothing harmful on session rows.
- [ ] A toast confirms the action; list reloads where state may change.
- [ ] Works when pane is in another session (cross-session send-keys).
- [ ] Binds documented in README.

## Approach notes

- fzf `become`/`execute-silent` + `reload($self list all)` pattern already used by `alt-x`.
- Decide y-vs-yes-to-all per harness; keep `ctrl-y` = single `y Enter`, add `ctrl-Y` for yes-to-all if needed.
- Layer: shell (tmux/fzf wiring). Depends-on: t1 (soft — better with live state, but functional without).

title: xtmux picker v0.2: actionable control surface + specialist awareness
description:
## Overview

Promote the fzf tmux session/pane picker from read-only switcher to an actionable, truthful, create-able control surface — with first-class awareness of specialist (`sp-*`) runs and rich worktree/bead context in previews.

## Goals

- **Truthful state**: agent and specialist states come from written hooks/options, not capture-pane guessing.
- **Act, don't just attach**: approve/interrupt/send-to panes directly from the list.
- **Create flow**: spawn worktree/new sessions from inside the picker.
- **Specialist-aware**: `sp-*` sessions are peers of agents in attention ranking, with job/bead/role enrichment and stale/orphan detection.
- **Safe + observable**: confirm before destructive kills, staleness badges, frecency, cache invalidation.

## Non-goals

- No TUI rewrite (bubbletea/gum). Stay bash + fzf.
- No daemon. No replacing tmux-resurrect.
- No mouse-support work.

## Success criteria

- [ ] `@agent_state` populated by pi/claude/codex hooks; WAIT/RUN/DONE badges reflect real transitions.
- [ ] Act-on-preview: one keystroke to approve / interrupt / send a line to any pane.
- [ ] Create flow: `prefix` + key → fzf over worktrees + recent dirs → new session.
- [ ] `sp-*` sessions show job/bead/role/state; feed attention ranking; stale/orphan panes flagged.
- [ ] All Tier 1/2/3 polish shipped; `test/contract.sh` green.

## Context

- Repo: https://github.com/Jaggerxtrm/xtmux (branch `main`).
- Perf baseline + architecture captured in `docs/perf-audit.md`.
- Status-line script (`scripts/git-pane-status.sh`) output contract must stay byte-identical (also used by the tmux status bar).
- Specialist data verified: session name `sp-<role>-<jobhash>`, cmd `bun`; jobs at `~/dev/specialists/.specialists/jobs/<hash>/`; `sp ps` reports running/waiting/orphans.
notes:
--- Audit 2026-06-30 (pre-implementation review of operator's hook plan) ---

Verified against authoritative sources:
- Claude Code hook events+semantics: context7 /anthropics/claude-code (all 9 event names valid: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, Notification). Confirmed live via operator's plugins (~30k hook refs).
- pi (v0.80.1) npm docs: pi has NO settings.json-style hooks — uses TypeScript extensions via pi.on(event). Correct event mapping added to xtmux-rib.2.
- ⚠️ pi `needs-input` gap: no documented event for awaits-permission. Sub-investigation logged in xtmux-rib.2.

Findings that changed the board:
1. NEW xtmux-rib.17 (P0, cache-split): regression in the perf-audit cache — it freezes agent-derived sort/badges for the TTL. Blocks xtmux-rib.2. tmux 3.5a has no option-changed hook, so must fix structurally.
2. NEW xtmux-rib.18 (P1, attn-jump binds): operator's draft had wrong script path (tmux-picker.sh vs tmux-session-picker) + M-digit collision risk. Path-corrected + collision policy documented.
3. UPDATED xtmux-rib.2: pi section rewritten (extension-based, not settings.json); needs-input gap logged.

Verified-correct (no board change): deliver() send-keys gate (#4), wait-for rendezvous semantics (#5), attn-jump target freshness (bypasses cache).

title: PR #108 remediation: occurrence-aware pane validation + ancestry-preserving fuzzy search
description: Blocking-review remediation on PR #108 (nav topology): (1) rebase xt/xjif onto current origin/main; (2) p:$sid:%pane validation must prove the session+pane OCCURRENCE via session-scoped display-message reading #{session_id}+#{pane_id} (bare %pane lookup cannot validate linked-pane occurrences; tmux -t sid:%pane silently falls back to the session current pane); (3) real-tmux regressions for linked-window pane occurrences (TEST D) incl. foreign-claim refusal; (4) ordinary fuzzy search must be ancestry-preserving: pane match retains parent window+session, window match retains parent session — implemented as chain projection bound to fzf change event (list-active-nav-chain), empty query re-emits flat tree verbatim, fields 1-5 byte-identical; (5) actual fuzzy-query behavior tests (contract §36 + real-tmux TEST E, real fzf --filter); (6) rerun merge-result CI, request final review, DO NOT MERGE. Side fix: wire packages/* as bun workspaces so beautiful-mermaid lands in bun.lock (pre-existing main-side CI break).
notes:
## Remediation round 2 — CI smoke failure (2026-08-18T23:05:32Z)

Root cause: production bug in picker_state_read. Under set -euo pipefail, REPLY=$(<missing-file) raises a redirection error that exits the script even under a caller's '|| true'. Cold CI runner (no state files) => list-active-nav* projections exited before rendering => empty output => §36 dispatcher test failed. Pre-existing on main since the original nav commit.

Fix 42e3e7da: [ -f ] guard in picker_state_read (cold-start returns empty). Regression guard: §36 runs all three dispatcher projections against a clean TMPDIR and asserts non-empty flat output; fails on unfixed picker with exact CI signature, passes with fix.

Local on 42e3e7da: nav-contract 308/0, full verify-json-api.sh PASS. Awaiting CI.


## Remediation round 3 — real-tmux TERM (2026-08-19T00:31:59Z)

After the state-dir fix, CI smoke progressed to nav-real-tmux and failed TEST A:
CI job environments have no TERM set, and tmux attach refuses a terminal it
cannot query ('terminal does not support clear'), so the script-wrapped attach
never produced a client. Fix 21afd41: pin TERM=xterm-256color in start_client

title: fix(xtmux): message-send returns 'coordination backend error' during xt end teardown after cwd deletion
description:
SYMPTOM: xt pi investigator agents consistently see 'xtmux unavailable: coordination backend error; inspect manually' when running xtmux message-send AFTER xt end has torn down their worktree/session-cwd. Observed twice on xt/thinking-row-fix and xt/thinking-toggle-fix teardowns.

REPRO: run any xt pi agent that (1) does work, (2) opens PR, (3) runs xt end which removes worktree + deletes cwd out from under the shell, (4) attempts xtmux message-send to report completion. The message-send fails with the coord backend error.

VERIFIED NOT REPRODUCIBLE from stable sessions — spfix pane self-probe worked cleanly (msg-1786758736).

HYPOTHESIS: xtmux's coord backend reads state (settings? sqlite path? session-meta?) via a cwd-relative or worktree-relative resolution. When xt end deletes the worktree cwd, the backend loses its handle.

INVESTIGATION SCOPE (STRICT):
- xtmux message-send code path
- Coord backend init / open / read layer
- cwd resolution semantics vs worktree deletion race
- xt end sequence — where does it delete cwd relative to hook lifecycle
- Correct fix candidates: (a) resolve backend paths absolutely at load, (b) fall back gracefully if cwd disappears, (c) do the message-send BEFORE xt end deletes cwd (may require xt end reordering — check if xt is core-owned)

DELIVERABLES: root-cause + fix PR to Jaggerxtrm/xtmux. Test: simulate cwd deletion between message-list and message-send.

NON_GOALS: no release, no version bump, no scope expansion. This packet is xtmux coord-backend + message-send only.
notes:
OBSERVED DURING DEMO (2026-08-15 by coordinator): related targeting bug worth investigating alongside the coord-backend error.

REPRO from any session:
  xtmux message-send --to 'spfix:%875' --from test --text 'x' --expects-reply=true
  xtmux message-list --for spfix --json | jq '.[] | select(.senderId=="test") | {target:.recipientId, targetPane:.targetPaneId}'

EXPECTED: {"target":"$560","targetPane":"%875"}
ACTUAL:   {"target":"$560","targetPane":"%962"}  (session-active-pane at send time)

The colon-form 'session:%pane' target is being reduced to just the session; the pane suffix is ignored and delivery goes to whatever pane happens to be active in that session at send time. This means:
- Messages from investigator agents addressed to spfix:%875 are being delivered to a DIFFERENT pane
- The recipient's Stop hook (inbox-reminder-stop.mjs) queries --pane $TMUX_PANE, so the reply never surfaces on the intended target
- This is a routing correctness bug in message-send target parsing, independent of the coord-backend-error-on-teardown

RECOMMEND: either fix the parser to honor the pane part, OR reject 'session:%pane' as invalid and document that clients must pass '%pane' alone.

WORKAROUND for callers now: address the pane directly ('%875') instead of 'session:%pane'.
ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-08-15): The coord DB path is absolute (XDG_STATE_HOME/xtmux/observability.db) — the cwd-relative-resolution hypothesis is REFUTED. The failure is Bun refusing to start from a deleted cwd ('error: The current working directory was deleted'). xt end deletes the worktree that the agent session's cwd points at; the next message-send spawns the obs runtime (node launcher scripts/xtmux-obs.mjs -> bun, or direct bun run) from the deleted cwd and Bun exits 1 before cli.ts executes. FIX: scripts/xtmux-obs.mjs now restores a valid cwd (repo root, else home) before spawning Bun; bin/tmux-session-picker obs_runtime_argv prefers the launcher over direct 'bun run' so every Bun spawn gets the guarantee. SECOND BUG (session:%pane routing): tmux does NOT accept a pane id as the window specifier in session:%N shorthand — 'spfix:%875' parses as session:window, the %875 window lookup fails, and tmux silently falls back to the session's CURRENT window, so #{pane_id} returns the ACTIVE pane (verified: from inside spfix every session:pane form returned the calling/active pane; bare %875 resolves correctly). FIX: message_send now extracts the %N suffix via target_pane_id(), verifies it is a live pane, and passes it as --to-pane. REGRESSION TESTS added to test/contract.sh (deleted-cwd message-send through the full picker chain; session:%pane routing against a tmux mock emulating the misparse). Branch xt/xtmux-coord-fix -> PR to main.
FIX REFINEMENT (2026-08-15): routing all obs calls through the node launcher (obs_runtime_argv launcher-first) BROKE monitor ownership — the launcher spawns bun as a child, so owner_pid (process.pid of the runtime) no longer equals the pid the caller spawned, and SIGTERM to the caller orphans the wait. Final design keeps the original rung order (binary -> bun -> launcher) and wraps the direct-Bun rungs in a pid-preserving exec wrapper: OBS_ARGV=('bash' '-c' 'cd "$1" || exit 1; shift; exec "$@"' xtmux-obs $root <runtime>) — cd restores a valid cwd (Bun refuses deleted cwds), exec keeps the PID and signal delivery. The node launcher rung keeps its internal cwd restore (scripts/xtmux-obs.mjs). Verified: json-coordination 'killed durable wait' passes again; both new contract regressions pass; full bun suite + contract suite clean.
close_reason: Root-caused + fixed both bugs in PR #106 (xt/xtmux-coord-fix): (1) Bun refuses deleted-cwd startup — launcher restores cwd, picker uses cd-then-exec wrapper preserving owner_pid; (2) tmux session:%pane misparse — message_send extracts %N via target_pane_id. Regression tests in test/contract.sh; contract 290/290, bun 415/416 (1 pre-existing). Reported to spfix:%875 (msg-1786770267-2846198).

title: Response episodes: durable episode model for agent_turns (xtmux-9yo follow-up on PR #105)
description: Replace the latest-assistant-message model with durable response episodes so the viewer renders one user prompt + all Claude continuations (hook-block follow-ups) as one unit. Invariant: latest DB row != response. Schema: agent_episodes table + agent_turns.episode_id (migration 0014). Signals: Claude UserPromptSubmit hook opens episode E + records transcript cursor; Stop hook appends candidate A; stop_hook_active continuations append B to SAME episode; next real UserPromptSubmit closes E / opens E+1. Obs-side: agent.episode.open dispatch; agent.turn.done gains episode_open=0|1 (attach vs close+open); lazy-open when no open episode (pi/codex unchanged). Stop hook: prefer input.last_assistant_message (official race-free field; transcript 'isn't guaranteed to include the final message at Stop time'), settle-retry tail read becomes cursor-filtered fallback. Viewer projection: findLatestEpisode + xtmux agent-episode CLI — primary substantive response + substantive follow-ups, short hook acknowledgements collapsed (never replace primary). Keep PR #105 gate: BLOCKED until this lands; #103 must consume the episode projection, not LIMIT 1.
acceptance_criteria: Two Stop hooks of one turn (stop_hook_active) share one episode_id; a new UserPromptSubmit opens a fresh episode; last_assistant_message is preferred over transcript reads; the settle-retry read is cursor-filtered; findLatestEpisode returns primary+followUps+collapsed; agent-episode CLI works; contract+integration+unit tests pass; full gates green.

title: xtmux-view transcript navigation: --list / --turn / --cycle
description: Next increment after PR #103 (v0.1). Data substrate already supports it: agent_turns is append-only per (instance_id, turn_index) with completed_at_ms; store.mjs query already orders (completed_at_ms DESC, id DESC). Proposed shape: (1) xtmux-view --list <target> -> newest N turns (index, local time, first line); (2) xtmux-view --turn <idx|N> <target> -> render a specific turn (same render path); (3) optional --cycle: popup runs a persistent loop that re-renders next/prev turn on n/p keys (requires a tiny key reader in the popup command; glow has no content-switch binding, glow dir-mode file browser is the lazy alternative). No schema change needed.

title: Capture race: Claude Stop hook stores stale last_message_text
description: hooks/claude/claude-agent-turn-capture.mjs reads the transcript at Stop; when Claude Code's async transcript writer has not yet flushed the final assistant line, lastAssistantText() returns the PREVIOUS message. Observed 2026-08-15 on %849 (session $54, transcript 59e01e3f): turn ended 00:03:24.391Z with the brief ('Real status right now: ... Loop is now genuinely...', end_turn, line 2835) but agent_turns row 7902 (02:03:25) stores the older 'Pi alive with the requested model...' (line 2812, 00:02:00Z, stop_reason tool_use). Hook_success Stop attachments at .532Z/.424Z/.666Z confirm the hook ran; only one row was written with stale text. Settled-file read returns the correct text (replica of lastAssistantText verified) -> timing race, not logic bug. Suggested fix: after first read, re-stat/retry for ~1s until file size settles or a newer assistant text appears, then emit. Impact: xtmux-view popup and any agent_turns consumer show a previous message for the latest turn. xtmux-view itself is faithful to the DB (PR #103 acceptance unaffected).
close_reason: Settle retry implemented: readTail() polls every 25ms up to 1s, returns when assistant text advances or size is stable across a full poll gap; turnKey uses settled size+text. Regression test streams the final line mid-run. Gates: contract tests 2+3 pass, full bun test 409 pass (1 pre-existing unrelated fail), nav-contract 91, contract.sh 242, installer 28, tsc clean.

title: K3-xtmux — Adopt byte-identical compatibility links safely
description:
## PROBLEM
The global installer refuses to replace an existing compatibility link target even when the existing regular file is byte-identical to xtmux's managed payload. A prior hand-copied git-pane-status.sh therefore blocks reinstall despite carrying identical content.

## SUCCESS
Teach compatibilityLinks reconciliation to adopt byte-identical existing files through an ownership-safe, content-based path while preserving refusal for foreign or drifted content.

## SCOPE
xtmux installer compatibilityLinks handling, focused fixtures, diagnostics, and idempotence tests.

## NON_GOALS
Do not overwrite foreign files, broaden managed-directory ownership, change Codex hooks.json ownership, or add a destructive force default.

## CONSTRAINTS
Compare content before mutation. Preserve a recoverable or documented transition when replacing an identical file with the managed link. Dry-run must report the exact action. Repeated install must be idempotent.

## VALIDATION
Tests cover identical regular file adoption, foreign-content refusal, symlink target correctness, dry-run, and second-run no-op behavior.

## OUTPUT
A focused K3-xtmux installer hardening change related to the Codex parity adapter but independently reviewable.
close_reason: Compatibility links now adopt byte-identical copies of the packaged script via sha256 comparison, with recoverable .pre-xtmux backup, explicit refusal diagnostics, and a new --dry-run. Drifted content (including our own older revisions) still refuses by design. PR #94 merged; installer 24/24, bun test 370/370, typecheck clean.

title: fix(pkg): drop ./ prefix from bin paths so npm publish keeps the commands
description: npm 11 flags ./-prefixed bin targets as invalid and strips them during publish (verified: bin path './foo.sh' -> 'bin[foo] was invalid and removed'; 'foo.sh' -> clean). package.json uses ./bin/... and ./scripts/... for all 7 bins, so a published @jaggerxtrm/xtmux would install with NO linked commands, breaking xtmux-ro1's success criterion (fresh npm i -g must carry the full surface). Fix: strip the ./ prefix from the 7 bin entries (npm's standard convention; npm pkg fix does exactly this). Pre-publish prerequisite found via npm publish --dry-run.
close_reason: Stripped the ./ prefix from all 7 package.json bin entries (bare relative paths). Verified: jq shows 0 ./ values, npm publish --dry-run reports 0 bin-removal warnings (was stripping all 7 before), live xtmux-events symlink unaffected. Publish will now link every command. Pre-publish prerequisite for xtmux-ro1.

title: topology --json omits host.tmux_server_id, which xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1 requires
description:
Found while validating a live snapshot against the merged Core schema (xtrm-dev/core 92d64eeb) during xtmux #61.

The contract declares host.required = ['host_id','tmux_server_id']. topology_json emits only:
  "host":{"host_id":"..."}

So every snapshot xtmux has ever produced fails schema validation on this one property — predates the lineage work and is unrelated to it. With the agent object now widened, this is the ONLY remaining validation error:
  errors: 1
   - ['host'] 'tmux_server_id' is a required property

docs/xtmux-gaps.md 5.4 already asks to 'make the tmux server identity explicit or derivable', so the intent exists; the emitter never caught up.

Fix options: derive from the tmux socket path/pid (tmux display-message -p '#{pid}' or the socket inode) and emit host.tmux_server_id, OR ask Core to relax it to optional. Prefer emitting — a topology aggregating multiple hosts wants to distinguish two tmux servers on one host.

Deliberately NOT folded into #61, which is additive to the agent object only.

title: Stacked PRs are auto-closed unrecoverably when their base branch is squash-merged
description:
Hit on xtmux #59 (2026-07-22). #59 was stacked on #58's branch xt/wave-8b-xtmux. Squash-merging #58 deleted that branch; GitHub auto-closed #59.

Every repair path is refused:
- gh pr edit 59 --base main -> GraphQL projects-classic deprecation error
- REST PATCH state=open -> 422 'state cannot be changed. The <head> branch was force-pushed or recreated'
- Recreating the base ref then reopening -> same 422. Permanent, not retryable.

Recovery is only: open a NEW PR from the same head, cross-link, lose the review-thread continuity on the old one. Done as #61.

Doctrine fix for the multiplexing/stacked-PR flow: retarget a stacked PR to main BEFORE its parent merges, not after. Marking the child draft (which we did) keeps it out of the merge queue but gives zero protection against base-branch deletion.

Secondary: with the child's review history stranded on a closed PR, a re-review of the replacement can resurface findings already answered — #61 immediately drew a fresh P1 that partly restated known context.

title: Core must widen xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1 agent object for role/worktree/branch/parent_pane_id
description:
xtmux topology --json now publishes agent.role / agent.worktree / agent.branch / agent.parent_pane_id (xtmux-vau).

The schema Core ships in @xtrm/contracts (packages/contracts/schemas/xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1.json) declares "additionalProperties": false on the pane agent object with only 7 properties: instance_id, state, bead_id, task, prompt_file, parent_session_id, last_transition.

Any Core-side validation of an xtmux snapshot will therefore REJECT the new fields. Names were taken from xtrm.topology.projection.v1 (role, worktree, branch, parent_pane_id) so the widening is a straight copy, not a negotiation.

Cross-repo: the change lands in ~/dev/core, not here. Filed from xtmux so the dependency is not lost.
notes: BLOCKING GATE for xtmux PR #61 (replaces #59). Codex raised this as P1 on #61 (r3626934943): merging #61 before Core widens the schema means the aggregation viewer rejects precisely the snapshots carrying the new lineage. Ordering: core PR #479 (fix/xtrm-vtqlg.4-widen-topology-agent, xtrm-dev/core) must merge FIRST, then #61. As of 2026-07-22 #479 is open, CI pending, 1 unresolved thread. The Codex thread on #61 is deliberately left UNRESOLVED so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED until the prerequisite lands. Failure mode is narrower than total: only snapshots with at least one lineage option set fail validation.
close_reason: core PR #479 merged 92d64eeb; widened schema validated against a live lineage-carrying snapshot (0 errors on agent); xtmux #61 merged 125f1e4e

title: feat(telemetry): human-readable event render + metadata convention (slices A+B)
description:
Give the xtmux event journal a richer, Archon-like shape — additive only, V1 NDJSON/TSV output stays the byte-identical default.

Slice A — human renderer: `log tail|query|follow --format human` renders the existing envelope as `LEVEL [ts]: type (duration)` + indented key/value lines. New code path; default output untouched so V1 goldens/contracts hold.

Slice B — metadata convention: standardize payload keys `module`, `level`, `duration_ms`; surface correlation_id as `runId`. Telemetry start/finish/interrupted and agent turn.done envelopes emit `module`+`level` so the human view is rich by default. Additive payload keys only (no type changes; tests assert fields, not whole payloads).

Deferred (not this bead): the cross-domain timeline VIEW keyed on bead/instance/task — build when audit-replay / 'what did this task do' / sre-triage evidence assembly needs it. Generic span columns on event_journal were evaluated and rejected (hierarchy already exists typed; no tree-walk consumer; correlation_id is deliberately not a trace id).
close_reason: Slices A+B implemented and verified: --format human renderer on log tail/query/follow (additive, V1 NDJSON/TSV default untouched) + module/level/duration_ms payload convention emitted by telemetry start/finish/interrupted and agent turn.done. 276 bun tests + 285 contract checks green; live smoke confirms Archon-shaped output. Timeline view deferred by design.

title: installer registers every xtmux hook 3x in ~/.claude/settings.json
description:
Filed from xtrm-tools Wave 6 (core bead xtrm-xus17). Confirmed on the operator machine 2026-07-21 and reproduced by 'xt doctor settings --scope home', which reports 11 duplicate-registration findings, each at 3x.

Every xtmux hook appears three times in ~/.claude/settings.json: one copy tagged {_source:'xtmux', _xtmux:{version,hash}} plus two untagged clones. 33 xtmux registrations total for 11 unique (event, matcher, command) tuples. By contrast the xtrm global block has 19 registrations, each exactly once.

Affected:
  SessionStart / PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop / UserPromptSubmit / Notification / SubagentStop / SessionEnd -> hooks/xtmux/agent-state.sh (x3 each)
  PostToolUse -> auto-monitor-on-send.sh (x3), auto-monitor-consumed.sh (x3)
  Stop -> auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs (x3)

Consequence: agent-state transitions fire three times per event and the auto-monitor drain runs three times per Stop.

Presumed root cause: the installer appends its block without first removing what it previously wrote. The untagged copies predate provenance tagging, so a _source/hash sweep alone will not find them — ownership has to be proven some other way. xtrm-tools solved the equivalent problem with a coverage+hash proof (cli/src/core/legacy-hook-dedupe.ts, PR #464) rather than provenance markers; that shape is worth copying.

OWNERSHIP: the fix belongs here. xtrm-tools deliberately does NOT dedupe this block — it has no ownership rules for another installer's entries. Core ships detection only: 'xt doctor settings' names the owner and points at this bead. Do not expect a Core-side workaround.

title: topology --json agent object omits role/worktree/branch/parent_pane published by Core PR #465
description:
## PROBLEM

`xtmux topology --json` (xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1) exposes a per-pane `agent` object with
instance_id, state, bead_id, task, prompt_file, parent_session_id, last_transition.

Core PR #465 (xtrm-6hey0.1/.2) began publishing four more pane options at launch time:
`@agent_role`, `@agent_worktree`, `@agent_branch`, and `@agent_parent_pane`. The topology
projection does not read them, so every consumer that wants a pane's role, worktree, or
branch must re-query tmux per pane with `show-options` — N extra subprocesses to recover
data the topology walk already had in hand.

Found while building Core's aggregated topology projection (core xtrm-d1fod.3, audit
~/dev/11.md P2-05), which currently works around this with exactly that per-pane
show-options loop.

## SUCCESS

The `agent` object in xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1 carries role, worktree, branch and
parent_pane_id when the corresponding pane options are set, and consumers can drop their
per-pane show-options workaround.

## SCOPE

- The topology projection producer (bash picker `topology --json` path).
- The xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1 schema in @xtrm/contracts — additive optional fields, no
  version bump.
- Bridge relay is verbatim, so it should need no change; confirm.

## NON_GOALS

- Changing existing agent fields or their semantics. `task` keeps carrying
  `role:<name>`; `role` is additive and does not replace it.
- Making any of the new fields required. Bare (non-role) panes legitimately have none of
  them, and a required field would break every non-agent pane.
- Reading pane content. Unrelated surface.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Additive only: omit absent metadata rather than emitting empty strings, matching the
  schema's existing "omits absent agent metadata" rule.
- snake_case, consistent with the rest of the schema.
- Core must keep working against the current shape until this lands; the consumer-side
  workaround is a fallback, not a hard dependency.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xtmux topology --json` on a host with a live `--role` coordinator pane shows the
      four new fields populated.
- [ ] A bare pane shows the agent object without them (omitted, not empty).
- [ ] Schema validation passes for both cases.

## OUTPUT

The updated schema fields, sample topology output for a role pane and a bare pane, and a
note to core xtrm-d1fod.3 that the per-pane show-options workaround can be retired.

## REFERENCES

- Core PR #465 (c978d010) — publishes the pane options.
- Core epic xtrm-d1fod, child xtrm-d1fod.3 — the consumer.
- Audit ~/dev/11.md P2-05.

title: Enrich host-wide xtmux session event stream
description:
PROBLEM: scripts/test-session-events.sh follows only one tmux session and emits sparse journal metadata. Operators want one stream for every open session on the host, including readable repository/session/agent context.
SCOPE: Update only scripts/test-session-events.sh to follow all xtmux major events and specialist job.started events, enrich output from xtmux topology/dashboard metadata, and retain clean shutdown behavior.

title: extend serena_orphan_killer to cover 'bun sp run executor/debugger' orphans
description:
## PROBLEM

Discovered 2026-07-20: 22 orphan bun processes running \`sp run executor/debugger\` from Jul 14 (r6g sprint), all with PPID=1 (parent tmux panes gone), consuming ~1Gi RAM. The existing reap cron script (\`/home/dawid/projects/mercury/infra/scripts/serena_orphan_killer.sh\`, cron */30) targets ONLY \`serena start-mcp-server\` processes — the bun sp orphans slip through and accumulate indefinitely.

Same root cause as serena reap: specialist processes spawned inside a tmux pane don't get reaped when the pane/orchestrator dies. But sp children have different process signatures (\`bun ... sp run executor|debugger --bead <id>\`), so the serena-scoped script doesn't match them.

## SUCCESS

- A companion or extended reap script kills orphan \`bun.*sp run (executor|debugger)\` processes with PPID=1 and etime > threshold (e.g., 6h — same default as serena)
- Cron entry runs it periodically (either extend the existing */30 slot or add a sibling entry)
- Logged to \`\$HOME/.local/state/sp-orphan-killer.log\` for observability

## SCOPE

Two options:

**A (small, additive)**: create \`serena_orphan_killer_sp.sh\` sibling in \`mercury/infra/scripts/\` mirroring serena_orphan_killer.sh structure; add cron line to run it \`*/30\`. ~40 LOC.

**B (unify)**: refactor \`serena_orphan_killer.sh\` to a generic \`orphan_killer.sh --pattern <regex>\` that reads a config listing which patterns to reap; invoke twice (or from cron with different args). ~60 LOC + config file.

Option A wins on ponytail (no abstraction until second reason to unify).

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT reap active pane children (PPID != 1) — only orphans
- Do NOT touch active worktrees/beads state — reaping is process-level only, storage/DB left alone
- Do NOT enable dry-run by default — mirror serena script's ergonomics

## VALIDATION

- Manual: create 2 test orphan processes, run script with 0s threshold + dry-run, verify only matched patterns land
- After 30-min cron cycle: log shows accurate report of what was reaped or "no-op"

## Related

Discovered while cleaning up post-r6g sprint. Root cause of the accumulation: previous session did not kill children when killing tmux panes (that itself is a xtrm/xtmux behavior gap — separate bead: consider making \`xt end\` / worktree remove kill child sp processes too).

title: integrate xtmux monitor-agent wakes with Claude Code task-notification pipeline
description:
## PROBLEM

`xtmux monitor-agent <target>` fires its wake via a tmux-side mechanism (marker file / picker signal / send-keys internal) designed for a live operator watching the picker or a monitor pane. When the caller is a Claude Code session, the wake never reaches the Claude Code harness — `wakeDelivered=true, wakeConsumed=false` forever, and no `<task-notification>` message appears in the model's next turn.

Concrete evidence 2026-07-18: monitor `monitor-1784387505920-484533` on pane `%6185` (audit worker), pane went `running → done` in ~92s, `xtmux monitor-list --json` confirmed `terminalStatus=process_gone, wakeDelivered=true, wakeConsumed=false`. Operator asked ~24h later why no notification arrived. Zero telemetry surfaced the silent drop.

Claude Code today receives task-notifications ONLY from:
- `Bash` tool with `run_in_background: true` — process exit fires the harness pipeline
- `Monitor` harness tool — stdout lines are events

xtmux monitor-agent is invisible to both channels. Any orchestrator flow that arms an xtmux monitor and expects Claude Code to pick it up will silently miss the wake.

## Environmental facts (verified 2026-07-19)

- Claude Code exposes these env vars into subprocesses: `CLAUDECODE=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=<uuid>`, `CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID=<session_id>`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli`, `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1` when applicable.
- Claude Code hook events (from `.claude/settings.json` and `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` schemas): `SessionStart`, `SessionStart:compact`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `Notification`, `PreCompact`. `UserPromptSubmit` fires at each turn boundary and can emit `additionalContext`, which the model sees as an injected system-reminder.
- Claude Code has NO documented push API for external processes to inject notifications mid-turn. Any external integration must ride an existing hook event boundary.
- No `auto-wake` / `autoWake` symbol currently exists in `/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/src` (2026-07-19 grep); V2 auto-wake references in prior docs may refer to correlated-reply flow, not a Claude-Code-facing primitive.

## SUCCESS

`xtmux monitor-agent <target>` invoked from inside a Claude Code session (detectable via `CLAUDECODE=1`) results in a `<task-notification>` reaching the model's next turn when the target leaves working state, WITHOUT changing existing operator-picker semantics.

Verification round-trip:
1. Claude Code session A invokes `xtmux monitor-agent <target>`
2. Target flips `working → done`
3. Session A's next `UserPromptSubmit` turn contains a system-reminder describing the wake (target, terminal status, timestamp) — same shape as the existing `<task-notification>` messages

Existing operators (picker, monitor pane, non-Claude-Code callers) see zero behavior change.

## THREE PROPOSALS + FEASIBILITY VERDICTS

### Proposal A — queue file + UserPromptSubmit hook (RECOMMENDED)

**Design**:
1. `xtmux monitor-agent`, when it detects `CLAUDECODE=1` in its env at registration time, ADDITIONALLY writes wake events to a per-Claude-Code-session queue: `~/.xtrm/wake-queue/<CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID>.jsonl` (append-only, one JSON line per wake).
2. Wake event shape: `{"ts":<ms>,"monitorId":"...","target":"%6185","terminalStatus":"process_gone","startedAtMs":...}` — enough for the model to identify which worker finished.
3. New Claude Code hook file shipped in `xtmux` package (or added to `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` template): a `UserPromptSubmit` hook that reads the queue, emits each pending wake as `additionalContext`, then truncates the queue.
4. Hook script location: `xtmux/scripts/claude-code-drain-wakes.mjs`. Registered via `hooks.json` entry:
   ```json
   { "UserPromptSubmit": [{ "matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{"type":"command","command":"node /path/to/scripts/claude-code-drain-wakes.mjs $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"}] }] }
   ```
5. Hook exits 0 with `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"<drained wakes as text>"}}` on stdout.

**Feasibility**: HIGH. All primitives already exist. Zero changes to Claude Code core. Additive to xtmux (~30 LOC).
**Cost**: 20 LOC in xtmux monitor-agent (env detect + queue write) + ~50 LOC drain script + hooks.json entry.
**Tradeoffs**: One turn of latency (wake surfaces at next turn boundary, not instantly). Acceptable for the typical "worker finished, tell the orchestrator" case.

### Proposal B — Claude Code push API (external mid-turn injection)

**Design**: xtmux monitor-agent detects the Claude Code session, resolves the session's IPC endpoint, PUSHES the notification mid-turn (same delivery as internal `<task-notification>`).

**Feasibility**: LOW without changes to Claude Code core. Verified 2026-07-19:
- Claude Code has no documented external push endpoint. Hooks are REACTIVE (fire on Claude Code events); MCP is a client-server pattern where Claude Code is the client.
- The internal task-notification pipeline is driven by the `Bash run_in_background` and `Monitor` tools' process/stream lifecycle — the harness reads their state, no external API accepts injections.
- Options to enable: (a) Claude Code adds a "push" endpoint / socket for external callers — a real feature ask on the Claude Code side, out of xtmux scope; (b) xtmux ships an MCP server that Claude Code polls, but polling by Claude Code is turn-boundary anyway — collapses to Proposal A.

**Verdict**: NOT FEASIBLE from the xtmux side alone. Would require Claude Code to expose external push capability. File a separate ask upstream if wanted; do not block on it here.

### Proposal C — Claude-Code-detecting wrapper using run_in_background semantics

**Design**: `xtmux monitor-agent` detects `CLAUDECODE=1` and forks a shell process that:
1. Polls the target's `@agent_state` at the requested interval
2. Exits with code 0 when the target leaves working state, or non-zero on timeout
3. Because it's a forked bash process invoked FROM WITHIN Claude Code's Bash tool context (with `run_in_background: true` semantics), its exit triggers the Claude Code task-notification pipeline natively

**Feasibility**: MEDIUM. Requires the caller to be `Bash(run_in_background:true)` OR requires xtmux monitor-agent to somehow enroll the child process INTO Claude Code's task pipeline retroactively. The second half is the hard part: Claude Code's harness attaches to the Bash tool's PIDs at invocation time; a fork from a normal `xtmux monitor-agent` shell command doesn't get enrolled.

Concrete constraint: `run_in_background: true` is a property of the Bash TOOL CALL, not of the child process. The tool call must originate from the model. `xtmux monitor-agent` is invoked as a foreground command, its stdout returns, done — no run_in_background envelope.

Workable variant: **xtmux monitor-agent-cc** — a new command that PRINTS a bash script the operator/model should invoke via Bash+run_in_background. Model runs:
```bash
xtmux monitor-agent-cc <target> --timeout Nm | bash
```
where the printed script does the polling and exits when target flips.

**Verdict**: FEASIBLE but changes the calling shape — operators must use the new command via the Bash tool with run_in_background. Does not replace `xtmux monitor-agent` for picker/operator use; it's an additional primitive optimized for Claude Code invocation. Cost: ~40 LOC + docs update.

**Advantage over A**: no queue file, no hook state, notification fires instantly (as soon as target flips), and the exit code carries the status. No turn-boundary latency.
**Disadvantage vs A**: caller must remember to use the new command + Bash+run_in_background pattern. Existing xtmux monitor-agent calls silently keep failing on Claude Code (unless we also add a warning stderr when we detect CLAUDECODE and no --for-picker flag).

### Recommended path

**Ship both A and C**:
- **A** covers "operator already invoked xtmux monitor-agent, wants Claude Code to see the wake at next turn" — the common accidental case that bit us today. Additive, no calling-shape change.
- **C** covers "operator explicitly wants instant push-into-Claude-Code notification" — the new intentional primitive. Explicit shape, zero latency.
- **B** is filed as an upstream ask to Claude Code, tracked separately if pursued at all.

Order: A first (fixes the silent-drop bug today), C second (adds the new primitive).

## SCOPE

- `/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/src/commands/monitors.ts` — env detection at register time, additional queue-file write
- New: `/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/src/domains/monitors/claude-code-queue.ts` — queue writer + drainer helpers
- New: `/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/scripts/claude-code-drain-wakes.mjs` — UserPromptSubmit hook drain script
- `.xtrm/config/hooks.json` template in xtmux — add UserPromptSubmit entry (opt-in)
- Docs: `docs/monitors.md` (or equivalent) — new section "Consuming wakes from Claude Code"
- Proposal C only: new command `src/commands/monitor-agent-cc.ts` + tests

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT modify Claude Code core in this bead
- Do NOT change existing `xtmux monitor-agent` calling shape or defaults — additive only
- Do NOT block on Proposal B (Claude Code push API) — separate ask, out of scope here
- Do NOT unify with xtmux V2 correlated-reply flow — different mechanism, different consumers

## CONSTRAINTS

- Queue file path per-Claude-Code-session — do not mix wakes from multiple concurrent sessions
- Truncate queue atomically in the hook drain (rename-and-replace pattern) to avoid lost wakes if the hook runs concurrently with a new monitor firing
- Preserve existing operator-picker semantics — the picker still shows monitor rows and their terminal status
- Do not require Claude Code to be installed to build/run xtmux (env detection must gracefully no-op when CLAUDECODE unset)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `CLAUDECODE=1 xtmux monitor-agent <target>` writes to `~/.xtrm/wake-queue/$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID.jsonl` when target flips
- [ ] `xtmux monitor-agent <target>` without CLAUDECODE writes nothing to the queue dir (opt-in via env)
- [ ] UserPromptSubmit hook drain script emits `additionalContext` with the wake payload
- [ ] End-to-end: in a Claude Code session, invoke `xtmux monitor-agent %pane`, cause pane to flip working→done, on the NEXT user prompt turn a system-reminder appears with the wake details
- [ ] Existing xtmux monitor-agent regression tests pass unchanged
- [ ] New tests: queue writer, queue drainer, atomic truncate, no-op when CLAUDECODE unset
- [ ] For Proposal C: `xtmux monitor-agent-cc <target> | bash` invoked via `Bash(run_in_background:true)` exits when target flips, task-notification appears with exit code

## OUTPUT

Two PRs against xtmux (one per proposal), or one bundled PR with both, plus a docs section explaining when to use each. If Proposal B is pursued upstream, file the ask against Claude Code separately and link here.

title: W6 core: enable --prompt/--model/--thinking on xt claude|pi WITHOUT --role
description:
Enable `--prompt`, `--model`, `--thinking` (and probably `--skill`) on `xt claude` and `xt pi` WITHOUT requiring `--role`. Approved by orchestrator per user request 2026-07-17.

## SCOPE

/home/dawid/dev/core/  (xt/xtrm-cli). Fresh feature branch off origin/main.

## Problem statement

Today `xt claude --no-attach` errors: "Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print". And `--prompt` / `--model` / `--thinking` are guarded by:
`✗ --model / --thinking / --skill / --prompt / -- passthrough require --role`

This blocks the natural multiplexing pattern of "spawn a fresh general-purpose xt claude/pi in a detached tmux session with a specific initial prompt and model". Operators have to fall back to raw `tmux new-session -d -s foo claude` bypassing xt's worktree + session-meta setup.

## Requirement

- `xt claude <name> --prompt <text> [--model <m>] [--thinking <t>] [--skill <s>...]` works WITHOUT `--role`
- `xt pi <name> --prompt <text> [--model <m>] [--thinking <t>] [--skill <s>...]` works WITHOUT `--role`
- `--no-attach` combined with `--prompt` launches detached tmux session with the prompt fed as initial input
- Behavior stays the same when `--role` is present (specialist path unchanged)

## Design (draft — validate with codebase reality)

Likely lives in `cli/src/**/claude.ts` and `cli/src/**/pi.ts` (or equivalent command modules). Look for the guard message text `require --role`.

Split into two knobs:
1. Role-only flags (kept): `-- passthrough`, anything that depends on `sp view <name>` (specialist model/thinking merge)
2. Role-optional flags (relaxed): `--prompt`, `--model`, `--thinking`, `--skill`

For non-role launch:
- `--prompt <text>` → written to a temp file, fed to claude/pi as `--print`/prompt file on cold boot inside detached tmux
- `--model <name>` → forward as `claude --model` / `pi --model`
- `--thinking <level>` → warn-and-drop for claude (no such flag) as it already does with role; forward for pi
- `--skill <name>` → append to skill autoload list (may or may not be supported without role — investigate)

## Validation

- `xt claude test1 --no-attach --prompt "echo hi"` creates detached session; pane shows claude with the prompt processing
- `xt pi test2 --no-attach --prompt "echo hi" --model openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna` creates detached session on that model
- `xt pi test3 --role executor --prompt "..."` still works (role path)
- `xt claude test4` (no prompt, attached) still works

## Constraints

- Ponytail: smallest diff. Relax the guard only for the fields listed. Do not restructure the whole launch pipeline.
- Small PR. Include a test if the existing suite has command-level tests; skip if it doesn't.
- No new deps.

## Deliverables

- PR on xtrm-cli core repo
- Bead closed with the PR link and a one-line usage example for the new capability

description:
Layer: boundary (NDJSON protocol over stdio/SSH)
Strategy: protocol contract tests driving the bridge as a subprocess + one real `ssh localhost` smoke
Covers: xtmux-j46.9

## PROBLEM

The bridge is the remote attack surface. A crash on a malformed frame is a DoS, an unbounded frame is a memory bomb, and a mutation that slips past read-only mode is remote code effect on the operator's live panes.

## SCOPE

test/contract.sh (bridge cases), test/lib/ (NDJSON client driver).

## SUCCESS / assertions required

- [ ] Handshake: bridge.hello returns schema_version xtrm.xtmux.bridge.v1, host_id, and the negotiated capability list.
- [ ] Parity: topology.snapshot / journal.query / pane.capture / health.get return the SAME payload as their local CLI counterparts for the same input (assert equality, not shape).
- [ ] journal.follow over the bridge honors the same cursor semantics (no duplicates on reconnect).
- [ ] Read-only rejection: every mutation method name (pane.input, message.send, message.ack, handoff.send, monitor.register) is rejected with a structured error AND has no side effect (assert DB + pane state unchanged).
- [ ] No exec: there is no method that executes an arbitrary command — assert the method table is a fixed allowlist.
- [ ] Framing: oversized line/frame -> structured error; process still alive and answers the next request.
- [ ] Framing: malformed JSON -> structured error; process still alive.
- [ ] Bounds: an unbounded query (no limit) is clamped, not streamed unbounded.
- [ ] Request ids: responses correlate to request ids; notifications carry explicit event method names.
- [ ] Lifecycle: graceful EOF and cancellation exit 0.
- [ ] Scoping: every returned resource id is scoped by the bridge's host_id.

title: Read-only xtmux bridge --stdio (NDJSON, capability-negotiated)
description:
## PROBLEM

An Electron/Console viewer needs to observe remote xtmux hosts. There is no bounded remote surface today, and shipping an unrestricted remote shell or a bespoke SSH stack would be a security regression (gaps doc 7).

## SUCCESS

`ssh <host-alias> xtmux bridge --stdio` speaks newline-delimited JSON with request ids and capability negotiation: bridge.hello returns schema_version xtrm.xtmux.bridge.v1, host_id and the capability list. Read-only methods topology.snapshot, journal.query, journal.follow, pane.capture and health.get work; every mutation is rejected. Malformed requests are answered with an error, not a crash. Reconnect = topology refresh + last committed journal cursor.

## SCOPE

bin/tmux-session-picker (`bridge` dispatch), new bridge module in src/ (framing, schema validation, method table), docs (protocol + deployment), test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- Mutating methods (pane.input, message.send, message.ack, handoff.send, monitor.register) — separately permissioned, separately reviewed, later PR.
- Implementing an SSH stack, storing keys, or storing credentials: the system OpenSSH client and the user's ~/.ssh/config own transport.
- A long-running daemon.
- A second database or a second event schema — the bridge only reads existing contracts.

## CONSTRAINTS

- NO arbitrary command execution method, ever.
- Enforce maximum line/frame size and bounded result sizes; oversized frames are a structured error.
- Validate every request against a versioned schema; unknown methods -> structured error.
- A malformed request must not terminate the process unless framing is unrecoverable.
- stdout is protocol-only; stderr is bounded diagnostics only.
- Read-only mode rejects every mutation EVEN IF the local xtmux binary supports it.
- All resource ids are scoped by the bridge's host_id.
- Depends on .3 (topology), .4 (pane capture), .5/.6 (journal query/follow).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: bridge.hello returns the negotiated capability list and host_id.
- [ ] Contract test: each read-only method returns the same payload as its local CLI counterpart.
- [ ] Contract test: a mutation method name in read_only mode is rejected with a structured error and no side effect.
- [ ] Contract test: oversized frame and malformed JSON -> error response, process still alive and answering the next request.
- [ ] Contract test: cancellation and graceful EOF exit 0.
- [ ] Contract test: reconnect (topology refresh + --after-id resume) yields no duplicate journal items.
- [ ] Smoke: `ssh localhost xtmux bridge --stdio` handshake succeeds with no credentials stored by the client.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, a recorded handshake + read-only rejection transcript, and the SSH deployment note.

- Impact: Read-only bridge not security boundary. Credential intended for viewer grants remote mutation/shell.

- Verification after fix: Dedicated bridge key succeeds handshake; same key rejects `ssh host id`, mutation commands, PTY, forwarding.

### S-02 — High — Unlimited `journal.follow` requests create unbounded DB poll loops

- Category/CWE: CWE-400, uncontrolled resource consumption.
- Evidence: `src/bridge/serve.ts:27,35-63,80-95`. Every distinct request ID creates timer loop. No per-connection follow cap, request quota, or minimum interval. Each loop opens DB every 500 ms at `41-56`.

- Impact: CPU, timer, SQLite connection, file-descriptor pressure. Bridge session can degrade host.
- Recommended fix: Cap active follows per connection, preferably one; reject excess with structured `XTMUX_BRIDGE_RESOURCE_LIMIT`. Add lifecycle timeout and test cap/cancellation cleanup.
- Verification after fix: Send cap+1 follows; excess rejected; DB-open rate stays bounded; cancel frees slot.

### S-03 — Medium — stdout ignores backpressure; replies/results lack bridge byte cap

- Category/CWE: CWE-400.
- Evidence: `src/bridge/serve.ts:22-24` calls `out.write()` without checking return/drain. `src/bridge/stdio.ts:181-193` returns journal pages capped only by row count. `src/bridge/stdio.ts:166-169` relays full topology. `src/domains/events/page.ts:148-162` has no payload/result byte cap.

- Impact: Remote peer causes bridge memory growth. Violates bounded-result requirement.
- Recommended fix: Pause input while output backpressures; await `drain`; enforce response byte ceiling for topology/journal/follow and emit structured size error or pagination truncation.

title: Add xtmux log follow --after-id (committed-event stream)
description:
## PROBLEM

Polling the journal page endpoint works but adds latency and load for a live viewer. Gaps doc 6.4 allows a follow stream, but only once page semantics are proven — a premature stream would fork the event schema.

## SUCCESS

`xtmux log follow --after-id 1843 --json` writes one committed journal item per line, in the same envelope as `log query` items. On reconnect the consumer resumes from its last materialized journal_id with no duplicates and no gaps. Graceful EOF and SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown.

## SCOPE

src/cli-log.ts, src/domains/events/query.ts (tail-follow read), bin/tmux-session-picker (`log follow` dispatch + help), docs, test/contract.sh.

## NON_GOALS

- A websocket/HTTP server.
- Push semantics as an authority: notifications are hints; the consumer advances its cursor only from committed rows.

## CONSTRAINTS

- MUST NOT introduce a second event schema — items are byte-identical in shape to `log query` items.
- Only committed rows are emitted; never emit before commit.
- Blocks on .5 — the page contract must be merged and stable first.
- Bounded backlog on start: replays from --after-id, never dumps unbounded history without a cursor.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: follow from a cursor, emit N events concurrently, assert every one arrives exactly once in ascending id order.
- [ ] Contract test: kill + restart follow at the last received id -> zero duplicates, zero gaps.
- [ ] Contract test: item shape is identical to a `log query` item for the same journal_id.
- [ ] Contract test: SIGTERM exits 0 with a flushed stream.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, reconnect-without-duplicates evidence.
close_reason: merged as #32: log follow --after-id, NDJSON of committed journal items reusing the journalPage envelope (no second schema). Cursor advances only after write; SIGTERM exits 0; refuses to stream without a cursor. Review caught --after-id=N being rejected — fixed in the shared log arg parser. 235 contract pass / 0 fail.

title: monitor-list crashes with raw SQLiteError on a fresh observability DB
description:
## PROBLEM

On a brand-new observability DB, monitor-list dumps a raw SQLite stack trace instead of an empty result:

  $ XDG_STATE_HOME=$(mktemp -d) XTMUX_OBS_V2=1 xtmux monitor-list --json
  SQLiteError: no such table: monitors
      at prepare (unknown)
      at prepare (bun:sqlite:345:37)

Sibling commands on the same fresh DB behave correctly — unread-count returns {"recipientId":"%1","unreadCount":0,"oldestUnackedAtMs":null}. So the messages tables are created on init (or lazily) and the monitors table is not; it appears only once a monitor is armed.

Impact: a fresh machine (or any new XDG_STATE_HOME) running 'xtmux monitor-list' before ever arming a monitor gets a stack trace, not '[]'. In --json mode this violates the documented error contract (stdout must be empty and stderr must carry one {code,message,detail} object; exit codes are defined, 3 = structured storage/schema failure). A raw SQLiteError is neither.

## SUCCESS

monitor-list on a fresh DB returns an empty list (human: nothing; --json: []), or fails with the documented {"code":"XTMUX_..."} envelope and the right exit code. No raw SQLite traces reach the user in any mode.

## CONTEXT

Found while capturing live --json field shapes for xtmux-d0a.15 (the help surface). Not caused by .15 and not fixed there. Likely the same family as the .14 finding: paths that only worked because an existing machine had state that a fresh install does not.
notes:
ORCHESTRATOR REPRO (main 6f20973): confirmed. `XDG_STATE_HOME=$(mktemp -d) XTMUX_OBS_V2=1 xtmux monitor-list --json` → exit 1 with a raw 'SQLiteError: no such table: monitors' + bun stack trace. It does fail loudly (exit 1, not 0 — an earlier read of exit 0 was a pipeline artifact), so this is not a silent-corruption path.

SHARPER FRAMING: this now VIOLATES A DOCUMENTED CONTRACT. d0a.15 (merged, ad304ee) makes xtmux help state: 'Errors are exit 2 with a usage line; under --json they are {"code":"XTMUX_...","message":...}'. A raw SQLiteError stack is neither. So the fix is not cosmetic — the JSON error contract we just published to every agent is already untrue for at least one command.

Fix should either migrate-on-demand (fresh DB → empty array, which is the honest answer: there ARE no monitors) or emit the typed XTMUX_* JSON error. Blast radius check: message-list/unread-count/audit do NOT crash on a fresh DB, so monitor-list looks isolated — but a contract test should assert the typed-error shape across every --json command on a fresh DB, not just this one, or the next command to miss it ships the same way.
close_reason: Fixed: monitor/telemetry/audit arm now calls migrate() like message-*. The 'hot path cannot afford migrate()' premise was measured false (79ms migrating vs 94ms not). Regression test tests/contracts/fresh-db.test.ts is table-driven over the shared dispatch arm; 2/3 assertions fail without the fix. PR pending on branch xt/d0a21-migrate.

title: Adopt 'xtmux' prefix in multiplexing skill prose (source: ~/dev/core)
description:
## PROBLEM

The skills read `tmux-session-picker <cmd>` throughout — a legacy binary name that does not
match the product. Once xtmux-d0a.14 lands the `xtmux` alias, the prose should say `xtmux`.

CRITICAL, and the reason this is its own bead: these skills are xtrm-MANAGED assets. The
deployed copies under `~/.xtrm/skills/default/**/SKILL.md` carry a managed marker and are
REGENERATED by `xt update --apply`. Their source of truth is a DIFFERENT REPO:
`~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/**/SKILL.md`. Editing the deployed copy is silently reverted —
this exact class of failure hit the operator earlier the same day, when a regenerated managed
hook block reintroduced a stale `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` path and blocked every tool in the session.

## SUCCESS

The multiplexing skill family reads `xtmux …` instead of `tmux-session-picker …`, changed at
the `~/dev/core` source so it survives `xt update --apply`, and shipped through core's normal
release. Nothing breaks if the change is partial or delayed, because the old name still works.

## SCOPE

In `~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/`:
- `multiplexing/SKILL.md` (647 lines, 47 CLI invocations)
- `multiplexing-team/SKILL.md` (352 lines, 27 invocations)
- `pr-reviewer/SKILL.md` (3), `deploy-monitor/SKILL.md` (5), `using-specialists/SKILL.md` (1)
- ~85 occurrences across 6 files total.

## NON_GOALS

- The ~1,400 occurrences across 153 files in OTHER repos under ~/dev. They keep working via the
  compatibility name; migrating them is attrition, not a project.
- Renaming subcommands (see xtmux-d0a.14 NON_GOALS).
- Restructuring the skills. Prose substitution only — no dual-path text, no harness fork. Both
  consult panes rejected those unanimously.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Edit at the `~/dev/core` source ONLY. A change to `~/.xtrm/skills/**` is not a change.
- Blocked by xtmux-d0a.14: do not document a command prefix that does not exist yet.
- Purely non-breaking. The old name keeps working, so this can land late without gating anything.
- Cross-repo: lands via a `~/dev/core` PR and its release cycle, not through this repo.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `grep -rc 'tmux-session-picker' ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/` returns 0 for the six
      files in SCOPE.
- [ ] After `xt update --apply`, the deployed `~/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md`
      shows `xtmux` — proving the change was made at the source and survived regeneration. This
      is the whole point of the bead; without it, the work is silently undone.
- [ ] Every command example in the changed prose actually runs as written under `xtmux`.

## OUTPUT

The ~/dev/core PR link, the grep counts before/after, and confirmation that a post-`xt update`
deployed copy still reads `xtmux`.
close_reason: core PR #411 merged (7dadbc24). Five skills migrated to the xtmux prefix at the SOURCE (~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/): multiplexing, multiplexing-team, pr-reviewer, deploy-monitor, code-review — 0 tmux-session-picker occurrences remain, 49 xtmux invocations in multiplexing alone. Verified the deployed copy still reads xtmux after 'xt update --apply' (46 -> 0), proving the edit was made at the source and survives regeneration — the trap this bead existed for. using-specialists/SKILL.md (1 occurrence) is vendored from the specialists repo with a pinned hash; editing it in core failed the vendor-freshness check, so it was dropped from the PR and moved to a follow-up bead (xtmux-d0a.22).

title: Roll out native tools, document migration, and measure prompt/runtime cost
description:
## PROBLEM

Even correct tools can regress workflows if loaded twice, activated indiscriminately, undocumented, or materially increase prompt/runtime cost. The final rollout must make native tools the preferred Pi path while preserving CLI/Bash fallback and operator understanding.

## SUCCESS

Project settings load the extension exactly once, selected tools are active by default for trusted xtmux sessions, documentation maps CLI↔JSON↔tool actions, and measured startup/prompt/command overhead stays within agreed bounds. Bash compatibility remains available with a documented deprecation decision rather than silent removal.

## SCOPE

- `.pi/settings.json`/extension load wiring, tool activation metadata and `/reload` workflow.
- `docs/observability-redesign.md` or focused native-tools document, README/help references.
- Benchmark/smoke evidence and optional changelog entry.

## NON_GOALS

- Removing CLI or Bash compatibility in this release.
- Publishing MCP/npm packages.
- New tool actions outside the classified matrix.

## CONSTRAINTS

- One extension registration path; reload/session replacement must not duplicate handlers/tools/timers.
- Document V2 default-on and explicit V1 fallback accurately.
- Set a measured prompt schema budget and startup/tool-call latency budget from baseline; optimize only if breached.
- Rollout evidence records counts/durations/tool names only; no prompts, message bodies or secrets.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fresh startup and three `/reload` cycles retain exactly one copy of each tool/handler.
- [ ] Tool catalog/help matches implemented action schemas and exclusions.
- [ ] CLI fallback examples still work and no-flag/V1 fixtures remain green.
- [ ] Prompt token/schema size, startup latency and p95 tool-wrapper overhead are compared to baseline.
- [ ] Full JSON and Pi E2E gates pass on the final installed configuration.
- [ ] Documentation names rollback/disable procedure and residual MCP work.

## OUTPUT

Rollout commit, documentation links, installed tool inventory, performance/prompt-cost table, final E2E evidence, rollback instructions and epic-close readiness report.

title: Implement Pi sessions, handoffs, and observability tools
description:
## PROBLEM

After the coordination pilot, Pi still needs Bash/TSV for session inventory, hygiene, handoffs and operational inspection. Those workflows should consume the validated JSON API without exposing interactive renderer internals or unsafe raw mutation access.

## SUCCESS

Domain-grouped native tools provide approved session inventory/control, handoff lifecycle, and observability query/actions with typed schemas/results, compact rendering and guarded destructive operations. Tool count and prompt metadata remain bounded.

## SCOPE

- `xtmux_sessions`, `xtmux_handoffs`, `xtmux_observability` definitions using the shared framework.
- Approved actions from the command classification matrix: read-only list/inspect/audit/health plus bounded switch/interrupt/handoff/telemetry actions.
- Confirmation policies, result renderers and focused tests/docs.

## NON_GOALS

- fzf/popup/filter/preview UI as LLM tools.
- Database migrations, retention, shadow internals, install-hooks or arbitrary tmux send-keys.
- MCP packaging.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Read-only actions may run in all modes; switch/interrupt/kill-like actions fail closed without explicit confirmation policy.
- Preserve tmux identity and actionability classifications from JSON contracts.
- Keep no more than the domain-grouped tool set established by the framework; use action enums, not dozens of active tools.
- Output is bounded; telemetry includes action/outcome/duration/IDs/counts, never command bodies or secrets.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Session JSON rows render and identify the same pane/session as live tmux ground truth.
- [ ] Handoff create→send→accept→complete works through native tools with durable IDs/events.
- [ ] Audit/health/telemetry queries return structured details and compact summaries.
- [ ] Interactive-only/admin actions are absent from tool schemas.

title: Post-3xs: .37 context injection soft — LLM system prompt not receiving Reply-required line
description:
## PROBLEM

Verified in 3-pane final smoke on 2026-07-13 by pi on xtmux:1.3 (%2362).

.37 was designed to inject 'Reply required: <sender> (<bead>)' into pi's
LLM system prompt via before_agent_start systemPrompt chaining. In the
live smoke:

- UI widget correctly shows 'Reply required: $1732 (xtmux-3xs.smoke-final)'
- Model-visible system prompt does NOT contain the injection
- Pi acted on the duty on next turn — but that acceptance came from
  reading the UI widget in the pane, not from the injected system prompt

## SUCCESS

before_agent_start systemPrompt chain actually appends the Reply-required
line to the pi runtime's next LLM call's system prompt. Verifiable by
introspecting the effective system prompt from within the extension.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts — verify the before_agent_start handler
  is actually registered AND that its return value is the systemPrompt
  the pi runtime uses. Some pi APIs use return-value composition; others
  use ctx-mutation. Check the docs.
- Add a smoke assertion: dump the effective system prompt during a turn
  where an obligation exists; grep for 'Reply required'.

## SEVERITY

Soft — pi's UI-visible warning already surfaces the duty, and pi (LLM)
is disciplined enough to read UI chrome. But the specification is not
being met, and non-disciplined agents would miss the signal.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.37 close (22bcf10): 'Supported before_agent_start
  systemPrompt chaining now injects pending sender+bead duties into LLM
  context'
- xtmux-3xs.34 final smoke report (2026-07-13)
notes: Decision: no fix and no soft-only downgrade. Live goal turn carried the exact model-visible <xtmux-reply-obligation> system instruction for 732 (xtmux-3xs.39), proving before_agent_start chaining reaches the LLM. Pi docs explicitly specify returning { systemPrompt: event.systemPrompt + ... }; extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts follows that API, and the contract asserts the chained return. The final smoke's 'soft/invisible' result reflected lack of introspection in that turn, not failed injection.
close_reason: Closed as false-positive: live model context contains the reply-obligation system instruction; documented chaining and contract are correct, so no code or soft-only downgrade is needed.
