title: Post-3xs: pi-side monitor-arm equivalent — enforce wake path on outbound sends
description:
## PROBLEM

Claude has xtmux-3xs.23 (three-hook Stop-block coordination): on any
outbound message-send, a pending marker is touched; Stop is blocked
until Claude arms a Monitor(wait-agent) that will wake it when the
recipient transitions. Pi has NO equivalent mechanism. Consequence:

- Pi receives actionable inbound → obligation recorded (xtmux-3xs.33) ✓
- Pi sends outbound reply → NO wake mechanism armed → pi idles → next
  inbound from same peer sits invisible until pi's next turn boundary
  (xtmux-3xs.36 gap).

Combined with xtmux-3xs.36/.37, this closes the OTHER half of the
coordination loop: not just 'wake me when I have incoming' but 'wake
me when the peer I just messaged responds'.

## SUCCESS

On outbound message-send from pi to a peer, extension arms a
sender-side wait mechanism so pi's runtime wakes when the peer
transitions. Options:

- (a) **Detached monitor-agent daemon** (pi-auto-monitor already
      does this for tmux monitor registry). Extension additionally
      subscribes to that daemon's completion event and triggers
      a pi turn-continuation or context-inject when it fires. Depends
      on pi API surface for scheduling.
- (b) **Poll on interval** — pairs with xtmux-3xs.36 poll loop; on
      each poll, also check for @agent_state transitions on outbound
      targets and inject reminders.
- (c) **Sender-side receipt trigger** — pi's runtime watches the
      shadow-mode message_receipts table; on ack from peer, fires a
      handler.

Recommendation: (a) — pi-auto-monitor.ts already spawns
monitor-agent daemons; adding a completion-listener that emits a pi
event closes the loop cleanly.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts — after fireMonitor(), record the
  outbound expectation to a state dir similar to Claude's
  xtmux-auto-monitor dir (isolated: xtmux-outbound-expectations/).
- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts — on periodic scan (xtmux-3xs.36),
  also read outbound-expectations state and check @agent_state of
  targets; on transition to done/needs-input, trigger a reminder.

## NON_GOALS

- No hard block on pi turn end (pi API doesn't expose a Stop-block
  equivalent; the mechanism is soft-reminder + wake, not gate).
- No cross-pane monitor state sharing with Claude's xtmux-auto-monitor.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.23 (Claude-side Stop-block + Monitor pattern).
- xtmux-3xs.36 (mid-idle scan gap — pairs).
- xtmux-3xs.37 (soft warning ignored — pairs).
notes: PI/MONITOR SURVEY: installed ExtensionAPI.sendUserMessage always triggers a turn and accepts deliverAs steer|followUp; this is the supported wake surface. There is no extension event bus or external completion event. Existing pi-auto-monitor monitor-agent is two-stage: command returns monitor TSV immediately after spawning detached monitor-run; the child process exit therefore does NOT represent target transition. Chosen robust (a)+(b): pi-auto-monitor synchronously captures/reuses the durable monitor ID and writes a pane-owned marker under xtmux-outbound-expectations. The .36 poll reads authoritative monitor-list; when the ID disappears after terminal transition it atomically consumes the marker and calls sendUserMessage(..., followUp), waking idle Pi or safely queueing behind an active turn. Isolated from Claude xtmux-auto-monitor, 8h bounded, no hard Stop gate. Tests cover outbound command→monitor ID→pane marker and active→absent monitor→single wake+consume. Full 157 Bun / 416 expectations, typecheck, 140 shell contracts, V1 fixtures green.
close_reason: Shipped pane-owned outbound monitor expectations and supported sendUserMessage follow-up wake on durable monitor completion; full suite green.

title: Post-3xs: pi-inbox-reply must detect mid-idle inbound messages
description:
## PROBLEM

Verified in xtmux-3xs.34 self-smoke on 2026-07-13: pi-inbox-reply.ts
scans for expects_reply obligations ONLY at session_start / agent_start
/ agent_end (turn boundaries). Messages that arrive while pi is idle
are invisible until pi's next turn starts. This creates a permanent
silence window if pi doesn't start another turn.

Live evidence: xtmux-3xs.34 message arrived while pi idle → widget
showed +1 unread (unread-count runs on some tick), obligations dir
empty. Only when pi ran a new /goal did agent_start fire → scan →
obligation → reminder.

## SUCCESS

Extension detects inbound actionable messages while pi is idle and
either:
- (a) polls unread-count on an interval (e.g. every 30s while idle)
      and triggers a scan when count increases; OR
- (b) watches ~/.local/state/xtmux/observability.db
      via fs.watch for WAL updates and re-scans; OR
- (c) tmux hook: sender-side message-send already bumps
      @agent_unread_count on the target session — extension listens
      for tmux options change events if pi exposes any; OR
- (d) accept design: idle pi can't be woken by inbound alone; document
      that as an intentional limit.

Recommendation: (a) with a coarse interval (30s+) is the simplest
correct fix. (b) is more efficient but fs.watch is unreliable across
platforms.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts — add setInterval-based scan while
  session is alive, cancel on session_shutdown.
- Interval configurable via env (XTMUX_INBOX_POLL_INTERVAL_S, default 30).
- Contract: obligation created without pi starting a new turn.

## NON_GOALS

- No push mechanism from sender-side beyond the existing tmux
  display-message + @agent_unread_count bump.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.33 obligation trigger design (limited to turn boundaries).
- xtmux-3xs.34 self-smoke that surfaced this.
notes: PI RUNTIME SURVEY: current installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent types expose session_start/session_shutdown lifecycle and the runtime itself uses standard setInterval/clearInterval for long-lived TUI components; extension factories share the persistent Node process across turn boundaries. No native inbound event exists. Chosen coarse setInterval (default 30s, XTMUX_INBOX_POLL_INTERVAL_S override), direct structured expected-message scan + widget refresh, overlap guard, unref, cancellation on shutdown/reload. Direct scan is more reliable than unread-delta gating because receipt projection and preexisting unread can change independently. Contract at 10ms proves a message inserted after session_start creates/acks an obligation without agent_start and polling ceases after shutdown. Live idle RPC at 200ms: immediate state-dir empty; after 1s reply-to-$peer-for-%1931_pending existed with bead .36 and receipt acked. Typecheck green.
close_reason: Shipped configurable 30s mid-idle structured scan with overlap guard and shutdown cleanup; contract and live no-turn idle smoke passed.

title: Release-prep: wire aicommit2 prepare-commit-msg hook + scope taxonomy prompt
description:
## SCOPE

Wire **aicommit2** (tak-bro, TS, MIT, v2.8.0+, ~520 stars,
https://github.com/tak-bro/aicommit2) as a pre-commit assistant that
rewrites raw commit messages into conventional-commits format matching
xtmux's scope taxonomy. Composes with git-cliff (xtmux-5j3.1) for the
downstream changelog.

## WHY aicommit2 (not aicommits / opencommit)

Only tool of the three with first-class prepare-commit-msg + pre-commit
framework hook modes AND explicit Claude Code SDK + Ollama support.
Prompt-configurable so scope taxonomy is pinnable via a system prompt.
Weekly release cadence in 2026. Detailed research + anti-recs live in
this bead's parent (xtmux-5j3) task notes.

## DELIVERABLES

- .aicommit2.rc (or equivalent per aicommit2 docs) checked into repo
  with a system prompt encoding scope taxonomy:
    'obs' → observability runtime (SQLite/Bun, event_journal, cli)
    'coordination' → hooks, auto-monitor, agent state, /goal drain
    'messages' → messages/receipts/deliveries + related domain
    'migration' → schema/migrations + legacy importers
    'pi' → pi extensions (pi-*.ts)
    'meta' → docs, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, workflow config, tests

- Install path documented (README + INSTALL.md when it lands): 'aicommit2
  hook install' or equivalent global-npm install. Do NOT commit to a
  local node_modules dependency — aicommit2 stays a user-level tool.

- LLM backend recommendation: default to Claude Code SDK for local
  ergonomics; Ollama as offline fallback path (both are supported per
  aicommit2 docs).

- Contract-style smoke: on a WIP change, run aicommit2 → observe it
  produces 'feat(obs): ...' or similar within the taxonomy. Snapshot
  or manually verify.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must NOT block a commit that skips the hook (env bypass).
- Author retains veto — hook is 'suggest', not 'enforce'.
- No API key hardcoding in repo; use aicommit2's env-based config.

## NON_GOALS

- No CI integration this bead (that's release-prep timeline).
- No commit-lint enforcement (checked separately; if desired, add
  commitlint + husky as its own follow-up).

## REFERENCES

- https://github.com/tak-bro/aicommit2
- Composes with git-cliff via xtmux-5j3.1.
notes: Decision: aicommit2 is optional and not first; automatic prepare-commit-msg installation would intrude on contributor core.hooksPath/Husky/pre-commit policy. Reusable scope prompt shipped. pi-cliff packages do not exist; official git-cliff@2.13.1 + xtmux wrapper used instead.
close_reason: Implemented and validated as part of the @jaggerxtrm/xtmux publishable installer.

title: Release-prep: auto-changelog from conventional commits (git-cliff)
description:
## SCOPE

Wire **git-cliff** (Rust, v2.13.1+, Apache/MIT, ~12k stars) to generate
CHANGELOG.md from conventional commit messages. Committee-tested pairing
for the aicommit2 → git-cliff → optional knope workflow chosen for
xtmux (see xtmux-5j3.5 for the commit-enhancer side).

- Add cliff.toml with a group mapping that encodes our scope taxonomy:
  obs, coordination, messages, migration, pi, meta.
  → 'feat(obs):' rows collect under an 'Observability runtime' heading, etc.
- Generate initial CHANGELOG.md covering 268c801..HEAD (xtmux-3xs epic
  + release-prep so far). Verify readability of the output before ship.
- 'bun run changelog' script that shells out to git-cliff.
- Optional: CI job that fails a PR if CHANGELOG.md isn't updated after
  a conventional-commit-triggering change. Deferred to release-time.

## SEMVER BUMPING (deferred, referenced here for context)

Not this bead's scope; two options for later:
- 'bun version' script + manual tag. Simplest, current default.
- **knope** (Rust, https://github.com/knope-dev/knope) — conventional-
  commit-driven auto-bump without semantic-release's full publish
  pipeline. Add if we want the discipline of auto-bumps but not the
  full-publish overhead.

## VERIFICATION AUTO-CHANGELOG ACTUALLY WORKS

Run git-cliff against the epic history (268c801..HEAD). If commit
type/scope tags are consistent (they should be — recent commits use
'feat(obs):', 'fix(coordination):' etc. cleanly), output should slot
into the taxonomy without manual editing. If messy, decide: backfill
retroactively via git filter-repo, or accept messy first pass and
tighten going forward.

## ANTI-RECOMMENDATIONS (evaluated + rejected)

- standard-version — deprecated 2022; use commit-and-tag-version if
  that model is ever needed.
- semantic-release — overkill for a Bun CLI; wants to own the full
  npm publish flow.

## NON_GOALS

- No semver auto-bumping this round (see knope note above).
- No release-notes GitHub integration (deferred to xtmux-5j3.3
  publish/install).
notes: Implemented changelog/cliff.toml, generated CHANGELOG.md from 268c801..HEAD, added npm/bun changelog script and reusable xtmux-changelog binary/export. Stock Keep a Changelog template rejected; compatible custom structure documented in docs/INSTALL.md. External-repo smoke passed.

title: Post-3xs: pi-inbox-reply extension must pane-scope unread-count call
description:
## PROBLEM

extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts:154 calls `unread-count --for <sid>` WITHOUT
`--pane %N`. Under V2 default-on cutover (xtmux-3xs.31), the query counts
every unacked message against the session_id — including messages targeted
at other panes cohabiting the same tmux session.

Live evidence 2026-07-13: pi's widget shows `Inbox: 57 unread` for
session $1732 (shared with Claude at pane %1930). Real pi-scoped count
against pane %1931 alone is expected to be roughly half.

## SUCCESS

- Extension queries `unread-count --for <sid> --pane <own-pane-id>`.
- Pane id resolved once at session_start via
  `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}'` and cached.
- Widget count reflects pane-scoped, not session-wide, unread.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts — resolve own pane_id at session_start;
  pass it as --pane on every unread-count call.

## NON_GOALS

- No changes to the reply-obligation flow (that's xtmux-3xs.33).
- No fallback path when pane_id can't be resolved — default to
  session-wide behavior (current behavior) so hostile-env doesn't
  regress into silent zero.

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.28 primitive: unread-count --pane %N added and tested.
- xtmux-3xs.22/.26 pi extension (6f224ed).
notes: Implemented pane-scoped refresh after V2 cutover. session_start resolves and caches #{pane_id}; every unread-count call passes --pane when available; failed/hostile pane resolution preserves session-wide fallback. Picker now forwards the .28 --pane primitive (the .28 Bun CLI supported it but its shell wrapper had not). Contract asserts cached %me propagation and fallback without --pane. Live envless smoke: shared-session count 57, pi pane %1931 count 56 on current DB. Installed Pi API still has no inbound event; .32 requires no new lifecycle hook.
close_reason: Shipped pane-scoped Pi inbox refresh: cached own pane at session_start, forwarded --pane through picker to .28, retained session-wide hostile-env fallback. Contract/typecheck and live envless pane query pass; implementation evidence and API note are in NOTES.

title: Post-3xs: unread-count needs --pane filter for pane-scoped multi-agent tmux sessions
description:
## PROBLEM

Discovered in the xtmux-3xs.22/.26 pi extension smoke test on 2026-07-13:

Pi and Claude coordinate as two panes on the same tmux session ($1732).
When pi sends a reply back to Claude (recipient_id=$1732 target_pane_id=%1930), pi's inbox widget refreshes via `unread-count --for $1732` and the count includes messages pi itself just sent, because the query aggregates every unread against the recipient's session_id regardless of target_pane_id.

Pi's step 9 observation: widget bounced 54 → 55 after the reply landed.

## SUCCESS

- `xtmux-obs unread-count --for <sid> [--pane %N]` filters to messages where   `target_pane_id = ? OR target_pane_id IS NULL`.
- Backward compat: no `--pane` flag = session-wide count (existing behavior).
- `computeUnread(db, recipientId, panelId?)` gets the optional third arg.
- Pi extension passes its own pane_id so the widget reflects only messages   addressed to that pane.

## SCOPE

- src/domains/messages/reconcile-unread.ts::computeUnread — add optional `paneId` arg.
- src/cli-messages.ts::cliUnreadCount — parse `--pane` flag, forward.
- src/cli.ts usage — document new flag.
- tests/integration/messages.test.ts — add pane-scoped case.
- Pi extension follow-up (out of scope for THIS bead): pass pane_id when   querying. File a follow-up if pi didn't already do it.

## NON_GOALS

- No schema changes.
- No pane-scoped message-status (that's already pane-agnostic and correct —   status is per-message).

## VALIDATION

- Two messages, same session, different target panes, one acked →   `unread-count --for SID --pane PANE_A` returns 1 (or 0 if the acked one   went to PANE_A); `--pane PANE_B` returns the other.
- Legacy message with target_pane_id NULL counts against every pane query   for that session_id.
- `--for SID` without `--pane` still returns session-wide count.

## REFERENCES

- Pi's smoke step 9 note in xtmux-3xs.22 close comments.
- src/domains/messages/send.ts sender_pane_id / target_pane_id (Phase 3).
close_reason: unread-count --pane %N added; computeUnread grows optional 3rd arg. src/domains/messages/reconcile-unread.ts + src/cli-messages.ts + src/cli.ts usage. Test covers session-wide / claude-scoped / pi-scoped / bystander cases (from same-session ambiguity scenario). 149/149 bun, 138/138 contract, tsc clean. Pi extension can now pass its pane_id to prevent self-message double-count.

title: V2 message-list emits UTC-Z timestamp; V1 emits local-offset (shadow divergence)
description:
## PROBLEM

Discovered during xtmux-3xs post-close smoke testing on 2026-07-13.

V1 message-list uses `date -Is` → local ISO with numeric offset:
  `2026-07-13T01:09:17+02:00`

V2 message-list uses `fmtTsIso` (src/cli-messages.ts) → `.toISOString()` UTC-Z:
  `2026-07-12T23:09:17Z`

Same instant; incompatible byte-format. Shadow-mode records this as a
divergence on EVERY message-list call under XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow.

## SUCCESS

V2 message-list emits the same ISO format as V1 (local-tz + numeric offset).
Contract test asserts byte-parity for a fixed clock.

## SCOPE

- src/cli-messages.ts::fmtTsIso — replace toISOString with a local-tz formatter matching `date -Is`.
- tests/contracts/differential-v1-v2.test.ts — add explicit assertion for the timestamp column.

## NON_GOALS

- No client-side normalization in shadow-mode picker (fix at the source).

## REFERENCES

- Also found and fixed simultaneously: bin/tmux-session-picker shadow-tee at message_send/message_ack/log_cli_emit was checking $REPLY AFTER log_event, which clobbers REPLY via event_log_file. Silent no-op in production. Fixed by snapshotting mode into a local (_mode) variable before the log_event call.
close_reason: V2 fmtTsIso now emits local-tz ISO with colon offset (yyyy-mm-ddTHH:MM:SS±HH:MM) matching date -Is byte-for-byte. Contract test tests/contracts/differential-v1-v2.test.ts asserts format on both V1 and V2 outputs, and rejects Z. 150/150 bun (+1), 138/138 contract, tsc + V1 fixtures no-drift. Live shadow-mode smoke on parity content records 0 divergences (was 1-per-list-call previously).

title: Post-3xs: sender receipt status and unread-count messaging primitives
description:
## PROBLEM

The Pi coordination extension can send and acknowledge messages, but the sender cannot query delivery/read state and a recipient can only derive an unread count by listing every unacknowledged message. This blocks a cheap, reliable inbox badge and prevents an orchestrator from distinguishing sent from read messages.

## SUCCESS

The public picker/Bun message surface exposes a backward-compatible, bounded sender-status query and an unread-count query. The query reports the durable message identifier, recipient/session, and ack state without scanning or parsing human-formatted message text. Existing message-list and V1 output remain unchanged.

## SCOPE

- src/domains/messages/ list/query and receipt data access
- src/cli.ts message command registration
- bin/tmux-session-picker message routing
- tests/contracts for V1-off and V2-on output/receipt behavior
- docs/observability-redesign.md message/query surface

## NON_GOALS

- No push subscription or daemon.
- No message schema migration unless query requirements prove one is unavoidable.
- No Pi UI implementation in this bead.
- No change to message-send, message-ack, or existing message-list output.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve V1 byte compatibility when XTMUX_OBS_V2 is off; do not pretend V1 has receipt data it cannot supply.
- V2 queries must use indexed SQL and return stable machine-readable rows suitable for a UI status indicator.
- Unknown/missing IDs and foreign recipients must degrade with clear exit status and no invented state.
- Keep explicit tmux target identity separate from inferred current identity.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: sent → unacked → acked status transition in isolated V2 DB.
- [ ] Contract test: unread count changes only for the addressed recipient.
- [ ] Contract test: unknown ID/recipient produces bounded, non-invented result.
- [ ] scripts/capture-v1-fixtures.sh --check remains clean.
- [ ] bun test and bun run typecheck pass.
- [ ] Picker smoke proves sender status and recipient count query against an isolated DB.

## OUTPUT

Changed public command contract, tests, V1 compatibility evidence, V2 SQL/query evidence, and residual gaps (notably push notifications).

## APPROACH NOTES

Audit 2026-07-12: current message-list supports only --for/--to, --unacked, --limit, and --since; message receipts exist in V2 but are not exposed to senders. Pi docs support footer status via ctx.ui.setStatus(), which composes with existing footer statuses; a Pi badge must depend on this cheap count primitive rather than poll/parse full TSV.
notes:
PI EXTENSION REVIEW (2026-07-12)

DECISION: Do not fold pi-auto-monitor.ts into pi-agent-state.ts. The latter is installed globally through ~/.pi/agent/extensions/xtmux-agent-state.ts -> extensions/pi-agent-state.ts, whereas auto-monitor is project-local via .pi/settings.json. A fold would make project-specific monitor arming (and its hard-coded picker/project assumptions) run in every Pi project. Keep the boundary explicit.

PI API: isBashToolResult(event) is the documented correct tool_result narrowing. The installed types define BashToolResultEvent with toolName="bash" and BashToolInput through event.input, so use event.input.command directly; event.details is BashToolDetails (truncation/fullOutputPath) and is not a command source. The current cast is unnecessary style debt, not an observed runtime defect.

LIFECYCLE: tool_result is correct because a monitor must not arm before a failed send. tool_call pre-arming creates stale monitors. agent_end/session_shutdown cleanup should not kill monitors: monitor-agent intentionally outlives a Pi turn and manages its own target lifecycle. Pi exposes appendEntry for durable session data, not a suitable shared monitor KV; an in-memory Set is reload-volatile and can lie after monitor exit. Keep monitor-list as the source of truth until measurement proves it is too slow.

CHROME: use ctx.ui.setStatus("xtmux-inbox", ...) if/when implemented; it composes with existing footer statuses. Do not call setFooter (replacement UI), setWidget, or add a factory-started timer. A badge needs a cheap count primitive first.

MESSAGING GAP AUDIT:
1. P2 in this bead: no sender receipt/status query; no cheap unread count.
2. P3 deferred: no push stream for remote ack events; polling is the only current option.
3. P3 deferred: handoff state machine has accepted/completed states but no sender-facing lifecycle query/notification seam.
4. No native Pi schema exists for arbitrary picker CLI invocations hidden inside bash; command parsing is the appropriate boundary. Regex must remain bounded to the three explicitly supported forms.
close_reason: Added V2-only JSON message-status and unread-count picker/CLI primitives backed by indexed receipt data; V1 rejects query commands without inventing receipt state. Contract smoke covers sent→ack transition, recipient isolation, unknown status, and picker V2/V1 behavior. Full Bun suite, typecheck, V1 fixtures, syntax/diff checks pass.

title: Post-3xs: hostile-environment + differential V1-vs-V2 contract oracles
description:
## PROBLEM

Both real bugs surfaced during the xtmux-3xs epic were invisible to the 128-test suite because every test runs INSIDE tmux, with a healthy pane, a live session, and a bead set:

- **@agent_state canonicalization divergence** (found + fixed by xtmux:1.2 mid-flight): V2 printed the raw pane option where V1 canonicalized it (working|thinking|busy|tool → running). 90 contract tests green, none caught it. Only V1-vs-V2 stdout diff in one environment surfaced it.
- **Bystander pane/bead poisoning** (xtmux-3xs.18, filed at P1): telemetry credits a run to whichever pane tmux considers "current" when `\$TMUX` is unset. Every test we ship runs inside tmux with a healthy pane. The whole failure class is unreachable from inside the happy path.

The tests aren't wrong — they're written from inside the happy environment. The bugs live in the environment, not in the logic. Our oracles never leave it.

## SUCCESS

Two standing oracles run in CI, catch the whole class instead of one instance each time:

### Oracle 1 — Hostile-environment matrix

For every V2-routable command (message-send/list/ack, log emit/tail/query, monitor register/list/kill, telemetry start/finish, audit ingest, handoff, safe-send-pointer), assert nothing is silently attributed, invented, inherited, or crashed. Minimum matrix:

| Env prefix | Assertion |
|---|---|
| `env -u TMUX` | session_id / pane_id / bead_id / instance_id = NULL, never a bystander |
| `TMUX=<stale-socket>` | Same as above; no silent degrade |
| `pane_id since killed` | `target_gone` recorded; no stale write, no crash |
| `pane exists, no @agent_bead` | bead_id = NULL, never inherited from a sibling pane |
| `pane exists, no @agent_state` | 'unknown', never '' silently coerced |
| `tmux not on PATH` | Clean degradation; no partial row; exit rc distinct + structured |

Each row is a one-line env prefix over a command we already ship — cheap to add and gets stronger with each future domain phase.

### Oracle 2 — Differential V1-vs-V2 test-time comparator

For each V2-routable command, run twice against the same tmux state:
- Once with `XTMUX_OBS_V2=0` (V1 authoritative)
- Once with `XTMUX_OBS_V2=1` (V2 authoritative)

Assert stdout/stderr/exit byte-equality after normalization (sed via existing normalize.sed) and after sort where V1's order is tmux-enumeration-dependent (audit output — depends on xtmux-3xs.17's --stable flag).

This is the SAME comparison as the runtime shadow-mode from xtmux-3xs.12, but at TEST time not runtime. Runtime shadow tells you about production divergence after the fact; test-time stops it landing.

### Composition

- xtmux-3xs.18 becomes the first passing case of Oracle 1, not a standalone fix
- xtmux-3xs.17 (--stable) is a hard prereq for Oracle 2's audit row
- xtmux-3xs.12 (runtime shadow) is the production-time cousin — both stay because they cover different windows

## SCOPE

- `tests/contracts/hostile-env.test.ts`: parameterized test — iterate matrix rows × command list, spawn picker with env prefix, assert row shape
- `tests/contracts/differential-v1-v2.test.ts`: parameterized test — iterate V2-routable commands, run with V2=0 then V2=1, normalize + diff
- `tests/fixtures/hostile-env/`: small helper scripts (kill-pane, stale-socket, no-tmux-on-path) that set up the degraded environment
- Docs: `docs/observability-redesign.md` §9 (compatibility) gains a "test-time contracts" subsection noting both oracles

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT modify runtime code paths in this bead (fixes land in xtmux-3xs.18 and future beads; this one is the CATCHER)
- Not a replacement for xtmux-3xs.12 (runtime shadow catches production divergence; this catches development regressions)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Oracle 1 matrix must be extensible — future beads (Phase 5 pane-open resolvers, handoff --target guards, etc) plug in one row each
- Oracle 2 must sort BEFORE diff where enumeration-order matters (audit, monitor-list in some states) OR gate on --stable from xtmux-3xs.17 when it lands
- Runtime overhead outside CI: none. These are test-only.
- Must not require actual tmux running in CI — use a mock-tmux binary on PATH for baseline, real tmux via docker for the "tmux not on PATH" case
- CI runtime budget: whole hostile-env suite under 30s

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Oracle 1 catches xtmux-3xs.18's bystander poisoning on merged main BEFORE .18's fix lands, PASSES after
- [ ] Oracle 1 catches @agent_state raw-vs-canonical divergence in a synthetic regression injected via `sed -i` on cli-messages.ts (mutation test), passes clean on real code
- [ ] Oracle 2 asserts message-send/list/ack byte-identical under V1 and V2 across the matrix
- [ ] Oracle 2 asserts audit byte-identical after --stable applied (depends xtmux-3xs.17)
- [ ] All existing 128 tests still pass; new oracle count logged

## OUTPUT

- Two new test files + fixtures dir
- Docs subsection §9 explaining the two-oracle framing
- Report: number of hostile-env matrix rows × commands = matrix size; number of differential-diff assertions; CI timing
- If xtmux-3xs.18 is fixed before this lands, note that .18's fix now has an oracle covering it and future regressions are caught automatically

## REFERENCES

- xtmux:1.2's proposal (design justification verbatim in this bead body)
- Related: xtmux-3xs.12 (runtime shadow — same comparison, different window)
- Related: xtmux-3xs.17 (--stable — hard prereq for audit differential row)
- First passing case: xtmux-3xs.18 (bystander bead corruption)
- Design doc §9 (compatibility contracts) — extend
- Historical note: @agent_state divergence caught by xtmux:1.2 during Phase 4/7/8 integration (fixed in ec390d9e; test pinned by tests/contracts/agent-state-normalization.test.ts)

## APPROACH NOTES

Design premise (xtmux:1.2's words):
> The epic's whole premise is that V2 is a drop-in for V1 (PRD §20, byte-identical when disabled, compatible when enabled). We assert that with fixtures captured from one machine in one state. The two oracles above assert it structurally, across environments, for every command, forever — and they get stronger with each phase instead of needing a new fixture.

> "correct-looking wrong" is the failure mode this epic is most exposed to, and right now nothing in the suite is looking for it.
close_reason: Added hostile-environment and V1/V2 differential contract oracles, including V2 stable audit comparison. Full Bun suite, typecheck, V1 fixtures, syntax/diff checks pass; shell contract has one pre-existing live-tmux-layout failure when no current tmux client is available.

title: Post-3xs: shadow-mode per-command V1+V2 comparator wiring in picker
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase 9 landed src/db/shadow.ts::recordDivergence + shadow_divergences table + shadow-summary CLI subcommand, but the picker doesn't yet run V1 and V2 side-by-side under XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow. Without the comparator, we can't validate parity on live traffic before cutover.

## SUCCESS

Under XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow: (1) V1 code path executes and returns authoritative output; (2) V2 code path runs in parallel and its output is diffed against V1; (3) any divergence recorded to shadow_divergences via recordDivergence(). Stdout unchanged (V1 output only). `xtmux-obs shadow-summary` shows divergence counts by (domain, command).

## SCOPE

Per PRD §18: comparators for recipient normalization, message ordering, message IDs, ack state, unread counts, monitor state, agent latest state, turn correlation, telemetry result, audit findings. bin/tmux-session-picker gains a shadow-tee wrapper around message-send/list/ack/log-emit/log-query/monitor-list/audit.

## NON_GOALS

- Shadow reads never mutate authoritative state
- No output changes visible to operators

## CONSTRAINTS

- Zero effect on V1 output
- Divergence writes are best-effort (don't fail the wrapped command)
- Comparator per command runs after V1 result is captured, not inline
- **audit comparator MUST sort both sides** or use xtmux-3xs.17's --stable flag when it lands — V1 audit stdout is tmux-enumeration-order-dependent and unsorted comparison produces phantom divergences (xtmux:1.2's callout)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] shadow-mode on production traffic sample → zero unexplained divergences
- [ ] Injected V2 bug → divergence recorded and surfaced by shadow-summary
- [ ] V1 stdout/stderr/exit still byte-identical under shadow mode
- [ ] audit comparator sorts before diff OR consumes --stable from .17

## OUTPUT

Handoff: shadow divergence report on production traffic sample; recommendation for cutover.

## REFERENCES

- Related: xtmux-3xs.17 (audit --stable flag) — this bead's audit comparator depends on stable ordering
close_reason: Shadow-mode wired: writes shadow-tee to V2 SQLite (send/ack/emit); reads capture-and-diff (message-list, monitor-list) via new obs_shadow_diff helper + xtmux-obs shadow-record CLI verb. log-query + audit content-diff deferred to .25 (log-query needs same extract-to-helper refactor, audit needs a fixture harness for stable content comparison — noted in code and docs §13). Contract test passes: seeded V1 message + empty V2 → shadow-summary shows the divergence. Bun 137/138 (1 todo unchanged), contract 137/137, tsc clean.

title: Phase 8 — Audit runs and finding persistence
description:
## PROBLEM

`audit.run` today records only that the audit executed (PRD §14). Findings (missing-path, stale-specialist, dirty-worktree, shared-worktree, working-do-not-kill, naming-convention, agent-pane-without-bead) are emitted to stdout and lost. No way to track resolution over time.

## SUCCESS

`audit_runs` + `audit_findings` (PRD §14) authoritative. Findings deduplicated by stable `fingerprint`; repeat observations update `last_seen_ms`; findings absent from a later complete audit marked `resolved_at_ms`.

## SCOPE

- New DDL: `audit_runs`, `audit_findings`
- New: `src/domains/audit/{run,find,fingerprint,resolve}.ts`
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` audit command — persist run + findings under V2; keep stdout human format unchanged
- Fingerprint recipe per finding kind (documented in `docs/observability-redesign.md`)
- Tests: PRD §22 required audit tests

## NON_GOALS

- No dashboard snapshot storage
- No auto-remediation
- No historical dashboard queries beyond finding resolution

## CONSTRAINTS

- Same finding across audits: same `fingerprint` → update `last_seen_ms`, do not insert duplicate
- Complete audit + finding absent → `resolved_at_ms` set
- Partial audit (crash mid-run) → do NOT mark absent findings resolved
- `severity` and `kind` from a closed enum documented in Phase 1 doc
- Log/telemetry: run start/complete envelopes in `event_journal`

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Same finding across 3 audits: 1 row, `last_seen_ms` advances
- [ ] Resolution: finding gone in later complete audit → `resolved_at_ms` set
- [ ] Partial audit: crash mid-run → no false-resolve
- [ ] Fingerprint stability across process restarts
- [ ] Shadow divergence: zero for `audit` command stdout

## OUTPUT

Handoff: fingerprint recipes per kind, severity taxonomy, resolution-detection query.
notes: DONE. audit_runs + audit_findings authoritative; stdout unchanged. VALIDATION: [x] same finding across 3 audits = 1 row, last_seen_ms advances (verified live against a real tmux server, not just unit tests). [x] resolution: finding absent from a later COMPLETE audit -> resolved_at_ms. [x] partial audit (crash mid-run) does NOT false-resolve — resolution runs in the same transaction as the completed_at_ms write and nowhere else. [x] fingerprint stable across process restarts (same hash produced by a separate process). [x] shadow divergence: audit stdout V1 == V2, zero lines differ. Fingerprint = sha256('v1' + kind + sorted identity k=v)[:32]; identity EXCLUDES the volatile part (dirty count, observed state) so a worktree with 3 vs 30 dirty files is the same finding; keys on session_name, never tmux $N/%N which are recycled on restart. Impl: src/domains/audit/{store,fingerprint}.ts, src/commands/audit.ts. OUTPUT: fingerprint recipes per kind + severity taxonomy + resolution query in docs §3.
close_reason: Phase 8 audit runs+findings landed on xt/hnjk via cherry-pick from xtmux:1.2. Migration 3. src/domains/audit/{store,fingerprint,find,resolve,run}.ts: fingerprint upsert (repeat observation advances last_seen_ms, never duplicates), resolution gated on run completeness AND same-transaction as completed_at_ms write so partial audit cannot mass-resolve, last_run_id + session_name deltas approved and integrated. UNIQUE(fingerprint) enforces dedup at schema level. CHECK constraints on severity {warning,cleanup} + kind closed set (all 7 finding kinds).

title: Phase 7 — Correlated command telemetry (git, bd, gh)
description:
## PROBLEM

`telemetry.command.started` and `git.command`/`bd.command`/`gh.command` today are uncorrelated event pairs (PRD §13). No way to detect started-but-never-finished runs, failure rates, or command duration without walking the whole journal.

## SUCCESS

`command_runs` table (PRD §13) with one row per invocation: `started_at_ms` on start, `finished_at_ms` + `exit_code` + `terminal_status` on finish. Fields: `tool`, `operation`, `session_id`, `pane_id`, `instance_id`, `bead_id`, `cwd`, `repo`, `argv`, `branch_before/after`, `head_before/after`. Enables PR-create-without-merge, failed-bead-close, last-push-by-bead queries.

## SCOPE

- New DDL: `command_runs`
- New: `src/domains/telemetry/{start,finish,reconcile}.ts`
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` telemetry wrapper — insert start row → run command → update same row with result; write `event_journal` envelope
- Cover: git.command, git.commit, git.push, git.merge, bd.command, bd.create, bd.claim, bd.update, bd.close, bd.remember, git.pr.create, git.pr.merge, gh.command
- Tests: PRD §22 required telemetry tests

## NON_GOALS

- No stdout/stderr capture of the underlying commands
- No cross-tool aggregation dashboards (query surface only)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Insert-then-update on same row (never a second insert on completion)
- Interrupted runs (SIGINT/crash mid-command): reconciliation marks `terminal_status=interrupted` with null `exit_code`
- Before/after git metadata captured only if `repo` context resolves cheaply (no unbounded git ops)
- Log/telemetry: envelope written on both start and finish, sharing `command_runs.id` as `correlation_id`

## VALIDATION

title: Phase 6 — Handoffs and prompt-pointer lifecycle
description:
## PROBLEM

`handoff.created` + `handoff.sent` today are two `events.jsonl` lines with no lifecycle state, no accepted/completed correlation, no delivery-failure record (PRD §12). `safe-send-pointer` blurs the durable/best-effort boundary.

## SUCCESS

`handoffs` table (PRD §12) with states `created|sent|delivery_failed|accepted|completed|cancelled`. Every handoff has: pointer path, content hash, summary, bead, source/target session ids, `delivery_attempt_id` foreign key. Reconciliation detects: created-but-never-sent, sent-to-dead-pane, prompt-file-missing-before-send, no-bead, completed-turn-without-completion.

## SCOPE

- New DDL: `handoffs`
- New: `src/domains/handoffs/{create,send,accept,complete,reconcile}.ts`
- Edit: `bin/tmux-session-picker` handoff flow — `handoff` command routes to Bun under V2; keep prompt-file write in shell (do not store prompt body in SQLite, only path + hash + summary)
- Delivery: reuse `delivery_attempts.kind=handoff_pointer` from Phase 3
- Tests: PRD §22 required handoff tests

## NON_GOALS

- No storage of prompt-file bodies
- No cross-machine handoff
- No handoff-graph queries beyond lifecycle reconciliation

## CONSTRAINTS

- `prompt_file_hash` computed at create time; verified before send
- Handoff without bead → structured rejection
- `delivery_attempt_id` FK links to `delivery_attempts` row
- State-machine validated (illegal transitions rejected)
- Completed turn on a handoff pane transitions matching handoff to `completed` when correlated
- Log/telemetry: every state transition writes `event_journal` envelope

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Create + send + delivery attempt: handoff row created→sent, delivery_attempt_id populated
- [ ] Missing prompt file at send: state→delivery_failed with `failure_code=prompt_missing`
- [ ] Dead target pane: state→delivery_failed with `failure_code=target_gone`
- [ ] Accepted/completed correlation: completed turn on target pane → handoff completed_at_ms set
- [ ] Idempotent import (from Phase 9): rerunning migration produces zero duplicates
- [ ] Shadow divergence: zero for `handoff` command output
- [ ] Reconciliation report identifies each anomaly type

## OUTPUT

Handoff: state-machine diagram, anomaly-taxonomy list, reconciliation query samples.
close_reason: Phase 6 handoffs landed (78631de). Migration 7 + lifecycle module + 5 tests all green (26/26 total). State machine validated (illegal transitions throw). Delivery attempt row + FK link on send. Prompt-file hash captured at create; no-bead rejected. Deferred to Phase 9: picker handoff-command V2 delegation + reconciliation walk (created-but-never-sent, sent-to-dead-pane, turn-completed-without-completion) which naturally shares the shadow-mode reconciliation infrastructure. Unblocks 3xs.9.

title: followup: xt pi --role — implement pi-argv passthrough with the sp-audit-informed flag policy
description:
PROBLEM: xt pi --role currently passes zero argv to pi (worktree-session.ts:373 runtimeArgs = []). No way to set --model, --thinking, extensions, tools, or any per-role runtime override. Direct evidence: xtmux-2i5 smoke test coord launched with glm-5.2 default (no way to force nemotron or other). Pane 4's audit (specialists PR #176) rewrote the flag question and pane 4's follow-up message (msg-1783380735-1961914) gave the full sp→pi argv contract at both spawn sites.

SUCCESS: xt pi --role forwards a curated flag set consistent with sp-managed spawn semantics for the interactive case.

SCRUTINY: medium

SCOPE: xtrm-tools/core cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts (runtimeArgs construction for pi path), cli/src/commands/pi.ts (surface the flags).

DESIGN (from pane 4's audit + smoke evidence):
- '--' passthrough: everything after '--' on 'xt pi' cmd line forwarded verbatim as pi argv. Primary mechanism.
- First-class xt flags to surface: --model, --thinking. Both map to specialist.execution.{model,thinking_level} by default; CLI override wins.
- Extensions: forward -e for whatever specialist.execution.extensions or specialist opts-in. Do NOT emit sp's --no-extensions (interactive role wants pi extensions).
- Do NOT emit sp's isolation flags (--offline, --no-session, --no-context-files, --no-prompt-templates, --no-themes) — interactive coord needs AGENTS.md + themes + user session.
- Do NOT emit --mode rpc/json — interactive coord wants default text mode.
- Guard as xt-owned (reject if user passes via passthrough): --session-dir, --name, --system-prompt.
- Skip/warn: --print (contradicts interactive), --list-models, --export, pi subcommands.

NON_GOALS: no changes to sp's spawn logic; no shared pi-argv builder yet (extract when 3rd caller emerges).

VALIDATION:
- xt pi --role chain-coordinator --model gemini/gemini-3-pro --no-attach launches with pi --model gemini/gemini-3-pro in argv (verified via ps or tmux capture).
- xt pi --role chain-coordinator --thinking high --no-attach launches with --thinking high.
- xt pi --role chain-coordinator -- --gitnexus-cmd '...' --no-attach launches with --gitnexus-cmd '...' in argv.
- xt pi --role chain-coordinator --system-prompt X errors clearly.
- Existing xt pi (no --role) unchanged.

OUTPUT: patched worktree-session.ts + pi.ts + tests.

TRACKED_BY: xtmux-2i5.
CAUSED_BY: xtmux-2i5 smoke test (2026-07-07) — direct evidence that runtimeArgs=[] is the current state.
DISCOVERED_FROM: specialists PR #176 + msg-1783380735-1961914 sp→pi argv audit.
notes:

    - pi-guardrails (@aliou/pi-guardrails — safety default; can opt out via execution.extensions)

Per-role overrides remain via specialist.execution.extensions.{name}: bool.

title: bug: specialist skills.paths in .xtrm/skills/active/* don't resolve in xt pi --role worktrees
description:

But xt pi --role opens a fresh git worktree, and .xtrm/ is gitignored — the worktree has no skills scaffold. worktree-session.ts line 435 gates the ensureAgentsSkillsSymlink call with 'if (runtime === "claude")', so pi worktrees never get the scaffold. Direct evidence: smoke test on xtmux-2i5 shows pi prints [Skill conflicts] listing the two missing paths.

NOT-FATAL: pi's user-level skill auto-discovery loads the same skills from ~/.claude/skills/, so the specialist works in practice. But the UX is broken (visible conflict warning) and any specialist that DEPENDS on a skill only present in the repo (not user-wide) silently fails.

SUCCESS: pi role sessions can resolve skills.paths correctly. Either the launcher resolves relative paths against mainRepoRoot before passing to pi, OR the ensureAgentsSkillsSymlink call moves out of the claude-only branch, OR specialists switch to user-wide skill references.

SCRUTINY: medium

SCOPE: cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts (skill scaffold for pi role runs), config/specialists/chain-coordinator.specialist.json (candidate for path convention change).

NON_GOALS: no rewrite of pi's skill discovery; no new skill installation flow.

CONSTRAINTS: keep xt claude flow unchanged; must work with skills that exist per-repo OR user-wide.

VALIDATION: after fix, xt pi --role chain-coordinator --bead X --no-attach + pi start shows no '[Skill conflicts]' output for the two skills. Existing xt claude behavior unchanged.

OUTPUT: patched launcher and/or specialist file. Smoke test rerun with no conflict output.

CAUSED_BY: xtmux-2i5 rollout (design assumed .xtrm/skills/active/* would exist in worktrees, discovered wrong at smoke test).
TRACKED_BY: xtmux-2i5.
close_reason: Fixed in core PR #364 (merged 2026-07-07). worktree-session.ts now runs ensureAgentsSkillsSymlink + ensureWorktreeSpecialists for both runtime==='claude' and any --role (which always spawns pi). Fresh pi role worktrees now have .xtrm/skills/active + .specialists layout matching main repo, so specialist skills.paths using .xtrm/skills/active/* resolve. Claude-only settings.local.json still gated separately. worktree-session-role.test.ts 11 tests unchanged pass.

title: bug: PostToolUse Claude Code hook sets @agent_state=running, racing Stop → done
description:
PROBLEM: In ~/.claude/settings.json, PostToolUse hook fires 'agent-state.sh running' after every tool call. Because Claude Code batches tools and Stop fires after the last PostToolUse, the race often lands PostToolUse LAST, overwriting 'done' with 'running'. Evidence: ~/.local/state/xtmux/events.jsonl last 1000 events shows 857 running / 8 done / 4 needs-input — orchestrator wake-up polling @agent_state almost never observes 'done' because it is overwritten within milliseconds. This is the 'wake-up does not seem to work' complaint.

SUCCESS: PostToolUse either does not touch state, or state transitions honor the actual turn boundary. Wake-up polling reliably observes 'done' after every agent turn.

SCRUTINY: high

SCOPE: ~/.claude/settings.json PostToolUse hook — one-line removal. Optionally: pi-agent-state.ts turn_end/agent_end path (for parity — Pi already separates turn_end from tool_execution_start correctly; verify no equivalent bug on the Pi side).

NON_GOALS: no @agent_state schema change; no new state values; no rework of the agent-state.sh script itself.

CONSTRAINTS: PreToolUse must remain (correctly sets running at tool start). Stop and SubagentStop must remain (correctly set done). Removing PostToolUse must not lose signal — the next PreToolUse or Stop will cover the boundary.

VALIDATION: 1) after removal, run a Claude Code turn with 3-tool batch, then observe events.jsonl — last state per pane before Stop should be 'running', Stop transitions to 'done', no further running until next UserPromptSubmit. 2) Ratio of done to running events in a normal session flips to reasonable (roughly 1 done per turn end, not 1 done per 100 tool calls). 3) picker wake-up polling on target pane sees done for at least 1s window after each turn.

OUTPUT: patched settings.json hook block, event-log evidence showing corrected ratio, updated xtmux-2i5 tracker.

PREREQ_FOR: xtmux-2i5 (xt pi --role). Discovered by evidence-based investigation in xt-design.3 during epic execution.
close_reason: PostToolUse hook removed from ~/.claude/settings.json this session. Evidence: last N events in events.jsonl now show only PreToolUse, no PostToolUse. Ratio corrected.

title: bug: message-send is silent append — no delivery signal to recipient pane
description:
PROBLEM: tmux-session-picker message-send appends a JSONL line to events.jsonl and returns 0. Recipients only see messages if they explicitly run message-list --for <self>. No bell, no tmux display-message, no pane wake. Escalation channel is a black hole under moderate load. events.jsonl also grows unbounded — no rotation, no --since default, no backlog-age view.

SUCCESS: message-send delivers a real signal: a bell / tmux display-message / picker-poll tick to the target pane so a running agent can notice. Recipient can see backlog age and unacked count without hand-crafted grep. events.jsonl gets bounded rotation.

SCRUTINY: high

SCOPE: bin/tmux-session-picker (message-send, message-list, ack, event log rotation), optionally pi-agent-state.ts if pane-side polling needs an extension hook.

NON_GOALS: no full pub/sub bus — keep it flat-file. No push-notification via external service. Rotation strategy is size-triggered (e.g. rotate at 10MB, keep 3), not time-triggered.

CONSTRAINTS: keep message-send synchronous and cheap. Delivery signal must degrade gracefully if the target pane is dead or unattached — never block.

VALIDATION: 1) message-send to a live target triggers a pane bell (or equivalent) that a Pi/Claude Code session can react to. 2) message-list --unacked shows backlog age in a human column. 3) rotate on size; older messages remain queryable from rotated files. 4) target-dead case: message-send exits nonzero with clear stderr, does not silently append.

OUTPUT: patched tmux-session-picker, log rotation, minimal delivery-signal wire test.

PREREQ_FOR: xtmux-2i5 (xt pi --role). Discovered by Agent C runtime-critique in xt-design.3 (finding F1).
notes: SMOKE-EVIDENCE (2026-07-07, xtmux-2i5 rollout): auto-notification path DOES fire correctly. agent_end → agent.turn.done + message-send with to=@agent_parent_session (session_id, e.g. $1495). But message-list --for uses string-exact matching. Orchestrator polling with pane target ('xt-design.3') or session name ('xt-design') MISSES the message routed to session_id ($1495). Fix scope expanded: message-list --for should ALSO normalize pane_id / session_id / session_name / pane-shorthand to the same underlying session, so any of them find the same messages. Also file: pane-vs-session address-space split. Reference log: /home/dawid/.local/state/xtmux/events.jsonl msg-1783377835-3746213.
close_reason: Shipped in a0f665f. Session-id normalization (recipients match regardless of alias), delivery signal via @agent_unread_count / @agent_unread_since / tmux display-message, dead $N/%N/@N targets exit nonzero + log message.failed, size-triggered rotation (XTMUX_EVENT_LOG_MAX_BYTES default 10MB, keeps 3), message-list --unacked age column, ack decrements counter. Contract tests: 129 pass, 0 fail.

title: bug: @agent_parent_session uses tmux session name (#S) not #{session_id} — silent misroute on session recycle
description:
PROBLEM: scripts/agent-state.sh and extensions/pi-agent-state.ts track parent session by tmux session NAME (#S). Names are user-facing, mutable, and reused across sessions (common after xt end + reattach). A child agent whose @agent_parent_session=main continues to send escalations to whichever session is currently named 'main', which may be an unrelated occupant.

SUCCESS: parent-session tracking uses tmux #{session_id} (e.g. $3), which is stable per session-instance and never recycled. Escalations either reach the original parent or fail loud when the id is gone.

SCRUTINY: high

SCOPE: scripts/agent-state.sh (metadata setters), extensions/pi-agent-state.ts (publish path that reads @agent_parent_session and calls message-send), bin/tmux-session-picker message-send (target resolution — accept both id and name, prefer id).

NON_GOALS: no rework of the message queue itself (that's a separate bead, xtmux-2i5 prereq #2). No breaking change to existing sessions with name-based parent set: on first read, migrate to id if the current pane's parent is still resolvable.

CONSTRAINTS: back-compat — accept both id and name for target resolution during transition. Emit a one-time warning when name-based routing is detected.

VALIDATION: 1) new pane launched with @agent_parent_session gets an id-shaped value ($N), verified by tmux show-options. 2) after 'tmux rename-session parent new-name', escalations from the child still route to the ORIGINAL session, not the current occupant of 'parent'. 3) if the parent session is killed, message-send target resolution fails clearly (exit code + stderr), not silently.

OUTPUT: patched agent-state.sh + pi-agent-state.ts + safe-send-pointer/message-send, regression test that exercises the rename-then-escalate scenario, xtmux-2i5 tracker updated.

PREREQ_FOR: xtmux-2i5 (xt pi --role interactive specialist launcher). Discovered by Agent C runtime-critique in xt-design.3 (finding F2).
notes: Applied patch to extensions/pi-agent-state.ts publishTurnDone(): both agent.turn.done log event and message-send --from now use #{session_id}. Log event also carries session_name for human display. Requires xtrm-tools rebuild + user reinstall to pick up. Verified compiles by inspection; runtime test blocked on rebuild pipeline.
close_reason: reader (extensions/pi-agent-state.ts) uses #{session_id} since 8f4d46b (live via symlink at ~/.pi/agent/extensions/); writer (core PR #362 worktree-session.ts) sets @agent_parent_session=parent's #{session_id}. End-to-end loop is session-id-based. Docs updated at 85fccf5. Migration warning skipped (no legacy panes carry name-based value; new spawn only).

title: Epic: xt pi --role interactive specialist launcher
description:

SUCCESS: Interactive coordinator specialists (starting with chain-coordinator) can be launched via 'xt pi --role <name>' as fresh Pi sessions with their own context, escalating judgment calls to the parent orchestrator via existing xtmux message primitives.

SCRUTINY: high

NON_GOALS: No new coordination bus (reuse xtmux). No .role.json schema (reuse .specialist.json). No @agent_role metadata (use @agent_task prefix). No --adopt flag (fresh worktree only). Both using-specialists-mpx and using-specialists-coordinator skills killed — extend existing multiplexing skill instead.

title: Create flow: fzf over worktrees + recent dirs → new session
description:
## Context

Worktree sessions are spawned constantly but the picker only switches between existing ones. Adding a create flow makes it a one-stop switcher.

## What to build

- `ctrl-n` → a second fzf over candidate dirs:
  - `git worktree list` across known repos (all panes' git roots + a configured repo list).
  - `z`/`zoxide` recent dirs as a fallback/supplement.
  - Recent worktrees by convention (`.xtrm/worktrees/<name>` → default session name `<name>`).
- On select: `tmux new-session -d -c <path> -s <name>` then switch to it.
- Derive `<name>` from the dir basename (collisions → append short hash).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ctrl-n` opens a dir picker; selecting creates + switches to a new session.
- [ ] Worktrees and zoxide dirs both appear.
- [ ] Name collisions handled deterministically.
- [ ] README documents the flow + key.

## Approach notes

- Reuse `git_root_for_path` infra to enumerate known roots.
- Gate `zoxide`/`z` behind availability; degrade gracefully.
- Layer: shell.
close_reason: Abandoned/reverted by operator request: Ctrl-n create flow caused confusing/noisy job/worktree enumeration; feature removed for now.

title: Confirm before kill: prompt on session alt-x
description:
## Context

`alt-x` kills a session/pane silently in one keystroke — risky for a busy agent session. Pane-kill is cheap; session-kill should prompt.

## What to build

- When `alt-x` targets a **session** row, show a confirm (fzf `execute` → `tmux command-prompt -p 'kill session X? [y/N]'` or an inline confirm), default No.
- Pane-kill stays immediate (cheap, reversible enough).
- Optional: push killed session names to a "recently killed" list file for awareness (not full resurrect integration).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `alt-x` on a session prompts; `alt-x` on a pane is immediate.
- [ ] Confirm defaults to cancel (No).
- [ ] No regression to the existing kill flow for panes.
- [ ] README updated.

## Approach notes

- Reuse `tmux command-prompt` for the confirm to avoid a second fzf spawn.
- Layer: shell.
close_reason: Completed: Alt-x pane kill remains immediate; session kill now uses tmux command-prompt defaulting to cancel, with kill-confirm helper, README update, and contract tests.

title: Staleness badge: surface idle time from window_activity
description:
## Context

`attn_list` already fetches `#{window_activity}` but never displays it. Dead/idle sessions aren't visually obvious.

## What to build

- Compute idle duration per session from `window_activity` (epoch) vs now; render a compact badge (`idle 12m` / `idle 2h` / `idle 3d`) on session rows.
- Dim or rank long-idle sessions lower (below the attention-ranked head).
- Optional env `TMUX_PICKER_STALE_MINS` (default 60) threshold for "stale" styling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Session rows show idle duration badge.
- [ ] Sessions idle > threshold are visually de-emphasized.
- [ ] `window_activity` reused (no extra tmux calls beyond existing list query).
- [ ] Status-line/list contract tests still pass.

## Approach notes

- `tmux list-sessions -F '#{session_id}...#{session_activity}'` (note: `session_activity`, not window) — verify the right format var during impl.
- Humanize durations in bash (min/hr/day).
- Layer: core (formatting) + shell (tmux var). Depends-on: t0.
close_reason: Completed: session rows now render idle duration badges from session_activity, stale sessions are dimmed/sorted below active non-attention sessions by TMUX_PICKER_STALE_MINS, and contract tests cover formatter/list behavior.

title: Cache invalidation: tmux set-hooks for session-created/closed
description:
## Context

The `list` TTL cache (default 3s) means a freshly created session is invisible for up to 3s. Shrinking the TTL hurts cold perf; instead invalidate on lifecycle events.

## What to build

- `tmux set-hook -g session-created 'run-shell "rm -f ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-picker-cache-<uid>/*"'`
- Same for `session-closed` (and optionally `window-linked`/`window-unlinked`).
- Ship as a snippet in README + an `install.sh`-optional hook installer, so the operator opts in.
- Keep `Ctrl-r` as the manual force-refresh (already bypasses cache).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New session appears in the picker on next open without waiting for TTL expiry.
- [ ] Killed session disappears immediately.
- [ ] No-op when cache dir absent.
- [ ] README documents the set-hook lines.

## Approach notes

- Cache dir already per-uid: `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-picker-cache-<uid>/` (see `list` subcommand).
- set-hook `-g` (global) so it fires regardless of attached session.
- Layer: shell.
close_reason: Completed: added clear-cache subcommand, optional install.sh --tmux-hooks hook installer, README hook snippets, and contract coverage for cache clear/hooks.

title: Cross-repo docs/ npm exclusion: verify in core + xtmux (r6g.9 follow-up)
description:
## PROBLEM

The specialists package explicitly ships one public document and excludes internal planning/design material. Verify the same publication boundary in xtrm-dev/core and xtrm-dev/xtmux so npm tarballs do not expose repository-only docs.

## SUCCESS

Both package manifests use explicit allow-lists with no broad `docs/` entry, and `npm pack --dry-run --json` proves that no `docs/plans/**` or `docs/design/**` path is shipped. If either package leaks those paths, tighten only that manifest and rerun the same check.

## SCOPE

- `/home/dawid/dev/core/package.json` (`files` only, if correction is needed)
- `/home/dawid/dev/xtmux/package.json` (`files` only, if correction is needed)
- Read-only comparison with `/home/dawid/dev/specialists/package.json`
- npm dry-run tarball manifests for `xtrm-tools` and `@jaggerxtrm/xtmux`

## NON_GOALS

- Publishing a new npm version or GitHub release
- Reorganizing, deleting, or rewriting repository docs
- Adding a reusable packaging framework or dependency
- Broad package-size/performance cleanup outside docs exclusion

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve every currently intended package payload entry.
- Prefer a no-code verification outcome when the tarballs are already clean.
- If correction is needed, use explicit allowed doc paths; do not add wildcard `docs/` inclusion.
- Do not modify unrelated or pre-existing dirty files in any repository.
- No runtime telemetry is applicable; the machine-readable `npm pack --dry-run --json` manifest is the audit artifact.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Core `package.json#files` contains no `docs/`, `docs/plans`, or `docs/design` wildcard/path.
- [ ] Core dry-run tarball contains no path under `docs/plans/` or `docs/design/`.
- [ ] xtmux `package.json#files` contains only intended explicit docs paths and no broad `docs/` wildcard.
- [ ] xtmux dry-run tarball contains only `docs/INSTALL.md` and `docs/keys.md` under `docs/`, with no planning/design docs.
- [ ] Run the dry-run checks from clean source state and confirm they produce no tracked source changes.
- [ ] Record package name/version, docs entries, total file count, and pass/fail for each repo in the handoff.

## LIBRARIES

N/A — this is package-manifest verification and, only if needed, a pure edit to existing `package.json#files` arrays. npm's built-in pack manifest is the oracle; no new dependency or helper is warranted.

## OUTPUT

Report per repository: manifest policy, exact packed `docs/` entries, total files, whether a source edit was required, changed files, and residual risk. If both are already clean, close as verified with no source-code change.

## REFERENCES

- Parent: xtmux-r6g.9
- specialists v3.21.0 reference: only `docs/overrides-guide.md` is packed
- Recent state: core PR #432 and xtmux PR #50 covered release/package hygiene without introducing a docs wildcard
design:
## Execution plan

1. Snapshot `git status --short` in core and xtmux so pre-existing changes are not touched.
2. Inspect each root `package.json#files` array and classify every docs entry as explicit or wildcard.
3. Run `npm pack --dry-run --json` in each repo; extract all `files[].path` values beginning with `docs/` and assert none begin with `docs/plans/` or `docs/design/`.
4. Stop with no source edit when clean. If a leak exists, edit only the leaking repo's root `package.json`, replacing broad docs inclusion with the smallest explicit allow-list that preserves public docs.
5. Repeat step 3 and verify `git diff --check` plus repo status. No publish, release, full test suite, or companion test bead is needed: npm's generated pack manifest directly tests this one-time publication contract.

## Planning baseline (2026-07-18)

- core `xtrm-tools@0.11.0`: 450 files, zero `docs/` entries; plans/design excluded.
- xtmux `@jaggerxtrm/xtmux@0.1.0`: 86 files; only `docs/INSTALL.md` and `docs/keys.md`; plans/design excluded.
- specialists reference `@jaggerxtrm/specialists@3.21.0`: only `docs/overrides-guide.md`.
- Expected implementation: verification-only/no source diff unless repository state changes before execution.
- Impact: LOW; no runtime symbols or execution flows are involved. Only npm publication payloads are in scope.

All manifests use explicit allow-lists; docs/plans/** and docs/design/** are excluded. No package source edits required. Core remained clean; xtmux only has the workflow-owned .beads/interactions.jsonl change.

title: Bridge: scope pane.capture to the topology snapshot
description:
PROBLEM: bridge pane.capture accepts any %id on the host's tmux server, not just panes present in the topology the peer was shown. For a read-only observation tool granted a bridge key this is arguably by design (topology already reveals every pane), but a peer could enumerate %0..%N and read panes with on-screen secrets. Found by adversarial review of j46.9 (Finding 5).
SCOPE: src/bridge/stdio.ts (pane.capture handler), src/domains/identity/pane-capture.ts.
SUCCESS: pane.capture restricted to panes present in a prior topology.snapshot, or an explicit decision to leave it host-wide with rationale.
NON_GOALS: cross-tmux-server capture (already impossible).
CONSTRAINTS: must not break the local pane capture command, which is unscoped by design.
VALIDATION: TBD — needs exploration.
OUTPUT: TBD — needs exploration.
close_reason: Merged #41: resolved as documented decision, not code. capture reaches exactly the panes topology already enumerates, so scoping is a no-op today (would only guard a per-viewer topology filter that doesn't exist). docs/bridge.md states the real invariant: whole-host observation, boundary is the key not the method.

title: Bridge: cap request rate / offload blocking spawnSync off the event loop
description:
PROBLEM: bridge handlers run synchronously in the stdin data listener; topology.snapshot and pane.capture use spawnSync, which blocks the whole event loop for the subprocess duration. A peer spamming topology.snapshot stalls all follows (throughput DoS, not a crash). Found by adversarial review of j46.9 (Finding 4).
SCOPE: src/bridge/serve.ts, src/bridge/stdio.ts.
SUCCESS: bounded per-connection request rate and/or non-blocking subprocess execution so one peer cannot pin the event loop.
NON_GOALS: rearchitecting the whole runtime off synchronous SQLite.
CONSTRAINTS: forced-command deployment already limits the bridge to one authenticated peer, so this is hardening, not a live exploit path.
VALIDATION: TBD — needs exploration.
OUTPUT: TBD — needs exploration.
close_reason: Merged #41: per-connection request-rate cap (sliding window, XTMUX_BRIDGE_RESOURCE_LIMIT before any subprocess spawn), mutation-tested. spawnSync-offload declined as disproportionate runtime-wide change, documented.

title: Flaky: fresh-db 'audit never leaks a raw SQLite error' fails as a 5s TIMEOUT on a busy tmux server
description:
## PROBLEM

tests/contracts/fresh-db.test.ts asserts that `audit --json` on a virgin DB emits no raw SQLiteError. On a machine with many live tmux sessions the command takes 4-5s (measured: 3.9-4.5s on feat/xtmux-j46.6, 4.7-5.2s on main — main is SLOWER, so this is not caused by any j46 change), which drifts across bun's default 5000ms per-test timeout. It then fails as a TIMEOUT, not as an assertion — so the failure message points at SQLite error leakage, which is not what went wrong. That is the worst kind of flake: it accuses the wrong subsystem.

Reproduced ~1 in 6 runs locally with ~10 live sessions. CI has a near-empty tmux server and has never hit it.

## SCOPE

tests/contracts/fresh-db.test.ts; possibly bin/tmux-session-picker audit (the walk itself).

## SUCCESS

Either the audit walk is fast enough that the assertion is what decides the test, or the test gets an explicit timeout with a comment saying WHY audit is slow (it is O(live panes), unlike its table-mates). A bare timeout bump with no explanation just moves the cliff.

## NON_GOALS
- Rewriting the audit command for performance (separate concern unless the walk turns out to be accidentally quadratic — worth one look).

## CONSTRAINTS
- The test must still fail if audit genuinely leaks a SQLiteError / 'no such table'. Do not weaken the assertion to fix the timing.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] 20 consecutive runs green on a tmux server with 10+ sessions.
- [ ] The SQLite-leak assertion still fails when migrate() is skipped (prove it stayed load-bearing).

## OUTPUT
Root cause (slow walk vs too-tight timeout), the fix, and the 20-run evidence.

title: xtmux help has hit its scannability ceiling (160/160 lines) — restructure before the next command family
description:
## PROBLEM

test/contract.sh asserts `xtmux help` stays within 50-160 lines, on the theory that a help text nobody can scan is a help text nobody reads. After j46 added three command families (IDENTITY/context, PANE CONTENT/pane capture, and the log query --after-id cursor), help sits at EXACTLY 160 lines. The next command that documents itself — j46.6 (log follow), j46.8 (handoff --wait-ready), j46.9 (bridge --stdio) are all queued and all need help entries — fails the test on arrival, and the tempting 'fix' is to bump the bound, which quietly retires the guard.

I trimmed my own j46.5 prose to land at 160 rather than raise the bound, but that is a stopgap: I bought exactly zero lines of headroom.

## SCOPE

bin/tmux-session-picker (help_text / mux_help), test/contract.sh (the length assertion), docs/json-command-api.md (the natural home for the detail that comes out of help).

## SUCCESS

Either help is restructured so detail lives in docs and help stays a scannable index (preferred — this is what the guard is FOR), or the bound is deliberately re-set with a written rationale for the new number. Not: bumped by 10 whenever it trips.

## NON_GOALS

- A --json help surface (already rejected in the matrix: a second surface to keep in sync).

## CONSTRAINTS
- The contract test that checks help field names against LIVE --json output must keep working: that is what stops help from drifting into fiction.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Help passes the length assertion with real headroom for the queued .6/.8/.9 entries.
- [ ] The help-vs-live-json field-name contract test still passes.

## OUTPUT
Restructured help + the rationale for whatever bound is chosen.
close_reason: Resolved in #34 the way this bead asked for: the band was re-set 160->200 ONCE, deliberately, with the rationale written into the test next to the assertion — not nudged by +5. The checks that keep help honest (two-way dispatch cross-check, documented field names vs LIVE --json output) are untouched. Help now has real headroom for .9/.10.

title: Deploy gap: xtmux context is on main but not in the installed binary (npm @jaggerxtrm/xtmux@0.1.0)
description:
## PROBLEM

`xtmux context --current --json` is merged to main (009901a) and works from a source checkout. It is NOT in what users and agents actually run: `~/.local/bin/xtmux` symlinks into the npm global package `@jaggerxtrm/xtmux@0.1.0`, published by PR #20 before the command existed. Running the installed binary today returns:

    {"code":"XTMUX_JSON_UNSUPPORTED","message":"context does not support --json",...}

Specialists' capture path treats malformed/unsupported output as "no origin" and runs normally (spec section 15). So the failure is SILENT: installed Specialists records no pane binding, Console shows no pane->job edges, and nothing anywhere errors. Merged is not deployed.

SCRUTINY: high

## SUCCESS

The binary that `xtmux` resolves to on this machine (and for any consumer installing from npm) answers `context --current --json` with `xtrm.runtime-origin.v1`. Specialists' F4 live E2E binds a real job to a real pane through the INSTALLED command, not a PATH override.

## SCOPE

Release path: package version + npm publish (see /releasing), or a decision to repoint ~/.local/bin/xtmux at the source checkout. CHANGELOG.

## NON_GOALS

- Changing the context contract itself (frozen, merged, tested).
- Deciding the operator's install mode for them — npm-published vs source-linked is their call.

## CONSTRAINTS

- `npm publish` is an operator-authorized action. Do not publish autonomously.
- Any interim workaround (PATH override to the source checkout) must be labelled as such and must NOT be how the acceptance E2E is finally proven.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xtmux context --current --json` from a plain shell (no PATH override) returns the v1 payload.
- [ ] `sp run` from a real agent pane records a spawn binding end-to-end through the installed command.

## OUTPUT

The released/relinked artifact, plus proof the installed command answers correctly.

## REFERENCES

Deploy-gap doctrine: /multiplexing "merged != running artifact". Same failure class as a merged PR whose container was never rebuilt.
notes:
RESCOPED — this is not an epic blocker, and calling it one was wrong.

I applied the deploy-gap doctrine (/multiplexing: 'merged != running artifact') reflexively. That rule exists for production services where a stale container makes every metric describe the old world. The premise does not hold here: the only consumer that matters today is the Specialists session on this same machine, and 'npm link' already makes ~/.local/bin/xtmux resolve to main. The contract is reachable through the exact fixed command string the spec requires (verified: plain 'xtmux context --current --json' returns the v1 payload, exit 0; outside tmux exits 1 with a structured error and empty stdout).

So nothing in xtmux-j46 or in the Specialists epic is blocked on a publish. A release serves OTHER machines and other users — that is release cadence, which is the operator's call on the operator's schedule, not a gate this epic gets to invent.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE and is worth keeping: whenever the next release IS cut, it must carry the xtmux-j46.19 vendored-bun fix, or the published package will ship a picker whose entire V2 JSON surface is dead for any user without system bun. That is a real defect (PR #26), it is tracked on its own bead, and it stands on its own merits regardless of when a release happens.

Downgraded P1 -> P3. Acceptance for the epic is proven through the linked install, not through npm.
close_reason: Resolved by source-link, per operator decision 2026-07-14. The world moved under the bead: ~/.local/bin/xtmux -> npm global is an 'npm link' symlink to the source checkout, so the installed binary already answers context --current --json with xtrm.runtime-origin.v1 (verified). Operator chose source-linked as the intended install mode; local consumers (this machine + Specialists here) work. Fresh-npm-registry publish is deferred out of the epic to xtmux-ro1 (P4).

title: Structured activity spans (thinking/tool/text start-end) — telemetry enhancement
description:
## PROBLEM

Compact thinking telemetry records cumulative character counts only, so exact durations (thinking_stream_duration_ms, time-to-first-activity, segment counts) cannot be computed (gaps doc 9.3). Explicitly NOT a blocker for the topology viewer.

## SCOPE

extensions/pi-agent-state.ts, src/domains/telemetry/, src/domains/events/query.ts, docs.

## SUCCESS

Agent activity is recorded as start/end span events {phase, segment_id, turn_index?, activity: thinking|tool|text, duration_ms?, char_count?} without storing any raw thinking content, enabling exact observed-stream durations.

## NON_GOALS

- Storing thinking/tool/text content.
- Claiming provider compute time — this is OBSERVED STREAM DURATION and must be documented as such.
- Blocking any other child of this epic.

## CONSTRAINTS

- No raw content, ever; char_count only.
- Reuse the existing event envelope; no new event stream.
- Must be describable as observed stream duration, not provider compute time.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Contract test: a turn emits paired start/end spans with matching segment_id.
- [ ] Contract test: duration_ms is derivable and no content field is persisted.
- [ ] Journal query shows spans for a live Pi turn (smoke).

## OUTPUT

Changed files, contract-test output, a sample span pair from a live turn.
close_reason: Merged #40: agent.activity completed-span telemetry via pi message_update/tool_execution boundaries; observed-stream-duration + no-content invariants pinned by unit + contract tests (each mutation-verified). Also fixed the #38 bridge topology flake.

title: Docs + skills + changelog for the new xtmux contracts
description:
## PROBLEM

title: pi-extension-load test fails opaquely when node_modules is stale
description:
## PROBLEM

`tests/contracts/pi-extension-load.test.ts` spawns `node_modules/.bin/pi` via spawnSync without
asserting the binary exists. When it is absent — e.g. any checkout that has not re-run
`bun install` since xtmux-d0a.13 added `pi` to devDependencies — spawnSync returns no status and
the failure surfaces as:

    expect(received).toBe(expected)
    Expected: 0
    Received: undefined

That message says nothing about the actual cause. It cost the orchestrator a false regression
scare on integrated main: both PRs were green in CI (where `bun install --frozen-lockfile` runs),
and the local failure looked like a merge regression rather than a stale node_modules.

## SUCCESS

A missing `pi` binary produces an actionable message naming the cause and the fix
(`bun install`), instead of `Received: undefined`.

## SCOPE

- `tests/contracts/pi-extension-load.test.ts`

## NON_GOALS

- Changing the isolation logic (HOME / PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR / --no-extensions / decoy marker).
  That part is correct and has teeth — leave it alone.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Do not skip the test when pi is missing. A silently-skipped contract is how a vacuous green
  gets reintroduced — the exact failure class d0a.13 existed to kill. Fail, but fail LEGIBLY.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] With `node_modules/.bin/pi` absent, the test fails with a message naming the missing binary
      and `bun install`. Assert on the message, not just the exit status.
- [ ] With pi present, behaviour is unchanged (still isolated, still leak-detecting).

## OUTPUT

The changed assertion and its output under both conditions.
notes:
ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION: I closed this as 'moot — only bit the tool-pilot workflow'. That was WRONG. tests/contracts/pi-extension-load.test.ts lives on main permanently (shipped by d0a.13) and is unrelated to the tool pilot. Its opaque failure ('Expected: 0, Received: undefined', with no mention of the missing pi binary) cost ME a false regression scare during integration on main, before the pilot even existed. It will cost the next person with a stale node_modules the same. Reopened. Still P3, but real.
PR #16 (xt/04vp-pi-test, off new main e19886b). All 4 checks green. No Codex thread.

FIX: assert node_modules/.bin/pi exists BEFORE spawnSync. New output (reproduced with ONE variable changed — intact env, only the binary moved aside; no PATH surgery):

  error: pi binary not found: <root>/node_modules/.bin/pi
  This test pins the Pi extension API and cannot run without it.
  Your node_modules is stale — `pi` (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent) is a devDependency.
  Fix: run `bun install` (CI runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`).

Also named the OTHER path to 'status: undefined': a spawn that fails outright (EACCES on a non-executable shim, ENOEXEC on a broken install) surfaces identically, so result.error is now reported instead of being left to the exit-status assertion.

FAIL not SKIP: this test is the only thing pinning the Pi extension API; a skip would hide it on CI too — if pi ever fell out of the lockfile the pin would silently evaporate rather than go red. A missing dependency is a broken environment, not an absent capability.

Assertions NOT weakened: exit 0 + three extensions + ambient-extension decoy (no leak from PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR) all still run — 3 expect() calls, same as before.

OBSERVATION (flagged, not fixed — outside SCOPE/NON_GOALS): expect(extensions).toHaveLength(3) asserts a local array literal has 3 entries. True by construction; pins nothing about what pi actually loaded. Real coverage is exit status + ambient decoy. Making it meaningful requires parsing pi's output.

GATES (from inside tmux): bun install --frozen-lockfile / build / bun test 177 pass 0 fail / typecheck clean / verify-json-api PASS.
close_reason: PR #16 merged. pi-extension-load now asserts the binary exists and names pi + 'bun install' in the failure; also handles result.error (EACCES/ENOEXEC), the same status:undefined symptom. Fails rather than skips — a skip would have hidden it on CI too, and this test is the only pin on the Pi extension API. Original assertions (3 extensions, exit 0, ambient-extension decoy) preserved.
