title: Post-3xs: pi-inbox-reply warning is soft — agent may ignore reminder
description:
## PROBLEM

Verified in xtmux-3xs.34 self-smoke on 2026-07-13 after forcing a
new pi turn: obligation marker created, widget shows
'Reply required: $1732 (xtmux-3xs.34)', agent_end fires
ui.notify('Reply required: ...', 'warning'). BUT pi did not send a
reply. The warning is a soft UI signal; the agent doesn't parse it
as an action item automatically.

This is the layer above the mechanism: the extension surfaces the
obligation correctly; the agent's tool loop doesn't act on it.

## SUCCESS

Pick and implement one of:

(a) **Stronger UI signal** — e.g. inject the obligation reminder as
    an appended agent_end message that pi reads as part of turn
    output. Uses pi.on('turn_end') appendEntry or similar (per pi
    bundled examples like 'notify').

(b) **Pre-turn injection** — before pi's next agent_start, inject a
    system message into pi's context noting the pending obligation.
    Forces the agent to see it as part of its own instructions.

(c) **Auto-compose stub** — as an opt-in mode, extension composes a
    template reply and stages it for pi to complete + send. Riskier;
    could produce garbage replies.

(d) **Accept + document** — extension surfaces reminders; discipline
    layer is on the agent's own conversational compliance. Document
    the limitation in the SKILL.md / operator brief.

Recommendation: (b) — injecting a context note before the next turn
gets the message into pi's LLM prompt as instruction, which the model
is more likely to act on than a warning line in the UI chrome. Ties
to xtmux-3xs.36 (mid-idle scan) — combined they close both gaps.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts — pi.setHeader or context injection
  hook if pi API exposes one.

## NON_GOALS

- No auto-reply composition without operator opt-in (safety, matches
  xtmux-3xs.26 non-goal).

## REFERENCES

- xtmux-3xs.34 self-smoke: warning fired, agent ignored.
- xtmux-3xs.36 (mid-idle scan gap — pairs with this).
notes: PI API SURVEY: installed types.d.ts exposes before_agent_start with BeforeAgentStartEvent.systemPrompt and BeforeAgentStartEventResult.systemPrompt replacement; handlers are chained. setHeader exists but is UI chrome only. appendEntry is explicitly not sent to the LLM. sendUserMessage always triggers a turn and is inappropriate for merely strengthening an existing turn. Implemented option (b): append a bounded xtmux-reply-obligation directive to the assembled system prompt before each agent run when pane-owned markers exist. Injection contains only sender+bead metadata, never untrusted inbound summary text; it instructs agent-authored reply and forbids auto-compose. Contract proves pending marker produces the directive; existing consume test proves matching outbound send removes it. Typecheck green.
close_reason: Shipped pre-turn system-prompt obligation injection using supported API; no auto-compose and no inbound text trust escalation.

title: Post-3xs: obligation introspection command (xtmux-obs obligations list)
description:
## PROBLEM

Reply obligations live at /run/user/1000/xtmux-reply-obligations/
as filesystem markers. Their existence is only surfaced at agent_end
(via pi-inbox-reply.ts warning) and via the widget count. There is
no way to query 'what am I currently expected to reply to?' outside
those hook boundaries.

Cheap safety net: a CLI/extension command that lists all current
obligations for a given pane. Operators (and agents themselves) can
sanity-check pending obligations without waiting for a turn boundary.

## SUCCESS

- 'xtmux-obs obligations list [--pane %N]' returns JSON array of
  active obligations from the state dir: [{sender, beadId, messageKey,
  summary, createdAtMs, expiresAtMs}]. Optional --pane filter.
- Widget (nice-to-have): pi-inbox-reply.ts adds a keybinding or
  slash command to trigger a refresh of the widget's reminder line
  without waiting for agent_end.
- Bead close: worked-example of using the command mid-turn to
  discover a pending obligation before going idle.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-inbox-reply.ts — expose a helper that reads the
  state dir + returns the parsed obligation list.
- src/cli.ts — new 'obligations list' subcommand that reads directly
  from the same state dir (obligation state is filesystem-owned, not
  DB-owned, so no schema change).

## CONSTRAINTS

- No schema change (state is filesystem, deliberately).
- No cross-pane visibility leak — pane owns its own obligations
  (--pane filter is opt-in wider).

## NON_GOALS

- No 'obligations clear <id>' verb — clearing is deliberately gated
  on matching outbound send, not manual override. The rm bypass
  documented in .23 drain-stop reason stays as the escape hatch.
close_reason: Shipped pane-scoped filesystem obligation introspection with requested JSON shape, no schema/clear verb, targeted contract/typecheck/build green.

title: Post-3xs: auto-monitor tmux has-session precheck for phantom targets
description:
## PROBLEM

Even with xtmux-3xs.29's XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_SKIP_TARGETS env, the operator
still has to remember to set it every session. Discipline fails.

## SUCCESS

Before touching a pending marker or spawning monitor-agent, run
`tmux has-session -t <target>`. If tmux exits 1 (target missing), skip.
Any other exit code (tmux itself broken, timeout, etc) falls through to the
existing behavior — better to touch than to silently drop a wake we could have
armed.

Applied to both Claude Hook 1 and pi-auto-monitor.ts.

## SCOPE

- .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs — targetExists() helper via spawnSync.
- extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts — same helper (in-process spawn).
- test/contract.sh — a phantom-target case with a stub tmux that exits 1.

## NON_GOALS

- No caching of has-session results (correctness > perf; subprocess costs ~5ms
  and only runs on send-pattern matches).
- No SKIP_TARGETS deprecation — env stays as an explicit override for
  cross-tmux-server smoke setups where has-session can't be trusted.

## REFERENCES

- Related: xtmux-3xs.29 (SKIP_TARGETS env — the manual/explicit version).
close_reason: tmux has-session -t precheck added to .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs and extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts. Phantom targets auto-skipped without any env config. New contract test proves phantom vs real behavior. .23 and .29 tests updated to stub tmux (has-session accept-all). 150 bun / 140 contract (+1) / tsc pre-existing runtime-only. .29 SKIP_TARGETS env still available as explicit override.

title: Post-3xs: auto-monitor XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_SKIP_TARGETS env for synthetic targets
description:
## PROBLEM

Post-close smoke testing repeatedly trips the Claude auto-monitor drain-stop
hook on synthetic test targets (`alice`, `dst`, `bob`, `smoke:1.99`).
Every seeded send touches a `<target>_pending` marker; drain-stop then
demands a Monitor(wait-agent) arm for something that will never respond.

## SUCCESS

- `XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_SKIP_TARGETS` env: colon-separated exact-match list.
  Matching targets skip BOTH the pending-marker touch AND the monitor-agent
  spawn. Same shape as PATH.
- Applied in Claude Hook 1 (`.xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs`) AND the
  pi extension (`extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts`) so smoke tests unset once
  and everything downstream honors it.
- No new bead required for the pi side — pi should fold it into the same
  extension since the mechanism is identical.

## SCOPE

- .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs — parse env, skip early.
- extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts — same.
- Contract test in test/contract.sh: send to a skipped target → no marker.

## NON_GOALS

- Auto-detect synthetic vs real targets via `tmux has-session` — adds a
  subprocess spawn per send and isn't reliable for cross-tmux-server tests.
- `_PATTERN` regex — YAGNI until an operator actually needs it.

## REFERENCES

- Drain-stop reason string already documents the `rm` bypass; skip env is
  the ergonomic version.
close_reason: XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_SKIP_TARGETS env (colon-separated exact-match) added to .xtrm/hooks/auto-monitor-on-send.mjs AND extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts. Contract test proves skip behavior end-to-end. 150 bun / 139 contract (+1) / no regressions. Smoke tests can now export XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_SKIP_TARGETS=alice:dst:bob and stop tripping drain-stop.

title: Post-3xs: shadow-mode read comparators for log-query + audit
description:
## PROBLEM

xtmux-3xs.12 landed shadow-tee for writes (message-send/ack, log-emit) and read
comparators for message-list + monitor-list. Two read commands were deferred:

- log-query — V1 body is an inline awk/grep pipeline over rotated JSONL. Extract
  into a _log_cli_query_v1_body helper (mirror the pattern used for
  _message_list_v1_body in xtmux-3xs.12) and add the same capture/diff/emit
  shape.
- audit — the walk reads live tmux state which can drift between two invocations,
  producing racy false-positive divergences on a live V1-vs-V2 comparison.
  xtmux-3xs.17's --stable makes ORDER comparable; a fixture-driven audit
  harness (mock dashboard output, run V1 walk + V2 walk against the same
  fixture) would make CONTENT comparable.

## SUCCESS

- log-query has the same shadow-diff shape as message-list under XTMUX_OBS_V2=shadow.
- audit shadow comparator either (a) uses a stable input fixture harness, or
  (b) documents why runtime comparison is out of scope and is closed as
  "documented, not applicable".

## SCOPE

- Extract _log_cli_query_v1_body from log_cli_query() in bin/tmux-session-picker.
- Add shadow branch mirroring message_list's shape.
- Contract test extension: seed rotated JSONL, run under shadow, verify divergence
  detection.
- audit: either wire a fixture path or close as documented.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Zero effect on V1 output under mode=off.
- Best-effort — cannot fail wrapped V1 command.

## REFERENCES

- Parent design decisions: docs/observability-redesign.md §13 (deferred to
  follow-up section).
- Pattern: _message_list_v1_body + shadow branch in message_list() (this repo,
  merged in xtmux-3xs.12).
close_reason: log-query shadow-diff shipped (same shape as message-list — extract _log_cli_query_v1_body, add shadow branch). audit content-diff explicitly declined: audit_walk reads live tmux state which drifts between two invocations; live V1-vs-V2 comparison would produce racy false positives. .17 makes ORDER comparable via --stable; CONTENT comparability would require a fixture-driven harness (mock dashboard output + stub tmux) which is out of shadow-mode scope. Order comparison suffices for the audit oracle path (covered by .19's differential test suite). Contract 138/138.

title: Post-3xs: Pi inbox status badge using message count primitive
description:
## PROBLEM

Pi has no unobtrusive, project-scoped indication that the current tmux session has unacknowledged xtmux messages. The current full-list polling workaround is unnecessary work, while a footer status would compete with the operator's existing footer chrome.

## SUCCESS

A project-local Pi extension uses the message unread-count primitive to mount a compact `xtmux-inbox` widget below the editor. It renders a one-line inbox badge when nonzero, is removed at zero, refreshes only at documented lifecycle/tool boundaries, and never replaces the existing footer.

## SCOPE

- extensions/pi-auto-monitor.ts or a deliberately named project-local inbox extension
- .pi/settings.json extension registration only if a new project-local file is required
- focused extension/runtime smoke evidence

## NON_GOALS

- No custom footer, overlay, polling daemon, push subscription, or pi-lens-style persisted diagnostic state.
- No fold into globally installed extensions/pi-agent-state.ts.
- No sent/read history UI beyond the inbox badge.

## CONSTRAINTS

- BLOCKED until sender receipt/count primitive lands.
- Use `ctx.ui.setWidget("xtmux-inbox", ..., { placement: "belowEditor" })`, mirroring pi-lens placement but with a distinct key. Do not use setFooter or setStatus.
- Feature-detect setWidget for host compatibility; clear it with `undefined` at zero and on shutdown.
- Render a supplied string array or a width-safe component; do not copy pi-lens's raw diagnostic widget/persistence machinery.
- Preserve $TMUX guards and best-effort failure behavior.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] E2E: addressed unacked message produces a nonzero below-editor inbox widget after refresh.
- [ ] E2E: ack clears the widget.
- [ ] E2E: no TMUX/no DB/CLI failure leaves no stale widget and does not fail a Pi turn.
- [ ] Reload smoke proves no duplicate widget registration.
- [ ] Existing auto-monitor E2E remains green.

## OUTPUT

Project-local widget implementation, extension reload/E2E proof, and confirmation that existing footer chrome remains intact.

## APPROACH NOTES

pi-lens master uses ctx.ui.setWidget("pi-lens", factory, { placement: "belowEditor" }) plus a /lens-widget-toggle command. Reuse only that composable placement and optional-toggle concept. Its diagnostic persistence, explicit width-fitting, render callback, and stale-file reconciliation solve a far larger problem and are out of scope for one inbox count.
notes:
PRE-IMPLEMENTATION PI HOOK SURVEY (installed npm package + repo/user extensions, 2026-07-13)

API inventory: installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent docs/extensions.md and dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts enumerate project_trust, resources_discover; session_start/info_changed/before_switch/before_fork/before_compact/compact/shutdown/before_tree/tree; context; before_provider_headers/request and after_provider_response; before_agent_start, agent_start/end/settled; turn_start/end; message_start/update/end; tool_execution_start/update/end; model_select, thinking_level_select; tool_call/result; user_bash; input. There is NO message_received or notification_received event. message_* is Pi conversation lifecycle, not xtmux transport. No persistence callback exists; appendEntry persists only in one Pi session tree. For cross-session/project-local obligations, filesystem state is the correct durable seam.

UI inventory: setStatus(key,text) contributes footer status; setWidget(key,string[]|factory,{placement}) is keyed composable content above/below editor; setFooter/setHeader replace those chrome regions. Installed TUI docs require component render lines <= width, but string[] is explicitly supported. Decision: follow current bead/non-negotiable and use setWidget('xtmux-inbox', lines, {placement:'belowEditor'}), feature-detect it, and clear with undefined. The brief's earlier setStatus wording is stale and conflicts with the bead; setStatus would be footer content.

Extension inventory: repo pi-agent-state is global, event-driven state publication (session_start, before_agent_start, agent_start, tool_execution_start, turn_start/end, agent_end, shutdown), only in-memory debounce/message state, no UI, best-effort pi.exec, and a required TMUX guard. Repo pi-auto-monitor is project-local, successful bash tool_result only, no UI/persistence, durable detached monitor ownership, and idempotency via monitor-list. User custom-provider-qwen-cli only registers provider/OAuth and persists tokens through Pi auth; user xtmux-agent-state is the global copy/symlink; disabled xtprompt registers command/shortcut and temporary custom UI, in-memory toggle only. Bundled examples surveyed: widget-placement proves keyed belowEditor widgets; status-line proves setStatus is footer; plan-mode combines setStatus/widget and appendEntry session restoration; notify uses agent_end; auto-commit uses session_shutdown; file-trigger uses fs.watch but is intentionally rejected here because no polling/watcher is needed. Bundled README index was checked across tools, gates, session, UI, provider and communication examples; none exposes an external inbound-message hook.

Refresh map: session_start (restore UI from SQLite/files), agent_start (catch changes since idle), successful/relevant tool_result for message-send/ack/list (update immediately), agent_end (final reminder), session_shutdown (clear chrome only). No timer/daemon/watcher.

IMPLEMENTATION/VALIDATION: pi-inbox-reply.ts is loaded exactly once through the already project-local pi-auto-monitor.ts registration. It calls .21 unread-count only at session_start, agent_start, and relevant bash tool_result boundaries; no timer/watcher. Keyed string[] widget is belowEditor, absent at zero, and cleared without TMUX or on unread-query failure/shutdown. Contract covers nonzero→zero, DB failure, and no-TMUX. Pi package load/reload smoke succeeded; existing auto-monitor remains loaded. Full result: 148 Bun tests + 138 shell contracts, zero failures; tsc and V1 fixtures clean.
close_reason: SHIPPED below-editor xtmux-inbox widget via the existing project-local pi-auto-monitor registration. Close NOTES contain the full installed npm event/UI inventory, repo/user/bundled extension survey, hook map, and validation evidence. Uses structured unread-count; zero/no-TMUX/query failure/shutdown clears unread chrome; no footer, polling, watcher, or duplicate registration. Verified 148 Bun + 138 shell contracts, typecheck, V1 fixtures, Pi extension load smoke.

title: Post-3xs: audit stdout sort under V2-only --stable flag
description:
## PROBLEM

Reported by xtmux:1.2 in their PR #1 handoff: V1 `audit` stdout emission order follows tmux enumeration order and is NOT stable across runs. This defeats byte-comparison of audit output in tests / shadow-mode / operator diffs. Under V2=0 we preserve V1 order for byte identity (per PRD §20); under V2=1 we could sort for determinism iff opted-in.

## SUCCESS

`xtmux-obs audit` gains a `--stable` (or picker gains `audit --stable`) flag that sorts output by (severity, kind, session_name, path). Default off preserves V1 order.

## SCOPE

- src/commands/audit.ts: sort branch under --stable
- tests/contracts/audit-stable.test.ts: two audit invocations on same input → byte-identical stdout under --stable

## NON_GOALS

- Do not change default behavior (byte identity preserved)
- No sort of persisted rows (order in DB is already deterministic on id)

## CONSTRAINTS

- V1 golden fixtures continue to pass without --stable
- Under --stable, output must be identical across process restarts on same input

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Without --stable: byte identity with V1 preserved
- [ ] With --stable: two invocations produce identical output
- [ ] Golden fixture harness updated with a `-stable.golden` companion

## OUTPUT

Flag added + one contract test + docs note.
close_reason: Added V2-only audit --stable display ordering while preserving default/V1 and persistence order. Contract, targeted oracle tests, syntax/diff checks, and compiled backend rebuild pass.

title: Post-3xs: retention scheduling documentation
description:
## PROBLEM

`src/db/retention.ts::applyRetention()` exists and is tested but there is no CLI subcommand exposing it, and no operator documentation on how to schedule it. Without a schedule the DB grows unbounded regardless of the well-tested preservation rules.

## SUCCESS

- Document a systemd timer + cron example in docs/observability-redesign.md §6 for running it daily
- Reference the retention envs in the same section for tuning

- docs/observability-redesign.md §6: scheduling section (systemd .timer + crontab)

## NON_GOALS

- No in-process scheduler (explicitly forbidden by PRD §25 "no mandatory daemon")

## CONSTRAINTS

- Docs give both systemd and cron examples so operators on either flavor are unblocked

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xtmux-obs retention` after seeded data deletes expected rows per Phase 10 tests

title: Post-3xs: PRAGMA optimize on connection close
description:
## PROBLEM

SQLite's own docs recommend running `PRAGMA optimize` before closing a connection so query-planner stats stay fresh. We don't. Cost of skipping it is a slow slide toward worse plans as data volumes grow.

## SUCCESS

`openDb(cfg).close()` runs `PRAGMA optimize` before `raw.close()`. Optional env override `XTMUX_OBS_SKIP_PRAGMA_OPTIMIZE=1` for benchmark comparability. One-line change.

## SCOPE

- src/db/connection.ts: modify `close()` to call `PRAGMA optimize` first

## NON_GOALS

- No scheduled `ANALYZE`
- No `VACUUM` (Phase 10 already ruled that out)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must not fail the close on `PRAGMA optimize` error (best-effort)

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Close still completes on a fresh DB
- [ ] 128 tests still green
- [ ] Verified via `PRAGMA analysis_limit` state on next open

## OUTPUT

Two-line diff + updated docs/observability-redesign.md §5 note.
close_reason: PRAGMA optimize runs on close (best-effort), opt-out via XTMUX_OBS_SKIP_PRAGMA_OPTIMIZE=1. Docs §5 updated. 140/141 tests. Smoke: fresh DB + close + reopen + health all green.

title: Post-3xs: slow-query envelope in db/connection.ts
description:
## PROBLEM

SQLite has no `pg_stat_statements` equivalent. Without slow-query logging, a bad plan (missing index, table scan under retention pressure) surfaces only as p99 latency after operators notice — days after the regression lands.

## SUCCESS

Every prepared statement runs through a timing wrapper. When execution exceeds a threshold (default 25ms; env `XTMUX_OBS_SLOW_QUERY_MS`), an envelope lands in `event_journal` with `type=db.slow_query, domain=db, payload={sql, duration_ms}`. Zero cost when nothing is slow (single Date.now delta per prepare).

## SCOPE

- src/db/connection.ts: wrap `raw.prepare` to time `all()`/`get()`/`run()` calls
- src/config.ts: XTMUX_OBS_SLOW_QUERY_MS (default 25)
- tests/integration/slow-query.test.ts: seed a slow query via synthetic `sleep()` UDF or a deliberately large scan; assert envelope written

## NON_GOALS

- No per-statement identifier / normalization (SQL text is enough)
- No histogram / p99 tracking within the runtime

## CONSTRAINTS

- Wrapper must be transparent to existing call sites (no signature changes on `raw.prepare().all|get|run`)
- Threshold check must be cheaper than the average query it wraps

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Query taking >threshold ms writes envelope; query under threshold does not
- [ ] All 128 existing tests still pass with wrapper enabled by default
- [ ] Overhead measured against Phase 10 benchmark: p50 delta < 0.5 ms

## OUTPUT

Wrapper diff + one test + before/after benchmark delta. Note: xtmux:1.2 was consulted but couldn't reply (idle); if they object to the shape of the wrapper (e.g. prefer a build-time flag over runtime env), rewrite accordingly.
close_reason: Slow-query wrapper landed in src/db/connection.ts. XTMUX_OBS_SLOW_QUERY_MS env default 25ms; 0 disables. Envelope prepared lazily (first slow query) so openDb-before-migrate is safe. 3 new tests (over threshold writes, under threshold does not, threshold=0 disabled). Bun 140/141 (todo unchanged). Overhead: within 500-iter run-to-run noise (< 0.5ms p50 delta constraint met by absolute-value margin).

title: Post-3xs: legacy monitor TSV importer + typed row reconstruction
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase 9 legacy-jsonl importer sinks monitor.started/done/timeout/killed events into event_journal via the unknown-type fallback — history preserved, but the typed monitors row is not reconstructed from historical .tsv files. This is fine for forensic replay but the importer's monitorsImported counter overcounts (it counts envelopes, not rows).

## SUCCESS

`src/migration/legacy-monitor-tsv.ts` reads $TMPDIR/tmux-picker-state-*/monitors/*.tsv and inserts one monitors row per historical monitor with terminal_status derived from PID + heartbeat freshness. Rerun-safe via UNIQUE(monitors.id).

## SCOPE

- src/migration/legacy-monitor-tsv.ts
- src/migration/runner.ts (wire the tsv importer alongside jsonl)
- tests/integration/migration-monitors.test.ts

## NON_GOALS

- Live monitor rows (already handled by src/domains/monitors/store.ts)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Source .tsv files never deleted by importer
- Idempotent on rerun

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Import test: N .tsv files → N monitors rows; rerun → zero new rows
- [ ] Terminal-status derivation matches xtmux:1.2's monitor lifecycle taxonomy

## OUTPUT

Handoff: monitor import counts by terminal_status; sample tsv → row transformation.
close_reason: Legacy .tsv → monitors row importer landed in src/migration/legacy-monitor-tsv.ts + wired into runner.ts. Terminal-status derivation from state + timeout freshness. Idempotent via INSERT OR IGNORE on PK. 2 new integration tests pass; 143 total bun, tsc clean.

title: perf(pi-ext): debounce agent-state writes; drop message_update handler
description:
extensions/pi-agent-state.ts fired setState('running') on every message_update event — many times per pi turn, each triggering a tmux set-option write. Add a debounce (XTMUX_PI_STATE_DEBOUNCE_MS, default 5s) that skips repeat writes for the same state within the window, and drop the message_update handler entirely (agent_start/tool_execution_start/turn_start already cover the 'running' state transitions).

Result: fewer redundant tmux set-option -p @agent_state calls per pi turn. Purely a hot-path cleanup; no operator-visible contract change.

Change is already in the working tree on main (must have been drafted during xtmux-1hq / xtmux-bje work). Just needs a bead + commit.
close_reason: Shipped in xtmux commit e0493d6. Debounce (XTMUX_PI_STATE_DEBOUNCE_MS=5000ms default) + drop message_update handler. .gitignore also collapsed 12 per-worktree entries into 2 wildcards in same commit.

title: bug: pi process tool strips PATH — spawns can't find npm globals (sp, xt, gh)
description:

Evidence: chain-coordinator smoke test (2026-07-07) called 'process start explorer-smoke sp run explorer ...' and got exit code 127 (command not found). Same coordinator's bash tool finds sp fine. Only affects the process tool.

SUCCESS: pi process tool inherits (or explicitly propagates) the parent shell's PATH so npm-installed binaries resolve. OR docs make the requirement to use absolute paths explicit.

SCOPE: pi extension host (process tool spawn config). No repo file, likely upstream pi runtime.

NON_GOALS: no rework of process tool API. no fallback shim inside sp.

VALIDATION: 'process start test sp --version' returns pi version, not exit 127.

TRACKED_BY: xtmux-2i5 (surfaced during smoke test).

REMEDIATION for now: dispatch sp via the bash tool (& for background) instead of the process tool. Documented in using-specialists-v3 §Notification.
close_reason: Documented workaround shipped in specialists PR #177 (merged 2026-07-07): using-specialists-v3 §Notification now spells out that pi's process tool strips PATH — use bash tool for sp/xt/gh dispatch; if process is unavoidable, wrap in 'bash -lc' or use absolute paths. Upstream fix belongs in pi runtime — out of xtmux scope. Workaround is field-tested (bash-tool dispatch was used successfully in the xtmux-2i5 smoke).

title: Assisted handoff wizard for bead + /tmp pointer workflow
description:
## Goal
Add an assisted handoff flow that helps the operator delegate safely without automating unsafe send-keys.

## Flow
- Select target session/pane.
- Create or select bead.
- Generate /tmp prompt-file for session-specific constraints.
- Show exact safe-send-pointer command.
- Require explicit confirmation before sending.

## Acceptance
- No multiline prompt is sent directly.
- The bead remains the durable task contract.
- The handoff flow can be cancelled at every step.

title: Multiplexing cleanup/audit report
description:
## Goal
Add an audit command/report for end-of-session multiplexing hygiene.

## Checks
- stale specialist sessions
- orphan worktrees or missing project paths
- agent panes without bead metadata
- dirty worktrees
- naming convention violations
- working sessions that should not be killed

## Acceptance
- Audit is read-only by default.
- Output separates safe cleanup candidates from warnings requiring operator judgment.
close_reason: Audit report shipped: audit is read-only and emits TSV warning rows (dirty/shared/working/no-bead/naming) separate from cleanup candidates (missing path/stale specialist). Validation: bash -n scripts/bin/tests, make test (113 pass, 0 fail), live audit smoke.

title: Timer registry for active agent monitors
description:
## Goal
Track active wait-agent timers/monitors so the orchestrator knows what it is waiting on.

## Behavior
- Add/list/kill monitor entries.
- Show target pane/session, condition, start time, timeout, and last observed state.
- Avoid custom IPC; use simple state files/process metadata compatible with tmux workflows.

## Acceptance
- A user can list active monitors after starting them.
- Monitors clean up their registry entry on completion or kill.
close_reason: Timer registry shipped: monitor-agent starts registered background waits, monitor-list reports active target/pane/state/start/timeout/interval/updated, monitor-kill removes entries, completed monitors auto-clean. Validation: bash -n scripts/bin/tests, make test (112 pass, 0 fail), live monitor smoke.

title: Live preview: tap-to-refresh (ctrl-t) + optional auto-tick
description:
## Context

Preview is a snapshot. Watching an agent think shouldn't require re-highlighting.

## What to build

- `ctrl-t` → `transform-preview` / reload preview for the current line (manual refresh).
- Optional auto-tick: a fifo helper (`tail -f` fed by a `while sleep N` loop) that refreshes the preview pane every N seconds while the cursor is stationary. Guarded behind `TMUX_PICKER_LIVE_PREVIEW` (default off — fragile/fragile resource).
- Document the tradeoff; ship tap-to-refresh as the default.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ctrl-t` refreshes the preview in place.
- [ ] Auto-tick mode is opt-in, documented, and cleans up its background loop on close.
- [ ] No leak of background processes after the popup exits.
- [ ] README updated.

## Approach notes

- Tap-to-refresh is trivial + robust; lead with it.
- Auto-tick via a named pipe + trap cleanup; consider `fzf --bind` with a reload scheduled by `sleep` — verify no leftover PIDs.
- Layer: shell.

title: Sessions-only vs expanded mode: tab toggles nesting
description:
## Context

At 11 sessions/21 panes nesting is fine; at 50 it's noise. A sessions-only overview doubles density.

## What to build

- `tab` toggles a sessions-only source (collapse pane rows) vs expanded (current).
- Persist last mode in `@picker_mode` tmux option or a state file.
- Border label reflects current mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tab` switches between sessions-only and expanded.
- [ ] Mode persists across opens.
- [ ] Expanded remains default on first run.
- [ ] README updated.

## Approach notes

- Implement as a `--with-nth`/source swap via reload with an env var the script reads.
- Layer: shell.
close_reason: Sessions-only nesting shipped: build_list accepts expanded/sessions-only mode, mode persisted in picker state, Tab toggles nesting, Space marks rows for bulk kill, list-active preserves active filter + mode, README/tests updated. make test: 75 pass, 0 fail.

title: Bulk multi-select: --multi + alt-X bulk kill
description:
## Context

Killing 6 stale worktree sessions one-by-one is tedious.

## What to build

- Enable fzf `--multi`; `tab` to mark rows.
- `alt-X` (capital) → kill all marked via fzf `{+}` expansion; keep `alt-x` for single.
- Reuse confirm logic from t5 for any marked session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tab` marks/unmarks; `alt-X` kills all marked.
- [ ] Mix of session+pane rows handled (session kill confirms, pane kill immediate).
- [ ] List reloads after.
- [ ] README updated.

## Approach notes

- fzf `{+}` = all marked, `{}` = current. Depends-on: t5 (confirm reuse).
- Layer: shell.
close_reason: Completed: enabled fzf --multi with visible marker, Alt-X bulk-kill binding, bulk session confirmation/pane immediate handling, README docs, and contract tests.

title: Richer filters: ctrl-f submenu (repo/branch/command/free-text)
description:
## Context

Current filters are state-only (all/waiting/running). At 30+ sessions, slicing by repo/branch/command or free-text grep is needed.

## What to build

- `ctrl-f` → a submenu/preview-switched filter mode:
  - by repo (distinct git roots), by branch, by command (agents only / shells only / bun only), free-text grep over pane capture.
- Implement via fzf `transform-query` + `reload($self list <filter-spec>)`; extend `build_list` to accept a filter spec beyond `all|waiting|running`.
- Cheap now that `list` is TTL-cached.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ctrl-f` offers repo/branch/command/free-text filters.
- [ ] Filter applies without a full cold rebuild (cache or scoped).
- [ ] Existing all/waiting/running binds unchanged.
- [ ] Contract tests pass.

## Approach notes

- Generalize the `list` subcommand arg into a small spec language (e.g. `repo:xtrm-tools`, `cmd:pi`, `grep:term`).
- Free-text grep captures lazily (cost only when that filter active).
- Layer: core (filter parse) + shell (fzf wiring). Depends-on: t0.
close_reason: Richer filters shipped: ctrl-f submenu with repo/branch/cmd/grep, list-active subcommand for robust fzf reloads, filter state survives cache invalidation. 25 unit + 15 integration tests, 72 pass.

title: Inline rename: alt-r for session/window
description:
## Context

## What to build

- `alt-r` → `tmux command-prompt -I <current> -p 'rename:' 'rename-session -t {2} %%'` (session) / `rename-window` (pane).
- No-op / correct target based on row type.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `alt-r` renames the highlighted session or window in place.
- [ ] List reflects the new name after reload.
- [ ] README updated.

## Approach notes

- `command-prompt -I` pre-fills current name for edit.
- Layer: shell.

On 2026-07-14 that checkout sat on main at 4003abe, 6 commits BEHIND origin/main (d7c29ec) — so the installed binary lacked the bridge and the other post-.8 merges ('xtmux bridge' returned 'unknown command'). title: Preview enrichment substrate: bead/worktree/git context for dashboards
description:
## Context

Originally this was framed as "dashboard enrichment". With the new `xtmux-mux` epic, the dashboard responsibility belongs to orchestrator-facing work (`xtmux-mux.6`). This task should instead provide the reusable preview/data enrichment layer that the orchestrator dashboard can consume.

## What to build

- Enrich session/pane preview with worktree context useful to any picker user:
  - explicit `@agent_bead` is already supported by `xtmux-mux.4`; keep it as the preferred source.
  - when `@agent_bead` is absent, derive a bead/issue id from known worktree/session conventions when possible (e.g. `.xtrm/worktrees/<name>`, session names, specialist metadata).
  - show bounded `bd show <id>` summary only when derivation is confident.
- Add git worktree health to preview:
  - uncommitted dirty count (`git status --short | wc -l` or equivalent)
  - bounded `git diff --stat`
  - optional branch/upstream/ahead-behind if cheap and already available
- Keep preview fast and safe:
  - no unbounded command output
  - no failure when not in a repo, no bead exists, or `bd` is unavailable
  - no dashboard/list-mode policy here; just preview enrichment helpers/output.

## Relationship to multiplexing dashboard

`xtmux-mux.6` should own the orchestrator dashboard/list-mode composition: state, bead/task, dirty tree, collision hints, idle/stale. This task owns the underlying preview enrichment and data extraction that can feed that dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria

- Worktree session preview shows bead id + title/status when explicit or confidently derivable.
- Preview shows dirty count and bounded diff stat for git worktrees.
- Missing bead/non-repo/unavailable tools degrade gracefully.
- Contract tests cover explicit metadata, derived/missing bead, dirty git preview, and non-repo behavior.
notes: Remodeled after xtmux-mux work: dashboard composition now belongs to xtmux-mux.6; this bead provides reusable preview/data enrichment (derived bead + git dirty/diffstat) consumed by orchestrator-facing dashboard work.
close_reason: Preview enrichment substrate shipped: conservative derived-bead detection from dot-number session/path conventions, bounded bd show context, git-worktree dirty count and bounded diff-stat in pane/session previews. Validation: bash -n scripts/bin/tests, make test (106 pass, 0 fail), tmux smoke for derived bead + git preview.

title: Help overlay: ? swaps preview pane to a binds cheatsheet
description:
## Context

The border-label hint is cramped; discoverability is low once binds multiply.

## What to build

- `?` → swap the preview pane content to a binds cheatsheet (all current keys), `?` again to restore.
- Generate the cheatsheet from a single source of truth (a `docs/keys.md` or an env-driven table) so it never drifts from actual binds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `?` toggles a cheatsheet in the preview area.
- [ ] Cheatsheet reflects all implemented binds (auto-derived, not hand-maintained).
- [ ] No key collisions with existing binds.
- [ ] README updated.

## Approach notes

- Land after the control-surface binds (t4/t5/t6/t7/t9/t10/t11/t12) are finalized so the cheatsheet is accurate.
- Layer: shell.

title: Frecency: persist last-used + count for idle-tail ranking
description:
## Context

Sessions you live in should float up below the attention-ranked head. Pure alphabetical sorts bury them.

## What to build

- On switch (`jump_to_target`), record `session_id` + timestamp to `~/.local/state/xtmux/frecency`.
- Compute a frecency score (recent + frequency) and use it to break ties below attention rank.
- Compact the log periodically (cap N entries).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Frequently/recently switched sessions rank higher among non-attention rows.
- [ ] Log file bounded (no unbounded growth).
- [ ] Degrades gracefully if state dir unwritable.
- [ ] Contract tests pass (sort change).

## Approach notes

- Score: recency-decayed count (e.g. last 100 switches, weight by age).
- Keep the attention-ranked head untouched (WAIT/RUN first), frecency only orders the rest.
- Layer: core (score) + boundary (state file). Depends-on: t0.

value: A consumed outbound wait must not satisfy a later same-target obligation: compare monitor.startedAtMs >= obligation.createdAtMs, and make wait-agent --wait-for-transition start a fresh cycle instead of reusing a consumed wait. Preserve default no-transition replay/idempotence.

A Specialists observability DB can appear malformed when the main .db is healthy but a mismatched -wal/-shm overlays an incompatible page-1 header. Compare normal PRAGMA quick_check/page_count with mode=ro&immutable=1; if immutable is healthy, stop all holders, archive DB/WAL/SHM, remove only sidecars, reopen, verify, then restart holders.

xtmux-j46.11 activity spans (PR #40): pi extension (extensions/pi-agent-state.ts) emits one COMPLETED span per streamed segment as an 'agent.activity' event {activity: thinking|text|tool, segment_id, turn_index, started_at_ms, duration_ms, char_count?}. Sources: message_update's assistantMessageEvent gives thinking_start/thinking_end and text_start/text_end with contentIndex + final content (content.length = char_count, no content stored); tool_execution_start/end keyed by toolCallId. Only *_start/*_end acted on — *_delta ignored so emission is bounded to segment boundaries. KEY DECISIONS: (1) completed span not start/end pair — start_time AND duration on one event, half the writes, no correlation (same 'record the fact not every observation' shape as monitors). (2) NO typed table — agent.activity falls through cli-log.ts default branch to emitEvent(), so it pages back through the SAME journalPage cursor as everything else, not a second schema. (3) duration_ms is OBSERVED STREAM DURATION (wall-clock between provider *_start/*_end), clamped to 0 on backward clock, NEVER provider compute time — this is a hard doc+test invariant. (4) tool spans carry NO char_count (result is content, a NON_GOAL) — omitted, never emitted as 0. Pure helper activitySpanArgs() is the unit-testable core. Also fixed a flake in the #38 bridge topology.snapshot test: it compared full payloads of two reads ms apart, so ticking last_activity_ms / a pane's current_command exiting startup->successor flaked it; now compares stable structure (names, window/pane ids, geometry) only.

@agent_instance_id rotates ONLY on --new-instance (Pi session_start / Claude SessionStart), never on idle: rotating per-idle would make every turn look like a new agent and scatter a pane's Specialists jobs across phantom instances. 'off' deliberately preserves the id (post-mortem attribution); the next --new-instance overwrites. host_id is a UUID at $XDG_STATE_HOME/xtmux/host-id, written atomically (bash 'set -C' / node 'wx') so concurrent pane starts agree; NEVER derived from /etc/machine-id — that would publish a stable host fingerprint into forensic events handed to another repo. scripts/agent-state.sh host_id() and src/domains/identity/host-id.ts must stay byte-compatible.

@agent_parent_session must be tmux #{session_id} (stable per-instance) not #S (mutable name). Reader side patched in extensions/pi-agent-state.ts (8f4d46b), writer side in core PR #362 (worktree-session.ts sets parentSessionId from tmux display-message). Message routing loop is session-id-based end-to-end.

V2 audit --stable must sort only the displayed audit TSV; preserve the raw walk order for persistence and all default/V1 output. Split the header before sorting the body: head+tail sharing a pipe loses data because head can consume the pipe buffer.

xtmux-3xs.30: auto-monitor hooks now run tmux has-session -t <target> before touching pending marker (Claude Hook 1) or spawning monitor-agent (pi extension). Exit 1 = target missing → skip. Any other exit (subprocess error, timeout) falls through to touch — better to arm a wake than silently drop one. Cost: ~5ms subprocess per send-pattern match (already rare). Fixed the recurring smoke false-positive from .29 which needed operator to remember env. .23 and .29 contract tests updated to stub tmux exit-0 for their synthetic targets. Companion to .29 SKIP_TARGETS env (kept as explicit override for cross-tmux-server smoke).

Claude Code notification gap (.23) closed by three-hook coordination + Monitor tool. auto-monitor-on-send.mjs touches ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/xtmux-auto-monitor/<target>_pending on every send match (skips wait-agent to avoid feedback). auto-monitor-consumed.mjs (via .sh prefilter, matcher: Monitor|Bash) deletes the marker when it sees "wait-agent <target>" in tool_input.command. auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs (Stop matcher) prunes stale markers (default TTL 1h via XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_TTL_MS), then if any remain outputs {"decision":"block", "reason": "..."} with the exact Monitor(command:"tmux-session-picker wait-agent <target> --wait-for-transition ...") invocation Claude must call. Loop guard: honors input.stop_hook_active — never blocks twice in a row. Bypass: XTMUX_AUTO_MONITOR_DRAIN_DISABLE=1. Depends on .20 (--wait-for-transition semantics) landed earlier. Registered in .claude/settings.json PostToolUse Monitor|Bash + Stop groups. Verified by test/contract.sh block "auto-monitor: three-hook Stop-block coordination (.23)".

When parsing colon/newline repo lists in bash via process substitution, use while read ... || [ -n "$item" ] because printf without a trailing newline makes a plain read loop skip the final/only entry.

Bash hot-loop perf: command substitution $(fn) costs ~2.4ms per subshell fork. For functions called 50+ times per render (formatters, normalizers), use the REPLY global convention (fn sets REPLY, caller reads $REPLY) instead of var=$(fn ...). Measured in xtmux: 125x speedup on paint(), took warm list from 500ms to 122ms. Applies to any bash tool with per-row formatting in a loop.

Beads 1.1.0 already owns lifecycle facts in its Dolt events table: UUIDv7 id plus created/claimed/updated/closed/reopened/status_changed, actor, old_value, and new_value. Host streams should project these as bd.<event_type>; use UUIDv7 time because created_at is currently local wall time mislabeled Z.

Never branch feature B off feature A's branch when A has an open PR: B's PR then CONTAINS A's commits, and squash-merging B lands A on main — bypassing A's own review gate entirely. This happened on xtmux #29 (j46.4 branched off j46.7): #28 was correctly BLOCKED on two unresolved P2 review threads (required_conversation_resolution is ON for main), and merging #29 silently landed those exact bugs anyway. Branch every feature from origin/main. If a branch must build on unmerged work, say so in the PR body and merge the parent first. Symptom of the mistake after the fact: 'gh pr view <A> ' shows BLOCKED/CLEAN while its content is already in main, and a fix branch cut from the old branch conflicts (mergeStateStatus=DIRTY) because it re-applies commits main already squashed.

The read-only xtmux bridge (j46.9, first REMOTELY-reachable surface, PR #38) passed two independent security reviews that caught FIVE issues the happy-path tests missed — the auditor caught 3, the adversarial pass caught those plus 2 more, including the worst one. Worst (High): the journal.follow loop was a detached 'void (async()=>{})()' with NO catch, and deps.db() (opens DB + can throw SQLITE_BUSY when a local writer holds the lock past busy_timeout) sat OUTSIDE its try — a throw became an unhandledRejection and killed the whole process; the sync path had the twin hole (dispatch ran handlers with no try inside the stdin 'data' listener = uncaughtException). main()'s try/catch covers NEITHER because both fire from detached callbacks after serveBridge is suspended. Med-High: the 'read-only' bridge called migrate()+PRAGMA optimize on every request and every 500ms poll — a remote read issuing DDL + BEGIN IMMEDIATE write locks + migration inserts on the shared DB; fixed with a new openReadOnlyDb() (readonly:true, no WAL pragma, no optimize) and the bridge NEVER migrates, so a read against a fresh host errors and creates NO db. Also: unbounded concurrent follows (cap MAX_FOLLOWS=4, XTMUX_BRIDGE_RESOURCE_LIMIT), stdout backpressure ignored (pause input until drain), and frame cap counted UTF-16 code units not bytes (~3x loose; Buffer.byteLength now). Plus S-01 (High, docs): the read-only guarantee is only as strong as the SSH key — a viewer key with shell access is NOT a boundary; docs/bridge.md documents the forced-command authorized_keys deployment (command=,no-pty,restrict) that makes it one. LESSONS: (1) a detached async task or a sync event-listener handler that can throw needs its OWN try/catch — the outer await's try/catch does not cover it; this is the concrete shape of 'a peer that can kill the server owns a DoS primitive'. (2) 'read-only' must mean read-only at the STORAGE layer, not just the method allowlist — check what the DB session actually does, not just which verbs are refused. (3) two reviewers with different assumptions beat one: the specialist auditor missed the crash bug the adversarial pass found. Follow-ups: j46.21 (event-loop blocking from spawnSync), j46.22 (scope pane.capture to topology). Codex bot on #38 independently re-raised the follow cap.

xtmux-3xs.11: bun build --compile produces bin/xtmux-obs (101MB single-file, --minify --sourcemap). Registered in package.json scripts as "build". picker bin/tmux-session-picker::obs_runtime_argv populates OBS_ARGV=[bin/xtmux-obs] when present, else [bun, run, src/cli.ts]. All call sites (obs_call, obs_call_strict, log_cli_emit/tail/query, message_send/ack/list, delivery-record, telemetry_start) use this helper. Deleted dead obs_v2_bun and obs_runtime_cli. Benchmark on 100k×100 corpus, 200 iters: bun-run baseline p50=73/p95=111/p99=134 → compiled p50=60/p95=76/p99=93 (all under 100ms PRD §21 target). Binary gitignored (/bin/xtmux-obs) — build locally. Cutover HOLD remains due to .12 shadow comparator + .19 differential oracle — not runtime perf.

SQLite pragma ORDER is load-bearing: 'PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL' takes an exclusive lock and is the one pragma that genuinely contends when several processes open a virgin DB at once. src/db/connection.ts set busy_timeout AFTER it, so the WAL switch ran with SQLite's default timeout of 0 and failed instantly with a raw 'database is locked' instead of waiting. Always set busy_timeout FIRST. Related: a *deferred* transaction cannot be rescued by busy_timeout either — SQLite refuses to honour it when upgrading a deferred read lock to a write lock (deadlock risk), which is why migrate() needed BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Both were found on a 2-core CI runner and were NOT reproducible on the dev machine even pinned to 2 cores under 24-way concurrency — for concurrency bugs, CI is sometimes the only environment that reproduces, and that is a reason to trust it over a green local run.

Cache split rule for tmux tools mixing slow static data (git root/status) with fast-changing derived state (agent badges/sort): cache ONLY the slow near-static half at the data layer (persistent table, long TTL), never the rendered output. tmux 3.5a has no option-changed hook so invalidation must be structural. Learned in xtmux xtmux-rib.17: a rendered-output TTL cache silently froze @agent_state-derived sort/badges for the whole window, making attention hooks pointless.

xtmux-1lb.5 (PR #380 merged 63646980): launchRoleTmuxSession now delegates attach-command choice to a pure chooseAttachCommand(sessionName, insideTmux) helper. Inside $TMUX → ['switch-client', '-t', name] (avoids nested-tmux warning); outside → ['attach-session', '-t', name]. This is the seam the expanded .5 child (current-pane exec + --new-session/--parent/--child + XTMUX_AGENT_* + log emit) inherits — the branching logic in launchRoleTmuxSession's exit path is already extracted.

claude-stop-transcript-settle-retry-2026-08-15: the Claude Code Stop hook (hooks/claude/claude-agent-turn-capture.mjs) must not read the transcript once — the async transcript writer can flush the final assistant line after Stop fires, so a single read stores the previous turn's text in agent_turns.last_message_text. Fix (xtmux-9yo): poll readTail() every 25ms up to a 1s cap, stopping when the assistant text advances (final line landed) or the file size is unchanged across a FULL poll gap. Key lesson: the settle comparison must span a poll gap — comparing the first two back-to-back reads settles instantly even when a fragment landed just before read #1 (caught by the mid-flush regression test, which streams the final line in 8-byte fragments every 10ms so size can never settle early). turnKey dedup uses the settled size+text so idempotence identity matches a later read.

Codex CLI 0.146.0 records hook trust POSITIONALLY, not by content. ~/.codex/config.toml holds [hooks.state."<abs hooks.json path>:<event_snake_case>:<entryIndex>:<hookIndex>"] with trusted_hash. An entry's trust therefore belongs to its INDEX. Consequence for any installer that writes ~/.codex/hooks.json: PREPENDING your entry shifts every pre-existing unowned entry down one index, so its recorded trusted_hash key no longer matches its position and the operator's own hook silently becomes untrusted and inert — with no error anywhere. xtmux did exactly this in every release up to v0.2.3; fixed in xtmux-s96.4 by appending behind unowned entries. Note the event name is snake_case in the trust key but CamelCase in hooks.json (session_start vs SessionStart). Rule: an installer sharing a positional-trust config file must never reorder entries it does not own. Related: xtmux is the sole writer of ~/.codex/hooks.json; Core must never write it.

Cutting an xtmux release with git-cliff: `git cliff --prepend CHANGELOG.md` ERRORS in this repo (Node stack trace, file untouched). Working method: (1) `node scripts/changelog.mjs --tag vX.Y.Z --strip header > /tmp/full.md` (regenerates full history sans header); (2) extract the new version block: awk '/^## \[X.Y.Z\]/{f=1} /^## \[PREV\]/{f=0} f' /tmp/full.md; (3) splice it into CHANGELOG.md between the 4-line header and the prior version, preserving the prior section byte-for-byte (verify with diff). No persistent [Unreleased] section is kept — git-cliff regenerates per release, so the committed CHANGELOG is header + released-version sections only. A stream cursor has three failure modes that are all SILENT — no error, no crash, just wrong data: (1) an INCLUSIVE cursor redelivers the last-handled row on every reconnect forever; (2) an empty page returning next_after_id=0 REWINDS a caught-up consumer to the head of the journal and replays everything — the empty page must ECHO the cursor the caller sent; (3) when retention deletes rows below the consumer's cursor it has a hole it can never fill, so serving it the next surviving page looks like a clean resume while rows go missing permanently — that must be a structured XTMUX_CURSOR_EXPIRED carrying oldest_available_id. But a cursor sitting exactly AT the boundary (oldest-1) lost NOTHING and must be served normally, or healthy consumers get spuriously reset. Cursor = committed SQLite rowid; never a timestamp (two events share a millisecond, clocks move) and never event_key (optional/domain-specific). Test it with a paging WALK asserting every row seen exactly once ascending — a count check alone passes for DESC pages and off-by-ones.

npm 11 strips ./-prefixed bin targets during publish: a bin value like "./bin/foo" triggers `npm warn publish "bin[x]" script name bin/foo was invalid and removed` and the published package.json loses that command (npm i -g then links nothing). Use BARE relative paths ("bin/foo", "scripts/foo.mjs") — npm pkg fix normalizes ./ away anyway. xtmux package.json bin entries were fixed to bare paths (xtmux-ee0) so @jaggerxtrm/xtmux publishes with all 7 commands (xtmux, tmux-session-picker, xtmux-obs, xtmux-monitor, xtmux-events, xtmux-install, xtmux-changelog). Verify with `npm publish --dry-run` (want zero bin warnings) before npm publish (xtmux-ro1). Note: npm pack tarball retains bins even with ./, so pack alone does not catch this — use publish --dry-run.

tmux #{pane_current_command} names ONLY the foreground process, so it lies about agent panes launched through a wrapper: an 'xt claude' pane reports 'node' (the node wrapper bin/xt), not 'claude' — the real claude runs one level below it. xtmux-k0d: safe-send-pointer keyed its auto-double-Enter off that name, so xt-claude panes got double_enter=0, Claude Code's paste-detection ate the single Enter, and the pointer sat unsubmitted in the input box while the sender was told 'sent'. SILENT NON-DELIVERY — the worst failure a send can have. Fix: when the command name is inconclusive, walk the pane's process subtree (pgrep -P + ps -o comm=, depth 3) and look for claude. Discriminates correctly: 'xt claude' -> true, bare claude -> true, 'xt pi' -> false (a spurious 2nd Enter into a pi pane would submit whatever sits in its prompt). Same caveat applies to #{pane_current_path}, which reports the shared checkout rather than the worktree for these panes.

extract_bead_id in bin/tmux-session-picker scans a WHOLE filesystem path with a regex; before the fix, [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*\.[0-9]+ also matched 'tmp.9' inside /tmp/tmp.9aBcDeFgHi (mktemp's suffix starts with a digit ~1 in 6). Effects: (a) production — a pane whose cwd is a temp dir was labelled with the bead 'tmp.9', an id that exists nowhere; (b) CI — test/contract.sh flaked ~1 run in 3 and turned main red on an unrelated commit. It was INVISIBLE locally because derive_bead_id has a fallback branch that re-scans the path relative to root, and when bd is installed to validate candidates it recovers the right answer — CI has no bd, so only CI saw it. TWO LESSONS: (1) a regex over a whole path must anchor on the SHAPE of what it is looking for (real bead ids are <prefix>-<slug>.<n>; requiring the dash rejects tmp.9); (2) when a test only fails in CI, suspect a tool that exists locally and not in CI (bd, jq, tmux) masking the defect — and pin the regression on the PURE function (extract_bead_id), not the one whose fallback hides it.

xtmux-d0a.20: spawnSync on a missing binary returns status:undefined, so an exit-code assertion fails as 'Expected: 0, Received: undefined' — naming neither the binary nor the cause. It cost a false regression scare on integrated main: CI runs bun install --frozen-lockfile and stays green, so only stale local checkouts see it, and the failure looks exactly like a merge regression. Rule: any test that spawns a binary must assert the binary exists (and check result.error for EACCES/ENOEXEC, same undefined symptom) with a message naming the binary and the fix command. FAIL, do not skip: a skip would hide it on CI too, and pi-extension-load is the only thing pinning the Pi extension API.

Keep pi-agent-state and pi-auto-monitor separate: pi-agent-state is a global raw extension symlink, while auto-monitor is project-local opt-in. Folding would make project monitor behavior global. isBashToolResult is the correct documented narrow; after it event.input.command is typed, while event.details is result metadata, not the command source. Footer setStatus composes; setFooter replaces chrome.

Pi coordination command output can contain a compact first JSON object followed by middleware text; parse only the first complete string/escape/nesting-aware object, ignore unrelated JSON, and preserve actionable errors for xtmux-shaped malformed contracts.

Pi coordination continuations must re-read SQLite before sending, batch at most 20 validated message keys, suppress unsafe metadata, and defer terminal wake consumption while Pi already has pending messages.

Pi coordination parsing uses two classification thresholds: complete parsed JSON must contain every command-specific envelope field, while syntactically incomplete JSON may use a narrower multi-field signature solely to surface malformed xtmux output.
Pi inbox refreshes must share a per-cycle mutation budget across receipt acks, wake consumption, and pre-send rechecks; omit optional status enrichment rather than issuing unbounded serial reads.

pi extensions: a ctx captured at event time is invalid after session_shutdown (reload/new/fork/switch). Never hold a captured ctx across async boundaries; keep active ctx in closure state and re-read it after every await.

Pi inbox pane scoping: cache #{pane_id} at session_start and pass --pane to every unread-count; if TMUX/pane lookup fails, omit --pane to preserve session-wide behavior rather than report silent zero.

Pi has no external inbound-message hook. Project-local xtmux coordination therefore refreshes at session_start/agent_start and relevant bash tool_result boundaries; successful ack plus non-empty bead is actionable acceptance. Use keyed belowEditor setWidget, filesystem markers per canonical sender, and agent_end notify; never setFooter, poll, auto-reply, or clear on ack.

Pi reply obligations can become stale when operation order is reply then late manual ack: outbound reply clears the marker, but pi-inbox-reply's message-ack tool_result recreates it even though inbox is empty. Track in xtmux-3ua.

Pi has no inbound-message event, but extension setInterval timers survive idle turn boundaries in the persistent runtime. pi-inbox-reply uses a 30s configurable structured scan, overlap guard, unref, and session_shutdown cancellation.

Pi monitor-agent returns immediately after spawning monitor-run, so its process exit cannot signal peer completion. Capture the durable monitor ID, persist a pane-owned outbound expectation, and have the idle poll consume it when monitor-list no longer reports the ID; ExtensionAPI.sendUserMessage(..., followUp) is the supported wake mechanism.

Pi runtime's process tool spawns subprocesses with a stripped PATH — npm globals (sp, xt, gh) exit 127 (command not found). Workarounds: (a) use pi's bash tool which inherits PATH normally, (b) if process is unavoidable, wrap in 'bash -lc' or use absolute paths ($(which sp)). Upstream fix belongs in the pi runtime, out of xtmux scope. Documented in using-specialists-v3 §Notification (specialists PR #177, merged 2026-07-07).

Pi reply polling must pair durable obligation recording with a sendUserMessage(followUp) wake only on first idle discovery; boundary scans should mark message keys seen without waking, preventing active-turn and refresh noise.

Pi before_agent_start can replace/chained-append the assembled systemPrompt. Reply obligations inject only sender/bead metadata (never inbound summary text) so the LLM sees the duty without elevating peer content or auto-composing.

Sender-declared Pi reply obligations: messages.expects_reply defaults false in the domain, but public beaded message-send defaults true with --expects-reply=false FYI opt-out. Pi scans structured expected/unacked rows at session_start, agent_start, and agent_end; it writes marker before auto-acking receipt, so only matching outbound send fulfills and restart does not recreate consumed work.
Pi inbox mutation budgets are extension-cycle state: all refresh handlers share one budget, and only session start or completion of agent_settled resets it; pre-send rereads stay mutation-free.

Pi SQLite coordination cutover: obligations list is sender/requester-owned (outgoing reply expectations), while recipient reply duties must come from pane-scoped message-list --expects-reply without --unacked so automatic ack does not erase restart recovery. Pi may combine both projections; only incoming duties enter the system prompt, and summary text stays out.

Pi tool-result extensions must not assume every stdout value beginning with `{` is one xtmux JSON document. Parse only recognized coordination envelopes and ignore unrelated, pretty, concatenated, or middleware-augmented output; tool commands themselves own failure reporting.

Pi structured_return + bun vitest can wedge indefinitely (~80min observed, twice, same session). When the subprocess dies or the invocation is unmapped, pi holds Working... forever and C-c does nothing. Recover by killing the subprocess PID (from pstree of pane_pid → sh→bun). If pi's own bun runtime gets killed, the tmux session survives but the harness is dead — commit + push from orchestrator, kill session. Do not run FULL vitest suites via structured_return in pi — use targeted files (e.g. tests/unit/cli/foo.test.ts) to avoid the hang.

Any 'is the target ready?' check MUST match the pane's CURRENT @agent_instance_id, never just the pane id. 'xtmux log query --type agent.ready --pane %N' is a HISTORY query: a pane whose previous agent readied and exited still has an agent.ready row, so a pane-scoped check returns true immediately and --wait-ready injects a handoff into a pane whose new agent has not finished initializing — the exact failure readiness exists to prevent. No @agent_instance_id at all means NOT ready (never 'ready by default'). Same class as: send-keys success is an ATTEMPT, never acceptance. Caught by review on PR #34.

release cadence for xtmux: 'make release VERSION=v<X.Y.Z>' on a clean main runs git-cliff --tag, commits CHANGELOG.md as 'docs(changelog): cut v<X.Y.Z>', tags, and pushes tag+HEAD. Tag push triggers .github/workflows/release.yml which runs tests, npm publish, and 'gh release create' with the tag's CHANGELOG section as notes. 'make changelog' alone regenerates against [Unreleased] without cutting a tag.

response-episodes-model-xtmux-gdk-2026-08-15: one episode = one user prompt + all Claude continuations until control returns to the operator. Invariant: the latest agent_turns row is NEVER the response — the episode is. Schema: migration 0014 (agent_episodes table + agent_turns.episode_id; index ae_pane_open on (pane_id) WHERE closed_at_ms IS NULL). Signals: Claude UserPromptSubmit hook (hooks/claude/claude-user-prompt-episode.mjs) emits log emit agent.episode.open with settled-size cursor + arms tmux @agent_episode_pending/@agent_episode_cursor; the Stop hook emits episode_open=1 on every non-continuation stop (stop_hook_active=false), 0 on continuations; pi extension emits episode_open=1 per agent_end; codex hook mirrors stop_hook_active. Obs: agent.episode.open dispatch closes+opens; completeTurn resolves the episode inside its tx (attach to the open episode with matching instance_id, lazy-open when none). Text source: input.last_assistant_message is PRIMARY (Claude docs: the transcript 'isn't guaranteed to include the final message at Stop time on all versions'); the settle-retry tail read is the cursor-filtered fallback. Viewer projection findLatestEpisode (xtmux agent-episode CLI): first substantive candidate (>=200 chars) is primary, later substantive ones followUps, short hook acks collapsed — a Mermaid response A can never be displaced by a later 'acknowledged' candidate. Retention prunes closed episodes with their turns. #103 must consume the episode projection, not LIMIT 1.

xtmux context --current --json (xtrm.runtime-origin.v1, merged 009901a) is the ONLY sanctioned way for Specialists to learn which pane/agent spawned a job. Invariants that must never be relaxed: (1) require BOTH TMUX and TMUX_PANE — TMUX_PANE alone resolves against a bystander tmux server, producing a fabricated verified:true origin that gets persisted in another repo's immutable forensic events; (2) omit absent optional fields, never emit "" — absent agent_instance_id means honest pane-level precision; (3) the command is EXEMPT from the --json XTMUX_OBS_V2 gate, because it reads tmux + the host-id file, never the observability store — gating it lets a legacy opt-out silently break the binding. Read-only: opens no DB, never lazily creates an agent instance.

scripts/test-session-events.sh follows the xtmux journal and Specialists job.started forensic events for one stable tmux session ID, normalizing both to a single arrival-ordered NDJSON stream; it intentionally does not globally timestamp-sort.

scripts/test-session-events.sh human render is now Archon-shaped multi-line blocks: a LEVEL [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm +ZZZZ]: type (dur) header plus indented key: value fields (colon flush, no alignment). Local time, ms, and UTC offset are computed in jq via localtime and mktime (offset = localtime|mktime minus epoch seconds; no GNU date dep). CONCURRENCY: the script runs 3+ followers sharing one output flock, so multi-line blocks must emit atomically. NUL-byte framing was REJECTED because a NUL truncates jq C-string output; instead each block is emitted as ONE JSON-encoded line (jq default output, newlines escaped) and a new emit_blocks helper reads one line per block and decodes it with jq -r under a single flock. --json keeps newline-delimited JSON via emit_lines. Supersedes the old single-line bracketed format.

scripts/test-session-events.sh human render supports ANSI colors: severity-colored LEVEL (info=green 1;32, warn=yellow 1;33, error=red 1;31), gray (90) timestamp, bold-cyan (1;36) event type, yellow (33) duration, cyan (36) field keys, reset after each segment. Color gating convention (reuse for other scripts): on when stdout is a TTY ([ -t 1 ]) AND NO_COLOR (no-color.org) is unset; --color forces on, --no-color forces off; machine/--json output never colored. Colors are ESC (\u001b) sequences emitted in jq via --argjson color bool and C(code)/R helpers; ESC survives the emit_blocks JSON-line round-trip (unlike NUL which truncates).

scripts/test-session-events.sh now follows major events for every session present in one startup dashboard snapshot and enriches NDJSON with session name/repo/path, session agents, pane agent/command/path; specialist child jobs are attributed through root_runtime_origin.tmux_pane_id. Restart the helper to include sessions opened later.

scripts/test-session-events.sh render() color gate: it passes `--argjson color "$use_color"` and jq does `if $color then`. In jq only false/null are falsy — the NUMBER 0 is TRUTHY. So to disable color you must set use_color=false (the script itself uses use_color=true|false, never 0/1). In scripts/test-session-events.test.sh set `use_color=false` before calling render for deterministic color-free assertions on the Archon block (header `]: <type>` + indented `key: "value"` fields). GOTCHA: never verify this test via `... | tail; echo $?` — the pipe reports tail's exit 0 and masks a real failure; run it bare (`bash scripts/test-session-events.test.sh; echo $?`).

scripts/test-session-events.sh surfaces xtmux command telemetry by selecting on the payload convention key .payload.module=="telemetry" (added xtmux-jd2), NOT a bd.* type regex — because Beads lifecycle events (bd.claimed/bd.closed/bd.created...) also stream through the xtmux journal and would collide with telemetry's bd.claim/bd.close. The module key disambiguates precisely and keeps the separate beads follower the sole source of lifecycle events. Render detail shows tool/outcome/exit/duration_ms/runId(correlation_id).

Shared-checkout git rule (xtmux, 3 agents on /home/dawid/dev/xtmux): NEVER 'git add <paths> && git commit' — bare git commit commits the WHOLE index, including anything another pane pre-staged. That is how 26fe3c7 shipped 16 unrelated files. Either 'git commit -- <explicit paths>' or run 'git diff --cached --stat' first and read it. Recovery when a contaminated commit is already pushed AND another branch is built on top: do NOT force-push (it orphans the downstream work) — fix forward, and let 'git rebase origin/main' drop the redundant commit via patch-id (it prints 'skipped previously applied commit').

SQLite live recovery pattern: take a consistent SQLite backup of the current DB, import intact append-only journals into that clone, verify identical schemas + quick_check/FKs, then under BEGIN IMMEDIATE two-way INSERT OR REPLACE current→recovery→live with foreign_keys temporarily off and validate foreign_key_check before releasing. This preserves post-incident live rows and historical recovery without a risky file/WAL trio swap.

tmux does NOT expand \t inside a -F format string — it emits a literal backslash-t. Format strings that need real tabs MUST use ANSI-C quoting: -F $'#{pane_id}\t#{pane_index}'. With plain single quotes, 'IFS=$'\t' read' never splits, every field after the first arrives EMPTY, and any comparison built on them is vacuous or impossible. This bit the xtmux-j46.3 topology geometry assertion: it could never pass against ANY implementation, and the mirror-image mistake (reading zero rows) would have PASSED while checking nothing. Verify with od -c, and always prove a new assertion can fail before trusting it.
tmux hooks support array indexes such as session-created[90]; using fixed indexes lets an installer be idempotent and avoid clobbering unrelated hooks on the same event.

tmux 3.5a: split-window into a session with NO ATTACHED CLIENT creates the pane correctly but prints 'no current client' and EXITS 1 (it cannot move focus). Neither -d nor -c avoids it. Under 'set -e' this killed scripts/xtmux-monitor.sh after the first split, leaving a plausible-looking 2-pane monitor. Older tmux exits 0 — which is why CI was GREEN and every dev machine running inside tmux was RED, on the same code. Rule: never trust the exit status of a split into a clientless session; ignore it and verify the resulting pane count (outcome check). Generalization for xtmux-d0a.19: a required gate that is green precisely where nobody looks is worse than a red one.

To ship a new xtmux CLI command (a scripts/ bash or mjs tool), register it in THREE places: (1) package.json "bin" map (name -> ./scripts/file), (2) package.json "files" array (so npm publish includes it), (3) scripts/install.mjs "bins" map (name -> join(root,"scripts",file)) which the installer symlinks into ~/.local/bin/<name> via link(). Source-linked installs point the symlink at the repo file directly. The command name (bin key) is independent of the filename, so a legacy-named file like test-session-events.sh can ship as xtmux-events. Use ${0##*/} in usage() so help shows the invoked command name. xtmux-events (scripts/test-session-events.sh) was added this way.

bin/tmux-session-picker resolves the V2 runtime in three rungs: compiled bin/xtmux-obs -> system bun -> node scripts/xtmux-obs.mjs (vendored bun from the npm 'bun' dependency). The third rung is the ONLY one that works on a published npm install: bin/xtmux-obs is not in package.json files:, and bun is not a system dep of a node user. It was missing until PR #26, which meant EVERY V2 JSON command (message-send, message-list, unread-count, monitors, log query, obligations) was dead on a bun-less npm install, failing with XTMUX_JSON_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE — an error that reads like a transient backend fault, not a missing runtime. Lesson: smoke-test through the real install path (npm link), never a PATH override; an override hides exactly this class of bug. Never delete the vendored-bun rung.

I closed xtmux-7ku (P0) on a verification that verified nothing: for 'a missing script must not block tools' I ran MY OWN wrapper snippet (sh -c 'p=/nonexistent; [ -f $p ] && python3 $p; exit 0') in isolation, saw exit 0, and called it proven. That tests the string I typed, not the hook that runs. The real ~/.claude/settings.json still had the raw unwrapped python3 command. Pane %1654 caught it and I reopened. RULE: when the claim is 'the system no longer fails', the evidence must come FROM the system — read the actual deployed config, or execute the actual registered command string extracted from it, or break the real thing and watch a real tool call survive. Evidence you reconstructed by hand is not evidence. Corollary discovered the same hour: my live delete-and-run test kept 'passing' spuriously because ANOTHER pane was concurrently running xt update --apply, which regenerated ~/.xtrm/skills and restored the file I had just deleted. Concurrent agents sharing a global tree will silently undo each other's experiments — check who else is installing before trusting a global-state test.

xtmux help-surface contract (test/contract.sh, xtmux-d0a.15, also run by scripts/verify-json-api.sh smoke): (1) `xtmux help` output must be 50-200 lines — the cap is deliberate, do not nudge it; to add a command you must trim elsewhere. (2) A "command" is defined as the first word of a line indented EXACTLY 2 spaces and starting lowercase; prose is indented deeper (3+ spaces) or starts uppercase or is at column 0. (3) Every such 2-space command line is cross-checked against the real dispatch table (the `case "${1:-}" in` arms in bin/tmux-session-picker); a command named in help that is not a dispatch arm fails as "phantom". Therefore STANDALONE bins (xtmux-obs, xtmux-monitor, xtmux-events) must NOT be listed as 2-space command lines — mention them as prose (e.g. a column-0 section-header note) instead. xtmux-events is mentioned in the OBSERVABILITY header this way.

xtmux installer owned() proves ownership of UNTAGGED Claude hook entries by command path. Any entry whose commands all live under /.claude/hooks/xtmux/ is xtmux-owned — only the installer writes there. Without that fragment, pre-provenance copies survive every remove-then-write cycle and accumulate (xtmux-2zh: 3x per hook).

xtmux json-api CI gate: scripts/verify-json-api.sh is the SUPERSET gate — it runs build, binary-freshness (src/*.ts newer than bin/xtmux-obs = FAIL), bun test, typecheck, shell contracts, v1 fixtures, and the live tmux smoke (scripts/smoke-json-api.sh). CI should invoke that script, not reimplement the steps in YAML. The freshness check exists because bin/xtmux-obs is a compiled bun artifact (untracked): running the smoke against a stale binary yields a FALSE PASS. Always 'bun run build' before smoking by hand.

xtmux native-Pi-tools pilot (d0a.8) MEASURED and CLOSED AS YAGNI 2026-07-13. Numbers on a fixed 4-call coordination task, native tools vs post-help CLI: retries 0->0, malformed calls 0->0, result tokens identical, subprocesses identical; invocation tokens 90->104 (+14); PER-TURN SCHEMA TOKENS 0->521. One task turn: 90 CLI vs 625 native (+594%). A tool schema is paid EVERY TURN; a Bash call only when invoked — the token argument for native tools is INVERTED. Root cause the tools were unnecessary: 'xtmux help' (d0a.15) closed 3 of pi's 5 real retries (--for required; the messageKey/summary null trap; the $1732 shell-expansion identity hazard) harness-neutrally for EVERY CLI, at a fraction of the cost. LESSON: when an agent-ergonomics problem shows up, fix DISCOVERABILITY before building tooling — and sequence the doc fix BEFORE the pilot so the pilot's measurement cannot be credited for wins the docs delivered.

xtmux-rib.11: filter submenu implementation insight —
1. Avoid fragile $(cat) quoting inside fzf bind strings by delegating the file read to a dedicated subcommand (list-active). This makes binds robust and the reload command trivial.
2. UI filter state belongs OUTSIDE the git cache dir so session lifecycle hooks (clear-cache) don't reset the active content filter.
3. Spec language grammar: comma-separated clauses, ANDed, unknown clauses silently ignored (never break the list). All attention presets (all/waiting/running) reset the content filter slot; ctrl-f sets a content filter; ctrl-r refresh preserves whatever is active via list-active.

xtmux ships bin/xtmux-obs as a 'bun build --compile' single-file binary with NO package.json or .git beside it at runtime. So 'version' build identity (commit/version/dirty/built_at) must be BAKED at build time via 'bun build --define __XTMUX_BUILD_*__=...' (see scripts/build.mjs); src/version.ts reads them via a 'typeof x==="string"' guard and falls back to live package.json+git only in dev/test. Plain disk/git reads like core's version.ts return nulls in the shipped binary.
